Part I

The Continent

This file extends the codex at asetheria-web.vercel.app without replacing it. Everything here is built on the codex as it stood when it was read (1,041 pages): canon facts are kept, contradictions are resolved in one direction and listed under Continuity notes, and every new person, house and district is tied to at least one thing that already existed. Each place shows its polished tagline with the current codex line under it, so either can be pasted back into the site. Secrets sit in the orange DM notes boxes; the button in the sidebar hides them all when you want to show a page to players.

The three empires, polished

Imperium Invicta The west · Latin basis

Codex now: Seven hills, one law: an empire that builds its roads before it wins its wars.

Seven hills, one law, and an army that never went home: the empire that built its roads before it won its wars, and now cannot pay the men who built them.

Motto: "Vincit qui se vincit" · Capital: Aeterna · Sovereign: the Imperator's empty chair; power: Dominus Militum Valerius Maximus

Iovianus Sandarion forged the Imperium out of fragmented human territories while demons, devils and warring gods poured across the land, then withdrew into seclusion in Aeterna "to mend his wounds" and has not been seen since. The Republic's Senate still meets and decides nothing. The Dominus Militum, a temporary wartime dictatorship made permanent, rules through the Council of Legates, provincial commanders now carving out private fiefs while they wait for the old general to die.

Five years of peace have exposed a war economy with no war: millions of demobilised legionaries promised land and pensions the treasury cannot pay, a grain dole fed by shrinking levies, coin debased quarter by quarter, and a patrician remnant that remembers the Republic and is waiting. The legions still drill. The merchant class prospers under military oversight and state levies.

Pressure points: the succession to Valerius Maximus · the veterans · the Annona · the Mavari co-rule at Mavelon · the Ephelanum Condominium.

Hellenoria The north · Greek basis

Codex now: A league of harbour cities: quarrelsome, brilliant and never far from the water.

A league of harbour cities that agree on almost nothing except the sea: quarrelsome, brilliant, and ruled from a capital whose emperor nobody has seen in ten years.

Motto: "Σοφία καὶ βούλησις, ἓν ἐσμέν" (Wisdom and will, we are one) · Capital: Hellarchon · Sovereign: Emperor Thalorion IV (unseen)

Mountains and coastline cut Hellenoria into city-states that grew up apart and govern themselves, bound by oath to the Imperial Family and, more practically, by the League of the Hellenes. Astraphael, the "Destructive Star", united them in the war and vanished after a duel with Iovianus Sandarion. The Arcane Academy sits under Hellarchon's violet dusk, which official texts call ancient magic and dissidents call a scar.

Peace has brought prosperity, westward colonies, the absorption of tieflings under the classified Voidfolk Accord, and every old quarrel back at once: democracies run by shipowning oligarchs, tyrants seizing the smaller cities, a Theoric Fund that cannot legally pay for a fleet, and a naval hegemon the rest of the League has begun to fear.

Pressure points: Hellarchon's hegemony · the tyrants · the emperor's absence · the Mavelon Contract arming Thebesieas · the Dreamers' Hunt.

Acheaoria The east · Persian basis

Codex now: The plateau empire of the King of Kings: gardens, fire-temples and caravans.

The plateau empire of the King of Kings: gardens in the desert, fire-temples, caravans to the edge of the world, and provinces that have started to keep their tribute.

Motto: "Together We Rise, Together We Conquer" · Capital: Persemenid · Sovereign: Shahanshah Vishtaspa III

Zindar Rashan al-Khavari united the Median tribes of the Dasht-a Khaliq with roads, and his heirs carried the empire across seventy percent of the continent before the war took most of it back. The Immortals never broke; the creed of assassins kills "only for the empire"; the arashshara, women overseers of production and trade, run the renaissance of craft that followed the peace. Qanats, wind-towers and ice-houses make the desert bloom.

Under the gold, the satraps are virtual kings, the court is a nest of eunuchs and rival zarates, the Magi resist every change, and the conquered peoples are remembering who they were. The redacted archive says Zindar was a servant from R'eyshar and Persemenid stands on a buried city.

Pressure points: withheld tribute · failing qanats · the Court of Vipers · the restless satrapies · the Cloudspine Feud with Duneforged.

The free powers Neither empire nor ruin

The Duneforged Citadel: House Caerthain's mountain-mining city in the south, Invictian-aligned, home of the Mithril Reserve, ruled by Duke Roderick Caesar over a thinning ore-body. Deiperduem: the neutral treaty city where the three road systems meet. The Malaunian Steppe, the Maeotis Helos and Zandar Isle belong to nobody and have outlasted everybody.

The old empires Fallen

Nethrana, the Kingdom of Mirrors and Mist, ruled from Eronis on Velothis by dream-walkers who bargained with the fractured gods of the Echo Plane and were unmade. Mycairos, the Kingdom of Bronze and Blood, built fortresses in old Hellenoria, dug up "the gift beneath stone", and emptied overnight on the eve of taking Velothis. Their ruins are where the codex's oldest secrets are buried.

The Grey Fog Why the gods do not walk

A grey fog walls the mortal plane off from every god, Titan and Outer power: they are confined to their own domains and temple-dimensions, and their grace reaches mortals only as it passes through the fog. Rifts and the Third Sun are cracks in it.

The Night of Five Stars The meteors

Long ago one great meteor and four lesser ones struck the continent. The four carried gems of pure elemental power (fire, water, air, earth) that have since been reforged, swallowed, carried between worlds and buried. See the Meteors and the Elemental Gems.

The ladder of rule: who counts as a duke

Every major city is governed by its empire's duke-equivalent, every town by a named governor, every village by a headman. The ranks line up across the three empires as below; each empire uses its own word, and a herald who mixes them up starts a diplomatic incident. The Duneforged Citadel uses the common tongue's titles (Duke, Marquis, Count), which its chancery writes as Dux, Marchio and Comes.

RankImperium InvictaHellenoriaAcheaoria

MarquisMarchio: warden of a frontier marchStrategos: elected general of a region or frontierMarzban: warden of a border march
CountComesEupatrid: head of a well-born houseAzata: lord of a zarate (noble house)
Town governorDuumviri (two annual magistrates) or a Praefectus (ports, garrison and road towns)Demarch, or a petty tyrannosFrataraka

Neutral and free: Deiperduem is run by an Arbiter drawn by lot; Duneforged by its Duke; Zandar Isle by a Hull-Reeve; Eronis by nobody.

Part II · The west

Imperium Invicta

Seven hills, one law, and an army that never went home. The capital first, then the cities (Mavelon as the DM has re-imagined it: a caldera port under two equal rulers; Romulo as the merchant capital), then the towns and villages.

The capital

Capital · Imperium Invicta · Latium Plains

Aeterna City

A million people on seven hills, fed by an aqueduct that is wearing out and a grain dole that is running out, and still the one city on the continent no army may enter under arms.

Codex now: Capital of the Imperium Invicta — a million people on seven hills, fed by aqueduct and grain dole, and the only city on the continent no army may enter under arms.

Ruler
General Valerius Maximus, Dominus Militum, in the name of an Imperator whose chair is empty
Title
Dominus Militum; the city itself under the Praefectus Urbi, Lucius Memmius Capito (rank of Dux, vir illustris)
Population
c. 1,000,000
Built on
Seven hills, a yellow river and a sacred line
Patron
Jupiter and Juno on the Arx; Mars and Bellona outside the line
Trouble
Short grain, light coin, and unpaid veterans camped at the boundary stones

Faith: The temples, shrines and cults of this city

The city

Seven hills and the valleys between them, and no view from any of them that is not building. Aeterna is brick-faced concrete six and seven storeys high, in streets so narrow that two carts stop each other, and over the roofs, on its double tier of arches, comes the Aqua Aeterna with sixty miles of Klynin spring water in it.

The public city is marble and the private city is not. Temples, basilicas and bath-houses are faced in stone from the Oros Mountain Range; the tenements behind them are plastered brick with the plaster coming off, and they burn often enough that the Vigiles are the busiest institution in the Imperium.

The boundary matters more than the walls. Inside the sacred line no soldier may bear arms. That is why the legions camp outside it, why a Legate lays down his command at the boundary stones before he walks to the Senate, and why the Obsidian Phalanx has been quartered beyond it for eight hundred years.

Aeterna produces almost nothing and consumes everything. Wealth arrives as tribute, rent and provincial revenue and leaves as construction, luxury and pay. The grain is the whole story: the Annona feeds the registered citizenry from provincial levies, the Golden Harvest Covenant supplies it, and the arithmetic has stopped working, because the Legates who govern the provinces now keep grain back to feed their own troops. Coin is being debased to cover the gap. The Temple of Juno records the debasement at every quarterly Assay, and the Mithril Reserve has begun discounting Invictian silver against its own weight. The city has not yet noticed. The city's bankers have.

No legion stands inside the line. The city is policed by the seven cohorts of the Vigiles, freedmen with axes and buckets and the only lawfully armed body within the walls, and defended by the fact that nobody has ever successfully besieged it. The real force sits outside: the Phalanx, the Legates' retinues in the suburbs, and several thousand demobilised legionaries with no land, no pension and a great deal of time. The Vigiles have been beaten by veterans twice this year. Both times the Council of Legates declined to intervene. Everyone involved understands what that means.

Life is loud, vertical and public. Most Aeternans rent rooms above shops, cook on charcoal in rooms that should not have fire in them, and eat out because their homes have no kitchens; the street is the living room. The day turns on the baths, free or nearly so, where business, gossip and politics are actually done. The Cycle of the Eternal Bloom buries the poor by subscription, which for most citizens is the most important contract they will ever sign. Above all this sits the patrician city: a few hundred families with country estates, private couriers and salons where the Imperium's real news changes hands. They resent the soldiers, remember the Republic, and are waiting.

Festivals. The Assay, quarterly at the Temple of Juno: trial pieces weighed against the standard before witnesses, once a formality and now the most closely watched morning in the city. The Ludi Aeterna, ten days of games each autumn, paid for by whichever Legate is buying popularity; the crowd is understood to be voting. The Vigiles' Night at midwinter, when the cohorts parade with axes reversed and every fire in the city is put out and relit from a single flame carried in from Romulo. And the Triumph, awarded by the Triumphant Vanguard of Glory under conditions the Treaty has made impossible to meet: none granted in five years, three Legates refused.

New lore

The empty chair. The Imperator's chair stands in the Hall of the Chair on the Mons Sedis: ivory and gilt bronze on a dais of seven steps, with a purple cushion changed on the first of every month. It has been empty since the Great Concord. The official form is that Iovianus Sandarion withdrew into seclusion to recover from his wounds, and every decree since has been issued "in the name of the Imperator, awaiting his recovery". Meals go into the sealed wing behind the hall three times a day. Physicians of the Radiant Heartwardens go in, come out and say nothing, which is their oath. Petitioners still lay written requests on the lowest step. A clerk gathers them at dusk, and nobody has ever seen one answered.

The stool. The Dominus Militum does not sit on the dais. He governs from a plain room in the old staff house below it, on the folding camp stool he has carried since his first command, and the city made the stool a joke, then a symbol, then a figure of speech: a man who "has the stool's ear" gets things done. Valerius Maximus is seventy-one, still rides, and has named no successor, because naming one would start the war the Council of Legates is already rehearsing.

What peace did. Peace came to Aeterna as people. Discharged legionaries walked home, found their land grants were paper, and came to the capital, where a dole ticket is easier to get than a farm. The tenements have taken perhaps a hundred thousand more mouths in five years, and rents in the Insulae have doubled. The Tent Rows have grown on the Campus Hastarum outside the line, where an armed man may lawfully keep his sword, and the Crimson Warlords' hall there feeds two thousand men a day and has not yet asked for anything in return.

Customs. Aeternans swear "as true as the stones" and mean the boundary markers. They measure rank by height, upside down: the poor live high and the rich live low, because the top floors burn first and the stairs are long. Every registered citizen wears a tessera, the bronze dole token, on a cord from the age of ten. Tesserae are heritable and saleable, and the price of one on the Mons Cerealis has tripled since the Treaty, which says exactly what the city expects of the next harvest.

Rumours. The geese on the Arx have stopped calling. The standard weight in Juno's temple is not the one it used to be. A lamp has been seen at a high window of the sealed wing. The Phalanx is at full strength for the first time in living memory and has started drilling at night.

Districts

The Mons Sedis Palace hill · Upper city

Palace and offices of state · courtiers, clerks, staff officers · cedar, lamp oil and floor polish

The hill of the Chair. The old palace of the Imperators covers its crown in courtyards stacked on courtyards, and most of them are offices now: the Military Prefecture, the chancery, the archive of the Council of Legates. The Hall of the Chair is at the centre and the sealed wing behind it. The south face drops straight into the Circus Aeternus, where the Imperator's box has been empty as long as the chair. Below the palace the old patrician mansions have been let, room by room, to the staff officers who actually run the Imperium.

Ties: gens Valeria; the Council of Legates; Political (Invicta); the Forum below.

The Arx Temple citadel · Upper city

Temples, mint and archive · priests, assayers, scribes · incense, hot metal and goose

A steep rock with two summits and the oldest gods on them: the great Temple of Jupiter on one, the Temple of Juno on the other, and on the saddle between them the record-house of the Aeterna Lexicon. Juno's precinct holds the Imperial Mint, fortified and windowless, where every bar is weighed twice and every worker searched twice, and the Geese Court, where the sacred geese that once woke the guards are fed from the temple stores and a guest who is rude to a goose is rude to the goddess. The quarterly Assay is held on Juno's steps. The Bankers' Stair runs down the rock to the Forum.

Ties: the Oathbound Sanctum; the Seekers of Eternal Truth; Quintus Arminius; the Purse (Invicta); Romulo keeps the master standard.

The Forum Civic heart · Valley

Law, market and religion on one pavement · everyone · wet stone, bread and argument

The original that every Invictian forum copies, and too small for the city it serves: a colonnaded square hemmed in by seven centuries of temples and basilicas, crowded from dawn. The Basilica of Aeterna hears cases from across the Imperium, and its property registers are where the bankers first saw the coin going light, a year before the Temple of Juno said so. The Curia of the Eternal Senate closes the north end, its bronze doors open for every session as the law requires. Between them stands the speakers' platform, where the Annona's shortfalls first show, in the form of a crowd. The Mithril Reserve's branch sits at the foot of the Bankers' Stair.

Ties: the Senate; House Calpurnia; gens Varria; Law (Invicta); Banking.

The Insulae of Aeterna Existing · Tenement quarter · Lower city

Brick tenements six and seven storeys high · most of Aeterna · charcoal smoke, wet plaster, frying fish

Behind the marble of the public city is the city people actually live in, and the worst of it fills the valley the locals call the Gullet. Brick-faced concrete six and seven storeys high, plaster coming off, streets narrow enough that two carts stop each other. Most Aeternans rent rooms above shops, cook on charcoal in rooms that should not have fire in them, and eat out because their homes have no kitchens. The blocks burn often enough that the Vigiles keep a station every four streets. Burial is by subscription to the Cycle of the Eternal Bloom. Since the Treaty the top floors have filled with veterans, and the rents have climbed with them; most blocks belong to House Ovinia, though no lease says so.

Ties: the Vigiles; the Cycle of the Eternal Bloom; House Ovinia; the Tent Rows.

The Mons Cerealis Plebeian merchant hill

Grain guild, shops and the circus · merchants, shopkeepers, guildsmen · flour, sawdust and horse

The commons' hill, outside the first sacred line until the city grew round it, and still proud of it. Ceres' temple crowns it, with the hall of the Golden Harvest Covenant beside it and the dole office in its portico, where tesserae are checked and the queue starts before dawn. The slopes are shops, workshops and collegia halls. The valley under the western flank holds the Circus Aeternus, three hundred thousand seats long, and by its gates the Amber Stalls, a lane of jewellers' booths where northern amber is sold with a story attached. Bring a loupe and a friend.

Ties: the Golden Harvest Covenant; Grain (Invicta); House Ovinia's new house; the Emporium at its foot.

The Emporium and Sherd Hill River docks · Riverside

Wharves, granaries and a hill of broken jars · porters, lightermen, Annona clerks · river mud, oil and grain dust

Where the barges from Fucostia tie up, under the Mons Cerealis. A mile of stone wharves, cranes worked by men in treadwheels, and behind them the great horrea of the Annona, each with a clerk at the door and a number on the lintel. Oil comes up the Tiberius in clay jars that cannot be reused, so for six hundred years the porters have smashed the empties and stacked the sherds: Sherd Hill, a hundred and fifty feet of broken pottery, with wine-shops dug into its flank because the cellars stay cool. The granaries are a third empty this autumn. The clerks have been told to stop chalking the levels on the doors.

Ties: Fucostia; the Prefect of the Annona; Grain (Invicta).

The Ripa Ulterior The Far Bank · Across-river quarter

Immigrants and foreign trades · Hellenorian-descended families, freed Acheaorians, dwarves, sailors · cumin, tannery and bread ovens

Across the Tiberius by four bridges and a dozen ferrymen. The Far Bank was never inside the sacred line, which made it the place where foreigners, freedmen and unlicensed gods could settle without asking. The Emberforge Collective's families keep their halls here; there is an Acheaorian street with a fire-shrine the Magi would not recognise, a dwarven lane of retired legion engineers, and, since the Treaty, the first Hellenorian wine-shops in a thousand years. The quarter's mills grind dole grain for House Lucretia's ovens, and the smell of bread at the third hour is the best thing in Aeterna. The Vigiles patrol it in pairs. The Far Bank patrols itself, in larger groups.

Ties: the Emberforge Collective; House Lucretia; Hellarchon's new traders.

The Campus Hastarum Field of the Spears · Outside the sacred line

Camps, war temples and the veterans' Tent Rows · soldiers, veterans, recruiters · leather, latrines and woodsmoke

The flat ground in the river's bend beyond the boundary stones, where armies may lawfully stand. Bellona's temple is here, where the Senate once received enemy envoys, and before it the war column, over which a spear is thrown to declare war; nobody has thrown one in five years. The Aeterna Garrison holds the north end on the standard camp plan. The Obsidian Phalanx keeps its ancient quarters beside it, at full strength. Between them sprawl the Legates' retinue camps and the Tent Rows, where some twelve thousand discharged men sleep under old legion leather. The voting pens where citizens once elected consuls are now a hiring market.

Ties: the Obsidian Phalanx; the Crimson Warlords; the Ironclad Legion's recruiters; Decimus Aurelianus Corvus; Military (Invicta).

The Horti The Gardens · Upper city

Patrician pleasure gardens and townhouses · old families and their households · roses, box hedge and, after rain, something else

Two centuries ago this ridge was the paupers' field, a line of open pits outside the old wall where the city threw its unclaimed dead. A consul bought it, laid twenty feet of earth over it and planted roses, and the patricians followed. The Gardens are now the richest ground in the city foot for foot: walled pleasure grounds, fishponds, colonnaded townhouses where the remnant's salons meet. After heavy rain the gardeners find bones in the paths and rebury them without comment. The Cycle of the Eternal Bloom keeps a columbarium at the ridge's end and a standing claim, never pressed, that the dead under the roses are still its members.

Ties: House Calpurnia; gens Varria; the Cycle of the Eternal Bloom.

Rule

In law the Imperium is ruled by the Imperator, and the Imperator's chair is empty. In practice General Valerius Maximus, Dominus Militum, governs from the Mons Sedis by decrees issued in the absent Imperator's name, and his authority is the loyalty of the legions he once led. The capital has no Dux: by ancient law no military governor may hold office inside the sacred line. Its civil governor is the Praefectus Urbi, Lucius Memmius Capito, who holds Dux rank, tries the Vigiles' prisoners at dawn, licenses the collegia and answers to the Dominus Militum alone. He is sixty, careful, and has survived two purges by owning nothing worth confiscating.

Three prefects matter more than their rank. The Prefect of the Annona, Sextus Naevius Macer, holds the grain contracts, the horrea and the barges, answers only to the Dominus Militum, and has twice petitioned to cut the ration; both refusals were correct. The Prefect of the Vigiles, Titus Oppius Ursus, commands the only armed men a Legate cannot lawfully order, and has begun quietly enrolling veterans. The Quaestor of the Mint, Gnaeus Laberius Asellus, strikes the coin the Assay then weighs. Outside the line the capital legion, the Praetorian Custodians, holds the Aeterna Garrison under Legatus Varus Decianus, loyal to the Dominus Militum and nobody else.

Who checks them: the Senate meets in the Curia, debates, votes and decides nothing; it ratifies decrees, confirms each Dux by acclamation and keeps the forms. The Council of Legates, nine commanders each with an army in his own province, meets on the Mons Sedis four times a year and in private constantly; its most dangerous members are Quintus Herennius Strabo of the north, Sextus Lollius Calvus of the south, and Decimus Aurelianus Corvus of the Latium Plains, whose legion sits a day's march from the line. The patrician remnant has money and memory, the Golden Harvest Covenant has the grain, and the crowd in the Circus has the numbers. Above them all is the line itself, and the question every faction asks each morning is who will cross it first. See Office (Invicta).

Houses and families

gens Valeria Military nobility · house of the Dominus Militum

Crest: a silver gauntlet closed on a laurel branch · Motto: "Valere est servire" (To be strong is to serve) · Seat: the old staff house on the Mons Sedis

An old plebeian family made great by the camp rather than the Senate: four generations of legion commanders and now a Dominus Militum. The Valerii own little land and less money than people assume. Their wealth is loyalty, held in the form of veterans who served under one Valerius or another and officers the general has promoted for forty years. They want the succession settled before he dies and cannot say so.

  • General Valerius Maximus, Dominus Militum — seventy-one; sleeps four hours, reads every provincial casualty list aloud to himself, and has buried two sons.
  • Valeria Prisca, his widowed daughter — keeps his house, his diary and a ledger of what each Legate owes him, the second most dangerous book in Aeterna.
  • Gnaeus Valerius Flaccus, nephew, Tribunus Laticlavius — capable, obvious, and assumed by everyone except his uncle to be the heir.
  • Lucius Valerius Maximus, Flaccus's son — twenty-three, five years a Treaty Guest in the Acheaorian compound at Deiperduem; he writes home weekly, and this year the letters have grown shorter.

Ties: Deiperduem (The Treaty Guests); the Mons Sedis; rivalry with Corvus.

House Calpurnia Patrician remnant · Comes

Crest: a gold wheat-ear crossed with a bronze stylus · Motto: "Ante legiones, leges" (Laws came before legions) · Seat: a walled townhouse in the Horti; estates around Romulo

Senatorial since the Republic and conspicuously poorer since the Dominus Militum became permanent. The Calpurnii lead the remnant in the Senate, where their head is princeps senatus: first to speak, last to matter. Their money is grain land around Romulo, worth less each year, and they have spent five years moving what they can out of debased silver into things a Legate cannot seize: Corinthian contracts, Mithril Reserve deposits, and a son-in-law abroad. The younger daughter's wedding at Lechaion, the Lechaion Marriage, scandalised the Senate and was very carefully planned.

  • Senator Gaius Calpurnius Rusticus, head, princeps senatus — sixty-four; has spoken against every decree for five years and voted for all of them.
  • Sulpicia Maior, his wife — runs the Romulo estates and the family's letters; a Sulpicia of Romulo by birth.
  • Gaius Calpurnius Rusticus the Younger, aedile — bought this year's street games and borrowed from House Ovinia to do it.
  • Calpurnia Prima, elder daughter — married to Lucius Ovinius Balbus; patrician blood for equestrian money, as every dinner party says.
  • Calpurnia Secunda, younger daughter — wife of Lykon Bacchiades, brother of Corinth's Prytanis; her letters come by Hellenorian courier, sealed twice.

Ties: Corinth and House Bacchiadai (The Lechaion Marriage); gens Sulpicia; House Ovinia.

gens Varria Senatorial · patrician remnant

Crest: an open book over a sheathed sword · Motto: "Scripta manent" (What is written stays) · Seat: a narrow old house in the Horti; the Villa Varriana above Falecosa

Senators and historians, never rich, always quoted. Its head, Senator Aurelius Varric, wrote the original chronicle of the Imperium Invicta and gave the empire the line it likes best about itself, "A civilization that conquers itself holds dominion over the cosmos", in what the record calls his Final Speech before the Eternal Senate. The family says he has retired to the Villa Varriana for his health. His seat is kept empty, his name is read at every roll-call, and nobody answers.

  • Senator Aurelius Varric — author of the chronicle; not seen in the Curia since the Final Speech; the published text carries an Inquisitor's corrections.
  • Senator Titus Varric, his son — took over the seat's duties, publicly regretted the word "cosmos", and is despised by his sister for it.
  • Varria Lucilla, his daughter — thirty-four, unmarried by choice, a copyist for pleasure, and the reader who has asked the Lexicon most often for the unedited manuscript.
  • Philemon, freedman secretary — took the senator's dictation for twenty-two years and has not taken anyone's since.

Ties: Falecosa; the Aeterna Lexicon; the Horti.

House Ovinia Equestrian · state contractors

Crest: a gold treadwheel crane on blue · Motto: "Nihil sine pretio" (Nothing without a price) · Seat: a new house on the Mons Cerealis, too big for its street

Equestrians: rich enough for a horse, not born enough for the Senate. The Ovinii made their fortune contracting for the war, in road gangs, siege timber and the hauling of the Annona. Peace moved them sideways. They hold the state contract to maintain the Aqua Aeterna, the charters for half the grain barges out of Fucostia and, through nominees, most of the tenements in the Insulae. They lend to patricians and marry their daughters, and they are the first family the Chyrsus Syndicate calls when it wants a partner in the capital.

  • Quintus Ovinius Balbus, head — fifty-eight; stammers in Invictian and never in arithmetic.
  • Lucius Ovinius Balbus, his son — runs the barge charters at Fucostia and knows the Annona's shortfall to the sack.
  • Calpurnia Prima, Lucius's wife — has quietly taken over the tenement accounts and raised no rents this year, which her father-in-law has noticed.
  • Hermia, freedwoman agent at the Basilica — files the aqueduct invoices, in which every span shored with one season's timber is billed as cut stone.

Ties: Fucostia; the Chyrsus Syndicate; the Insulae; Water (Invicta).

House Lucretia Freedman house · bakers to the Annona

Crest: a bread oven with three loaves · Motto: "Panem dedi" (I gave bread) · Seat: the ovens of the Far Bank; an oven-shaped tomb, already built, beside the Via Sacra Aeterna

Aulus Lucretius Eutychus was born a slave of the Lucretii, a patrician family that ran out of sons and money in the same decade. Freed by his master's will, he bought his master's house at the estate sale, took the name as the law allows, and made a fortune in bread. His ovens bake the dole grain into the city's loaves under state contract, so he knows to the loaf how short the Annona is running, and he has begun saying so to people who matter.

  • Aulus Lucretius Eutychus, head — sixty-four; wears his freedman's cap at festivals out of pride and a senator's-pattern ring the rest of the year out of spite.
  • Lucretia Fortunata, his wife, also freed — keeps the books and the keys, and buys tesserae from the dying; nobody has proved she does anything with them.
  • Aulus Lucretius Primus, their freeborn son — standing for quaestor; the patricians call him "the baker's boy" and will lose to him.

Ties: the Far Bank; the Annona; the Vigiles.

Notable figures

  • Quintus Arminius Imperial Archivist, Fourth Scribe of the Aeterna Lexicon — transcribes the agreed text in a fair hand and never annotates; the most honest man in the archive or the most useful. Knows where every censured page is shelved.
  • Inquisitor Marcellus Falco Imperial Inquisitor — the precise hand in the chronicle's margins, keeping what the empire remembers and what it wrote down the same document. Has read every seditious text in the archive, and wants the man who answers him.
  • "R." rebel historian · identity unknown — the hurried second hand that rebuts Falco line for line, in a copy that should never have left imperial hands and was somehow returned.
  • Scribe Pellion Meraquas scribe of the Lexicon, Fourth Circle of Mirrors — walked the Latium Plains, filed Praetor's Fall under Imperial Censure Tier II, and has not written a line since. He sits at the Lexicon's door most days and the Lexicon lets him.
  • Cassia Vetra Tribunus Angusticlavius of the Praetorian Custodians — seconded to the Vigiles as the legion's liaison; she calculates rather than shouts, values loyalty above everything, and is learning that the capital offers several kinds.
  • Marcus Ulpius Praefectus Castrorum of the Aeterna Garrison · mountain dwarf — logistics and bricks; has shored two of the Aqua's failing spans from camp stores and written a report on House Ovinia's invoices that nobody above him has read.
  • Legatus Varus Decianus Legatus Legionis, Praetorian Custodians · aasimar — the Dominus Militum's sword at the line; despises chaos, and regards the Tent Rows as chaos with a roll-call.
  • Sextus Naevius Macer Prefect of the Annona — "the Lean", to the city; knows the true level in every granary and says it only to the stool.
  • Titus Oppius Ursus Prefect of the Vigiles — a freedman's son with a broken nose and seven cohorts; wants his men to stop being beaten and has stopped asking how.
  • Junia Tertulla Keeper of the Standard, Temple of Juno — presides at the Assay and reads the figures aloud whatever they are; corresponds daily, and unhappily, with the Oathbound Sanctum.
  • Odvar Ironhand Dominus Argentar of the Mithril Reserve, Aeterna · dwarf — takes Invictian silver at eighty-six parts in the hundred this quarter, posts the rate on a slate by the door, and answers Lady Isolde Merca's letters the day they arrive.
  • Legatus Decimus Aurelianus Corvus the Iron Legate · Council of Legates — the commander whose legion camps nearest the line, and whom the Tent Rows already call by his first name.

Connections

  • Romulo — half a day by the Via Sacra Aeterna; the first city, the master weights, and the flame for the Vigiles' Night.
  • Fucostia — down the River Tiberius, a day by barge and two back; every sack of the Annona comes this way.
  • Anticata and Aepistra — up the Via Septentrionalis; Aepistra is six days out and the seat of the northern Legate.
  • Mavelon — by the Via Ferraria to the Iron Landing, or three days by sea from Fucostia; warships, and the nails Aeterna is built with.
  • Duneforged Citadel — three weeks south down the Via Ferraria; home of the Mithril Reserve that is discounting the capital's silver.
  • Falecosa, Nemibano and Napplesia — the wine hills, the grove the capital has failed four times to abolish, and the bay down the Via Litoranea where retired officers go to complain.
  • Deiperduem — by the Via Septentrionalis and the Treaty Road; Lucius Valerius Maximus is held in the Acheaorian compound, and Thrasyboulos Nikandrides in the Invictian one (The Treaty Guests).
  • Corinth — The Lechaion Marriage ties House Calpurnia to the Prytanis's family.
  • Ephelanum — The Ephelanum Condominium; its Dux is appointed from the Mons Sedis and his reports come through Aepistra.
  • Thessalonika and Persemenid — The Three Libraries; the Lexicon corresponds with the Porticoes and the Sage's Archive more often than its registers admit.
  • Hellarchon — the Hegemon's nephew is a Treaty Guest of the Imperium; Oros marble is landing on the Emporium wharves again.

The cities

City · Imperium Invicta · Latium Plains

Romulo City

The Imperium's first city, low-walled and two storeys high, where every institution keeps the copy that counts, including the master weights every great cargo and contract must be sealed against.

Codex now: The Imperium's first city and its ceremonial heart — small, ancient, and where every Invictian institution keeps the copy that counts.

Ruler
Dux Marcus Horatius Barbatus
Title
Dux of Romulo, vir illustris (a retired general's honour); trade under the Praefectus Ponderum
Population
c. 40,000 residents; half as many again in factors, caravaneers and pilgrims
Built on
One low hill, a mortarless wall and a rebuilt hut
Patron
Vesta of the first hearth, Janus of the gates, Juno of the weights
Trouble
Everyone needs Romulo's seal, and someone needs its master standard to be wrong

Faith: The temples, shrines and cults of this city

The city

Older than Aeterna and a twentieth its size. Romulo is low, walled in stone laid without mortar, and built around a hut that is certainly not the original and has been reverently rebuilt for nine centuries. Nothing inside the old wall stands above two storeys; the licence to build higher is essentially never granted, so the city looks much as it did when the Imperium was a market town with ambitions. Invictians come here to be reminded that the Imperium was once small.

Its business is archives, land and, now above all, trade. The Oathbound Sanctum keeps one of its three registers here; the Watchers of the Eternal Rest keep the veterans' rolls here rather than in Aeterna; a dozen guilds hold their founding charters in the basilica vaults. And because Romulo keeps the copy that counts of every institution, it keeps the master weights and measures: the standard pound, the standard foot and the standard measure of grain, against which every copy in the Imperium is checked. Every foreign cargo and every great contract must be weighed, registered and sealed here before it is lawful, so the merchant houses of Asetheria and of the Farshore Realms keep offices round the Guild Square. The concentration is deliberate: documents and standards kept in Romulo are outside the reach of anyone who takes the capital.

A town guard and no garrison, which is a statement rather than an oversight. The Order of the Silver Flame keeps a chapter house and guards the vaults. The city's real security is that sacking Romulo would be an act no Invictian faction could survive having done. That has held for nine hundred years. Several people have begun observing, quietly, that it has never been tested by Invictians.

Romulans are conservative to the point of obstruction and comfortable with it. They speak an older register of the language, keep festivals the capital abandoned, and regard Aeterna as a large, vulgar and regrettably necessary suburb. The priesthoods here are the senior ones: a rite performed at Romulo is the correct version, and disputes about practice anywhere in the Imperium come here for a ruling that is slow, thorough and final. The College of the Starlit Lute sends members every year to record the district's farm songs, the oldest attested anywhere.

Festivals. The Founding, a full day of processions ending at the hut, which every magistrate is expected to attend once. The Boundary Walk, when the old wall is walked and the sacred line re-marked with the Verdant Sentinel Order as wardens. The Reading of the Charters, three days of guild founding documents read aloud in full to a thin audience. And now the Weighing of the Standards each spring, when the master weights are brought out of Juno's strongroom and the copies from every city are tested against them in public.

New lore

The Treaty made Romulo rich again. Peace reopened the Farshore sea lanes, every cargo landed at Mavelon must be sealed here, and the seal-fee is a fortieth part. Factors' lodgings now crowd the suburb outside the wall, where the height licence does not run, and the caravan yards stink of camel and pepper. Romulans complain about all of it and collect the rents. The Vigiles' Night flame for Aeterna is still lit from Vesta's hearth here and carried to the capital by runners.

Districts

The Founder's Forum Sacred and civic heart · inside the wall

Forum, hut and basilica · priests, magistrates, pilgrims · old stone and thatch

The oldest forum in the Imperium and the smallest, a market square that became sacred by being first. The Founder's Hut stands at one end, thatch renewed each spring. The basilica's vaults keep the guild charters and the Imperium's founding documents. The baths are modest and built low, which Romulans regard as a virtue.

Ties: the Founding; gens Pinaria.

The Guild Square and the Hall of Weights Merchants' district · inside the wall

Offices, scales and seals · factors, weighers, notaries · wax, ink and foreign spice

A long colonnaded square behind the forum. Under the colonnade sit some sixty small offices, each with a mosaic on the pavement before its door showing the house's ship and emblem: the Qart-Hadethi elephant, the Tyrsan murex shell, Khemaret's ibis, Aksumar's coin, Sabaia's censer, Maurash's pepper vine, Pretanna's hound. Keftara's office has been shuttered for a decade; one swept, empty office is kept for the Seric Throne; a jade mask left by the Ixtali hangs over the weighers' door. At the square's end the Hall of Weights holds the public scales, and in the strongroom beneath it, under Juno's seal, the master standards.

Ties: House Vettia; Mavelon's Farshore Quays; the Oathbound Sanctum; Economic (Invicta).

The Vault Streets Archive quarter · inside the wall

Registers and rolls · scribes, archivists, Silver Flame guards · dust and lamp oil

Three lanes of low houses built over cellars cut into the hill, where the Oathbound Sanctum's register, the Watchers' veterans' rolls and the copies of a thousand great contracts are kept. Knights of the Silver Flame stand at each lane end. Since the Treaty a scribe here earns more than a centurion, and the veterans' rolls have acquired a guard of Crimson Warlords nobody asked for.

Ties: the Watchers of the Eternal Rest; the Order of the Silver Flame.

The Hearth Priests' quarter · inside the wall

Vesta's round temple and the colleges · priests and Vestals · woodsmoke and laurel

Vesta's small round temple, whose fire is the first fire of the Imperium and has not gone out in nine centuries, and around it the houses of the senior priesthoods, who rule on correct practice for every temple in the empire. Janus's double gate stands at the quarter's entrance, open, as it is in war; nobody has dared argue it should be shut.

Ties: Aeterna's Vigiles' Night; gens Pinaria.

The Ancestors' Row Patrician houses · inside the wall

Old family seats · patricians and their stewards · beeswax and cedar chests

Long, low houses whose atria hold the wax masks of the founding families' ancestors, each in its cupboard with its titles beneath. The families live in Aeterna and on their estates; they come here to bury, marry and be seen keeping the old forms. Several have quietly rented their front rooms to Farshore factors.

Ties: gens Sulpicia; House Calpurnia.

The Caravan Suburb Outside the wall

Inns, yards and lodgings · caravaneers, factors, pilgrims · camel, pepper and frying oil

Outside the old wall the height licence does not run, and the suburb has gone up four storeys in five years: inns, factors' lodgings, caravan yards, the Silver Flame chapter house and the hall of the Triumphant Vanguard of Glory, whose Master refuses Legates their triumphs and travels with an escort. The farmland beyond is the oldest in the Imperium and belongs to the same families it always has.

Ties: the Triumphant Vanguard of Glory; the Caravan of the Gilded Horizon.

Rule

Dux Marcus Horatius Barbatus, seventy-nine, holds Romulo as the traditional honour of a retired general who commands nothing; his granddaughter runs his household and most of his correspondence. The city's real business is in the hands of his deputy, the Praefectus Ponderum, Lucius Vettius Libo, who keeps the Hall of Weights and the seals and decides which cargoes are registered today and which next week. The Rex Sacrorum, Aulus Pinarius Natta, and the Virgo Maxima of Vesta, Tarquitia Lucilla, rule on rite, and a ruling from either binds the Dux. The Oathbound Sanctum holds copies of everything Libo seals, and the guilds of the Square can strike, which in Romulo means refusing to witness.

Houses and families

gens Sulpicia Patrician remnant · Comes

Crest: a plough under a star · Motto: "Primi in agris" (First in the fields) · Seat: the largest house on the Ancestors' Row

The biggest landowners of the Romulo district, patricians since before the Republic and hard-liners of the remnant. Grain prices have fallen and seal-fees have not, so they have begun buying offices in the Guild Square.

  • Servius Sulpicius Camerinus, head — brother of Sulpicia Maior of House Calpurnia; believes the Republic will return within his lifetime and is seventy-two.
  • Sulpicia Tertia, his daughter — manages the estates and leases front rooms to Qart-Hadethi factors at extortionate rates.

Ties: House Calpurnia.

gens Pinaria Patrician · priestly

Crest: a bronze sacrificial knife · Motto: "Rite et recte" (Correctly and rightly) · Seat: a crumbling house by the Hearth

The poorest of the founding families and the most respected; the Rex Sacrorum has come from this house for six generations. They own almost nothing but the right to say how a thing must be done.

  • Aulus Pinarius Natta, Rex Sacrorum — the one man in the Imperium still called king, and only of sacred things.

Ties: the Hearth.

House Vettia Freedman-descended · keepers of the weights

Crest: a balance with equal pans · Motto: "Aequa lance" (With an even scale) · Seat: the Hall of Weights

Descended from public slaves who kept the scales three hundred years ago; freed, enfranchised, and hereditary weighers ever since. Every factor on the Square courts them.

  • Lucius Vettius Libo, Praefectus Ponderum — honest, slow, and the most bribed-at man in the Imperium.
  • Vettia Rufina, his sister — chief weigher; can feel a light pound in her palm.

Ties: the Hall of Weights.

Notable figures

  • Himilkat of the house of Magon head of the Qart-Hadethi office · Farshore — tin, ivory and purple; keeps the largest office on the Square and the best table in the suburb.
  • Spurius Nonius Probus Master of the Triumphant Vanguard of Glory — has refused three Legates a triumph, correctly, and now travels with six guards.
  • Tarquitia Lucilla Virgo Maxima of Vesta — keeps the first fire and the master standards' second key.
  • Gaia Pomponia Atticilla Dominus Argentar, Mithril Reserve, Romulo — holds patricians' land deeds rather than coin, and lends to Farshore factors against Romulo seals.

Connections

  • Aeterna — half a day by the Via Sacra Aeterna; processions, patricians and the flame.
  • Mavelon — Farshore cargoes land there and come here to be sealed.
  • Duneforged and Deiperduem — export contracts and Reserve drafts registered at the Hall of Weights.
  • Atarabad — Silk Terminus contracts are sealed here when they continue beyond Aepistra.

Provincial capital · Imperium Invicta · the northern provinces

Aepistra City

A legion's camp that became a city when the legion moved two miles down the road: the Imperium's administrative model in brick, and the place where the Treaty Road's caravans end.

Codex now: An Invictian provincial capital built on the road — the Imperium's administrative model, exported and imposed.

Ruler
Dux Marcus Insteius Fronto (the city); Legatus Augusti Quintus Herennius Strabo (the province and its legions)
Title
Dux of Aepistra, vir illustris, appointed by the Dominus Militum
Population
c. 65,000
Built on
A legionary camp grid, kept when the legion left, with the camp-followers' town outside its old walls
Patron
Jupiter of the standards; Ceres for the estates; the old regional gods at home
Trouble
A Legate building a private fief around a Dux who cannot stop him

Faith: The temples, shrines and cults of this city

The city

A grid. Aepistra was founded rather than grown: the first legion of the northern conquest surveyed its camp on two crossing main streets with the headquarters at the intersection, and when the legion moved to a new fortress two miles out, veterans were settled in the old camp and the plan never changed. The forum stands where the headquarters stood. Everything an Invictian expects is present in the standard arrangement: basilica for the courts, baths, a theatre cut into the slope, an aqueduct from the hills. A citizen of Aeterna can find the law courts without asking directions, and that is the point. The city is an argument about what civilisation looks like, built in brick.

Its economy is administration and the road: tax assessment, courts and official traffic, with the relay station of the Cursus Legionis on the Via Septentrionalis. The farmland is worked in great estates owned mostly from the capital, and the grain goes to the Annona; the Golden Harvest Covenant has a strong chapter and has said loudly what it thinks of being paid in debased coin. The Chyrsus Syndicate holds the province's tax-farming contract, the single most resented fact in the city.

The local elite are enfranchised provincials with Invictian names, aggressively correct, lavish in public building and sensitive about being thought less Invictian than Aeterna; their Invictian is impeccable. Underneath, most of the city still speaks the older regional tongue at home and attends the imported rites without conviction. Festivals: the Founding Day, when the chief magistrate ploughs the boundary as the surveyors marked it; the Assize, half procession and half warning; and the Games of the Province, this year paid for by the Legate.

New lore

Peace made Aepistra a terminus. The Treaty Road from Deiperduem joins the Via Septentrionalis at its east gate, and the caravans of Atarabad now run all the way here (The Silk Terminus). House Suren-Pahlav keeps a factor in the caravan yards. The city is also the Imperium's administrative partner in The Ephelanum Condominium: the Invictian half's assessments of the red-earth estates, its legal appeals and the garrison rotations all pass through Aepistra's chancery, which keeps a Hellenorian-speaking clerk for the purpose. Meanwhile the Legate has been granting land to his own veterans and offices to his own clients, and the Order of the Silver Flame has increased its presence, which is generally a sign of what is expected.

Districts

The Principia Forum quarter · the old headquarters

Forum, basilica and chancery · magistrates, clerks, petitioners · ink, wax and pigeons

The forum at the crossing of the two streets, exactly where the surveyors put it. The basilica handles tax assessment for the whole province and the Chyrsus Syndicate's agents sit in its aisles. The old shrine of the standards is now the Dux's chancery, and the Ephelanum files fill its back rooms.

Ties: Ephelanum; the Chyrsus Syndicate; Tax (Invicta).

The Old Lines Barrack blocks turned townhouses

Elite residences · enfranchised provincial families · fresh plaster and imported marble

The long barrack blocks of the first camp, each rebuilt as a row of townhouses whose owners compete in porticoes. Every house has an Invictian name on the door and a grandmother inside who uses the old one.

Ties: House Flavia Brannoca.

The Canabae Camp-followers' town · outside the old walls

Taverns, workshops and the horse-fair · locals, carters, ex-soldiers · smoke, beer and dung

The settlement that grew against the camp's walls when it was still a camp: crooked streets in a grid city, taverns, tanneries and the horse-fair. The old regional tongue is spoken openly, the native rites are kept in back-yard shrines, and the Legate's recruiters drink here every night.

Ties: the Ollovici.

The Terminus Yards Relay station and caravan yards · east gate

Post-horses and caravans · couriers, Acheaorian caravaneers, customs men · camel, saddle-soap and saffron

The relay station of the Cursus Legionis, one of the busiest in the provinces, and beside it the new caravanserai where the Treaty Road ends. Whoever controls the station reads the province's correspondence first, which is why the Legate's men are always in the posting house.

Ties: Atarabad; Deiperduem; House Suren-Pahlav.

The Castra Nova The Aepistra Garrison · two miles out

Fortress and veterans' allotments · legionaries, settlers · leather and turned earth

The legionary fortress on the standard plan, two miles down the road, and around it the "Legate's Mile" of new allotments granted to his veterans, measured, ditched and recorded in his own name rather than the Imperium's. The city's walls are ceremonial; this is where the power is.

Ties: gens Herennia; Military (Invicta).

Rule

Dux Marcus Insteius Fronto governs the city for the Dominus Militum: courts, taxes, roads. His deputy, the Iuridicus Septimia Vera, runs the Assize and the appeals from Ephelanum. Above them both, in fact if not in law, sits Legatus Augusti Quintus Herennius Strabo, member of the Council of Legates, who commands the province's legions from the Castra Nova and has filled the posting house, the tax office and the council with his clients. The city council, led by Duumvir Tiberius Flavius Brannocus, has noticed and has no mechanism to act. The Chyrsus Syndicate's factor, Atinius Lucrio, holds the tax farm and answers to whoever renews it.

Houses and families

gens Herennia Military nobility · the Legate's house

Crest: a squinting owl on a spear · Motto: "Video" (I see) · Seat: the Castra Nova

A legion family that has commanded the northern provinces for three generations and stopped thinking of them as the Imperium's.

  • Legatus Augusti Quintus Herennius Strabo — "the Squint"; generous to his veterans, patient with the Dux, and counting the Dominus Militum's birthdays.
  • Herennia Galla, his wife — distributes the land grants personally, so the veterans thank her by name.

Ties: Mavelon (standing orders for iron); gens Valeria (rival).

House Flavia Brannoca Enfranchised provincials · Duumviral

Crest: a boar under a laurel · Motto: "Civis sum" (I am a citizen) · Seat: the largest house in the Old Lines

Descended from a native chief who opened his gates to the first legion and took an Invictian name for it; more Invictian than Aeterna and anxious to prove it.

  • Duumvir Tiberius Flavius Brannocus — paid for the new baths; flinches when anyone calls him Brannoc.

Ties: the Old Lines.

The Ollovici Native landholders · unreconciled

Crest: a white mare · Motto: in the old tongue only · Seat: the horse-fair in the Canabae

A native family that never took an Invictian name and still breeds the remounts the Cursus Legionis cannot do without.

  • Senna Ollovica, matriarch — sells horses to the relay station and the Legate alike, and keeps the old rites in her yard.

Ties: the Canabae.

Notable figures

  • Arshan Suren-Pahlav factor of House Suren-Pahlav · Acheaorian — meets every Atarabad caravan at the east gate; knows the Treaty Road's every toll and every bribe.
  • Kettil Ironhand Dominus Argentar, Mithril Reserve, Aepistra · dwarf — finances the caravans and holds the Legate's account, which grows faster than a Legate's pay allows.
  • Decimus Veturius Scaurus procurator for the Ephelanum files — reads Hellenorian, writes to the Archon's secretary weekly, and is the only man in the Imperium who understands the condominium's accounts.

Connections

  • Aeterna — six days down the Via Septentrionalis through Anticata.
  • Deiperduem — east along the Treaty Road, nine or ten days.
  • Atarabad and Corinth — The Silk Terminus: Atarabad's caravans end here or turn north for Corinth's Haulway.
  • Ephelanum and Hellarchon — The Ephelanum Condominium's Invictian files pass through Aepistra.

City · Imperium Invicta · the caldera coast

Mavelon City

A crescent of white cliffs round a drowned volcano: the Imperium's warship yard and greatest trading port, ruled by two equals who share one gate and two keys.

Codex now: A river city of bridges and mills in the Invictian interior — unfashionable, productive, and the place the Imperium's iron is actually worked.

Ruler
Reiks Ansvald of the Hrodnings (the Mavari north) and Dux Publius Arruntius Celer (the Imperial south), equal by treaty
Title
Reiks of Mavaholm, chosen by the Thing; Dux of Mavelon, vir illustris, appointed by the Dominus Militum
Population
c. 75,000 registered; nearer 100,000 in sailing season with crews and foreigners
Built on
A caldera port: cliff terraces, cave-houses and villas above a flooded crater, cut in two by a gate
Patron
Vulcan and Neptune in the south; the Mavari keep their own sea-father and ship-mother at the Thingstead
Trouble
A wartime treaty in a peacetime port: fewer hulls, idle crews, and two halves that remember the revolt differently

Faith: The temples, shrines and cults of this city

The city

A ring of cliffs four hundred feet high around a crater the sea broke into long before anyone kept records. The ring is broken in two places: the Race, a narrow channel where the tide pours in and out of the caldera twice a day, and the Mouth, the wide southern gap the warships use. Mavelon is built on the inside of the ring, white-and-ochre terraces stepping down the pumice to the water, cave-houses cut into the softer layers, switchback stairs worn into troughs, and colonnaded villas wherever the rock is good enough to hold a column.

The natives call the island Mavaholm. Invictian clerks wrote it down as Mavelon three centuries ago and never corrected it. The Mavari still live on the north side of the crescent, round their own harbour; the Imperium built the south side, its villas, its navy and its arsenal. A fortified gate across the narrowest neck of the cliff-city divides the two, and it opens only when two keys are turned in it at once.

It is not handsome in the way Aeterna is, and does not try. Its pride is its ships and its bridges, eleven of them spanning the ravines that cut the terraces, each kept by a guild that carves its mark on the parapet. Its haze is the arsenal's: forges and tide-mills along the inner shore under smoke that never quite clears, and outside the arsenal outfall the caldera water runs discoloured for a mile, which the city regards as evidence of prosperity.

Economy. Hulls, iron and trade. Mavelon builds and repairs the Imperium's warships, turns out the structural ironwork that holds the Imperium together, fittings, clamps, tools and the frames the Emberforge Collective sends to the aqueduct works, and lands more foreign cargo than every other Invictian port combined. Interior iron comes down the Via Ferraria to the Iron Landing on the mainland and crosses the strait by barge; ore comes increasingly from the Duneforged Citadel's Dune Mines by long-haul contract with the Caravan of the Gilded Horizon. Its customers are guilds and the state, so the debasement has hurt it less than the capital. Merchants from the Farshore Realms beyond Asetheria land here and nowhere else, then carry their goods inland to be registered at Romulo.

Military. An arsenal city, which makes it strategically vital and politically exposed. The garrison is small; the capacity to equip one is not. Two Legates have placed standing orders that far exceed their establishments' needs, paid promptly in good coin, which the city has accepted without asking questions and with a fairly clear idea of the answers. The Ironclad Legion recruits here heavily. So, more quietly, do the Crimson Warlords. And the fleet that used to need ten thousand Mavari oarsmen now needs four.

Way of life. Guild-run in the south, clan-run in the north, and work-proud on both sides. A master shipwright outranks a landowner socially, which visiting patricians find incomprehensible. The standing joke still holds: Aeterna is beautiful because Mavelon makes the nails. Festivals: the Bridge Walk, when each guild crosses its bridge and recuts its mark (a bridge whose guild has failed is walked in silence); the Quenching at midwinter, when every forge quenches at once and the caldera is said to steam, and does not, quite; the Apprentice's Piece, the yearly judging of first works, four centuries of which hang in the guild halls; and the two the Mavari added, the Midsummer Thing and the Keel-Silver.

New lore

The conquest. Some two hundred and forty years ago, in one of the war's long sea phases, the Imperium needed a harbour Hellenorian fleets could not reach. Mavaholm's caldera was perfect and the Mavari would not sell it. A fleet under Praefectus Classis Quintus Opimius Rufus forced the Mouth, burned the Mavari longship sheds and took the island in a summer. The Imperium built the south harbour, the slips and the villas, pushed the clans onto the north rim, and filled its galleys with Mavari rowers by levy.

The revolt. Ninety-one years ago, on the night now called the Burning of the Slips, the Mavari crews of the home fleet mutinied together, fired the warship slips, seized the north harbour and the neck of the city, and sent word that unless terms were offered the caldera would be handed to the Hellenorian fleet then three days off the coast. The Imperium, losing a war elsewhere, could not spare the ships to retake it.

The Oath at the Gate. The treaty that followed, sworn before the Oathbound Sanctum and on Mavari spear-rings, made the Reiks and the Dux equals in Mavelon. Each holds one of the two keys to the Gate. Disputes between the halves go to the Gate Court, which sits in the gatehouse with one judge from each side. Mavari serve the fleet as paid freemen, never as levied oarsmen. The north harbour is Mavari and its fish untaxed. And the arsenal pays the Thing a tithe of silver on every hull launched, the keel-silver. The Imperium signed it as a wartime expedient. Ninety years have made it sacred, and five years of peace have made it inconvenient.

How the halves live. Better than either admits. Warships sail with Invictian masters and Mavari steersmen, and the mixed crews drink together and fight together and occasionally fight each other. Intermarriage is common below the rank where it matters and, since the Gate Marriage eight years ago, at the very top: the Dux's son married the Reiks's daughter, and their small son is called Aulus by one grandfather and Audwin by the other. Mavari children learn Invictian on the slips; south-side boys learn Mavari curses on the same slips. Both halves walk the Bridge Walk.

The scuffles. They are a tradition with a calendar. Festival nights end in the Gate Fights, ritual brawls on the neck that the Vigiles of the south and the Thing's spear-wardens break up by agreement at the third hour. Worse incidents have their own names. The Nine Days, thirty years ago, when the Reiks of the day refused his key and the Gate stayed shut until the south ran out of fish. The Lictor's Axe, when a Dux's attendant's ceremonial axe went into the caldera and a Mavari went in after it, or after him. And now the Skelding feud, live since the spring, when a Skelding caulker died under a hull in the Sentia yard and the Imperium paid a fine to its treasury instead of a man-price to his kin.

Since the Treaty. The fleet is laying up hulls. Fewer launches mean less keel-silver, idle Mavari crews and empty slips. The Council of Legates has begun asking whether a wartime oath binds in peace. The Skeldings have begun asking the same thing from the other side. The Farshore merchants, meanwhile, have never been busier.

Districts

The Gate The Doorstead · the neck of the city

Fortress, court and border · judges, key-wardens, smugglers · wet stone and lamp smoke

A double gatehouse of black basalt across the narrowest point of the crescent, with a tower at each end: the Dux's key is kept in the south tower, the Reiks's in the north, and the bronze leaves open only when both are turned. The Gate Court sits in the hall above the arch, an Imperial judge and a Mavari doomsman side by side, and it hears everything that crosses the halves: debts, brawls, marriages, wreck-rights. The tunnels under the neck are older than the Gate and nobody has formally admitted they exist.

Ties: the Hrodnings; gens Arruntia; the Oathbound Sanctum; Law (Invicta).

The North Harbour The Mavari harbour · north side

Longships, fish and boatyards · Mavari crews and families · tar, herring and wet wool

The old harbour, inside the Race, where the clans beached their longships before the Imperium came and still do. Timber boat-sheds run up the shingle, the fish market opens at the turn of the tide, and the Mavari yards build fast clinker hulls the navy buys as dispatch boats and will not admit it copies. No customs post: the fish are untaxed by treaty. Idle crews sit on upturned boats and watch the south harbour's slips stand empty.

Ties: the Skeldings; the Race's tide-mills; the Hollows above.

The Hollows and the Thingstead Cave-houses · north rim

Clan homes and the assembly field · Mavari households · peat smoke, sheep and pumice dust

Cave-houses cut into the pale pumice of the north cliffs, whitewashed fronts and dark interiors, rising in rows to the rim. At the top, on the only flat ground on the north side, is the Thingstead: a ring of standing stones where the free spear-bearers meet at midsummer to make law, choose a Reiks when one dies, and hear the Lawspeaker recite the Oath at the Gate from memory. The Reiks's hall stands beside it, a long roof of ship-timber turned keel-up.

Ties: the Hrodnings; the Skeldings.

The South Harbour and the Farshore Quays Imperial harbour · south side

Navy, slips and foreign trade · sailors, customs clerks, factors from beyond Asetheria · pitch, pepper and cedar

Behind the Mouth, the Imperium's harbour: the navy anchorage, the covered warship slips cut into the cliff foot, and along the eastern mole the Farshore Quays, where ships from beyond Asetheria tie up. Tyrsan pilots in blue, Qart-Hadethi factors with their tin and purple, grain hulls from Khemaret, Sabaian sewn-plank ships smelling of myrrh, Maurashi pepper boats in on the monsoon, Pretannic tin-traders with hunting dogs. The Aurum Pact's isolation sheds stand at the mole's end; nothing lands without its certificate. Seric envoys are rare enough to be treated as omens, and the Ixtali have come twice in living memory.

Ties: House Sentia; the Abyssal Tideguard; the Aurum Pact; Romulo, where every Farshore cargo is registered.

The Mill Banks of Mavelon Existing · Naval arsenal · inner shore

Forges, ropewalks and tide-mills · smiths, ropers, arsenal hands · coal smoke, hot iron and hemp

Along the inner caldera shore run the forge-and-ropewalk terraces that make Mavelon the Imperium's arsenal: smoke, hammering, and a haze that never lifts off the water. Tide-mills in the Race drive the trip-hammers and bellows; ropewalks a quarter-mile long twist anchor cable on the terraces above. Below the outfall the caldera runs discoloured for a mile, which the city regards as evidence of prosperity. At midwinter, on the Quenching, every forge quenches at the same moment. The guild halls on the banks keep four centuries of apprentices' first pieces.

Ties: House Demetria; the Emberforge Collective; the Via Ferraria iron; Duneforged ore.

The High Crescent Villa terraces · south rim

Villas, palace and baths · nobles, admirals, rich merchants · jasmine, sulphur and whitewash

The south rim's upper terraces, white-and-ochre colonnaded villas stepping down the cliff with a view straight across the caldera at the Mavari caves. The Dux's palace, the Praetorium, sits at the summit beside a small forum ringed with guild halls rather than temples, and a basilica where most cases are guild disputes. The Baths of Mavelon are fed by the volcano's own hot springs and open before dawn for the forge shifts. Vulcan's temple faces Neptune's across the forum, and the priesthoods do not get on.

Ties: gens Arruntia; House Sentia; the Mithril Reserve branch.

The Ravines and the Eleven Bridges Guild quarter · both sides

Bridges, workshops and glass-cellars · guildsmen of both halves · dust, chisel-ring and silence

Eleven gorges cut the cliff-city from rim to water, and over each a bridge older than it looks, kept by a guild that carves its mark on the parapet; three of them cross wholly on the north side and are kept by Mavari guilds, which the Bridge Walk accepts without comment. Under the ravine walls lie the Glass-Stone Cellars, where clear volcanic glass and mica are split into window-panes with wooden wedges. The cellars are silent by custom, because a shout can crack a sheet end to end, and the splitters speak a sign-language of their own.

Ties: the guilds; the Gate; the Bridge Walk.

The Outer Flank Dyers' Fields and the Garrison · outside the ring

Fields, vats and a legion camp · dyers, soldiers, farm families · madder, wet ash and horse

The island's outer slope runs gently down to the open sea, and its ash soil is good. The Dyers' Fields lie in long alternate strips of red madder and yellow weld, harvested by families whose hands are stained for life; the guild wears the colour like a badge and hates Tyrsan purple with a passion. Below them, outside the city's sacred line, stands the Mavelon Garrison on the standard plan, small and conscious that it guards the means to arm a hundred legions.

Ties: the dyers' guild; the Farshore purple trade; Military (Invicta).

Rule

Two equals. Reiks Ansvald of the Hrodnings rules the north side and the Mavari wherever they are: chosen for life by the Thing, bound by its law, judged by it if he breaks the Oath. His deputy is the Lawspeaker, Gisla Thurwinsdottir, who recites the law at the Thing and can stop a Reiks mid-sentence by doing so. Dux Publius Arruntius Celer rules the south side and the Imperium's property everywhere, appointed by the Dominus Militum and removable by him at a stroke. His deputy for the arsenal is the Praefectus Fabrum, Titus Gellius Naso; the fleet itself answers to the Praefectus Classis, Servius Ancharius Nepos, who reports to Aeterna and not to the Dux, which both men resent.

Neither ruler can act alone on anything that crosses the halves. The Gate needs both keys; the Gate Court, presided over by the Imperial iudex Quintus Fadius Rufinus and the doomsman Odo Halfhand, needs both judges to agree, and when they do not, the case goes back to the two rulers, who must settle it together within nine days or the Gate stays shut. Who checks them: the Thing checks the Reiks, the Dominus Militum and the two Legates buying iron check the Dux, the guilds own the bridges and the apprenticeships, and the keel-silver means the arsenal's paymasters can starve the north whenever the navy stops building.

Houses and families

The Hrodnings Mavari clan · house of the Reiks

Crest: a black keel on a white wave · Motto: "We row for no one" · Seat: the keel-roofed hall at the Thingstead

Shipwrights and steersmen, the clan that led the Burning of the Slips and swore the Oath at the Gate. They hold the most ship-shares in the north harbour and most of the votes at the Thing, and they have staked everything on the treaty working: mixed crews, the Gate Court, the marriage.

  • Reiks Ansvald — fifty-two, a shipwright's scarred hands and a slow voice; turns his key every morning himself and has never once refused it.
  • Fridugund, his wife — holds the clan's ship-shares and the keel-silver accounts, and knows to the coin how long the north can live without a launch.
  • Ragnwulf Ansvaldson, the heir — twenty-six, steersman of a quinquereme, hot-tempered, and the best fighter at the Gate Fights two years running.
  • Hildegund Ansvaldsdottir — married to the Dux's son in the Gate Marriage; mother of the boy both halves claim.

Ties: gens Arruntia by marriage; feud-wary of the Skeldings.

The Skeldings Mavari clan · the hard men of the Thing

Crest: a broken oar crossed with a spear · Motto: "Remember the slips" · Seat: the deepest cave-rows of the Hollows

Caulkers, fishermen and the clan that lost most in the conquest and least in the treaty's favour. They never liked the Oath and have always kept it. A Skelding died under a hull in the Sentia yard this spring; the Imperium paid its fine to the treasury, not the man-price to the family, and the clan has declared a feud the Gate Court has no form for.

  • Eldest Brandulf Skelding — sixty-eight; speaks at every Thing against the Gate Marriage and has a granddaughter married south himself.
  • Hunwald Skelding, brother of the dead caulker — wants the man-price or Marcus Sentius Lupus's son.

Ties: House Sentia (feud); the Thing.

gens Arruntia Imperial · house of the Dux

Crest: a bronze ram on a warship's prow · Motto: "Per undas" (Through the waves) · Seat: the Praetorium on the High Crescent

A naval family of the second rank, which is to say competent. Three Arruntii have commanded squadrons out of Mavelon; this is the first to hold the Dux's chair, and he has spent eleven years making the treaty work because he served on mixed crews as a boy.

  • Dux Publius Arruntius Celer — sixty-one, ex-trierarch, speaks passable Mavari; knows his appointment is up for review and that the Council of Legates has a candidate.
  • Licinia Paulla, his wife — runs the Praetorium and the south side's charities, and sits with Fridugund at the Bridge Walk by long custom.
  • Gaius Arruntius Celer, their son — trierarch of the quinquereme Fides, husband of Hildegund, father of Aulus-or-Audwin.

Ties: the Hrodnings; gens Valeria, who appointed him.

House Demetria Emberforge masters · Hellenorian-descended

Crest: a lame smith's hammer on grey · Motto: "Opus loquitur" (The work speaks) · Seat: the great forge-hall on the Mill Banks

Hellenorian-descended ironmasters with Invictian citizenship four generations deep, masters of the Emberforge Collective in Mavelon. They make the arsenal's structural iron and the aqueduct frames, are paid late for all of it, and keep cousins in Corinth.

  • Master Demetrius Glaukos, head — sixty; a forge-scarred forearm and an exact memory for every insult the Imperium has paid his family.
  • Theodora Demetria, his daughter — writes the house's letters in two languages and handles the Corinthian accounts herself.

Ties: the Emberforge Collective; Corinth; the Mill Banks.

House Sentia Equestrian · shipbuilders and quay-holders

Crest: a gold anchor in a laurel · Motto: "Navigare necesse" (Sailing is necessary) · Seat: a villa on the High Crescent over its own yard

The largest private shipyard in the south harbour and the concession for the Farshore Quays' warehouses. The Sentii build merchant hulls for anyone and warships when the state pays, and they have married Mavari more than any south-side house, which has not saved them from the Skelding feud.

  • Marcus Sentius Lupus, head — paid the fine, refused the man-price on legal advice, and now walks with four Ironclad Legion guards.
  • Decimus Sentius, his son — yard-master; married to a Skelding granddaughter, which makes the feud a family matter in the worst sense.

Ties: the Skeldings; the Farshore Quays.

Notable figures

  • Gisla Thurwinsdottir Lawspeaker of the Thing — can recite the Oath at the Gate and every Gate Court ruling for ninety years; the only person both rulers will let interrupt them.
  • Hallveig Ironhand Dominus Argentar, Mithril Reserve, Mavelon · dwarf — finances Farshore cargoes against Romulo seals, and is the one banker on the island the Mavari trust, because she has never once smiled at them.
  • Servius Ancharius Nepos Praefectus Classis — commands the laid-up fleet; wants to cut the Mavari crews by half and blame the treaty for it.
  • Adonibaal of Tyrsa pilot · Farshore — the best pilot in the Mouth; sells charts of seas no Invictian has sailed, and buys rumours at the same rate.
  • Bomilqar harbour agent of Qart-Hadeth · Farshore — tin, ivory and purple; his republic is the Imperium's oldest sea rival abroad, and he is very polite about it.
  • Odo Halfhand Mavari doomsman of the Gate Court — lost three fingers at the Burning of the Slips as a boy of nine; the oldest man in the city who remembers the revolt.

Connections

  • Aeterna — up the Via Ferraria from the Iron Landing, about six days; the Dominus Militum appoints the Dux and can unappoint him.
  • Duneforged Citadel — south down the Via Ferraria; Dune Mines ore by Gilded Horizon contract.
  • Romulo — every Farshore cargo landed here must be registered and sealed against Romulo's master weights before it can be sold inland.
  • Fucostia and Napplesia — the coastal sea lanes; grain escorts north, retired admirals south.
  • Corinth — three days' sail; cousins, counting-houses and the iron that leaves for it (The Mavelon Contract).
  • Thebesieas — where that iron ends up, as spear-points.
  • Alderpool — charcoal down the old forest road to the Iron Landing.

Mountain city-state · Invictian-aligned · Cloudspine Ridge

Duneforged Citadel

A mining citadel cut in three tiers into the mountain that guards the southern pass: rich in smiths, debt and airships, and ruled by a house whose ore is running thin.

Codex now: (no tagline; the entry is a bare index of sub-tables: Families, Locations, Citadel Cathedral, Forbidden Zone, Military)

Ruler
Duke Roderick Caesar, House Caerthain
Title
Duke (Dux in the chancery), allied to the Imperium, not appointed by it
Population
c. 60,000 within the walls; more in the mine camps
Built on
A mountain cut into Upper, Middle and Lower city above a desert pass
Patron
Vulcan, Juno and Mercury, beside the Titans Anchiale and Hoplodamus
Trouble
Thinning ore, a humming mine, a great debt and an heir who says so

Faith: The temples, shrines and cults of this city

The city

The Duneforged Citadel is a mountain that has been worked from the inside out for five generations. Walls of the mountain's own stone ring three tiers: the Lower City of quarrymen, cisterns and furnaces at the foot; the Middle City of markets, shops and the arena; and the Upper City of palaces, temples and foundries on the plateaus. Above everything rise the fortresses of the Cloudspine Ridge, the Skyward Bastions on their cliffs, and the moorings of the Serathian Fleet's airships. Three times between dawn and dusk the bronze guardian called Talos walks the outer wall on a circuit it has never varied.

House Caerthain, "the Caesars", earned the citadel in the Continental War. Caesar Kaelen Caerthain, the Stormwall, led five hundred against fifty thousand, broke an Acheaorian advance and shattered the pass behind him; Empress-Lady Vaelis Caerthain founded the mountain navy that became the airship fleet. In the war's last decades Duke Roderick held the Ridge again against a coalition, land, sea and sky at once, and broke one more Acheaorian push at the pass. The south calls the Caesars its guardians, and means it.

The citadel lives by ore, smithing and money. The Dune Mines under the eastern slopes feed the Iron Furnaces and the Three Great Smithing Houses; the Mithril Reserve, the continent's bank, was founded here by House Merca and keeps its first vaults under the Vaulted Court. The Citadel Cathedral houses five temples under one roof: the Forge of Vulcan, the Temple of Juno where oaths bind and the coin is assayed, the Vault of Mercury, the Shrine of Anchiale and the Sanctum of Hoplodamus, patron of the trials in the Ju Colliseum. That Titans are honoured beside Invictian gods is a Duneforged peculiarity.

New lore

Peace has been harder than war. The assay reports from the Dune Mines have trended one way for a decade, and now the lower shafts have stopped altogether: deep tremors and a low, continuous hum, and Overseer Tarnak cannot get anyone to go back down. The Duke's answer has been to spend on the Forge of Vulcan and the cathedral rather than admit the problem. His heir, Roland, argues openly for buying land elsewhere while the house still has wealth to move, and several families have quietly begun doing exactly that. The house's war debt to the Mithril Reserve stands; Lady Isolde Merca lives in the Duke's household to guarantee it.

The Great Martial Festival is held at the Ju Colliseum once every five years, and this is the fifth year of peace. Fighters are arriving from all three empires. One of the names on the register is a Mihran, and House Mihran of Acheaoria has never accepted that its heir died honourably at the pass (The Cloudspine Feud).

Districts

The Helm Upper City · palaces and temples
