A wizard may cast whatever he likes in his own house; casting for pay or selling a made item requires a collegium seal ring, and the collegium answers in court for every spell its members sell. The Artisan's Forge licenses item-makers, the Luminous Arcanists license casters, and a dozen smaller collegia (augurs, healers, ward-setters) hold narrow charters. Priests of the state temples cast for the faithful under the pontiffs' rules and do not count as trade.

How it works
  • The tariff. The collegia publish a price list on bronze in the forum at Romulo, the copy that counts. A licensed caster may charge less but never more.
  • The receipt. Every licensed sale gets a wax-sealed receipt naming the spell, the caster and the buyer. The Speculatores collect copies.
  • Items. Magic items sold in the Imperium must carry a collegium mark. Unmarked items are seized on sight, and an unmarked weapon is presumed stolen from a legion.
  • Insurance. The Mithril Reserve insures marked items held on deposit. Odvar Ironhand at Aeterna and Gaia Pomponia Atticilla at Romulo write the policies.
Now

The Prismatic Shroud's glass-sellers' arcade in Romulo sells frozen Nethranan illusions to patricians and Legates' wives: a sunset that does not end, a dead child's laugh. Nikandros Phaos, a Hellenorian factor with an office in the guild square, is the biggest buyer of the glass. None of it carries a collegium mark, and the Speculatores have bought three pieces themselves.

At the table

Tariff of licensed spellcasting: cantrip 10 gp; 1st level 20 gp; 2nd 60 gp; 3rd 180 gp; 4th 400 gp; 5th 900 gp; plus material components. Identify 25 gp; remove curse 200 gp; raise dead 1,250 gp and a pontiff's consent. Unlicensed casting for pay: fine 200 gp or a month in chains. A Nethranan illusion-shard costs 150–2,000 gp in the arcade; each one carried, roll d20 at each long rest, on a 1 the bearer dreams of Eronis and gains no benefit from the rest. Reserve insurance: a tenth of value a year, paid out in full weight silver.

The Academy Seal and the Ship-Wizard New · Hellenoria

Category: Magic · Run by: the Arcane Academy of Hellarchon under Scholarch Kallisto Pyrphoros; the Lexicon Council; Inquisitor Vireon of the Truth-Flame

Overview

Hellenoria lets the market set the price of magic and lets the Academy decide who may join the market. Any mage with an Academy seal may cast for pay in any League agora, and prices are haggled like fish. Uncertified casters are not banned; they are unprotected, which means a client may refuse to pay them and a jury will laugh. Every trireme of the common fleet carries a certified ship-wizard for wind and fire, and every merchantman that can afford it hires one.

How it works
  • The seal. 100 gp and an examination (Arcana DC 15) at Hellarchon. It opens temple libraries and lodging with a city's proxenos.
  • The Lexicon stamp. A spellbook copied for sale must bear the Lexicon Council's stamp: 10 gp per spell level copied, a month's wait, and one spell may be struck.
  • The wind-trade. Wind is sold by the knot-cord at Corinth. Ixion Keraunios sells the best and does not hold a seal.
  • Hellenic fire. A state secret; selling it, or anything that looks like it, is treason.
Now

Mycairan bronze is turning up in Corinth's counting-houses: spearheads and arrowheads that strike as magic, out of the old workings under the silver deme and the ruin at Mycarion. The Academy wants it catalogued, the shipowners want it sold, and the tyrants are buying it for their bodyguards. Bergthor Ironhand, Dominus Argentar at Thebesieas, has refused to insure a single piece.

At the table

Market price of a certified spell: roll 1d6+7 × 10 per cent of the Invictian tariff (that is, 80 to 130 per cent), and haggle from there (Persuasion DC 12 takes a tenth off). A ship-wizard for a voyage: 5 drachmas a day plus a share of the cargo. Mycairan bronze in Corinth: spearhead 30 gp legally, 120 gp to a tyrant's agent; arrowheads 10 gp each. Each bronze weapon used, roll d6 per fight: on a 1 its next miss strikes the creature nearest the target. Owning an unstamped spellbook is not a crime, but it is evidence.

The Temple Licence and the Bazaar of Lamps New · Acheaoria

Category: Magic · Run by: the Magi, who license casters by temple; the arashshara, who license stalls; the Vaults of Equilibrium, who lend against magic; the Mithril Reserve at its branches

Overview

In Acheaoria a caster is licensed by a fire-temple, not by a school, because the question the law asks is not "Is he competent?" but "Is he pure?". A licensed caster pays the temple a seasonal purification and may then sell his services in any bazaar of the satrapy. Magic items are sold in licensed stalls under the arashshara, weighed and stamped, and the oldest market for them is the Bazaar of Lamps at Atarabad, where the stall-keepers keep a lamp burning to show the Magi they have nothing to hide.

How it works
  • Purity. Spells touching fire, earth or water impurely (a necromancer's rite, a fire-mage burning a corpse) require a Magus's leave and a purification of 25 gp.
  • The stall licence. An arashshara signs for every magic-item stall; she fixes the weights and takes a twentieth.
  • Royal reserve. War-magic and anything touching the Immortals belongs to the throne. Magus Rashnu-Vahram buys first and does not haggle.
  • Credit. The Vaults of Equilibrium lend against magic items left as pledges at a fifth a year, and keep what is not redeemed.
Now

Satraps who withhold tribute are buying war-magic without telling the Magi. Nethranan glass comes east from Zandar Isle into the Bazaar of Lamps, where the Enchanted Muse's dream-readers buy it to hunt Vesperine Ilaro. The Mithril Reserve's branches insure magic items deposited in their vaults, and the satraps use the policy to move treasure out of reach of the King.

At the table

Spellcasting in a bazaar: the Invictian tariff plus a tenth, plus 25 gp purification for any spell of fire or death. Healing by a fire-temple is free to the faithful who give a day of service. Nethranan glass in Atarabad: 200–3,000 gp, and the seller wants to know who the buyer dreams of. A Reserve insurance policy on a deposited item: a tenth of value a year; claims require the item's ward-signature, which the Arcanist-Securitas reads on DC 15 Arcana. A false claim found out: the claimant's name is posted in every branch on the continent.

Part VIII

Wilds, Regions and Ruins

The land between the cities: what lives there, what grows there, and what was left behind.

Between the roads

The three empires draw their maps from the road outward, and the maps go pale where the roads stop. This part covers the pale places: twenty-two wilds that no milestone reaches, from the Klynin springs that water Aeterna to the black notches of the Zaruk'thal Spine, and the ruins of the two Old Empires that came before. Each entry gives who claims the ground and who actually holds it, how long it takes to cross and how hard (the Survival DC for a day's navigation without a guide), what lives there, what can be carried out and sold, and who you will meet doing it.

Five years of peace have changed the wilds more than fifteen centuries of war. Patrols that once kept the frontier now sit unpaid in garrison towns. Demobilised soldiers squat on spring-land and pasture. Caravans take roads their grandfathers died on. Rifts still open, less often than in the war, and the things that come out of them have learned to wait. Where a wild has a secret, it is in the DM notes; where it has a price, it is in silver at the nearest market.

Creatures link to the bestiary. Travel times assume a party on foot with pack animals; halve them for light horse on open ground, double them in bad weather or without a guide.

Wild · Imperium Invicta · Mountain range

Klynin Mountain Range

Low, cold limestone hills that hold the capital's water, surveyed spring by spring and policed harder by the villages than by the law.

Codex now: The spring-bearing highlands that water the Imperium's capital — quiet, cold, and jealously surveyed.

Claimed by
Imperium Invicta: the water office (cura aquarum) of Aeterna
Terrain
Wooded limestone hills, gorges, springs, copper and calamine workings
Travel
3 days to cross · Survival DC 12 (DC 15 off the survey tracks)
Danger
Moderate (CR 1–5)
Trouble
Unpaid veterans tapping springs the law says belong to the capital

The land

Not high, not dramatic, and the most strategically valuable ground in the Imperium. The Klynin holds the springs; the springs feed the Aqua Aeterna; the aqueduct carries the water sixty miles to Aeterna. Every significant spring is measured, named, cut with a boundary stone and assigned in law to the water office. Tapping one without a licence is theft from the capital, and the penalty, unrevised in four hundred years, is still startling: the offender is sewn into the pipe he cut, figuratively in recent centuries and literally in the older ones.

The water comes out of the rock very cold, very clear and already moving. The engineers say the mountain is hollow with it. The villages say something lives in the hollow, that the water is clean because it is being kept clean, and that this is a courtesy rather than a property of limestone. Both agree on the practical point: nothing goes into the springs. The villages enforce it better than the office does.

New lore

Peace has been hard on the hills. Demobilised legionaries were promised land; the only unclaimed land near the capital is the Klynin, and all of its water is spoken for. Veteran squatters now farm the high meadows and dig illegal channels to their plots. The water office fines them in coin that is being debased, so the fines are paid cheerfully and the channels stay. The spring-wardens, hereditary families of the hill villages, have started blocking channels themselves, at night, with stones and occasionally with veterans.

Each spring has a name and a feast day. On the Fontinalia the villages throw garlands, never coins, into the basins, and the water office sends a junior clerk to count the garlands and record that nothing else went in.

Sites

The Headsprings New · spring basins

Sacred and surveyed · spring-wardens, water-office clerks · wet stone and moss

Seven walled basins where the Aqua Aeterna draws its first water, each with a bronze boundary plate and a warden's hut. The intake channel is grated, locked and inspected monthly. The grates are always clean on inspection day. The wardens will not say who cleans them the other twenty-nine, and the clerks have learned not to ask while standing on the slippery steps.

Ties: the Aqua Aeterna; Aeterna's water office; water systems.

The Calamine Diggings Existing · mine

Pale pits · brass-makers' agents · bitter white dust

Pale pits in the hills where brass-makers buy the stone that turns copper to gold, and a bitter salt crusts the walls. The diggers work under a water-office licence that forbids washing ore within a mile of a spring, so the ore is carried downhill dry, on mules, at twice the cost. Smugglers wash it in the springs anyway and sell it cheaper in the capital's foundries.

Ties: brass foundries of Aeterna; the coin Assay; Emberforge Collective.

The Green Gallery Existing · copper mine

Weeping green walls · paint-sellers, bead-makers · wet copper

A copper working in the foothills whose walls weep green, where miners cut malachite for paint and beads. The best seams run toward the hollow, and the miners stop where the rock begins to sound like a drum. The foreman keeps a list of men who did not stop. It is short and he is proud of that.

Ties: painters' guilds of the capital; the hollow.

Veterans' Meadow New · squatter settlement

Illegal and orderly · ex-legionaries, their families · woodsmoke and new-turned turf

Two hundred former legionaries of a disbanded legion have laid out a marching camp in the high grass, ditch and all, and farm inside it. Their channel to the Fons Caeruleus is the largest illegal tap in the range. They call their headman "Centurion" and pay no tax, on the grounds that the Imperium owes them four years' pay.

Ties: Watchers of the Eternal Rest (pension arrears); Crimson Warlords; military.

What lives here

  • Water elemental — the thing in the hollow; never seen above ground, only felt as a current where there should be none.
  • Hill giant — a family of three in the eastern gorges who trade with the villages in sheep and silence.
  • Black bear and brown bear — common in the beech woods, bold at the beehives.
  • Werebear — at least one spring-warden; the villages consider this a qualification.
  • Bugbear — a clan in the old copper adits that the water office officially does not know about.
  • Wolf — Plateau Wolves, grey and long-legged, follow the veterans' sheep.
  • Giant goat — on the limestone crags above the springs.

What can be gathered

  • Calamine — the Diggings; brass-makers pay 2 sp a basket.
  • Malachite — the Green Gallery; ground for green paint, 5 gp a pound for bead-grade.
  • Road basalt — the eastern quarries; paving for the Via Ferraria.
  • Balm of the Hill Country — a resinous herb on sunny slopes; dressings for wounds.
  • Witch's Rue — shaded gullies; village charms and the water office's rat poison.
  • Scarlet-grain — scale insects on the kermes oak; red dye, sold by the ounce.

Who goes there

  • Procurator Aquarum Lucius Sentius Varo head of the water office in the hills — wants the veterans gone without a riot; has four clerks and no soldiers.
  • Old Fonteia chief spring-warden of the Headsprings — speaks for the villages, and for something else when she is tired.
  • "Centurion" Gaius Pullo headman of Veterans' Meadow — wants the land deeded or the pay delivered; will settle for either, will fight for neither yet.
  • Verdant Sentinel Order Diana's knights — patrol the sacred springs and quietly side with the wardens.
  • Travellers from Nemibano and Falecosa, a day or two away in the hills.

Wild · Imperium Invicta · Plains

Latium Plains

The Imperium's grain and its heartland, fat and orderly for a hundred miles, with one field in it that the wind still bows to.

Codex now: “The wind still bows when it passes here. Something greater once stood upon this soil… and something older made it kneel.”

Claimed by
Imperium Invicta: the capital province of Aeterna
Terrain
Rolling grainland, chalk downs, lime kilns, coastal pine, one crater
Travel
4 days to cross by road · Survival DC 10 (DC 18 inside Praetor's Fall)
Danger
Low on the roads, Deadly at the Fall (CR 1–8)
Trouble
Veterans' land claims and a censured crater that is getting bigger at night

The land

The plains around Aeterna and Romulo are the Imperium's own farm: barley for the legions, wheat for the Annona, flint from the chalk, lime from the kilns, pine nuts from the coast. The roads are straight, the milestones are honest and the farms are worked by tenants of senators who have never seen them.

East of Campania Veta, past vineyards too well tended to be natural and orchards whose fruit never rots, the ground dips for nearly a mile into a bowl too symmetrical to be natural. The locals call it Praetor's Fall. Scribe Pellion Meraquas of the Aeterna Lexicon documented it under Imperial Censure Tier II; access to the record requires a Ciphered Seal of Red Marble. The wind inside circles an absent drain. Footprints vanish, or deepen into grave-shapes. At its heart stands an obsidian pillar twelve feet tall, smooth and warm, called the Witness. The Empire denies all anomalies, reassigned the nearby legion detachment and moved the road.

New lore

The peace sent the legions home, and the legions came home to the plains. Every estate now has veterans at the gate asking for the land they were promised, and every senator has a lawyer explaining why it must be some other estate. Two farms have been burned this year. The Annona barges still sail, lighter each quarter.

Pilgrims of a fringe sect walk to the Fall at the equinoxes, believing it a place of rebirth. More come every year since the treaty, many of them old soldiers. Most return broken. The ones who do not return are not looked for, because looking would mean admitting the Fall exists.

Sites

Praetor's Fall Existing · censured battlefield

Silent, warm, spiralling wind · pilgrims, a forbidden scholar or two · ozone and hot stone

The field that knelt. Theories: a heretic praetor, Lurentius Varro, who tried to make himself Imperator-Aeternum and was swallowed with his army (their banners were recovered half-buried in obsidian dust); a titan asleep beneath, the slope the curve of its back; hollow ground over ruins older than the Imperium. Surveyor Valcis Grane found the measurements doubled by night. Archivist Doria Vem saw herself kneeling at an altar in the Witness and vanished three days later; her sandals were found full of ash.

Ties: the Aeterna Lexicon; Aeterna; the Witness.

The Rye-Ghost Fields Existing · grain district

Gold and black · tenant farmers, Annona factors · bread and something sour

The barley here feeds the legions; the black-eared rye feeds the dreams of the villages. Ergot in a wet year sends whole hamlets dancing and seeing the dead. The Golden Harvest Covenant buys the clean grain and leaves the black, which the poor bake anyway because it is free.

Ties: Golden Harvest Covenant; the Annona.

The Chalk Downs Existing · flint quarry

White hills · knappers' families · chalk dust and sparks

Rolling white hills where black flint lies in the chalk like plums in a pudding. The knappers have worked here since before the empires and still sell strike-a-lights and threshing-sledge teeth by the thousand. They regard metal as a fashion.

Ties: farms of the plains; Romulo's markets.

Lime-Burners' Hollow Existing · kilns

Smoky, hot · kilnmen, builders' agents · burned stone

Kilns burn day and night, and builders come for lime and the grey volcanic sand that sets under water. Every concrete harbour wall in the Imperium began here. Since the peace the order books have halved, and the kilnmen have started burning cheaper stone. Somebody's harbour will notice in ten years.

Ties: Fucostia's moles; Mavelon's arsenal.

The Umbrella Pines Existing · coastal wood

Shaded, resinous · pilgrims, lovers, nut-gatherers · pine and salt

A coastal wood of flat-topped pines where pilgrims rest, lovers meet and the pine-nut gatherers climb with hooks. The Via Litoranea runs through its edge. The wood is the one place on the plains where nobody asks whose land it is.

Ties: the Via Litoranea; Napplesia.

What lives here

  • The Strix — the night-bird of the farm tales; a real one hunts the eastern villages near the Fall.
  • Werewolf — veterans bitten on frontier campaigns, home now and hiding it.
  • Wolf — Plateau Wolves along the downs in winter.
  • Ankheg — in the deep grain soils; ploughs turn them up in spring.
  • Cockatrice — farmyard terror, hatched in dung heaps by bad luck and worse hens.
  • Ghoul — on old battlefields of the civil wars, under the vines.
  • Shadow — the long shadows that leave Praetor's Fall with visitors and do not go back.

What can be gathered

  • Black flint — the Chalk Downs; 1 cp a strike-a-light.
  • Quicklime and pozzolana — Lime-Burners' Hollow; the Imperium's concrete.
  • Tufa stone — soft building stone from the plain's quarries.
  • Rye-ghost — ergot on the black rye; physicians buy it to hasten births, poisoners for other ends.
  • Judge's Hemlock — field margins; the state's own poison, sale licensed.
  • Umbrella pine nuts — the coast; 2 sp a pound.
  • Obsidian dust — the Fall only; forbidden to collect, sold under the counter as a focus for divination.

Who goes there

  • Scribe Pellion Meraquas Aeterna Lexicon — documented the Fall and has not written a word since.
  • Legatus Decimus Aurelianus Corvus Council of Legates — settles his veterans on the plains by force of personality and occasionally by force.
  • Golden Harvest Covenant Ceres's grain guild — buys the harvest, sets the price, can starve the capital.
  • Celestial Astromancers sky-watchers — time their eclipse charts to the Witness's hum, privately.
  • The pilgrims of the Fall, who call themselves the Kneeling.

Wild · Imperium Invicta · River

River Tiberius

The founding river: highway, sewer and rubbish-pit of the capital, a yellow god who takes his offering before every bridge.

Codex now: The Imperium's founding river — spine of the capital, sewer of the capital, and keeper of everything the capital has thrown away.

Claimed by
Imperium Invicta: the curators of the riverbed and banks
Terrain
Silt river, brick embankments, reed margins, travertine terraces
Travel
2 days by barge Aeterna to Fucostia · Survival DC 11 in flood
Danger
Low to Moderate (CR ⅛–4)
Trouble
A fifth bridge going up without the offering

The land

The river made Aeterna possible and has been paying for it ever since. It carries grain barges up from Fucostia at its mouth and carries everything else back down. It is yellow with silt, floods on no schedule any augur can predict, and runs between brick banks below the capital over a bed nobody has bricked: divers after lost cargo report amphorae, coin, statuary and the occasional weighted sack, layered in the order the Imperium threw them away.

The priesthood holds that the river is a god, owed an offering before any bridge is built. The engineers call this superstition and make the offering anyway. Four bridges were raised without it. None stands. Below the last bend there is a stretch of about two hundred paces where the silt simply stops and the water runs clear. No one drinks from it.

New lore

The Dominus Militum's office has commissioned a fifth bridge, the Pons Concordiae, to celebrate the Great Concord, and the contractor, a patrician house short of money, has quietly cut the offering from the budget. The divers' guild has stopped working near the piers. The Annona barges are fewer and the river's traffic is now as much salvage as grain: since the debasement began, people dive for old coin, which is worth more than new.

Sites

The Jet Strand Existing · shore

Black cliff-foot · beachcombers · wet coal and resin

A black cliff-foot where polished jet and honey-coloured amber wash up after the spring floods. The beachcombers are mostly widows of bargemen and hold the strand by custom older than the curators. Jet mourning-rings from here are sold in the capital at ten times the strand price.

Ties: mourning trade of Aeterna; Cycle of the Eternal Bloom.

The Kingfisher Reach Existing · river reach

Calm green water · fishermen, lovers · reed and mint

A quiet stretch where blue birds dive and, for a week each winter, the weather turns gentle. Bargemen call it the halcyon week and refuse to fight, sue or collect debts during it. Several contracts in the capital fall due on the first day after.

Ties: the halcyon calendar; river shrines.

The Travertine Cuts Existing · quarry

Warm white terraces · quarrymen · sulphur and hot water

Hot springs beside the river lay down stone as fast as the quarrymen cut it. Every great building in the capital wears this travertine. The quarry pays its dues to the river priests as well as the state, a habit nobody has been brave enough to stop.

Ties: builders of Aeterna and Romulo.

The Clear Water New · river stretch

Uncanny and still · nobody, on purpose · nothing at all

Two hundred paces below the last bend where the silt stops. The bed can be seen: clean gravel and, in the middle, a stone threshold with a worn step. Boatmen ship oars and drift through without speaking. Divers who went down have come back with nothing and an urge to return.

Ties: the river god's priesthood.

The Pons Concordiae works New · building site

Busy and nervous · labourers, engineers · wet mortar

Two piers of the new treaty bridge stand in the current. The cofferdams leak at night. Labourers have found river-sacks in the excavations, opened one, and now refuse to dig past dusk.

Ties: the Dominus Militum's office; offices.

What lives here

  • Quipper and swarms — below the sewer outfalls, fat on the capital.
  • Giant pike-eel (use giant constrictor snake) — the bargemen's terror in the deep pools.
  • Crocodile — escaped from arena stock; a breeding colony in the reed margins below the city.
  • Wererat — in the embankment drains, organised as a salvage gang.
  • Drowned dead — the weighted sacks, on the nights the river remembers them.
  • Water elemental — the river god's hand, at the fallen bridges.
  • Giant rat — everywhere the banks are brick.

What can be gathered

  • Jet and amber — the Jet Strand after the floods.
  • Tiburtine stone — the Travertine Cuts.
  • Window-stone — selenite sheets from the gypsum banks upstream; glazing for the rich.
  • Pen-reed and river reed — the margins; the Lexicon's scribes buy by the bundle.
  • River flax — retted in the backwaters; linen.
  • Cooling mint — the banks; physicians' fever draughts.
  • Old coin — the bed; pre-debasement silver fetches a premium at the Mithril Reserve.

Who goes there

  • Abyssal Tideguard Neptune's marine order — hold salvage rights on the lower river and bless the barges.
  • Curator Alveis Rufo curator of the riverbed — wants the bridge built on time and the priests out of his accounts.
  • Mother Tiberina priestess of the river god — has been refused the offering; has stopped arguing, which worries everyone.
  • The Divers' Collegium salvage guild — know the bed's layers like a library.
  • Bargemen from Fucostia.

Wild · Duneforged Citadel (Invictian-aligned) · Mountain range and fortress chain

Cloudspine Ridge

The fortress chain above the Duneforged Citadel where House Caerthain held a coalition of empires and earned its nobility, and still keeps its secrets.

Codex now: The chain of mountain fortresses House Caerthain held against a coalition of empires.

Claimed by
House Caerthain of the Duneforged Citadel
Terrain
High ridges, cedar slopes, crags, a volcanic shoulder, cliff fortresses
Travel
4 days along the ridge road · Survival DC 15 (DC 20 off the road)
Danger
High (CR 2–10)
Trouble
The Cloudspine Feud: Mihran blood-hunters on the passes

The land

A chain of mountain fortresses running above the Duneforged Citadel, and the ground on which House Caerthain earned its nobility during the Continental War. They held it against a coalition of invading empires, land, sea and sky-borne forces at once, and did not yield the line. Kaelen Caerthain's stand at the pass broke an Acheaorian advance. The Skyward Bastions that still watch from the cliffs date from that defence. The south calls the Caerthains its guardians because of this ridge.

New lore

The ridge is quieter and no safer. Under the treaty the pass is open to trade, and Acheaorian caravans now come up the road their grandfathers died on. Among them, every season, ride men of House Mihran, whose heir fell at Kaelen's stand. The blood-feud is not covered by the treaty because neither house signed it in its own name. The Adamantine Line under Commander Daud escorts every caravan, and the escort is half honour guard, half watch. Ridge villages sell cedar and goat cheese to both sides and keep two sets of saints' days.

Sites

The Skyward Bastions Existing · fortresses

Armoured, cold, drifting · Adamantine Line garrisons · wind and lamp oil

Armoured watch-fortresses mounted on the cliffs and repositioned by levitation crystals, so that an enemy's map of the ridge is wrong within a month. In the war they shifted at night to close gaps. Now two of the nine crystals are failing, and the Duke's artificers cannot cut replacements without a material the house refuses to name.

Ties: the Adamantine Line; the Serathian Fleet; Countess Aurelie Virellarion.

Kaelen's Pass New · pass and memorial

Narrow, windy, sacred · caravans, pilgrims, mourners · cold iron and incense

The pass where Kaelen Caerthain broke the Acheaorian advance. A cairn of shields stands at the top, Invictian and Acheaorian mixed, because the dead were buried where they lay. Caravans pause here by custom. Mihran riders leave red cords on the cairn every year on the day their heir fell; the garrison removes them at dusk, politely.

Ties: House Caerthain; the Cloudspine Feud; Xerastri.

The Cedar Stair Existing · forest

Stepped black-green slopes · carpenters of three empires · resin and sawdust

A stepped slope of mountain cedar where carpenters come for timber that outlasts them. The Duke licenses each tree. The Serathian Fleet's hulls are cut here, which is why the cutting licences are signed by Commander Daud, not by the forester.

Ties: the Serathian Fleet; shipwrights of Mavelon.

The Ibex Crags New · crags

Sheer and loud with wind · goatherds, eagle-catchers · goat and guano

Bare limestone towers where cliff-goats graze ledges no man can reach and giant eagles take the kids. Eagle-catchers lower themselves on ropes to rob the eyries; a trained eagle sells at Duneforged for the price of a house.

Ties: the Ju Colliseum's beast-pens; Duneforged falconers.

Lake Serathal Existing · sacred lake

Forbidden, still, bright · nobody admitted · snow and something sweet

The sacred lake atop the highest peak. The path is closed by the Duke's order and guarded by men who do not discuss what they guard. The lowland story is that the Caerthain dead are laid in its water. The water does not freeze.

Ties: House Caerthain; the Pact.

What lives here

  • Wyvern — the commonest danger above the treeline; they nest in war-ruined towers.
  • Griffon — wild prides, and tamed mounts of the Bastion couriers.
  • Giant goat and giant eagle — the Ibex Crags.
  • Roc — one pair over the Skyward Bastions; the garrison feeds them oxen to keep them friendly.
  • Red dragon and fire giant — the volcanic shoulder east of the ridge.
  • Kobold and goblin clans — in the old siege tunnels.
  • Talos of Duneforged — the bronze guardian, sighted on the ridge wall in bad years.

What can be gathered

  • Mountain cedar — the Cedar Stair; licensed, 50 gp a mast-grade trunk.
  • Mountain spikenard — high meadows; perfume root, worth its weight in silver.
  • Wolf's-bane — shaded scree; arrow poison and werewolf charms.
  • Cliff-goat wool and King's Eagle feathers — the Crags.
  • Old war iron — arrowheads and armour on the passes; the Vulkrim smiths buy it to re-forge.

Who goes there

  • Commander Daud, the Royal Protector the Adamantine Line — holds the ridge and the escort rota.
  • Duke Roderick Caesar House Caerthain — rides the ridge each spring to show the banner.
  • Azata Narsai Mihran House Mihran, caravan factor — trades on the pass and counts the cairn's shields.
  • The Serathian Fleet Caerthain airships — patrol above the Bastions.
  • Champion Spahbed Artabazos Mihran is rumoured to have crossed in merchant dress.

Wild · Free lands (war borderland) · Valley

Briar's Valley

Green pasture sealed inside forty years of thorn that grew after the massacre, and grows inward.

Codex now: A green valley closed by forty years of thornbrake — the hedge grew after the massacre, and it grew inward.

Claimed by
Nobody now; the rim villages pay no one and are asked by no one
Terrain
Sheltered valley, pasture, a stream, a thorn wall twice a man's height
Travel
1 day across, if you get in · Survival DC 14; cutting in, DC 16 Athletics per 10 ft
Danger
Moderate (CR ½–6)
Trouble
A land-hungry Legate wants the pasture opened

The land

Good pasture, sheltered water, gentle slopes, and a wall of thorn around the whole of it thick enough to turn a horse and high enough to hide a man standing on one. The brake is forty years old, and the rim villages can name the year: the valley's own militia was massacred inside it during the last serious campaign of the long war. The thorn came up the following spring, everywhere at once, and has thickened since.

It grows inward. Cut a path from outside and the cut closes from the far side within a season or two, as if the valley were sealing rather than the hedge spreading. Birds go in and out. Smoke has twice been seen. Local opinion is not that something is in there but that something is being kept in, that the arrangement works, and that it would be discourteous to interfere.

New lore

The rim villages hold a Thorn Day each spring on the massacre's anniversary: they lay bread and salt at the hedge and read the names of the militia, a hundred and twelve of them. The list has been read so often that children know it as a counting rhyme. Since the peace, an Invictian survey party has measured the valley for veterans' allotments, and the villages, who lost their own sons inside it, are not pleased.

Sites

The Thorn-Rows Existing · thicket

Choking, rustling · nobody living · crushed green and old iron

The tangle of vines and spiked hedge at the valley's heart, where the thorn grew inward and the plants have learned to hunt. The rows run in straight lines, like ranks, and the gaps between them are exactly a shield's width. Rusted spearheads hang in the canes at head height.

Ties: the massacre; the Militia Stone.

The Militia Stone New · memorial

Mossy, cared-for · rim villagers on Thorn Day · bread and wet stone

A boundary stone outside the hedge where the names are read. Someone inside keeps the inner face clean; the moss stops at the thorn line. A hundred and twelve names are cut on the outer face and a hundred and eleven on the inner.

Ties: the rim villages; Cycle of the Eternal Bloom.

The Smoke Farm New · steading

Seen from the ridge only · unknown · woodsmoke

A roofed farmhouse in the middle of the valley, visible from the rim with a good glass, where smoke was twice seen rising. The fields around it are mown. Nobody living has walked to it.

Ties: the last name on the stone.

What lives here

  • Awakened shrub — the thorn itself, in the Thorn-Rows; it moves to close gaps.
  • Awakened tree — three old oaks at the valley gates.
  • Stirge — Briar-Stirges, thorn-green, nesting in the canes.
  • Skeleton — the militia's dead, standing in their ranks inside the rows.
  • Ghost — the militia's captain, at the Smoke Farm.
  • Dryad — the hedge's keeper, who has not shown herself in forty years.

What can be gathered

  • Briar-hips — the outer hedge; a cure for winter coughs, 1 cp a handful.
  • Thorn-cane — cut outside; walking sticks that never split, 5 sp each, and they are said to point home.
  • Old militia gear — rusted, from the canes; the villages forbid taking it.

Who goes there

  • Mensor Quintus Aelianus Invictian land surveyor — has orders to plot allotments and a crew that will not go near the hedge.
  • Komarch Hesper Drys headwoman of the largest rim village — lost a father inside; will not see the valley opened.
  • Verdant Sentinel Order Diana's knights — one knight lives on the rim and watches the hedge for reasons she keeps to herself.

Wild · Hellenoria · Seas

Aeolus Reach

A twenty-mile wind-strait with the most predictable weather in the known world, except on the two days a season when it is not.

Codex now: The strait where Hellenoria's winds are made — reliable, charted, and answerable to something that does not always answer.

Claimed by
Hellenoria: the common fleet of the League under the Hegemon of Hellarchon
Terrain
Strait between two headlands, sea stacks, black and grey beaches
Travel
1 day to pass under sail · Survival (or vehicles, water) DC 12 with the chart, DC 20 without
Danger
Moderate, Deadly on off-chart days (CR 1–17)
Trouble
Wreckers on the southern cape and a forged wind-chart in circulation

The land

A twenty-mile channel between two headlands through which every wind in the Hellenorian archipelago appears to be issued. Sailors do not say the wind blows through the Reach; they say it is let out of it. The practical effect is predictable weather. A chart kept at Delphara, and copied badly everywhere else, gives the wind for each hour of each day of the sailing season, and it is right often enough that a captain who ignores it is thought not bold but stupid.

It is not right always. Perhaps twice a season the Reach delivers something that is not on the chart, and it is always enormous. On those days the keepers on the headland light no fire, on the grounds that a ship that cannot see the rocks will at least not see them coming. On the northern head stands a shrine where captains leave a knotted cord before passing through. Nobody unties the knots. They come undone.

New lore

The Reach is the Long Lane's choke-point, and peace has tripled its traffic: Invictian grain hulls, Acheaorian spice from the Haulway, Corinth's own triremes. Charts are now forged for profit. A "Delpharan copy" sold in the Corinthian market last spring had the off-chart days moved by a week, and three ships went down on the real ones. The Amphictyony has begun sealing genuine copies with a tripod stamp, which the forgers copied within the month.

Wind-sellers work the headlands: knotted cords that release a fair breeze when untied, one knot per day of sailing. Most are rope. The ones bought from the Wind-Seller of the Reach are not.

Sites

The Wreckers' Beacon Existing · lighthouse

Tall, black, pitch-smoked · keepers, swifts, one sorcerer · burning tar

A black-stone lighthouse on the southern cape with a pitch-burning fire-basket. The keepers say they save ships; the neighbours have seen the light move on stormy nights, and the cove below is generous with cargo. A sailor may ask for a bed in the keeper's house; the keeper asks what the ship carries, which is a reasonable question for a lighthouse. Never-Landing Swifts wheel round the lantern at dusk.

Ties: Ixion Keraunios; the next valley's markets; Corinth.

The Knot Shrine New · shrine

Wind-scoured, rope-hung · captains, wind-sellers · tar and salt

A roofless enclosure on the northern head hung with ten thousand knotted cords. Captains tie one before passing. The cords come undone in their own time, and old pilots read the order of the untying as a forecast. A priestess sweeps the loose cords into the sea at each new moon and will not say to whom she is sending them.

Ties: the Delpharan wind-chart; Delphara.

The Petrel Stacks Existing · sea stacks

Guano-white pillars · birds, harpies, egg-climbers · fish and ammonia

Rock pillars in the strait where storm-birds nest and the water below is thick with ink-fish, purple snail and eel. Egg-climbers work the lower ledges in spring. The upper ledges belong to harpies, who sing the climbers up and do not always let them down.

Ties: purple-dye works of the coast towns.

The Pumice Flats Existing · shore

Grey, light-footed · beach boys, scrub-sellers · sulphur and kelp

A wide grey shore where the sea throws up floating stone, and every boy on the strait knows how to sell it: for scrubbing hulls, smoothing parchment, filing horses' hooves. After an off-chart storm the flats are buried knee-deep, and nobody asks where so much stone came from.

Ties: scriptoria of Hellarchon.

The Torpedo Shallows and Emery Shore Existing · bay and beach

Sandy and black · fishermen, polishers · wet sand

A sandy bay where fishermen step carefully, because the flat grey fish in the sand hit like a hammer; physicians buy them live for headaches. Beyond it, the short black Emery Shore, where the sea grinds hard grey stone to the powder that gem-polishers pay well for.

Ties: Luminastra Alchemists; gem-cutters of Corinth.

What lives here

  • Charybdis of the Reach — the whirlpool, three surges a day, kept on the pilots' second chart.
  • The Keraunic Hydra — arrives with the off-chart storms, twice a season, many-headed and lit by its own lightning.
  • Harpy — the upper Petrel Stacks.
  • Air elemental — loose winds, "let out" without a chart.
  • Storm giant — seen once a generation standing in the strait to the waist.
  • Bronze dragon — an old one sleeps in a sea cave under the northern head and rescues sailors when it feels like it.
  • Merrow — follow wrecks.
  • Giant octopus and reef shark — the stacks' waters.

What can be gathered

  • Pumice — the Flats; a copper a stone, a drachma a sack.
  • Island emery and black flint — Emery Shore; polishers pay 5 sp a pound for fine powder.
  • Lodestone — the northern head; navigators' needles.
  • Purple-snail and ink-fish — the Stacks; dye and ink.
  • Weeping mastic — resin trees on the headlands; chewed, sold, and burned at the Knot Shrine.
  • Charybdis' Tears — salt-glass beads found on bare rock after a surge; prized by water-mages.

Who goes there

  • Ixion Keraunios Wind-Seller of the Reach · storm sorcerer — lives at the Wreckers' Beacon and sells winds in Corinth.
  • Keeper Damokles head keeper of the Beacon — ten years in the job, three new houses in the valley.
  • The pilots' guild of the Reach hereditary families — keep both charts and charge for the second.
  • Abyssal Tideguard Invictian marine order — escort grain hulls and resent having to hire a Hellenorian pilot.
  • Triremes of Nerissa Thalassine, Queen of the Haulway, running fast through on the chart's good hours.

Wild · Hellenoria · Seas

Nereid's Veil

A standing bank of sea-fog off the western coast, steered by ear alone and full of pleasant voices that know your name.

Codex now: The permanent sea-fog off the Hellenorian coast — beautiful, navigable by ear alone, and full of voices that know your name.

Claimed by
Hellenoria: the coastal League ports; in practice the pilot families
Terrain
Fog bank, reefs, islets, a quarry island, sponge shallows
Travel
2 days through with a pilot · Survival DC 18 without (sight useless; Perception by hearing)
Danger
High (CR 1–8)
Trouble
Too few pilots for peacetime traffic, and the voices getting bolder

The land

A bank of fog sits off the western coast and does not move with the wind. It thins and thickens with the season but it does not go and does not travel; ships pass into it as into a room. Inside, sight is worth nothing and hearing everything. Pilots navigate by surf on known rocks, by bells on moorings, and by counting. The skill takes a decade and cannot be written down, which is why the pilot families of the coast towns are wealthy and insular.

Then the voices. They are female, numerous, pleasant, and they use your name. Pilots are trained from childhood to answer nothing. Every League port's standing order is that a helmsman who replies is relieved at once and never goes back in, not as punishment but because those who reply once tend to reply again. Drowned sailors recovered from the Veil are, without exception, smiling.

New lore

Peace brought trade and trade wants pilots, and there are perhaps sixty qualified in the whole coast. Captains now hire half-trained apprentices at half the price. Two have replied. Both ships came out of the fog on the far side in perfect order, every man aboard smiling and none of them able to say what they had agreed to. The pilot families have doubled their fees and closed their schools to outsiders, and the Assembly at Hellarchon is debating whether a pilot's craft can be nationalised.

Sites

The Lamplit Quarries Existing · underground quarry

Wet, glowing · quarrymen, lamp-boys · lamp oil and cold stone

Marble cut underground by lamplight on an island inside the fog, where the stone glows faintly when it is cut. The quarrymen work in silence by rule, so that nobody answers a voice by accident. Lamp-quarried marble is the costliest in the League and is shipped out only with a pilot paid in advance.

Ties: Geolith Artisan Covenant; temples of Hellarchon.

The Sponge Banks Existing · reef

Clear rocky shallows at the fog's edge · free-divers · brine and blood-coral

Clear shallows off the foggy coast where free-divers cut sponge and coral and net the red mullet that die in colours. Divers carry a stone and a knife and go down with wax in their ears, which they consider the most important tool of the three.

Ties: physicians' and bath-house trade.

The Bell Line New · navigation moorings

Invisible, ringing · pilots, bell-wardens · wet bronze

Forty bronze bells on moorings through the fog, each with its own note, laid by the pilot families and re-tuned every spring. Pilots steer from bell to bell, counting strokes. Last season someone added a forty-first bell. Nobody laid it, and it is in tune.

Ties: the pilot families; Emberforge Collective bell-founders.

The Smiling Strand New · beach

Pale sand, quiet · beachcombers, mourners · seaweed

A cove inside the fog's southern edge where the drowned wash up. A priestess of the coast keeps a register of names and buries them facing the land. Families come to identify sons by their teeth, because every face is the same smile.

Ties: Eleusinian Mysteries.

What lives here

  • Merfolk — at the Sponge Banks; they trade with divers and will not enter the deep fog either.
  • Sea hag — a coven on a fog-bound islet, who sell answers to the voices' questions.
  • Merrow — hunt ships whose pilots lose count.
  • Sahuagin — raid the edges in the dark of the moon.
  • Ghost — the smiling drowned, who walk the decks of ships whose helmsman answered.
  • Hunter shark — below the Bell Line.
  • The voices — no stat block; they want an answer, not a fight.

What can be gathered

  • Lamp-quarried marble — the Lamplit Quarries; 40 gp a block before shipping.
  • Island emery — the quarry spoil.
  • Fire-stone — glowing veins in the quarry, cut out and sold to lantern-makers.
  • Blood-coral and sponge — the Banks; coral 10 gp an ounce.
  • Dying mullet — the Banks; served at oligarchs' tables for the show of colours as it dies.
  • Sea-onion — the islets; a rat poison and a heart cure, depending on dose.

Who goes there

  • House Pelagonides eldest pilot family — want the trade but not the competition.
  • Pilot Thaleia Pelagonis master pilot — has heard her dead mother's voice in the fog for six years and never answered.
  • Abyssal Tideguard Invictian marines — want a pilot school opened to Invictians under the treaty.
  • Geolith Artisan Covenant masons — buy the quarry's marble and send their own silent men to cut it.

Wild · Hellenoria · Mountain range

Olympus Mountain Range

The grey wall across Hellenoria's north, seat of the gods above the cloud and the reason no League army has ever held its own border.

Codex now: The high seat of the Hellenorian gods — and the reason no Hellenorian army has ever been able to hold its own northern border.

Claimed by
Hellenoria: three passes held by three rival city-states
Terrain
High limestone, cloud forest, snowfields, three passes, sulphur mines
Travel
3 days by a pass · Survival DC 15; DC 22 above the cloud
Danger
High (CR 2–13)
Trouble
Northfolk raiders through the unwatched pass, and the cloud lying to officers

The land

A wall of grey limestone across the north of Hellenoria, its upper third in cloud for nine months of the year. The Hellenorians place the seat of their gods above that cloud and are uninterested in whether anyone has checked. Several have. Their accounts do not agree, which the priesthood considers proof and the philosophers consider altitude.

Strategically the range is a gift that has ruined its owners. An army can cross only at three passes, and so can Hellenoria, and each pass is held by a different city-state that regards the other two as rivals. The League has never once garrisoned all three at the same time. The cloud does something to sound: orders arrive late, or twice, or in a voice that is nearly the right one. Officers learn to use horns and to distrust anything they hear that they wanted to hear.

New lore

The treaty ended the southern wars and freed nobody's attention for the north. The thaw beyond Olympus has loosed the cold country's peoples and beasts, and Northfolk raiders have twice come through the eastern pass while its garrison city argued with its neighbour about who should pay for the wall. The synedrion voted a common garrison two years ago. The Theoric Fund cannot legally pay for war, so the garrison has been funded as a "festival of watching", with priests, and very few spears.

Sites

The Three Passes New · passes and forts

Cold, contested · garrisons, shepherds, smugglers · snow and goat

The Pass of the Eagle (west), the Long Saddle (centre) and the Thunder Gate (east). Each fort flies its own city's colours and checks the others' couriers. The Thunder Gate is the weakest-held and the most used by raiders and by smugglers, who pay its commander a toll he calls a votive offering.

Ties: Thessalonika; the League synedrion; military.

The Gods' Table Grotto Existing · crystal cave

Shining, high, hushed · pilgrims, shepherds · cold stone and honey

A cave high on the range whose walls are lined with clear crystal, where, shepherds say, the gods once dined. A long flat stone in its centre is set with twelve hollows. Pilgrims leave honey cakes in them. In the morning the cakes are gone and the hollows are clean.

Ties: the priesthood of the twelve; crystal-cutters.

The Yellow Cleft Existing · mine

Sulphur-stained · condemned and desperate miners · rotten eggs

A crack in the high rock where gold-yellow orpiment and blood-red realgar are mined by men who do not expect to be old. The poison-stones go to painters and to the Arcane Academy, which buys more than painting requires and does not explain.

Ties: the Arcane Academy of Hellarchon.

The Cloud Line New · climbers' refuge

Fog-wet hut · summit-seekers, philosophers · wet wool

A stone hut where the cloud begins, the last shelter before the top. Its walls are scratched with the accounts of those who went up. No two agree. The most recent reads "it is a garden"; under it, in another hand, "it is a door".

Ties: the Porticoes of Thessalonika; Krates the Dog, who climbed it and refuses to say.

What lives here

  • Griffon, hippogriff and pegasus — in the cloud; pegasi are said to be the gods' and are never sold openly.
  • Cloud giant — above the cloud, polite to pilgrims, rude to soldiers.
  • Silver dragon — one, who has taken human shape in a shepherd village for forty years.
  • White dragon and ice mephit — the snowfields.
  • Harpy — the passes, mimicking orders.
  • Frost giant and winter wolf — come over from the north with the thaw.
  • Goat and brown bear — the lower slopes.

What can be gathered

  • Orpiment and realgar — the Yellow Cleft; 2 gp an ounce, deadly to process.
  • Brimstone — the Cleft's walls; fumigation and Hellenic-fire rumours.
  • Mountain crystal — the Grotto's outskirts; lenses and scrying spheres, 25 gp a clear fist.
  • Saviour's Sage — the high meadows; a fever tea.
  • Wolf's-bane — the scree.
  • Mountain honey — thyme and pine, the best in the League.

Who goes there

  • Strategos Lykomedes of the Thunder Gate elected frontier general — wants the League to pay; will take the raiders' money until it does.
  • Hearthfire Sanctum Hestia's order — keeps a fire burning in each pass-fort.
  • Krates the Dog Cynic philosopher — came down from the summit and barks at priests.
  • Northfolk raiders and their seers, testing the gate.

Wild · Hellenoria · Mountain range

Oros Mountain Range

The lower, greener range the Hellenorians call simply The Mountain, quarried for eight centuries and hollow in places nobody has mapped.

Codex now: The older, lower range the Hellenorians simply call The Mountain — quarried for eight centuries and hollow in places nobody has mapped.

Claimed by
Hellenoria: hill demes under the League; quarries leased by the Geolith Artisan Covenant
Terrain
Marble faces, olive terraces, scrub, cliffs, old galleries
Travel
2 days to cross · Survival DC 12; DC 17 in the galleries
Danger
Moderate (CR 1–9)
Trouble
Deep-gallery blocks that some temples refuse, and the Covenant digging deeper

The land

The Hellenorians name most things twice, once in poetry and once in the flat old word that came first. Oros is the flat old word: the mountain, what this range was called before anyone put gods on the taller one to the north. It is lower than Olympus, greener and far more useful. Eight centuries of quarrying have taken the marble for every temple in the League out of its western face, and the galleries run further than any surviving plan. Quarry crews still break through into worked chambers that nobody alive cut.

The stone is unusually white and cold and holds a chisel line so cleanly that sculptors say they are not carving but removing what was never meant to be there. Blocks from the deepest galleries are prized, expensive, and quietly refused by some temples.

New lore

Peace means building, and every city in the League wants a victory temple for a war it did not win. The Covenant has opened three new deep galleries to meet orders, and the deep marble now outsells the surface stone. The Heptapylon at Thebesieas returned a shipment last spring with no explanation but a note: "it was looking at us". The Covenant keeps the note in its hall and the price unchanged.

Sites

The Pentelic Terraces Existing · quarry

White-and-gold steps · masons, ox-drovers · stone dust and sweat

The quarry steps that every temple wants and few can afford. The Covenant cuts on its own schedule; the joke in the League is that a temple is finished when the Covenant is, not when the city is. Ox-sledges run blocks down a paved slide to the sea.

Ties: Geolith Artisan Covenant; Hellarchon.

The Deep Galleries New · old workings

Cold, echoing · deep-cutters, gargoyles · wet chalk

Tunnels behind the western face, cut in eight centuries plus an unknown number before. The oldest have square doorways too tall for men and grooves on the floor for sledges no ox could pull. Deep-cutters are paid triple and work in pairs tied by a cord.

Ties: the Covenant; Thebesieas's refused shipment.

Bloodstone Scree Existing · scree

Loose dark green flecked red · stone-pickers · wet iron

A long slope of loose green stone flecked with red where, they say, a hero's blood turned the rock. Soldiers carry a piece against wounds. The pickers sell the reddest stones to the Luminastra Alchemists.

Ties: Luminastra Alchemists.

The Boar Thicket Existing · scrub

Dense, thorny · hunters, heroes · crushed thyme and musk

Hillside scrub where a tusked beast the size of a pony is hunted by would-be heroes, and tortoises carry the shells of the old lyres. The beast has killed four heroes since the treaty. Their families blame the beast; the locals blame the heroes.

Ties: lyre-makers; young eupatrids seeking a name.

Olive Terraces and the Beekeepers' Hall Existing · groves and guildhall

Stone-walled, old · hill families · thyme and oil

Olives older than the League, tended by families who inherit trees by name, and a low lodge where the villages weigh, grade and seal their honey. The thyme smell reaches the road. These are the people who actually live on the Mountain and dislike the quarries' dust on their leaves.

Ties: The Golden Scythe Accord.

The Hellebore Cliffs and Lodestone Shelf Existing · cliff and mine

Wind-blown and bare · physicians, shepherds · sea-salt

Pale cliffs where physicians climb for black hellebore, the cure of madness, and mandrake that shrieks when pulled. Inland, a bare ledge of iron ore that pulls the needle off true, where shepherds will not sleep.

Ties: physicians of Delphara.

What lives here

  • Stone giant — the galleries' old cutters, some say; a family still lives deep.
  • Gargoyle — carved from deep-gallery marble, waking in the temples that bought it.
  • Grimlock — in the unmapped workings.
  • Xorn — eat the bloodstone seams.
  • Roper — hangs as a stalactite in wet galleries.
  • Copper dragon — a joker who leaves riddles chiselled on gallery walls.
  • Giant boar — the beast of the Boar Thicket.
  • Brown bear — Mountain Brown Bears in the oak woods.

What can be gathered

  • Pentelic marble — 30 gp a block; deep-gallery stone 100 gp.
  • Bloodstone and seal jasper — the Scree; amulets and signet stones.
  • Lodestone — the Shelf.
  • Madness-cure hellebore — the Cliffs; 5 gp a root, poison in the wrong dose.
  • Grey olive, juniper, torch-fennel — the terraces and scrub.
  • Thyme honey — sealed at the Beekeepers' Hall.

Who goes there

  • Master Mason Aristeides Lithourgos Geolith Artisan Covenant — opened the new galleries; insists stone is stone.
  • Demarch Melissa of the hill deme honey-wardens' leader — wants the quarry dust stopped.
  • Young eupatrids from Thebesieas and Corinth, hunting the boar for a name.
  • Physicians and Luminastra Alchemists on the cliffs.

Wild · Hellenoria · Plains

Elysian Plains

A warm bowl of green grass where it never rains, where the honoured dead keep pleasant company and travellers lose days and come back content.

Codex now: Grassland where the grass grows in the shape of the wind that blew a week ago, and the dead are said to be pleasant company.

Claimed by
Hellenoria, by piety: no city claims it, all honour it
Terrain
Shallow grass bowl, poppy fields, horse pasture
Travel
3 days across · Survival DC 10 for the route, Wisdom save DC 13 each night or lose a day
Danger
Low, and that is the danger (CR 0–6)
Trouble
Veterans walking in to stay

The land

A shallow bowl of pale grass three days across, warm in every season, where it has not rained in memory and the grass is green anyway. The Hellenorians hold that the honoured dead are kept here, and the plains do little to argue. The grass lies flat in the pattern of some previous day's wind. Travellers report conversations they are certain they had with people they cannot afterwards name, and arrive at the far side rested and a little lighter, in mood and once or twice in memory.

Nothing here is hostile. That is what unsettles the people of the margin, who graze the edge and do not sleep on it. A shepherd who loses a day comes back content. A shepherd who loses a season comes back content too, and that is the problem.

New lore

Since the treaty, old soldiers come. They walk in from every city of the League, and some from the Imperium, carrying the names of comrades they want to speak to once more. Most come out after three days, lighter. A growing number do not come out, and are seen at a distance, sitting in the grass in conversation. The margin villages now keep a register at the edge, and the families of the missing have started to petition the Amphictyony to have the plain closed. The Amphictyony has asked them how.

Sites

The Dreamfields Existing · fields

Red and pink, silent · harvesters in shifts · poppy and warm earth

Poppy and autumn crocus on the plain's edge, where harvesters work in silence and are kept awake by shifts: one watches while two cut, and the watcher shakes anyone who sits down. The poppy goes to physicians across the League. A harvester who sleeps in the field is left one night, by custom, before anyone goes to fetch him.

Ties: Luminastra Alchemists; the Dream Dormitory of Delphara.

The Horse Meadows Existing · pasture

Rolling green · breeders, wolves · horse sweat and grass

A rolling plain where the golden horses, the ones that sweat like blood, are bred, and the wolves keep the herds honest. The breeders swear the foals are sired by something in the deep plain. Acheaorian buyers pay in gold and ask no questions; Invictian buyers ask and pay less.

Ties: Argotiko horse plain; cavalry of three empires.

The Register Stone New · waystation

Quiet, kindly · margin villagers, mourners · bread and lamp oil

A whitewashed hut at the main path into the bowl, where a komarch's clerk writes down who goes in and crosses off who comes out. The book has four hundred uncrossed names since the treaty. Pinned to the door: lists of the dead, posted by people hoping someone inside will pass the message on.

Ties: the Amphictyony of Delphara; Eleusinian Mysteries.

The Ring of Heroes New · stone circle

Central, sunlit · nobody living for long · warm stone

At the bowl's heart, a ring of low stones each carved with a single name, some famous, some forgotten. A new stone appears now and then. The most recent bears the name of a Thebesian officer of the Sacred Band who died in the last war.

Ties: Epameinon Kleitarchos of Thebesieas.

What lives here

  • Ghost — the courteous dead; they talk, they do not harm, they ask you to stay.
  • Pegasus — at the Horse Meadows at dawn.
  • Riding horse — Heavenly Horses, golden and blood-sweating, half-wild.
  • Couatl — glimpsed over the Dreamfields; it guards sleepers from worse dreams.
  • Wolf — Plateau Wolves of the margins.
  • Deer — Hill Fallow Deer, unafraid.
  • The Cerynitian Hind — golden-horned, said to cross the plain once a year and never be caught.

What can be gathered

  • Poppy — the Dreamfields; sleep and pain, 1 gp an ounce of resin.
  • Gout-crocus — autumn crocus corms; a gout cure and a poison.
  • Rope-hemp — the margins.
  • Heavenly Horse foals — the Meadows; 400 gp and up.
  • Elysian grass — cut and dried, it stays green; mourners braid it into wreaths.

Who goes there

  • Komarch Eudora village head on the margin, keeper of the Register — wants the families' petition answered.
  • Old soldiers veterans of three armies — want a last word with the dead.
  • The Dream Dormitory's seers from Delphara — come to interview the dead, hunting news of Vesperine Ilaro.
  • Horse-buyers from Persemenid and the Lion's Mane Vanguard.

Wild · Acheaoria · Great desert

Dasht-a Khaliq

The Divine Wastes: the empire's eastern desert, where water is politics, the sand moves on its own schedule, and something the gods dropped is still rotting in the north-east.

Codex now: Biome: High fantasy desert wasteland with divine-tainted zones

Claimed by
Acheaoria, through three desert satrapies; the Sahari, in practice
Terrain
Dune sea, oasis basins, rock desert, petrified forest, fused black glass
Travel
18–24 days to cross by caravan · Survival DC 15 (DC 20 in Zahr al-Mawt or a khamsin)
Danger
High; Deadly in Zahr al-Mawt (CR 2–17)
Trouble
Water wars between oases; the dunes advancing a mile a season

The land

The eastern third of Asetheria is sand, and the sand is not neutral. The Dasht falls into three countries. Zahr al-Mawt, the Blossom of Death, lies in the north-east against what the maps call the Dead Realms: dark dunes, rotting winds, acid squalls and storms that whisper. Healing magic there runs at half strength unless a god of life or purity is behind it. Ruhaniin Vale, Spirits' Rest, is the civilised core: oases, qanat-fed terraces, sunken towns and the old city of Kharnesh on the Eye of Havar. Without a Sahari guide, a camp there wakes to mirages. Khamsin's Reach in the south-east is rock desert and petrified pine, studded with singing obelisks, and it is moving. At dawn the desert sometimes swallows another ten miles of somebody's land.

In the official account the desert is three loyal satrapies under the Shahanshah. In practice Kharnesh's water-castes decide who drinks, the Sahari decide who arrives, and the satraps decide how much of this to report.

New lore

The codex's "ruling Shah" of Kharnesh is a courtesy title. The satrap of the Vale styles himself shah inside his own walls, as desert satraps have for three centuries, and the court at Persemenid lets it pass so long as the tribute caravans arrive. For four of the five years since the Peace of the Signing, they have arrived light. The Scribes of the Infinite Ledger have noticed. The sandbreakers, conscript crews who plant salt-cedar and wattle fences against the drift, have not been paid since the war ended. More of them now work for the oasis houses than for the throne. The new obelisks keep appearing in Khamsin's Reach at a rate of about one a year. Two appeared this spring.

Sites

Kharnesh on the Eye of Havar Existing · old city, satrapal seat

Vertical · water-castes, clerks, Sahari envoys · wet stone and cumin

A city stacked up the walls of a sinkhole spring. Its tiers are ranked by water: the highest houses draw first and the lowest drink what the higher ones let fall. The caste you are born to is the cistern you were born above. The satrap holds the top terrace. The arashshara of the water-guild hold the sluice keys, which matters more.

Ties: the Vault of Silt; tribute roads to Persemenid; water law.

The Under-Sands Existing · sunken towns

Tunnels · miners, smugglers, worse · cool dust, lamp oil

A chain of towns the dunes buried and the people declined to leave. They are linked by tunnels and by passages that carry voices further than they should. One town stopped answering after last winter's tremors. The frataraka has posted a guard at the shaft head, facing in.

Ties: Kharnesh; drow of Lotha below; the Sahari "Sand Beneath the Sand".

The Vault of Silt Existing · aqueduct hub

Magi-guarded · engineers, mages · cold running water in the dark

A domed cistern where six qanats meet, kept steady by wards the mages call a leyline stabiliser and the muqanni call "the lid". If it fails, Kharnesh loses half its water inside a week.

Ties: Kharnesh; the Magi; the Qanat Line.

The Scar Fields Existing · fused glass wasteland

Zahr al-Mawt margin · masked scavengers · hot glass, sulphur

Black, ridged ground the divine war melted, warm even at midnight. Scavengers go in masked and in pairs for acher obsidian, hellstone and daemon iron. They sell in a back room at the nearest oasis, where the price depends on the buyer's nerves.

Ties: Honey-Palm Oasis; the Gallienain Cult (buyers).

The Caravan Stone Existing · rest-house

Crossroads inn · caravan masters, Wheelwalkers · cumin stew

A walled rest-house around one huge stone that every caravan master has carved his name on for a thousand years. The cook's cumin stew is why many choose this route. The stone is why nobody has poached the cook: his family's name is at the bottom of it.

Ties: Wheelwalkers; Caravan of the Gilded Horizon; roads east of Atarabad.

The Honey-Palm Oasis Existing · oasis market

Green pool · cotton growers, survivors · dates and wet earth

A pool ringed with tall date palms and a cotton field, with a market for everyone who survived the crossing. Water is sold by the skin at a price posted on a board. The board is repainted every week.

Ties: Scar Fields; the Myrrh Wadi.

The Royal Diggings Existing · quarries and mines

Red hills · convicts, satrap's counters · stone dust

The Purple Quarry yields imperial porphyry, closed to all but the King of Kings' cutters and carted out on its own paved road. Near it lie the Turquoise Diggings, where every stone is counted, and the Blue-Vein Pit, where copper ore and sky-blue stone come up by the thousand baskets. The Carnelian Washings are dry riverbeds, sieved at dawn. The Myrrh Wadi is cut by night and its gum sold against gold, and the Truffle Flats are dug by nomad women after thunder.

Ties: the Gilded Vault; royal monopolies.

The Stone Choir and the Shifting Pines Existing · Khamsin's Reach

Frontier · druids, surveyors · resin gone to stone

Wind-singing obelisks stand above a petrified forest where the dryads went to bone rather than leave. the Rose-Cliff City of the South is a rock-cut city whose spring drops a finger's depth each year. Its frataraka has begun selling the wells by the hour.

Ties: the Stormcallers' Choir; the ruined plateau observatory.

Fort Ostakhan New · dark imperial fort

Zahr al-Mawt · nobody, officially · bone dust

A marzban's fort built inside the curve of a god's rib, as cover from the bone storms. It went silent in the second year of peace. The satrapal ledger still draws its pay. A crystal dracolich is reported in the upper ribs. Nobody has gone to check whether the garrison is dead or has converted.

Ties: Cult of the Pale Sun; The Undying Legion.

What lives here

  • Gold-coat jackals and fat-tail scorpions — every road, every camp, every boot left outside the tent.
  • Dune-serpents — ridden by Sandsworn raiders in the Vale, hunting wild in the deep sand.
  • Blue dragons — lair under the rock desert and tax caravans by lightning.
  • Brass dragons — talkative, curious, and on good terms with the Sahari.
  • Jinn and ifrit — bound in old flasks, or loose, or the noble house's secret ally.
  • Dust mephits — in every khamsin, laughing.
  • Basilisks — Khamsin's Reach. Some of the petrified pines were not always pines.
  • Wandering Legions — zombies and skeletons in full Acheaorian gear, marching into the north-east.
  • Mummies of the god-corpse cults, and ghouls in every abandoned caravanserai.
  • Hell hounds — the Scar Fields, where the infernal war left its metals.

What can be gathered

  • Bitter myrrh — the Myrrh Wadi; temple and embalmer's gum, about 4 gp a pound.
  • Sand-truffle — the Truffle Flats after rain; a feast dish, 2 gp each at Persevalis.
  • Honey palm dates, tree-wool, sweet-root, red-hand leaf — oasis crops; cheap, filling, traded everywhere.
  • Phasegrass — grows on mirage ground; a sedative, and supposedly a mirage-ward if chewed.
  • Azurite, malachite, turquoise, carnelian, desert emerald — the Royal Diggings; satrap's licence required, and enforced.
  • Acher obsidian, hellstone, daemon iron — the Scar Fields; illegal to sell in three empires, which keeps the price up.

Who goes there

  • The Sahari desertborn guides and rangers — neutral, paid in water and silence; they know "the Sand Beneath the Sand", the old tunnels under the epochs.
  • Cult of the Pale Sun heretics — worship a dead sun-god buried in Zahr al-Mawt and want droughts to purify the land of cities.
  • Satrap Mardonak Havari satrap of the Vale, "shah" of Kharnesh — loyal by convenience; his tribute caravans have arrived a third short four years running.
  • Arashshara Tahmineh Ab-Dar keeper of the Kharnesh sluice keys — decides which tier drinks this week.
  • Wheelwalkers and the Caravan of the Gilded Horizon — the only reliable traffic; Predator's Guild hunters cull rot-lions for the bounty.
  • The Stormcallers' Choir — sing the rains onto the Truffle Flats; blamed for every khamsin.

Wild · Acheaoria · Inland salt sea

Kaspiran Seas

A salt sea with no outlet at the heart of Acheaoria. It sinks a hand's breadth every decade, and the shore it gives up was somebody's harbour.

Codex now: A salt sea with no outlet at the heart of Acheaoria, dropping a hand's breadth each decade and giving up what it covered.

Claimed by
Acheaoria; the shore satrapies divide it, the Magi forbid digging it
Terrain
Dense brine, salt flats, salt-cedar belts, pink lagoons, exposed ruins
Travel
5 days to sail across, 12 to ride round · Survival DC 14 (fresh water is the problem)
Danger
Moderate (CR 1–17; the last dragon turtle is CR 17)
Trouble
Night-diggers looting a city the Magi say does not exist

The land

A Hellenorian sailor would not call it a sea. It has no tide and no exit, and the water is salty enough to hold a swimmer up like a plank. Rivers run in and nothing runs out. What goes in stays, so the Kaspiran is a ledger of everything the empire has poured downstream, concentrated by two thousand years of evaporation. Its water is undrinkable, famously and immediately.

It is also falling, a hand's breadth a decade by the marks the satraps' clerks have cut into the rock since the founding. The new shore gives things up: jetties of no recorded port, and a road that runs out across the flats and carries on under the water. Last dry season the roofline of something with columns came up. The Magi have forbidden excavation. The fishermen dig anyway, at night, and sell what they find inland, where the ban is only a rumour.

New lore

The war kept the shore satrapies busy. Peace has sent their discharged spearmen home to fishing villages that cannot feed them, and night-digging has become an industry, with lamps out on the flats like a second town. The sturgeon catch is the best in memory, because nobody netted the deep water for fifteen years. Black sturgeon-egg now travels the Royal Road in sealed jars of ice at a price that would buy a horse. The satraps of the north and south shores both claim the newly dry land, since the treaty-maps were drawn to the old waterline. The Scribes of the Infinite Ledger have drafted a ruling. Nobody has asked them to publish it.

Sites

The Flamingo Lagoons Existing · lagoon

Salt-pink shallows · flame-waders, one herder · shrimp and brine

A string of shallow lagoons, pink with algae and shrimp, where the flame-waders stand in their thousands. At dusk the whole surface turns the colour of embers, and on windless evenings sailors have steered for it, taking it for a burning harbour. A herder's hut at the south end serves tea and tells tourists nothing they do not already know.

Ties: the Salt-Cedar Shore; plume-traders of Persevalis.

The Salt-Cedar Shore Existing · shore woodland

Feathery grey-green belt · winter herders · wormwood and old brine

A broad belt of salt-cedar weeping white crystals from its leaves, with silvery sea-wormwood in the hollows behind. There are no villages, only herders who winter here and drink from salt-lined wells. Reed-tigers den in the thickest stands, and the herders know which stands.

Ties: the Lagoons; sandbreaker crews of Dasht-a Khaliq, who buy cuttings.

The Drowned Road New · exposed ruin

Mudflats · night-diggers, Magi patrols · rot and lamp smoke

A paved road with kerbs, ruts and mile-stones in no known script. It runs from the old shore straight into the sea. Each decade another stretch dries out. At its present end, two hundred paces out, the column-tops of the roofline stand in the water like a ruined bench. The Magi post a fire-priest at the landward end, and the diggers launch their boats a mile further along.

Ties: the Magi; the Sage's Archive (which wants rubbings); smugglers to Tabrishi'ir.

The Clerks' Marks New · survey cliff

Carved rock face · Scribes of the Infinite Ledger · dry salt

A cliff cut with waterline marks every decade since the founding, each signed by the clerk who cut it. The highest marks stand a man's height above the oldest jetty. Pilgrims touch the founding mark for luck. The scribes note, without comment, that three marks from the war years were re-cut higher than they should be.

Ties: Scribes of the Infinite Ledger; the shore-boundary dispute.

What lives here

  • Reed-tigers (use tiger) — in the salt-cedar; and weretigers who say they are herders.
  • Giant crabs — on the flats at low wind, in hundreds.
  • Gray oozes — in the brine pools of the exposed ruins; they look like wet stone.
  • Steam mephits and dust mephits — where the hot springs meet the salt pans.
  • The last dragon turtle — old, slow, and apparently guarding the columns.
  • Black-egg sturgeon — the deep water; one fish is a family's year.
  • Flame-waders — the Lagoons, harmless and photogenic.
  • Brine-fly swarms — every summer, everywhere.

What can be gathered

  • Natron and sea-salt — the flats; embalmers, glassmakers and every kitchen; 1 cp a pound at source, 1 sp at Persemenid.
  • Black sturgeon-egg — the deep-water fishery; 25 gp a jar on the Royal Road.
  • Salt-cedar — windbreak cuttings and a dye-gall; sandbreakers buy it by the cartload.
  • Sea-wormwood — behind the salt-cedar; against worms and bad liquor.
  • Flame-wader plumes — moulted at the Lagoons; 5 sp a plume to milliners.
  • "Old work" — whatever the night-diggers bring up; illegal, and sold anyway.

Who goes there

  • The Magi fire-priests — forbid excavation and will not say why.
  • Ostad Barzin the Lamp night-digger boss · ex-spearman — runs forty boats and pays the fire-priest's nephew.
  • The Sage's Archive — wants rubbings of every inscription and has begun to disagree with the Magi in writing.
  • The River's Embrace — tends the river-mouth shrines and runs the ferries; knows which boats go out at night.
  • Predator's Guild — holds the reed-tiger culling rights.
  • Scribes of the Infinite Ledger — measure the waterline, and the satraps' claims against it.

Wild · Acheaoria · Lone peak

Mountain of Kharveth

A snowcapped peak alone on the flat plateau, ringed by no wells at all. The muqanni say its water is already spoken for.

Codex now: A solitary peak on the Acheaorian plateau where the qanat-diggers will not sink a shaft, and the empire has stopped asking why.

Claimed by
Acheaoria, on paper; a satrap's quarries and a prison mine on the lower flank
Terrain
Single mountain, scree, alabaster cuttings, snowcap; dry plateau all round
Travel
2 days to circle, 3 to summit · Survival DC 16
Danger
High above the cuttings (CR 1–8; the Div is CR 8)
Trouble
A new satrap wants wells; the muqanni have walked off

The land

A single mountain stands where the plateau is flat enough to see three days in every direction. It carries snow, and so it carries water, and by every principle of the Qanat Network it should be ringed with mother-wells. It is not. The muqanni, the hereditary tunnel-diggers, cannot afford superstition, yet they will not sink a shaft within a day's ride of Kharveth. The nearest their reason comes to translation is "the water there is already spoken for".

Three satraps have tried to compel them. The first two had conscripts dig the shafts. Both collapsed, with unusual losses, and the second time nobody could explain them. The third satrap sent surveyors, who came back with excellent measurements and one finding: the meltwater does not appear anywhere downhill in a quantity that matches the snowfall. The Magi have no doctrine on Kharveth, which for the Magi is itself a position.

New lore

The lower flank pays its way regardless. The Alabaster Cuttings feed a workshop village that ships lamps and burial urns across the empire. Higher up, the Cinnabar Shafts are worked by condemned men, because no free man will take the job. Peace has emptied the war prisons into those shafts. The mine's overseer complains that the new convicts are soldiers who know how to organise. The present satrap, newly appointed, is a reformer and a fool in about equal measure. He has offered a year's tribute remission to any muqanni guild that will dig, and every guild on the plateau has downed tools in response. Herders on the plateau leave a goat on the Leopard's Ledge each spring, for the cat they say.

Sites

The Alabaster Cuttings Existing · quarry

Honey-white cuts · carvers and lamp-makers · white dust on everything

Pale cuttings low on the mountain, where the stone is soft enough to carve with a knife. A lamp set inside one of its jars glows like a coal. The workshops at the foot turn out perfume jars, lamp-bowls and burial urns by the thousand. The stone is easy to carve and slow to forgive a careless blow, and a finished jar is worth ten times the block.

Ties: perfumers of Persevalis; tomb-builders of Persemenid.

The Cinnabar Shafts Existing · prison mine

Hot, narrow shafts · convicts and guards · thick, sweet poisoned air

Shafts sunk into the mountain's red side. The ore is bright red, the air tastes sweet, and a man who works the face for a year loses his teeth, then the steadiness of his hands, then his mind. The cap-rock above holds flecks of brassy devil's gold. The deepest shaft was sealed after the second collapse. The convicts say it was sealed from both sides.

Ties: quicksilver buyers among the Gallienain Cult; vermilion for the court painters.

The Leopard's Ledge Existing · crag

Cold rock shelf · one pale cat, one vulture · bone and wind

A broad shelf of broken rock above the highest pasture. Goat tracks cross it each morning, and the bones at the foot of the cliff say what happens to the goats by night. A plateau rock-leopard hunts here. The bone-breaker circles above and drops what the cat leaves onto the stones to crack the marrow.

Ties: the shepherds' spring goat; Predator's Guild.

The Two Dry Shafts New · collapsed qanat heads

Ruined mother-wells · nobody · cold air rising
