The Watcher, god of guardians and of vigilance that never sleeps. His iconography is a goliath in a closed helm. His rites are exacting and impersonal; he is owed correct observance and gives protection in return.

In the Imperium today. Watchmen, gatekeepers and bodyguards keep Helm's eye. The Vigiles of Aeterna are a state body and may not, but half their men wear his eye under their tunics. The Mithril Reserve's Custodes pray to him openly, and the Reserve has never asked the college's permission for anything.

Temples. His eye over the vault doors of the Mithril Reserve's branches at Duneforged and Deiperduem; a watch-chapel on the far bank at Aeterna. No order in the codex is sworn to him.

Of a cleric or paladin. Guard what you are given to guard. Never sleep on watch. Protect, do not conquer.

Hook. A Custos of the Mithril Reserve swears by Helm that the vault was never opened. The vault is empty, and his eye-amulet has turned blind.

Ilmater God of Endurance

Life · Lawful Good · Symbol: a pair of hands bound at the wrists · Holy day: the Day of Bound Hands, 1 Lambing

The Crying God, who suffers in the place of others. His iconography is a celestial couatl with bound wings. His priests keep strict rules in the belief that right order is a kindness, and their first rule is to go where the pain is.

In the Imperium today. Ilmater is the god of the Tent Rows. His priests feed the demobilised, nurse the crippled and sit with the dying, and they ask nothing. The state cults find this embarrassing. The Radiant Heartwardens, who are licensed physicians, work beside his priests and do not say so in their reports.

Temples. Hospices in the Tent Rows at Aeterna and among the settled veterans at Napplesia. No order in the codex is sworn to him; the Benevolent Hands of Acheaoria honour him beside Jarmik.

Of a cleric or paladin. Take on the suffering of others. Endure. Never turn away anyone in pain, whoever caused it.

Hook. A hospice of Ilmater is feeding four hundred men a day. Its grain comes from a Covenant granary that is officially empty.

Kelemvor God of the Dead

Death · Lawful Neutral · Symbol: a skeletal arm holding level scales · Holy day: the Judging, the first of the Five Days

The Lord of the Dead, judge of souls, who wants every death to be a fair passage and no more. His iconography is a revenant. His rites are exacting and impersonal. He hates undeath, because it cheats the scales.

In the Imperium today. Kelemvor is popular wherever the old gods charge too much to bury someone. His priests do burials at cost and destroy anything that rises. Since the Concord they have grown interested in Acheaoria, where rumours of the Immortals are told in every caravanserai on the Treaty Road.

Temples. Burial chapels outside the walls of Aeterna and Romulo; a quiet house at Deiperduem facing the Acheaorian compound. No order in the codex is sworn to him.

Of a cleric or paladin. See the dead to their rest. Destroy the undead. Never fear death, and never hasten it.

Hook. A priest of Kelemvor at Deiperduem asks the party to count the Acheaorian embassy guard twice a day for a month. He wants to know whether the same men come back.

Myrkul God of Death

Death · Neutral Evil · Symbol: a white skull on a black field · Holy day: the Feast of the Moon, the last night of Leaffall

The Lord of Bones, god of death as decay and as power over the dead. His iconography is a lich. His worship is quiet and self-serving. The faithful bargain for advantage and rarely speak of what they paid.

In the Imperium today. Myrkul's worship is forbidden everywhere and survives everywhere there are bones. Grave-robbers, unlicensed necromancers and a few physicians who want to understand the body pray to him. His cult is the reason the Cycle of the Eternal Bloom posts watchers in cemeteries.

Temples. None known. His mark has been found in the catacombs beneath Aeterna. No order in the codex is sworn to him.

Of a cleric or paladin. Fear nothing that dies. Gather the dead and their secrets. Never waste a corpse.

Hook. A body vanishes from a guarded catacomb beneath the Mons Sedis. The guards say it walked. The Vigiles say it was carried. Both are wrong.

Bhaal God of Murder

Death · Neutral Evil · Symbol: a skull ringed by drops of blood · Holy day: none kept openly

The Lord of Murder, god of killing for its own sake. His iconography is a vampire. His worship is quiet and self-serving; his faithful bargain with him and rarely say what they paid.

In the Imperium today. No one admits to worshipping Bhaal. The Vigiles keep a short list of killings that fit no motive. Each was found with a ring of blood drops around the body. The list has grown every year of the Peace, as men trained to kill for fifteen years come home with no one to kill.

Temples. None. No order in the codex is sworn to him. The Crimson Pact denies any connection, loudly.

Of a cleric or paladin. Kill. Let the killing be the point. A cleric of Bhaal is a murderer with spells, and every court will treat him so.

Hook. A Vigiles tribune asks the party to help with the list. The newest body was found in the Pantheum at Aeterna, on the bronze line, half inside the city and half outside it.

Loviatar Goddess of Pain

Death · Lawful Evil · Symbol: a nine-tailed whip · Holy day: the Rite of Nine, the ninth day of every month

The Maiden of Pain, goddess of hurt given and endured. Her iconography is a drow with a whip. Her worship is a hierarchy of obligation; she rewards those who serve without question, and her priests are effective, feared and well organised.

In the Imperium today. Loviatar's cult is forbidden, and it is found where pain is administered by the state: prisons, interrogation cells, the arena's back rooms. Some of the Speculatores' questioners keep her whip, and the Speculatores have decided not to know.

Temples. None openly. Her nine-knotted cords have been found in the cells below the Basilica at Aeterna and the arena at Duneforged. No order in the codex is sworn to her.

Of a cleric or paladin. Endure pain and teach others to. Give pain with precision, never in anger. Never show mercy you do not mean.

Hook. A prisoner freed from the Speculatores' cells will not leave. She says the questioner promised her a ninth day.

Talona Goddess of Disease and Poison

Death · Chaotic Evil · Symbol: three teardrops in a triangle · Holy day: none kept; she is appeased when plague comes

The Lady of Poison, mistress of disease. Her iconography is a medusa. Her worship is dangerous to the faithful and everyone near them; most of her shrines are hidden, and her cults are hunted.

In the Imperium today. Where Febris is begged to leave, Talona is begged to stay away from a particular house. Poisoners pray to her. So, to the scandal of the college, do some physicians, on the theory that a goddess of poison knows the antidote.

Temples. None. Her three teardrops are chalked in the marsh quarters of Aeterna during fever season. No order in the codex is sworn to her.

Of a cleric or paladin. Spread fear of sickness, and sell the cure. Study every poison. Never let a debt go unpaid in venom.

Hook. A physician of the Radiant Heartwardens is found with Talona's mark on her instruments. She swears it was put there to frame her, and she is right.

Shar Goddess of Darkness and Loss

Death, Trickery · Neutral Evil · Symbol: a black disc with a deep purple rim · Holy day: the Feast of the Moon's darkness, each new moon

The Mistress of the Night, goddess of loss, forgetting and secrets kept in the dark. Her iconography is a shadar-kai. Her worship is quiet; her faithful come to her because they want to forget, and she takes more than they meant to give.

In the Imperium today. Shar draws the grieving and the guilty. Widows of the war who want the pain gone pray to her, and so do soldiers who want to forget what they did on campaign. Her priests offer exactly that, and an empty space where the memory was.

Temples. None openly. Her cult meets in the Insulae at Aeterna in rooms with the lamps put out. No order in the codex is sworn to her; the Nightweaver Syndicate denies her and dresses like her.

Of a cleric or paladin. Keep the secret. Help the grieving forget. Never let light into a place that wants the dark.

Hook. A veteran hires the party to find out what he did in the war. A priestess of Shar took the memory, and his wife says he was happier before he asked.

Selûne Goddess of the Moon

Knowledge, Life · Chaotic Good · Symbol: a pair of eyes ringed by seven stars · Holy day: the full moon of each month

The Moonmaiden, goddess of the moon, navigators, lost travellers and women's mysteries. The codex writes her Selune. Her iconography is an eladrin. Her worship is warm and unruly, and her faithful honour her by acting on generous impulse.

In the Imperium today. Selûne shares the moon with Diana, and Diana's priests have decided to treat her as a cousin rather than a rival. Sailors at Mavelon, wanderers on the Treaty Road and women who need a goddess who is not anyone's matron pray to her. Her priestesses dance under the full moon on Mavelon's north side, and the Mavari join them.

Temples. Moon-shrines on the north side at Mavelon and at Deiperduem. No order in the codex is sworn to her.

Of a cleric or paladin. Guide the lost. Oppose the dark that steals memory. Change, as the moon changes, and be forgiven for it.

Hook. A Selûnite priestess asks the party to break into a house in Aeterna's Insulae where the lamps are never lit. She believes her sister's memory is inside.

Lathander God of Birth and Renewal

Life, Light · Neutral Good · Symbol: a sunrise of rose, red and yellow · Holy day: the Spring Dawn, the equinox morning that opens Sowing

The Morninglord, god of beginnings, births, youth and renewal. His iconography is an aasimar with the dawn behind him. His faithful are expected to help where they can and are given wide latitude in how.

In the Imperium today. Lathander is Aurora's rival for the same worshippers and is winning, because his priests marry, bless and found things without a licence fee. Veterans starting farms, merchants opening shops and couples the patrician rites would not marry go to him.

Temples. A dawn-chapel on the far bank at Aeterna; a larger one at Napplesia among the settled veterans; shrines on the Treaty Road. No order in the codex is sworn to him.

Of a cleric or paladin. Begin things. Bring new life and protect it. Never let the past bury the future.

Hook. The Dawnfire Alchemists accuse a Lathanderite chapel of stealing their dawn-gathered dew. The chapel says the dawn belongs to everyone.

Chauntea Goddess of Agriculture

Life · Neutral Good · Symbol: a rose blooming on a sheaf of grain · Holy day: the Greengrass, 1 Greening

The Great Mother of farmers and gardeners, of growth and the tilled field. Her iconography is a treant. Her faithful are expected to help where they can.

In the Imperium today. Ceres belongs to the grain dole and the city. Chauntea belongs to the smallholder, and the veterans given land they do not know how to farm have taken to her. Her priests teach ploughing and seed-saving for nothing, which has made her popular in the new allotments on the Latium Plains and unpopular with the Golden Harvest Covenant.

Temples. Field-shrines on the veterans' allotments outside Aeterna and Aepistra. No order in the codex is sworn to her.

Of a cleric or paladin. Grow and help grow. Teach the farmer. Never burn a field, even an enemy's.

Hook. The Golden Harvest Covenant wants a Chauntean priest's seed-saving lessons stopped. Her seed outyields theirs, and they sell the seed.

Silvanus God of Wild Nature

Nature · True Neutral · Symbol: an oak leaf · Holy day: the Midsummer Grove, the solstice that opens Highsun

Oak Father, god of wild nature in its balance. His iconography is a firbolg, like Diana's. His priests take no side, holding that the wild must stay in balance whoever profits.

In the Imperium today. Silvanus is worshipped in the Araucarian forest villages on the old forest road, where the Imperium's gods are a long way off. The Invictian college once declared him a local form of their own forest god, Silvanus of the boundaries, and his priests are content to let them think so.

Temples. Oak-groves at Alderpool, Nemorus and Silva Caminia. No order in the codex is sworn to him; the Circle of the Whispering Leaves keeps his groves.

Of a cleric or paladin. Keep the balance of the wild. Cut nothing that will not regrow. Never let one thing grow at the expense of all.

Hook. Mavelon's arsenal has contracted for a hundred great oaks from the Araucarian forest. A priest of Silvanus has marked every one with a red hand.

Mielikki Goddess of Forest

Nature · Neutral Good · Symbol: a unicorn's head · Holy day: the Greengrass, 1 Greening

Our Lady of the Forest, goddess of rangers, dryads and the life of the woodland. Her iconography is a dryad. Her faithful are expected to help where they can.

In the Imperium today. Mielikki is a ranger's goddess. Foresters, guides and the hunters who scout for armies pray to her, and so do some Silent Stalkers of the Glade, to Faunus's priests' annoyance. Her priests give shelter to anyone lost in a forest, and have sheltered deserters, which the legions have not forgotten.

Temples. Forest-shrines on the old forest road near Silva Caminia and in the woods around Nemibano. No order in the codex is sworn to her.

Of a cleric or paladin. Guard the forest and those lost in it. Live with the wood, not off it. Never hunt for sport.

Hook. A Mielikkian guide offers to take the party through the forest by a road that is on no map. She asks one thing: that they not tell the legions it exists.

Malar God of the Hunt

Nature · Chaotic Evil · Symbol: a beast's clawed paw · Holy day: the High Hunt, the first full moon of Leaffall

The Beastlord, god of the savage hunt and the blood that follows it. His iconography is a shifter, half beast. His worship is dangerous to the faithful and everyone near them; most of his shrines are hidden.

In the Imperium today. Malar draws the men who learned to enjoy the hunt in war. His cult holds hunts in the hills where the quarry is sometimes a man: a deserter, a debtor, a runaway slave. The Silent Stalkers hunt Malar's hunters, which is the one thing Faunus's people and the legions agree on.

Temples. None. Claw-marked stones are found in the Klynin hills above the Aqua Aeterna. No order in the codex is sworn to him.

Of a cleric or paladin. Hunt. Let the strong live and the weak feed them. Never let quarry escape.

Hook. A runaway reaches the party with claw-marks on his back and a Legate's brand on his arm. The hunters behind him are the Legate's own men.

Auril Goddess of Winter

Nature, Tempest · Neutral Evil · Symbol: a white snowflake on a grey diamond · Holy day: the first frost of Frostmonth

The Frostmaiden, goddess of cold, winter and the beauty of things that kill. Her iconography is a frost genasi. Her worship is quiet and self-serving; her faithful bargain for advantage and rarely speak of what they paid.

In the Imperium today. Auril is prayed to in the Klynin Mountain Range and on the high passes, not out of love but to be spared. Shepherds leave her a lamb at the first frost. Ice-sellers in Aeterna pay her priests to keep the snow-pits on the mountains full.

Temples. Cairns on the high passes above the Aqua Aeterna and on the Cloudspine Ridge near Duneforged. No order in the codex is sworn to her; the dark cult of the Melted Ice gathers where her ice retreats.

Of a cleric or paladin. Endure the cold and let the weak learn to. Keep the winter's beauty. Never warm a stranger for free.

Hook. The springs of the Aqua Aeterna have frozen in Highsun. The aqueduct's engineers blame a priest of Auril in the mountains. He blames them.

Talos God of Storms

Tempest · Chaotic Evil · Symbol: three lightning bolts from a point · Holy day: the first great storm of the year

The Destroyer, god of storms, earthquakes and wild destruction. His iconography is a storm giant. His worship is dangerous to the faithful and everyone near them. Most of his shrines are hidden and his cults are hunted.

In the Imperium today. Talos is propitiated by sailors, farmers and miners who fear him. His priests demand tribute to turn a storm aside, and a district that does not pay sometimes burns. Jupiter's priests consider him a usurper of the thunder and have the Stormlord Vanguard break up his rites.

Temples. None openly. Lightning-scarred altars stand on the headlands of Mavelon's caldera rim. No order in the codex is sworn to him. (The bronze guardian Talos at Duneforged has no known connection to the god, which nobody there believes.)

Of a cleric or paladin. Bring the storm and take tribute to hold it back. Destroy what is old and weak. Never pray for calm.

Hook. A priest of Talos demands a tribute of silver from Mavelon's south harbour or the winter storms will take the warship slips. The Dux will not pay; the Reiks has.

Umberlee Goddess of the Sea

Tempest · Chaotic Evil · Symbol: a wave curling left and right · Holy day: the First Tempest, the first storm of Fallow

The Bitch Queen of the waves, goddess of the cruel sea. Her iconography is a kraken, or a triton with a kraken's eyes. Her worship is dangerous to the faithful and to everyone near them.

In the Imperium today. Every sailor pays her. Captains drop coins over the side at departure; fishing villages throw a garland on the water each autumn. Neptune's Tideguard calls it superstition and collects its own fees. Most crews pay both and pray hardest to the one who drowns people.

Temples. A sea-shrine on the native north harbour of Mavelon; offering-rocks off Fucostia and Napplesia. No order in the codex is sworn to her.

Of a cleric or paladin. Make sailors pay. Punish those who scorn the sea. Never save a drowning man who has not paid.

Hook. An Umberlant priestess at Mavelon has declared that the next warship launched from the south harbour will sink unless it pays her a tithe instead of the Tideguard's fee.

Tymora Goddess of Good Fortune

Trickery · Chaotic Good · Symbol: a silver coin with her face · Holy day: Midsummer night

Lady Luck, goddess of good fortune, adventurers and the bold throw. Her iconography is a halfling tossing a coin. Her worship is warm and unruly, and her faithful honour her by acting on generous impulse.

In the Imperium today. Tymora is the adventurers' goddess, and the Peace has made adventurers of a great many men. Her coins are carried by mercenaries, couriers, treasure hunters and gamblers. Fortuna's priests regard her as their goddess with the dull parts left out.

Temples. Dice-house shrines at Duneforged, Deiperduem and on the quays of Mavelon. No order in the codex is sworn to her.

Of a cleric or paladin. Be bold. Take the chance. Share the winnings. Never let fear decide.

Hook. A Tymoran priest offers the party a coin that always lands face up. Its last owner is buried in a Mavelon cave-house; he used it once too often.

Beshaba Goddess of Misfortune

Trickery · Chaotic Evil · Symbol: black antlers on a red field · Holy day: the Five Days, when nothing should be begun

The Maid of Misfortune, goddess of bad luck and accidents. Her iconography is a night hag. Her worship is dangerous to the faithful and those near them. Most of her shrines are hidden.

In the Imperium today. Nobody worships Beshaba. Everybody appeases her. Invictians make the sign of the horns against her and leave a broken pot at the door during the Purgation. Her few true priests are hired to curse rivals and are paid by people who would deny ever having met them.

Temples. None. No order in the codex is sworn to her. Her antlers are scratched on the walls of debtors' prisons everywhere.

Of a cleric or paladin. Spread misfortune where it is owed. Make people fear you so they pay you to leave. Never let luck run unchecked.

Hook. A merchant whose ships have sunk three times in a year pays the party to find the Beshaban priest who cursed him. The priest says the merchant cursed himself, and can prove it.

Mask God of Thieves

Trickery · Chaotic Neutral · Symbol: a black velvet mask · Holy day: the darkest night of Deepwinter

The Lord of Shadows, god of thieves, shadows and the thing taken quietly. His iconography is a kenku. He is unpredictable, and so are his faithful; he is honoured by being given room rather than by being obeyed.

In the Imperium today. Mask is Mercury's shadow: what Mercury's merchants do by contract, his thieves do by night. Every thieves' guild in the Imperium keeps his mask in a back room, and the Tenebral Covenant keeps two, one for each empire it robs.

Temples. None openly. His shrines are in the cellars of Romulo's Vault Streets and on the quays of Mavelon. No order in the codex is sworn to him; the Tenebral Covenant and the Veilborn Syndicate pray to him beside their own gods.

Of a cleric or paladin. Take what is not guarded. Leave no trace. Never steal from a fellow servant of the shadow.

Hook. A thief of Mask has stolen the seal of the Hall of Weights at Romulo, and he is offering to return it to whoever pays most: the merchants, the Rex Sacrorum or the Mithril Reserve.

Cyric God of Lies

Trickery · Chaotic Evil · Symbol: a white jawless skull on a black or purple sunburst · Holy day: none; his feasts are always on a different day

The Prince of Lies, god of deception, strife and murder for advantage. His iconography is a changeling. His worship is dangerous to the faithful and everyone near them, and his cults are hunted.

In the Imperium today. Cyric draws the Court's liars and the provinces' forgers. His priests forge documents, invent rumours and set allies against each other for the joy of it. Since the empty chair, there has been so much lying in Aeterna that his priests say the city has converted without being asked.

Temples. None. No order in the codex is sworn to him. His sunburst has been found drawn on forged decrees "in the name of the Imperator".

Of a cleric or paladin. Lie. Divide. Turn every ally into a rival. Never tell the same lie twice.

Hook. A decree of the Imperator, signed and sealed, orders the Senate to reconvene. The seal is genuine. The Imperator has not been seen in five years.

Leira Goddess of Illusion

Trickery · Chaotic Neutral · Symbol: a downward triangle full of mist · Holy day: none; it moves

The Lady of the Mists, goddess of illusion and deception. Her iconography is a shadow demon. She is unpredictable, and so are her faithful; she is honoured by being given room rather than by being obeyed.

In the Imperium today. Illusionists, actors and confidence tricksters pray to her. The collegia license illusion as a craft, and Leira's priests regard the licence as an illusion too. Her cult has been seen in the Prismatic Shroud's company, and the Speculatores keep confusing her people with Arcus's.

Temples. None fixed. Her mist-shrines appear in the theatres of Aeterna and disappear. No order in the codex is sworn to her.

Of a cleric or paladin. Nothing is as it seems; make sure of it. Trust no fixed truth. Never reveal your true face to someone you do not love.

Hook. The party is hired by a woman who does not exist to find a man who does. The Speculatores want to know who hired them.

Mystra Goddess of Magic

Knowledge · Neutral Good · Symbol: seven stars around a red mist · Holy day: the Starfall, the night of the Leaffall meteor showers

The Lady of Mysteries, goddess of magic itself and of its weave. Her iconography is an eladrin. Her faithful are expected to help where they can.

In the Imperium today. Mystra is the goddess every mage owes and the collegia cannot license. Licensed collegia observe her quietly; unlicensed hedge-wizards pray to her openly, because she has never asked for an examination fee. Hellarchon's Arcane Academy keeps a cell for her, and the Invictian college resents that too.

Temples. A chapel on the far bank at Aeterna; the Academy's cell at Hellarchon. No order in the codex is sworn to her.

Of a cleric or paladin. Learn magic, use it, and share it with those who will use it well. Guard it from those who will not. Never destroy a spell that cannot be relearned.

Hook. A Mystran priestess has begun teaching magic free in the Tent Rows. The Artisan's Forge of Wonders calls it unlicensed casting. The veterans call it the first useful thing anyone has given them.

Azuth God of Wizards

Knowledge · Lawful Neutral · Symbol: a left hand pointing upward, outlined in fire · Holy day: the Day of the First Spell, 1 Fallow

The High One, god of wizards, of magic as study and discipline. His iconography is a high elf. His rites are exacting and impersonal; he is owed correct observance and gives order in return.

In the Imperium today. Azuth is the licensed mage's Ascended: the collegia accept him because he values examinations and correct procedure as much as they do. Collegium masters keep his hand on their desks. He is the one Ascended the Invictian college has considered licensing, and has not, because of what the others would demand next.

Temples. Desk-shrines in the collegia at Aeterna; a reading room at Deiperduem. No order in the codex is sworn to him; the Luminous Arcanists honour him beside Phoebus.

Of a cleric or paladin. Study. Use magic with discipline and record what you do. Never cast a spell you do not understand.

Hook. A collegium master asks the party to fetch an Azuthan text from Hellarchon's Academy. The Academy says the text is not theirs to give. The Lexicon Council says it does not exist.

Oghma God of Knowledge

Knowledge · True Neutral · Symbol: a blank scroll · Holy day: the Day of the Blank Page, 1 Deepwinter

The Lord of Knowledge, god of ideas, invention and the free passage of knowledge. His iconography is a gnome with ink on his fingers. His priests take no side, holding that knowledge must move whoever profits.

In the Imperium today. Oghma is the scholars' Ascended, and the Three Libraries are full of his quiet followers. Copyists, librarians and translators keep his blank scroll. His priests believe every book should be copied and every archive opened, which makes them welcome in the Aeterna Lexicon and watched in every other archive.

Temples. A reading-shrine in the Lexicon at Aeterna; chapels among the Porticoes of Thessalonika and near the Sage's Archive at Persemenid. No order in the codex is sworn to him.

Of a cleric or paladin. Learn, record and share. Copy what might be lost. Never burn a book.

Hook. An Oghman copyist at the Lexicon has made one copy too many of the Old Empires chronicle, and the extra copy is missing.

Deneir God of Writing

Knowledge · Neutral Good · Symbol: a lit candle above an open eye · Holy day: the Day of Ink, 1 Blossom

The Lord of All Glyphs and Images, god of writing, art and literature. His iconography is a half-elf scribe. His faithful are expected to help where they can.

In the Imperium today. Deneir is the god of the scribes who write letters for the illiterate in every forum. His priests teach reading in the Tent Rows and copy wills for nothing, which has made him popular with the plebs and unpopular with the notaries. The Vestals, who hold the rich men's wills, consider him a competitor for the poor men's.

Temples. Scribes' shrines in the forums of Aeterna and Romulo. No order in the codex is sworn to him.

Of a cleric or paladin. Write it down. Teach others to read. Never forge, never deface.

Hook. A Deneiran scribe at Romulo has noticed that the same hand wrote three different guilds' founding charters, read aloud each Leaffall as centuries old.

Savras God of Divination and Fate

Knowledge · Lawful Neutral · Symbol: a crystal ball holding many eyes · Holy day: the Night of Seeing, the last of the Five Days

The All-Seeing, god of divination and fate. His iconography is a kalashtar, a mind that hears another voice. His rites are exacting: a true seeing requires correct procedure, and he punishes the careless with false visions.

In the Imperium today. Invicta reads the future through the augurs' birds and the Astromancers' stars, both licensed. Savras's seers are not, and they are hired more often. His priests read for Legates, merchants and lovers, and they answer to no college.

Temples. Seers' rooms at Deiperduem and on the far bank at Aeterna. No order in the codex is sworn to him; the Collegium of the Sacred Sight honours him beside its own patrons.

Of a cleric or paladin. See truly and tell what you see. Seek the pattern of fate, and do not pretend to change it. Never sell a vision you did not have.

Hook. Three seers of Savras have independently foreseen the same date. None will say what happens on it. All three have left the city.

Gond God of Craft

Knowledge · True Neutral · Symbol: a toothed cog with four spokes · Holy day: the Day of the Gear, the first day of Reaping

The Wonderbringer, god of invention, craft and the machine. His iconography is a modron, all gears. His priests take no side, holding that invention must go forward whoever profits.

In the Imperium today. Gond is the inventor's Vulcan. Vulcan's priests make the old thing well; Gond's make the new thing first. Artificers at Duneforged's Crucible Spire and engineers at Mavelon's arsenal keep his cog. Since the Peace, the arsenal's new slipways have been built to Gondsman drawings, which Vulcan's priests resent.

Temples. Workshop shrines in the Crucible Spire at Duneforged, under Countess Aurelie Virellarion, and on the arsenal terraces of Mavelon. No order in the codex is sworn to him.

Of a cleric or paladin. Invent. Improve. Share designs with those who will build them. Never destroy a working machine.

Hook. A Gondsman engineer at Mavelon has designed a ship that needs no oars. The arsenal wants it. The Tideguard refuses to bless a keel that its rites do not cover.

Waukeen God of Trade

Knowledge, Trickery · True Neutral · Symbol: a gold coin with a profile · Holy day: the Market of Nations, high summer at Deiperduem

The Merchant's Friend, god of trade, money and wealth. The codex calls Waukeen a god; most of the faithful say goddess, and the coins show a face that could be either. Iconography: a half-elf. The priests take no side, holding that trade must flow whoever profits.

In the Imperium today. Waukeen is the trader's Ascended, worshipped by merchants who cross borders and find Mercury too Invictian. The Farshore merchants at Romulo take to Waukeen quickly. The Mithril Reserve's Domini Argentarii keep a coin on the counting-table, and discount Invictian silver beneath it.

Temples. Counting-house shrines at Deiperduem and on the Guild Square at Romulo, outside the old wall. No order in the codex is sworn to Waukeen; the Chyrsus Syndicate prays to nobody else.

Of a cleric or paladin. Trade fairly and let money move. Keep honest accounts. Never hoard; idle coin is a sin.

Hook. A priest of Waukeen offers the party a fortune to bring him three trial pieces from the next Assay. He says it is a matter of faith.

Sune Goddess of Love and Beauty

Life, Light · Chaotic Good · Symbol: the face of a red-haired woman · Holy day: the Feast of Firehair, Midsummer

Lady Firehair, goddess of love, beauty and passion. Her iconography is a nymph. Her worship is warm and unruly.

In the Imperium today. Sune competes with Venus for the same devotees and wins the young. Her priestesses run bath-houses, dance-halls and beauty schools on the far bank, and teach that love is its own law. The college considers her a foreign Venus with poor manners. Patrician daughters visit her anyway.

Temples. A bath-temple on the far bank at Aeterna; a larger one at Napplesia, among the villas. No order in the codex is sworn to her; the Ivory Chorus sings for her beside Aphrodite.

Of a cleric or paladin. Love passionately. Make beauty and protect it. Never let ugliness, of body or spirit, go unanswered.

Hook. A patrician's daughter has run away to a Sunite temple at Napplesia. Her father sends the party to fetch her. The priestess says the girl is a free woman of age, and she is.

Lliira Goddess of Joy

Life · Chaotic Good · Symbol: three six-pointed stars of orange, yellow and red · Holy day: the Festival of Joy, the first full moon of Greening

Our Lady of Joy, goddess of happiness, dance and freedom. Her iconography is a sprite. Her worship is warm and unruly.

In the Imperium today. Lliira is the goddess of the festival without a state. Her dancers turn up wherever there is a crowd and start a party, and the party goes on until the Vigiles come. In the Tent Rows, where there is little else to be happy about, her cult is growing faster than any other.

Temples. None fixed; her dancers keep an open house in the Tent Rows at Aeterna. No order in the codex is sworn to her.

Of a cleric or paladin. Bring joy. Free the oppressed to dance. Never spoil a celebration.

Hook. A Lliiran dance in the Tent Rows has gone on for nine days. Nobody can stop dancing, and the dancers are smiling.

Milil God of Poetry and Song

Light · Neutral Good · Symbol: a five-stringed harp of silver leaves · Holy day: the Day of Song, 1 Vintage

The Lord of Song, god of poetry, music and eloquence. His iconography is a harpy, which his priests explain by saying that every song can wound. His faithful are expected to help where they can.

In the Imperium today. Bards and poets everywhere keep his harp. In the Imperium he is the god of the street singers who mock the Legates. The College of the Starlit Lute plays for Pomona but quietly thanks Milil, and Acheaoria's Melodic Circle sings to him beside Bala.

Temples. Singers' shrines in the theatres of Aeterna and at Persevalis, where Shirin Navaz is said to keep his harp. No order in the codex is sworn to him.

Of a cleric or paladin. Sing truth, beautifully. Inspire the despairing. Never let a good song die.

Hook. A satirical song about the Dominus Militum is sweeping the Insulae. The Speculatores want the author. The author is a priest of Milil, and the song is true.

Eldath Goddess of Peace

Life, Light · Neutral Good · Symbol: a waterfall falling into a still pool · Holy day: the Quiet Hour, dusk on the Treaty's anniversary

The Quiet One, goddess of peace, still water and the healing of the spirit. Her iconography is a water genasi. Her faithful are expected to help where they can.

In the Imperium today. Eldath is the goddess of the Treaty, though no empire would say so. Her priests keep vigil at the Quiet Ground at Deiperduem through the Quiet Hour. In the Imperium they run quiet houses where shaken veterans can sit by water and not be asked anything. Concordia's priests regard her as a rival with no rules.

Temples. The pools of Deiperduem; quiet houses by the springs at Napplesia and Falecosa. No order in the codex is sworn to her.

Of a cleric or paladin. Make peace and keep it. Shelter the weary. Never draw a weapon in a sacred grove or beside a sacred pool.

Hook. A pool of Eldath at Deiperduem has turned red at dawn, three days before the Treaty's anniversary.

The Hellenorian Pantheon

Hellenoria has no church. It has the Roll: twenty-one powers recognised by the Tribunal of the gods in Hellarchon, whose temples have asylum and whose priests have immunity. Every city keeps twelve of them in its own pantheon hall, in its own order, and fights about the order every year. Hellarchon ranks them by tradition, Corinth by takings, Thessalonika by documents, Helionyx by the shadow of a stick. The oracles carry more weight than any priest, and the imperial Truth-Flame reads every hymn before it may be sung. What follows is the Roll as a traveller meets it: who each god is, where the god is kept, who is sworn to the god, and what the god wants from the people who carry its power.

Zeus the Storm Lord

Tempest · True Neutral · Symbol: a thunderbolt in an eagle's claw · Holy day: the Diasia, the waning tenth of Anthesterion

King of the gods and lord of weather, shown as a broad, haloed aasimar with a cloud for a cloak. The codex makes him neutral, and his priests insist on it: the storm falls on the just and the unjust, and the god who throws it is keeping a balance, not taking a side. He is the god of oaths sworn to guests and of strangers at the door.

Worship today. Every assembly in the League opens with his name, and then gets on with its own favourites. He stands fourth in Hellarchon, tenth on Corinth's Board (his priests call it an insult; Corinth calls it arithmetic), and third in Thessalonika, where Zeus of Guests keeps the Horse Gate. The Emperor's unseen "voice" is compared to thunder behind cloud, by those who still say it kindly.

Temples: Thessalonika (Zeus of Guests); Hellarchon (the fourth chapel); Corinth; Atticenea, where the tyrant's unfinished temple has four columns. Sworn order: the Tempest Wrath Conclave.

Asks of a cleric or paladin: keep every oath made to a guest; never strike a suppliant at an altar; judge without favour even when the favour is your own city's.

Hera the Matron of Families

Family, Intrigue · Chaotic Neutral · Symbol: a pomegranate with a peacock's eye · Holy day: the Sacred Marriage, full moon of Gamelion

Queen of the gods, goddess of marriage, the household and the long memory of slights. Her images show a maned leonin matron, crowned, a sceptre across her knees. Her stories are about jealousy; her worship is about contracts. A Hellenorian marriage is an alliance between houses, and Hera is the party who remembers the terms.

Worship today. Women run it. Brides cut a lock of hair for her in Gamelion, the month of weddings; widows keep her in the house rather than the temple. She is fifth in Hellarchon, ninth in Thessalonika and eleventh on Corinth's Board, a ranking her worshippers find funnier than her priests do. The codex says she is honoured by being given room, and families do: nobody plans a marriage around her festival, and nobody plans one against it.

Temples: Hera of the Loom on the Widows' Terraces at Carianea, where every marriage in the town is woven into a cloth; chapels in Hellarchon, Thessalonika and Corinth. Sworn order: the Matriarch's Loom of Bonds, which meets in the loom-porch at Carianea.

Asks of a cleric or paladin: defend the household before the city; witness marriage contracts honestly; repay a wrong done to kin, by your own hand if the courts will not.

Poseidon the Earth Shaker

Sea · Chaotic Neutral · Symbol: a trident above a horse's head · Holy day: the Launching, early Mounichion

Lord of the sea, of earthquakes and of horses, shown as a triton with a beard of weed. He is not kind and does not pretend to be. A sea-power's god is propitiated, not loved: sailors promise him a share of the voyage, and they pay it, because the alternative is the bottom.

Worship today. The richest cult in the League. His high priest is the Archiereus of the Tribunal itself, Theodektes Eteoboutades, and he stands first on Corinth's Board by the weight of sailors' vows. Every hull in Hellarchon is launched under his eye, every Corinthian ship pours one sea on his altar and carries the other away, and at Argotiko the horse-breeders cart seawater inland each month so as to offend neither half of him.

Temples: Hellarchon (Poseidon of the Sheds); Corinth (Poseidon of the Isthmus, at the Haulway's midpoint); Helionyx (the Mole Temple); Argotiko (the Hippeion); Thebesieas (the Horse Gate); the reef altar at Carianea; the Dredging chapel at Ephelanum, its door silted half-open. No sworn order: the priesthoods are family property, chiefly the Isthmiadai and Aigeidai.

Asks of a cleric or paladin: pay the sea its share before your own; never refuse a rescue at sea; never ride a horse to death.

Demeter the Earth Mother

Agriculture · Neutral Good · Symbol: a barley sheaf crossed with a torch · Holy day: the Thesmophoria, Pyanepsion

Goddess of grain and the harvest, shown as a broad firbolg woman with a sickle in her belt. In her story she lost a daughter and the world went cold until she was given back. Her displeasure was never a thunderbolt. It was a famine, which is worse and slower.

Worship today. Hellenoria imports its bread, and so Demeter is the goddess of the quay as much as the field. Thebesieas, the League's granary, keeps her rites as the old texts give them: three days at the Thesmophoria, men excluded and not asking. The maritime cities keep her at the docks, where cargoes are weighed in her porch so nobody cheats under her eye. Her mysteries are taught by degrees and have never leaked.

Temples: Thebesieas (the Temple of the Furrow); Helionyx (the Bread House); Thessalonika (Demeter of the Granaries); the eighth chapel at Hellarchon; the First Furrow chapel at Ephelanum; a quiet offering under the pomegranates at Persevalis. Sworn orders: the Circle of the Eternal Grove, keepers of the Foloicauria; the Golden Scythe Accord.

Asks of a cleric or paladin: feed the hungry from your own store first; keep the mysteries; never burn a field, even an enemy's.

Hestia the Keeper of the Eternal Fire

Hearth, Home · Neutral Good · Symbol: a flame in a round bowl, never an image · Holy day: the first offering at every sacrifice; the Standing, 1st of Hekatombaion

Goddess of the hearth, who gave up her seat among the twelve to keep the fire. Her rare images show a centaur standing guard over a brazier; most of her chapels have no image at all, only a lamp. She has no myths, because a hearth does not need adventures, and she takes the first portion of every sacrifice to every other god.

Worship today. Load-bearing. A Hellenorian colony is founded by carrying fire from its mother city's hearth, and that act, not a charter, makes it a daughter rather than a rival. Every household keeps her; every city keeps a civic hearth in its town hall, where victors and ambassadors dine at public cost.

Temples: Hellarchon (the Common Hearth in the Prytaneion, kept by Mother Eirene Hestiaia); Delphara (the oldest fire in Hellenoria, at the Dodekatheon); Thessalonika, whose receipt for its fire survives; the hearth beside Hermes at Deiperduem. Sworn order: the Hearthfire Sanctum, which has refused fire twice, both times to tyrants founding "colonies" that were garrisons.

Asks of a cleric or paladin: keep a fire and share it; give any guest bread and a seat; take no side in a quarrel under a roof that is not yours.

Athena the Wise Guardian

Knowledge, Civilization · Lawful Good · Symbol: an owl on a round shield, an olive sprig · Holy day: the Panegyris, Hekatombaion (Greater every third year of the Pythiad)

Goddess of wisdom, craft and the defence of the city, born armoured from her father's head. Asetherian images show her as a warforged, jointed and plated, which her priests take as the plain truth of the story. She is the war goddess of the plan rather than the slaughter, and her priests keep strict rules in the belief that right order is itself a kindness.

Worship today. Hellarchon's Maiden, first in its pantheon and mistress of its Rock, whose strongroom holds the League Chest. Every Panegyris carries her a new robe from harbour to summit. Athena of the Olive at Atticenea is a rival flame; the two may not touch.

Temples: Hellarchon (the Maiden's Temple; the Smith's House, shared with Hephaestus); Delphara (the Shrine Before the Temple); Thessalonika (Athena of the Porticoes); Atticenea (the Old Tree); Athena of the potter's wheel at Araavyna. Sworn order: the Ecliptica Arcanum, mages who plan three weeks ahead.

Asks of a cleric or paladin: defend the city and its law; plan before you strike; teach what you know to anyone who will use it well.

Apollo the Radiant One

Light, Healing · Chaotic Good · Symbol: a laurel wreath around a lyre · Holy day: the 7th of each warm month (consultation day); the Pythian Games, Metageitnion

God of light, healing, music and prophecy, the lord of Delphara. His images give him an aarakocra's wings and a golden beak. He heals and he infects: the god who lifts the plague also sends it, and his physicians are taught the second half first.

Worship today. Through the oracle above all. The Pythia speaks on the 7th of each warm month, Lysandra Anthemis the Exegete turns her words into verse, and every city in the League, and several outside it, pays to ask. The Pythian Games come every fourth summer, music before athletics. Elsewhere he is a respected lodger: sixth in Hellarchon, seventh in Thessalonika and Corinth, and at Helionyx a guest below the sun-temple.

Temples: Delphara (the Temple of the Oracle; the Dream Dormitory); Helionyx (the Guest-Shrine); the Healer's temple at Loutrokleion; the Cauldron spring at Napplesia, licensed by a special Invictian law; chapels at Hellarchon, Thessalonika, Corinth and Ephelanum, where he walks before his sister. Sworn order: the Luminastra Alchemists, whose training begins with poisons. See Lysandra Anthemis.

Asks of a cleric or paladin: heal whoever asks; know the poison as well as the cure; never speak a falsehood in the god's name, even a kind one.

Artemis the Huntress of the Moon

Nature, Wild Hunt, Lunar Light · Neutral Good · Symbol: a crescent bow and a bee · Holy day: the Procession of the Image, mid-Thargelion

Huntress of the wild places and the moon, protector of the young and of women in childbirth. Her images show a tabaxi archer, light on her feet, a fawn at her heel. Her faithful are expected to help where they can and are given wide latitude in how.

Worship today. At Ephelanum she is simply the Lady, and her temple is also the richest bank on the southern coast. The Treaty made that city a condominium: the Hellenorian text names the goddess Artemis, the Invictian text names her Diana, and the two clauses keep two festival calendars. Elsewhere she is seventh in Hellarchon and eighth in Thessalonika, and the island cities keep her as Artemis of the Islands at Delphara. Hunters leave her the first kill of the season.

Temples: the Great Sanctuary at Ephelanum (see the city), under Hierarchis Melissa Aristarchis; the island altar at Delphara; chapels at Hellarchon and Thessalonika. No sworn order in the League; her priestesses are the Melissai of Ephelanum.

Asks of a cleric or paladin: protect the young of every kind; kill cleanly and waste nothing; keep the vows of the hunt even when no one is watching.

Hermes the Fleet-footed Messenger

Travel, Commerce, Mercenaries · Chaotic Good · Symbol: a herald's staff with two snakes · Holy day: the 4th of every month, his birthday

Messenger of the gods, patron of travellers, merchants, heralds and thieves, who stole his brother's cattle on the day he was born. His images show a shifter, half caught between man and hound, in a traveller's hat. He crosses boundaries for a living and is honoured by generous impulse rather than rite.

Worship today. First in Thessalonika, where Hermes of the Gate was there before the city and his herald family carries the scholars' post uninspected to every border. Tenth in Hellarchon, where every few years the merchants try to move him above Hephaestus and the smiths fill the Agora. Fourth on Corinth's Board. Waystones and roadside cairns are his; travellers add a stone.

Temples: Thessalonika (Hermes of the Gate); Thebesieas (the Isthmus Gate); the market hour at Helionyx; a hired niche in the Court of Guests at Atarabad; the blue-doored Hellenorian wing at Deiperduem, charged separately from Mercury. Sworn order: the Sunward Valiants, mercenaries who will not hold a line but have never broken a parley flag.

Asks of a cleric or paladin: carry a message unopened; honour heralds of every side; keep the roads open, and leave a stone.

Hephaestus the Forge Master

Forge · Neutral Good · Symbol: hammer and tongs over an anvil · Holy day: the Chalkeia, last day of Pyanepsion

Smith of the gods, lame, thrown from the mountain, married to Aphrodite and wronged by Ares, and the only god who makes the things the beautiful gods cannot make for themselves. His images show a deep gnome at the anvil, small, scarred and patient. He works while the others feast.

Worship today. Guild worship. Potters, bronze-casters and kiln-masters keep him; their temples run like workshops, with dues by the kiln and strike funds in the treasury. Ninth in Hellarchon (and fighting to stay above Hermes), sixth on Corinth's Board. In the Imperium his Hellenorian-descended smiths work to him rather than to Vulcan, which there is a statement.

Temples: Hellarchon (the Smith's House, priest Lampon Kerameus); Corinth (the Founders' Altar among the copper smelts, priest Kyra Glaukotis); the kiln shrine at Araavyna, shared with Athena of the wheel; the Smiths' Offering chapel at Ephelanum. Sworn order: the Emberforge Collective, structural ironworkers in the Imperium.

Asks of a cleric or paladin: make things well and mend what others throw away; stand by the lame and the mocked; never sign work that is not yours.

Aphrodite the Enchantress

Love, Beauty · Chaotic Good · Symbol: a scallop shell and a myrtle sprig · Holy day: the Bathing, when her image is carried to the sea, Thargelion

Goddess of love and beauty, born of the sea foam. Asetherian images show her as a tiefling, horned and smiling, which the Voidfolk take as a promise and the Truth-Flame takes as a problem. Her worship is warm and unruly: the faithful honour her by acting on generous impulse rather than by keeping rites.

Worship today. Second on Corinth's Board by sailors' vows, and queen of the Upper Fortress. In Hellarchon she has only a plinth outside the ring; in Thessalonika she has a plinth and a petition, and has been told to find a deed. Desire in a city-state is rarely private, so her priestesses are present at the negotiation of nearly every important marriage in the League.

Temples: Corinth (Aphrodite of the Rock, high priestess Lysidike the Rose); an island altar at Delphara; plinths at Hellarchon and Thessalonika; the wives of Carianea dedicate their mirrors to her at Corinth. Sworn order: the Ivory Chorus, singers who never sell what they hear.

Asks of a cleric or paladin: act on generous impulse; keep the confidences of lovers; never compel love, by spell or by contract.

Ares the Warlord

War, Strife · Chaotic Evil · Symbol: a broken spear over a vulture · Holy day: none public; a dog is killed before the Muster at Thebesieas

God of war's violence and strife, feared and little loved even by the other gods. His images show a minotaur in bronze, which is older than any Hellenorian temple. Where Athena plans the war, Ares is the war, and his worship is dangerous to the faithful and to everyone near them.

Worship today. Maintained, not loved. He is on the Roll and has no chapel in any pantheon hall. Thebesieas keeps one public altar to him, a block of black stone at the citadel gate, roofless, served by a keeper who must have lost something in war; nobody prays there, they only say the name once. Most of his shrines are hidden and his cults are hunted. Since the Treaty, unpaid veterans have started saying the name more often.

Temples: Thebesieas (the Unthanked Altar, keeper Phormion One-Arm). Sworn order: the Crimson Sigil of the Shattered Spear, who make broken blades into a creed.

Asks of a cleric or paladin: fight; never refuse a challenge; take what you win and owe no one for it. His paladins are almost always Oathbreakers or Conquerors.

Dionysus the God of Festivity

Life, Revelry · Chaotic Neutral · Symbol: an ivy-wound staff topped with a pine cone; a mask · Holy day: the Dionysia, Elaphebolion

God of wine, theatre, masks and ecstatic release, twice-born, the youngest and the loudest of the gods. His images show a satyr with a cup and a grin. He is unpredictable, and so are his faithful; he is honoured by being given room rather than by being obeyed.

Worship today. In the theatre. At Hellarchon his wooden image is carried in each Dionysia and set in the front row to watch the plays mock everyone, and his priest has the best seat by law. At Delphara he holds the mountain through the winter Silence while Apollo is away. Thessalonika admitted him to its Stoa a hundred and forty years ago "on probation" and he is still on it.

Temples: Hellarchon (Dionysus of the Theatre); Delphara (the Winter House and the Thyiades); Thessalonika; Corinth. Sworn orders: the Obsidian Veins, ecstatic mages with no records; the Obsidian Masquerade, where the mask holds the office.

Asks of a cleric or paladin: give room; break bread and wine with strangers; let the mask speak truths the face cannot.

Hades the Lord of the Underworld

Death, Wealth · Lawful Evil · Symbol: a key and a two-pronged staff · Holy day: the Naming of the Dead, Maimakterion

Lord of the dead and of the wealth under the earth, silver and dead men alike. His images show a horned duergar, stern and heavy, and the horns are why the Voidfolk were enrolled under him. His worship is a hierarchy of obligation: he rewards those who serve without question, and his priests are effective, feared and well organised.

Worship today. Last, by League custom, in every pantheon hall, on the lowest step by the west door, where the Voidfolk make their offerings because they have no shrine of their own. The Truth-Flame visits that chapel monthly. Mine-owners and moneylenders pay him quietly. Thebesieas alone keeps a public altar, because he keeps what is under the ground under it.

Temples: Thebesieas (the Hollow Gate); the last chapel at Hellarchon, Thessalonika and Corinth. No sworn order on the Roll.

Asks of a cleric or paladin: pay the dead their dues; keep every contract to its letter; collect what is owed, and never return what the earth has taken.

Hecate the Mistress of the Arcane

Arcana, Moon, Crossroads · Chaotic Evil · Symbol: a three-faced post holding two torches · Holy day: Hecate's Supper, the dark of each moon

Goddess of magic, crossroads and night, who carries torches between the worlds. Her images show a changeling with three faces, none of them her own. She stands where roads meet and where one condition becomes another, and her worship is dangerous to the faithful and to everyone near them.

Worship today. She is on the Roll and has a plinth outside Hellarchon's ring, and almost nobody offers there. Her real worship is at the edges: a supper left at a three-way crossing at the dark of the moon, a wooden three-faced post that widows set in the bare niche of Thebesieas's Dead Gate at every funeral and take home again. The Voidfolk were enrolled under her as well as under Hades.

Temples: Thebesieas (the Dead Gate niche); a plinth at Hellarchon. Sworn order: the Eclipsed Mirror, proscribed in four city-states and consulted by three of them; the seer Madame Trioditis is her known devotee.

Asks of a cleric or paladin: keep the thresholds; open nothing that cannot be opened both ways; feed the restless dead at the crossing.

Hercules the Champion

Strength, Adventure · Chaotic Good · Symbol: a knotted club on a lion's skin · Holy day: the Herakleia, every second summer

The hero of the labours: a mortal whose strength and stubbornness won him a place among the gods. His images show a goliath, and the roof of his great temple at Thebesieas had to be built round the statue. His worship is warm and unruly, and his faithful honour him by doing difficult things for other people.

Worship today. Thebesieas is his city. Its Polemarch swears on the founding hero's club, the Sacred Band swears at the tomb of his shield-bearer, and the Herakleia is wrestling, weight-carrying and a race in full armour, the winner's name cut on a lintel with room for perhaps eleven more. Elsewhere he is the god of the gymnasium, the porter and the man with too much to carry.

Temples: Thebesieas (the Temple of the Champion, priest Kallikles Iolaides; the Spring Gate); his altar at Delphara, heaped with captured spearheads instead of flowers. No sworn order; the Sacred Band under Epameinon Kleitarchos swears in his shadow.

Asks of a cleric or paladin: take on the labour nobody else will; finish what you start; atone in work, not words, for what you did in anger.

Nike the Winged Champion

Victory · Lawful Neutral · Symbol: a winged wreath · Holy day: the second crowning, last day of the Isthmian Games

Goddess of victory, daughter of the Titan Styx, who attends the gods in battle and contest. Her images show a fallen aasimar with dark wings, which troubles her worshippers less than outsiders expect: victory is not innocent. Her rites are exacting and impersonal. She does not care who deserves to win. She attends the winner.

Worship today. Athletes, generals and mercenaries. Fifth on Corinth's Board; her precinct there is a garden of living acanthus beside the stadium, where every Isthmian victor is crowned a second time. Hellarchon gives her a plinth outside the ring. A victor's first prize goes to her, by custom, and most victors keep the custom.

Temples: Corinth (Nike of the Laurel Court, priest Euagoras). Sworn order: the Order of Morning's Rise, Invictian mercenaries who take only contracts they expect to win.

Asks of a cleric or paladin: win; give the goddess the first share; never pretend a defeat was a victory in her name.

Nyx the Mistress of the Void

Darkness, Cosmic Mysteries · Neutral Evil · Symbol: a black veil set with seven stars · Holy day: the longest night, at the winter solstice

The primordial night, a power so old that even the Storm Lord declined to cross her. Her images show a drow woman veiled in stars. She is one of the few powers kept in both the Hellenorian and Invictian calendars under the same name. Her worship is quiet and self-serving: the faithful bargain for advantage and rarely say what they paid.

Worship today. She is on the Roll, has a plinth outside Hellarchon's ring and no chapel anywhere. Helionyx walled up her niche after its earthquake, deciding the night had been given too much honour in a city of the sun; people still push black olive stones into the mortar. Her followers claim she predates the pantheons and so stands outside the Tribunal's jurisdiction.

Temples: the walled niche at Helionyx; a plinth at Hellarchon. Sworn orders: the Nightweaver Syndicate, brokers of nocturnal fact (banned from Helionyx); the Crimson Pact, assassins; the Tenebral Covenant, thieves.

Asks of a cleric or paladin: keep what you learn at night; pay every bargain in full; never light a lamp where she has asked for dark.

Pan the Wild Shepherd

Nature · Chaotic Neutral · Symbol: the reed pipes; a goat's horn · Holy day: none fixed; the noon hush of high summer, when no shepherd pipes

Goat-footed god of shepherds, pastures and the wild hills, whose shout causes panic. His images show a horned centaur with a shepherd's crook. He is unpredictable, and so are his faithful; he is honoured by being given room rather than by being obeyed.

Worship today. Up the mountain. He has a plinth outside Hellarchon's ring and nothing inside any city wall, because a city is the opposite of what he is. His temples are caves on the Oros and Olympus slopes, a pipe hung on a thorn, a cheese left on a rock. Shepherds do not pipe at noon in Highsun because he is sleeping, and nobody wakes him twice.

Temples: Pan of the White Herds, the twelfth chapel at Ephelanum, which closes the year with the lambing; a plinth at Hellarchon; cave-shrines in the Oros and the Olympus range. Sworn order: the Primalhorn Kin, a horned tribal family of the high pastures.

Asks of a cleric or paladin: keep the flocks and the wild alike; let the wild be wild; never fence a spring.

Terra the Earthshaper

Land, Creation · Neutral Good · Symbol: an egg-shaped stone; a hand pressed into clay · Holy day: the Asking, when the year's first quarry face is opened

The Earth herself, mother of everything that grows and stands on her. Her images show an earth genasi, cracked like dry clay and smiling. She is one of the few powers kept in both the Hellenorian and Invictian calendars under the same name, and her faithful are expected to help where they can and are given wide latitude in how.

Worship today. Through the masons. Every temple in the League was cut by her covenant, whose rites are apologetic: permission is asked before a face is opened, and a portion of every quarry is left uncut. Crews will not work a face opened without the rite, whatever the League pays. In the countryside she is the mother who is thanked before the plough goes in.

Temples: a plinth at Hellarchon; the forgotten Serpent's Hollow under the oracle at Delphara; the altar at the common clay beds of Araavyna; quarry altars across the Oros. Sworn orders: the Geolith Artisan Covenant; the Tranquil Hand Enclave, druid-mediators of both empires.

Asks of a cleric or paladin: ask before you take; leave a portion; heal the ground you have broken.

Tyche the Goddess of Fortune

Luck, Fate · True Neutral · Symbol: a blindfolded woman with a rudder and a horn of plenty · Holy day: every new moon, when sea-loans are signed

Goddess of fortune and chance, and of the luck of cities. Her images show a genasi whose element changes with the light: fire, water, stone, air. Her priests take no side in the quarrels of the world, holding that her domain must stay in balance whoever profits.

Worship today. Bankers, factors, gamblers and farmers selling a harvest. Third on Corinth's Board, where her round shrine stands at the sea end of the Street of Counting-Houses and her image was blindfolded three centuries ago after a run of bad harvests. Thebesieas keeps her at the Grain Gate, because selling a harvest is a gamble. Every city keeps a figure of its own Fortune, crowned with its walls.

Temples: Corinth (Tyche of the Street, priestess Archippe Kybeia and the knucklebone oracle of the Kybeidai); Thebesieas (the Grain Gate). Sworn order: Fate's Spindle Circle, who argue destiny on her steps every evening.

Asks of a cleric or paladin: share a windfall; take no side in a wager; accept the throw.

The Titans

The Aetherian Ancients held the world before the three empires had gods of their own. The codex records fifty-one of them, and every tradition agrees on one point: they were put down, not killed, which is a different thing and implies a place. Asetherian tradition names the place as Vael'Tharan Mountain, warm on its worked face, warmest at night.

No empire keeps them as a state cult. Hellarchon's Tribunal leaves them off the Roll ("one does not need to recognise one's grandparents"), so their shrines have no protection in law. The Magi teach that they were "the first fires that went out" and leave it there. The Imperium struck its Titan from the calendar centuries ago. And yet their temples still stand: the Duneforged Citadel honours two beside the Imperium's gods, Helionyx worships the sun-Titan in public, and Kirimitsana has never thought to apologise for its bee-Titan. Elsewhere their worship is older and stranger than any state cult: a loaf left on a basin, a rope knotted for the wind, a room behind a toll-house where nobody admits to praying.

Adamus the Earth Keeper

Earth, Agriculture · True Neutral · Symbol: a ploughshare set in a square of green stone · Holy day: none kept; western farmers leave the last furrow unploughed at Sowing

The Titan of the settled earth: soil, boundary and the slow return of a field to rest. His priests take no side in the quarrels of the world, holding that the earth must stay in balance whoever profits from it. Where Terra is the earth as a mother, Adamus is the earth as a ledger: what is taken must be given back.

Remembered today in boundary stones and in the habit, older than any law, of leaving one furrow unturned. In the Invictian provinces old oak-groves are still called "the Earth Keeper's", and soldiers' wives in the colonies leave barley at the edge of the camp fields without knowing whose name they are using.

Temples: none in his name; the Lord of the Oaks is honoured in the grove at Aepistra. Sworn order: the Guild of the Emerald Sigil, artisans who cut balance into stone, wood and glass.

Asks of a cleric or paladin: never exhaust a field or move a boundary stone; give back what you take; weigh both sides before you act.

Anchiale the Flame Artisan

Fire, Craft · Chaotic Neutral · Symbol: a cooling ingot marked with a handprint · Holy day: the Banking, when the Citadel's forges are banked at the winter solstice

Titaness of the heat a forge holds after the flame dies down: the warmth that is still useful when everyone else thinks the work is over. She is unpredictable, and so are her faithful; she is honoured by being given room. Smiths say she lives in the hour after the pour, when a good worker fixes what went wrong.

Remembered today in the Duneforged Citadel, where the Citadel Cathedral keeps a Shrine of Anchiale under the same roof as the Forge of Vulcan. The Ju Colliseum names her patron of adaptability and cunning, and fighters who win by improvisation tip her shrine. The Citadel's alchemists keep her at the bench rather than at the altar.

Temples: the Shrine of Anchiale, Citadel Cathedral, Duneforged. Her best-known devotee is Countess Aurelie Virellarion. No sworn order.

Asks of a cleric or paladin: use what heat is left; mend before you replace; when the plan fails, improvise and do not apologise.

Andes Titan of Dawn

Light, Renewal · True Neutral · Symbol: a half-disc on a horizon line · Holy day: the first dawn after the Taken-Out Days

The Titan of beginning again: the dawn after a bad night, the field after a fire, the debt cancelled. His priests take no side, holding that renewal comes to the wicked and the good alike. He is not the dawn's light, which belongs to Eos, but its promise that the day will happen at all.

Remembered today mostly in a saying, "Andes owes you nothing", told to people who expect a fresh start as a right. Debtors released by an amnesty used to wash their faces at the first dawn after the Taken-Out Days, and in a few hill demes they still do. Since the Treaty a good many veterans have started doing it too.

Temples: none recorded. No sworn order; some dawn-rites of the Covenant of the Equinox (see Eos) began as his.

Asks of a cleric or paladin: give a second chance once; begin each day without yesterday's grudge; rebuild what was burned.

Anytus Titan of Order

Nature, Order · Lawful Neutral · Symbol: a notched tally-rod · Holy day: none kept; the Naming of the Rolls at Persemenid falls on his old day

The Titan of the order of things: seasons in sequence, the count kept, nothing missing from the roll. His rites are exacting and impersonal. He is owed correct observance, not affection, and gives order in return.

Remembered today by almost nobody under his own name. The Magi teach that the Titans were "the first fires that went out" and do not list them. Acheaorian scribes still cut a notch in a tally-rod before beginning any count, "for the counter", and cannot say which counter they mean.

Temples: a nameless niche in the pantheon at Persemenid; the old fire at Atarabad. No sworn order.

Asks of a cleric or paladin: keep the count; leave no gap in the roll; let nothing be done out of its season.

Asteria the Night Seer

Night, Prophecy · Chaotic Good · Symbol: a falling star over a floating island · Holy day: the nights of falling stars in Dustmonth

Titaness of falling stars and of oracles read in the night sky, who in the old story fled the Storm Lord by becoming a wandering island. Her worship is warm and unruly: her faithful honour her on generous impulse, and the impulse she likes best is a wish made for somebody else.

Remembered today every Dustmonth, when the falling stars come and children across Hellenoria are kept up to wish on them. Sailors say a falling star over the sea shows where an island used to be. The sky-priests of the Fallen-Star Shrine on Vael'Tharan keep a lamp beside a black stone that fell, and say her name when nobody from the Academy is listening.

Temples: the Fallen-Star Shrine, Vael'Tharan Mountain. No sworn order.

Asks of a cleric or paladin: read the sky and say what you see; help the hunted to flee; make your wishes for others.

Astraeus Titan of the Wind

Stars, Wind · True Neutral · Symbol: four winds blowing from the corners of a star chart · Holy day: dusk on the first day of the sailing season

Titan of dusk, father of the four winds and of the stars. His priests take no side: wind fills the sails of the pirate and the merchant alike. Captains buy knotted cords from wind-sellers and untie one knot for each breeze they need.

Remembered today in two places that would rather not be compared. At Thessalonika House Boreadai keep an upper room with four windows, painted with the steppe's horse-named constellations, where steppe riders bow to a sky-father with a horse's tail. On the Aeolus Reach captains leave knotted cords at a headland shrine and buy fair winds by the bag.

Temples: the Room of the Winds, Thessalonika; the headland shrine on the Aeolus Reach. His most famous worshipper is Ixion Keraunios, who prays to Zeus in public. No sworn order.

Asks of a cleric or paladin: pay for the wind you use; steer by the stars, not by rumour; carry news as fast as it will go.

Atlas the Strength Bearer

Endurance, Strength · Lawful Neutral · Symbol: a bent back beneath a ring · Holy day: none; the haulers keep the first Hauling of the year

The Titan condemned after the war of the gods to hold up the sky for ever. His rites are exacting and impersonal: the burden is owed, not loved, and carried until someone with the right to do so lets it be set down. He is the patron of the load that cannot be put aside.

Remembered today by people who carry things. Corinth's Haulway crews chant his name on the drag ropes, and the season's first ship hauled across by the magistrates is, in their eyes, his festival. Builders carve him into columns to carry roofs, and porters swear by him. No temple stands to him; he would not have time to visit it.

Temples: none; carved columns across the League, and the haulers' rope-shrine at Corinth. No sworn order.

Asks of a cleric or paladin: carry what is yours to carry; never drop a burden on someone weaker; endure, and do not complain where the load can hear.

Aura Titan of Freedom

Air, Freedom · Chaotic Neutral · Symbol: an open hand releasing a bird · Holy day: the morning a slave is freed

Titaness of the cool morning breeze, swift and unwilling to be caught. She is unpredictable, and so are her faithful; she is honoured by being given room, and the room she wants is the open air.

Remembered today at manumissions. When a Hellenorian slave is freed, the old custom is to open a door at dawn so the breeze can come in and the freedman can go out; many households still do it without knowing why. Runaways scratch a bird on the wall where they slept. The tyrants of several cities have banned the bird.

Temples: none; the bird scratched on walls from Hellarchon's Long Walls to the slave pens of Corinth. No sworn order.

Asks of a cleric or paladin: free what is caged; own no person; never stay anywhere only because you are expected to.

Clymene the Deceptive Muse

Fame, Deception · Neutral Good · Symbol: a laurelled mask · Holy day: the Reading at Thessalonika, when new works are heckled

Titaness of renown, mother of Atlas and Prometheus, whose name means fame. The codex pairs fame with deception, and her worshippers think that honest: reputation is a story told well, and a story is always a little false. Her faithful help where they can, usually by telling the right story about the right person.

Remembered today by poets, orators, heralds and anyone whose living depends on being talked about. A Hellenorian who has done something worth remembering pours a drop for Clymene before telling the story, so that it will be told after him. The Truth-Flame dislikes her; she is patron of exactly what it censors.

Temples: none; a drop poured at the Reading in Thessalonika and in every theatre. Close kin to the Muses Elder. No sworn order.

Asks of a cleric or paladin: make the good famous; let a kind lie protect a good name; never let a hero's story die untold.

Coeus Titan of Shadows

Knowledge, Shadows · Neutral Evil · Symbol: an axis-rod casting a shadow across a closed book · Holy day: none; any night the pole star is hidden by cloud

Titan of the inquiring mind and of the axis on which the heavens turn. The codex gives him knowledge and shadows: the questions that should not have been asked and the answers that came anyway. His worship is quiet and self-serving. The faithful bargain with him for knowledge and rarely say what they paid.

Remembered today as a scholar's superstition. Students at the Arcane Academy who need an answer before an examination burn a lamp in a shut cupboard for him, and stop once they graduate. Serious scholars keep doing it, seriously, and alone.

Temples: none known; the Academy at Hellarchon denies that its cellars have a second level. No sworn order. See Polus.

Asks of a cleric or paladin: ask every question; pay for every answer; never give knowledge away free.

Crius the War Strategist

Constellations, Conflict · Lawful Evil · Symbol: ram's horns around a star · Holy day: the rising of the Ram at the spring equinox

Titan of the constellations that mark the year, and of the ram that leads the stars in spring. Spring was campaigning season, so Crius is a war Titan by the calendar: the god of the war that starts on time. His worship is a hierarchy of obligation, and his priests, when he had them, were effective, feared and well organised.

Remembered today in the habit, kept by soldiers of all three empires, of opening a campaign when the Ram rises. The Invictian year begins in the old campaigning month for this reason, though no Invictian priest will say the Titan's name.

Temples: none; star-charts on every war-room wall. No sworn order.

Asks of a cleric or paladin: plan the war by the calendar; obey your superior and command your inferior; strike on the appointed day and not before.

Cronus Titan of Time

Time, Harvest · Lawful Evil · Symbol: a harvest sickle · Holy day: his midwinter feast, which survives without him in Aeterna, when masters serve their slaves and a mock-king rules each tenement

Titan of time and the harvest sickle, who overthrew his father and devoured his own children for fear of the same fate, and was overthrown by the one he missed. His worship is a hierarchy of obligation: he rewards those who serve his ends and devours those who would replace him.

Remembered today as the father of the six eldest gods, which every Hellenorian priest admits and none dwells on. In Aeterna eight grey columns behind the Basilica are the front of his temple, from the days when the Imperium was a hill town that counted its grain in a god's cellar; its vaults were the state treasury until he was struck from the calendar.

Temples: the Temple of Cronus under the Forum, Aeterna. No sworn order.

Asks of a cleric or paladin: reap what is ripe; keep time and make others keep it; let no heir take your place before you choose to give it.

Curetes Titan of Trickery

War, Trickery · Chaotic Neutral · Symbol: two bronze shields struck together · Holy day: none; the clash is made at any birth

The armed dancers who hid the infant Storm Lord from his devouring father by clashing their shields to drown his cries. The codex makes them one Titan of war and trickery: noise as cover, the feint, the dance that is also a drill. They are unpredictable, and so are their faithful.

Remembered today in two customs. Midwives in the hill demes bang pans when a child is born, "so the hungry one can't hear". And Hellenorian soldiers still learn the armed dance, leaping and striking shields in step, as drill and as prayer; the Sacred Band dances it before the Muster.

Temples: none; the dancing-floor by the Muster Ground at Thebesieas. No sworn order.

Asks of a cleric or paladin: protect the helpless by any trick that works; make noise when silence would betray; dance before you fight.

Dione the Life Seer

Prophecy, Life · Neutral Good · Symbol: an oak leaf over a dove · Holy day: the first windy day of Sowing, when the oak is first heard

Titaness of prophecy whose will was once heard in the rustling of a great oak. Her prophecies are of life rather than fate: births, healings, whether a sick man will live and a marriage bear children. Her faithful are expected to help where they can.

Remembered today at an oak in the northern foothills where barefoot priests who sleep on the ground interpret the leaves, officially for the Storm Lord. Pilgrims who cannot afford Delphara go there; the questions are humbler and so is the fee. Women asking about children bring doves.

Temples: the Speaking Oak in the foothills of the Olympus range, kept "for Zeus". No sworn order.

Asks of a cleric or paladin: tell the living what will help them live; tend the sick; listen longer than you speak.

Eos Titan of Light

Light, Dawn · Neutral Good · Symbol: a saffron veil lifted by a rose-coloured hand · Holy day: the dawns of the two equinoxes

Titaness of the dawn, who opens the gates of heaven each morning for the sun. Her faithful are expected to help where they can, and to be up early doing it. She is the gentlest of the light-Titans, and the most widely thanked without being named.

Remembered today above all at Helionyx, where she gets the first hour in the Hall of Hours, with milk and the first figs, before her brother the sun is honoured at noon. Fishermen greet her as they put out. Her old temple stood on an islet in the lagoon before the salt pans flooded it.

Temples: the first hour in the Hall of Hours, Helionyx, and the drowned Dawn Temple under the pans. Sworn order: the Covenant of the Equinox, druids of the moment between moments.

Asks of a cleric or paladin: rise early and open doors for others; keep watch through the night so that someone sees the dawn; mark every ending with a beginning.

Epimetheus the Beast Tamer

Beasts, Impulse · Chaotic Neutral · Symbol: an open jar with a bird escaping it · Holy day: none; the first day of the foaling

The Titan of afterthought, who handed every gift to the beasts before remembering mankind: claws to one, speed to another, nothing left for the naked creature on two legs. The codex calls him the Beast Tamer, and the beasts remember who was generous to them. He is unpredictable, and so are his faithful.

Remembered today by beast-handlers, drovers, horse-breakers and the menagerie keepers who supply arenas. They say "Epimetheus first" when they act on instinct with an animal, and are usually right. Everyone else uses his name for a fool who thinks after he acts.

Temples: none; a jar set over the stable door on the horse plain at Argotiko. No sworn order.

Asks of a cleric or paladin: trust the first impulse with beasts; give before you count the cost; open what others keep shut, and live with what comes out.

Eurybia Titan of Storms

Sea, Storms · True Neutral · Symbol: a steering oar beneath a rising star · Holy day: the night the storm stars rise over the water, early Fallow

Titaness of mastery over the sea: the force of the winds on the water and the rising of the constellations over it that tell a pilot when the storms will come. Her priests take no side; the storm drowns the just and the unjust, and she is the reason a good pilot knows which week to stay ashore.

Remembered today by pilots and steersmen. Poseidon is the sea's god; Eurybia is the sea's weather, and the men who read it touch the steering oar and say her name at the season's close. Her rising stars are on every pilot's chart, and the best charts, the Tyrsan ones, mark them in red.
