The Choir sings the rites at the correct times and the rains have usually come. Whether it causes them is left to philosophers who do not farm. Its timing is exact and its almanac the best in the empire. In a drought year it gets the blame. It has been driven out of three provinces in living memory and always comes back, because nobody else knows when to plant.

Houses: the Stone Choir in the Dasht-a Khaliq, whose oasis frataraka now sells the wells by the hour; singers on the Truffle Flats, blamed for every khamsin; circuits through the dry-farming belt below Mithratal.

Now: two dry years in three. The satraps want a guarantee; the Choir wants the Stone Choir's wells back.

Joining: learn the full rain-cycle and sing it at the right hour. Members are fed by the villages, in good years.

The Ten Thousand Royal guard

The King of Kings' guard has numbered exactly ten thousand for as long as there are records, because every loss is replaced the same day.

the King of Kings (sworn before Zann's roll) · The Impartial · Persemenid, the terrace · Hazarapat Aspachana Farnaka

A soldier who falls, sickens or is dismissed is replaced from a standing roll before the day is out, so the strength on parade always matches the rolls. Common Acheaorians will tell you the guard cannot die. The first regiment, the Thousand or Golden Apples, carries golden apple-weights on its spear-butts and is drawn from the old nobility, which makes it a guard and a hostage-house at once.

Houses: the first regiment along the north edge of the terrace, commanded for forty years by House Farnaka; a spearman within a throw of the King throughout the Royal Hunt in the Paradise; the yearly Naming of the Rolls in the House of the Count.

Now: the King is sixty-one, the last lion was slower, and the spearman stood closer. Farnaka controls access to the throne, and the succession is the real business of the guard.

Joining: nobles for the Thousand; for the rest, the standing roll, a waiting list some families have been on for generations.

Vaults of Equilibrium Banking order · temple-banks

Bala's temple-bank was once larger than the Mithril Reserve. It is losing, and lending to provinces that no longer pay.

Bala · The Impartial · Persemenid, the high temple-bank off the Square · Master of Scales Jahanbakht Zarrin

The Vaults lend on a god's authority, not a charter. Their notes are honoured in Acheaoria and nowhere else, while a Reserve letter of credit is good in every city on the continent. So they lend to the satrapies at rates the Reserve will not match, which wins business and an alarming book of debt from provinces that have stopped forwarding tribute.

Houses: the high temple-bank off the Square by Persemenid's bazaar, holding most of the court's debt; Master of Scales Pouran Dastvar at Atarabad, now asking for collateral that fits in a strongbox; Bahar Navabi at Mithratal, who holds more satrapal promises than any man alive; Navid Tahmasp at Persevalis, holding the court's paper on the harvest; a shrinking office in Deiperduem's Counting Ward.

Now: Jahanbakht has begun to wonder who exactly he can collect from.

Joining: priests of Bala, trained in reckoning. Depositors swear before the god.

Wheelwalkers Road merchants · the cousins

Jauhar's caravan families own no land, keep no house, and have a cousin in every city.

Jauhar · The Impartial · Atarabad, the courtyard of carts · Javid of the Wheels, the senior uncle

Wheelwalkers own no fixed property by custom and marry within allied families. A permanent house is the beginning of decline. Kinship is the business: a cousin in every caravan city is why the goods clear and the warehouse is honest, and cheating a partner means cheating a relative. A Wheelwalker convoy will go where nothing insured will.

Houses: a courtyard full of carts in Atarabad's Wind-Tower Quarter, because their headquarters may not have a roof; painted wagons camped more or less permanently on Deiperduem's Caravan Fields; the far-cousin premium charged from Qa'zshahrv'in eastward; papers carried in the name of House Suren-Pahlav when a name is needed.

Now: two caravans were lost last year beyond the Zaruk'thal notches. Javid knows which convoys will go east this year and which will not come back.

Joining: marry in. Outsiders may be adopted as "road cousins" after three journeys.

Continental orders

The Argentar Guild of bankers · the Mithril Reserve's public face

The Mithril Reserve's licensed bankers advise, assess and decide, and they remember debts.

Mercury, by courtesy · The Impartial · Deiperduem, the Counting Ward · Dominus Argentar Hildra Ironhand, for Marquis Edran Merca

An Argentar is the face the Reserve shows the world: licensed, public and answerable to the bank, not the client. They are not tellers. Each is adviser and agent at once, roles that do not always agree. Every major city has a stone branch, each run by a Dominus Argentar (often a dwarf of Clan Ironhand), guarded by Custodes, with an Arcanist-Securitas.

Branches (the Mithril Ledger): the largest outside the Citadel in Deiperduem's Counting Ward under Hildra Ironhand of House Ironhand; Odvar Ironhand at Aeterna, taking silver at eighty-six parts in the hundred; Dorgrim Ironhand at Hellarchon, holding the four-hundred-talent harbour bond; Hulda at Persemenid; Brokk at Atarabad; Odila Stonebrow at Mithratal; Ewald at Persevalis; Gunnvor at Xerastri; the mother-house of House Merca at Duneforged.

Now: discounting debased Invictian silver, and chalking every discount in Deiperduem by morning. Lady Isolde's monthly letter goes to every branch.

Joining: seven years as a counting-clerk and a bond posted by family. Argentarii are paid a salary, never a commission.

Caravan of the Gilded Horizon Merchant company · long-haul freight

Mercury's caravan crosses every border, carries anything legal, and is curious about nothing.

Mercury · The Impartial · Romulo, the Caravan Suburb · Mercator-Magister Titus Viator Celer

Mercury governs merchants, messengers, travellers and thieves, on the reasoning that they are one profession seen at different moments. The Gilded Horizon is the largest overland freight company on the continent. It carries anything lawful in the jurisdiction it is crossing, will not ask what is in a sealed crate, and will not carry the same crate twice if it caused trouble.

Houses: yards in Romulo's Caravan Suburb; the Treaty Road service to Deiperduem three times a week, with drivers lodged at the Green Lamp; eastern legs booked in Atarabad's Caravanserai Ring; the long-haul ore contract from Duneforged's Dune Mines to Mavelon; a hired niche for Mercury in Persemenid's Court of Guests.

Now: volume has trebled and escorts doubled, because the roads are full of veterans with no land.

Joining: drivers and guards by contract; partners by purchase. Every member carries a sealed waybill and a Mercurial lamp.

Ironclad Legion Military order · heavy infantry for hire

Sworn to raw force, hired by all three empires and trusted by none.

Vis · The Impartial · Deiperduem, the contract barracks · Primus Ordo Kaeso Durmius; at Deiperduem, Prefect Vibius Strabo

Heavy infantry drilled to Invictian standard that has fought for all three empires, sometimes in the same year. It claims no cause and despises companies that do. Contracts are short and rates high, and its record of honouring both is the only reason anyone tolerates it.

Houses: six hundred men at Deiperduem under Prefect Vibius Strabo, on a contract that forbids them other work in the city and ends next spring; recruiters on the Campus Hastarum, at Mavelon, and at the Malaunian hiring fair.

Now: recruiting is effortless and employment is not. Several thousand professionals under arms, unpaid and owing no allegiance, are a problem every capital has noticed and none has solved. Three embassies and one unnamed bidder want the Deiperduem contract.

Joining: pass the drill and sign. Pay is by contract, with a death-bond to the family.

The Chyrsus Syndicate Guild of merchants · tax-farmers

The closest thing on the continent to a cartel, and it does not pretend otherwise.

Wealth and Influence · The Impartial · Deiperduem, the toll-house on Interest Lane · Factor Oribasios Kell (public face)

The Syndicate bids for what states would rather not run: tax collection in difficult provinces, harbour dues, tolls on the dry bed of the Xeruezcho Canal. It pays a fixed sum up front and keeps the difference, so it has every reason to squeeze and none to care what follows. All three empires use it, all three complain, and none can stop.

Houses: the toll-house across Interest Lane from the Mithril Reserve in Deiperduem's Counting Ward, holding the city's tolls on a long contract; agents in the aisles of Aepistra's basilica, holding the province's tax farm, the most resented fact in the city; partners in House Ovinia at Aeterna; toll-collectors on the Treaty Road and the old canal.

Now: contracts have grown longer since the Treaty, and Kell is lobbying to extend Deiperduem's before anyone reads it again.

Joining: buy a share. Agents are paid a percentage of what they collect.

Eleusinian Mysteries Religious order · death and rebirth

Initiates go down in the dark and come up someone else, and do not say what they saw.

Spiritual rebirth (Demeter and the Maiden) · The Virtuous · the Elysian Plains, the Register Stone · Hierophant Eumolpos the Twelfth

Guardians of ancient rites who shepherd souls through death and rebirth. Initiation is open to anyone who speaks a civilised tongue and has shed no blood unpurified: slave, citizen, Acheaorian or Invictian. The rite is to shed the old self. The Mysteries are continental because death is, and the treaty has tripled their pilgrims.

Houses: the Register Stone on the Elysian Plains, where messages for the dead are posted in the hope someone inside will pass them on; a hall of initiation near the Smiling Strand in Nereid's Veil; initiates in every city, unmarked.

Now: veterans want to be initiated in thousands, to be rid of what they did. The Hierophant wants the rite kept small and slow.

Joining: purification, a fast, the procession, and the night in the hall. Initiates pay what they can and never speak of it.

Mithradaic Cult Religious order · soldiers' brotherhood

A soldiers' mystery of endurance and brotherhood, held in caves, with grades from Raven to Father.

Strength and Brotherhood (the Covenant-spirit) · The Virtuous · Mithratal, the Grotto of the Bull · Pater Patrum Ardavast Mehrdad

A martial mystery cult that forges warriors in body and soul through endurance and sacrifice. Brotherhood is its altar and pain its prayer. Members pass through seven grades in painted caves, and a man's grade outranks his rank: legionaries, Ironclad Oath troopers and Valiant skirmishers meet below ground as equals. It spread through the armies in the war, in all three, and came home with the veterans.

Houses: the Grotto of the Bull below Mithratal, where it began with the old covenant-spirit; caves near the camps of Aeterna, Xerastri and Thebesieas; a cell among the Ironclad Legion at Deiperduem.

Now: it is the one place veterans of opposing armies drink together. The Legates want to use it; the Fathers will not have it.

Joining: men who have borne arms; ordeals by heat, cold and fasting. Brothers pay for each other's funerals.

The Circle of the Whispering Leaves Religious order · grove-keepers

They keep the small sacred groves of three empires, the ones too modest for any priesthood to defend.

Nature and Harmony · The Virtuous · Marshroot Grove · Elder Linden of the Hush

A religious order that communes with nature's quiet truths and believes harmony is found in stillness, in rustling leaves and drifting pollen. In practice they are the wardens of the thousand little groves the war nearly cut down: the village oak, the spring-copse, the shrine-thicket at a crossroads. They plant, they mend, and they sit very still until a woodcutter feels foolish.

Houses: the mother-grove at Marshroot Grove in the Maeotis Helos; a hut at Willowheart; walking wardens in the Araucarian forest villages of Nemorus and Alderpool.

Now: veteran colonies need timber and are felling sacred copses no register records. The Circle wants every small grove written down in the Oathbound Sanctum's register, which is not a druid's instinct.

Joining: tend a sapling for a year without speaking of it. Members carry no iron blade.

The Collegium of the Sacred Sight Magical society · seers

It trains seers and sells futures, whether or not you are ready for them.

Divination and Prophecy · The Virtuous · Delphara, the Exegetes' Stoa · Lysandra Anthemis, the Exegete (patron)

A magical society devoted to prophecy: omens in smoke, stars and silence. Its seers are trained in all three traditions (Invictian augury, Hellenorian oracle, Acheaorian dream-almanac) and hired by anyone. It is the only school on the continent that grades prophecy by outcome, and it fails half its students.

Houses: the stoa of the Exegetes at Delphara, where Lysandra Anthemis examines graduates; a seers' hall at Deiperduem, the only place an Acheaorian may study augury; students at the Arcane Academy of Hellarchon.

Now: three of its best seers had the same vision this year, of a third sun. The Collegium wants to know whether that is a prophecy or a leak.

Joining: make three verifiable predictions in a year. Students pay fees; graduates tithe.

The Veiled Caste Philosophical circle · anonymous government

They hold that power is only stable in the hands of people nobody can name, and keep proving it.

Secrecy and Power · The Impartial · Deiperduem (as far as anyone knows) · unnamed, on principle

Visible authority can be flattered, threatened and replaced, they argue, so durable government is anonymous. The Caste does not conspire so much as advise, everywhere: Legates, oligarchs, satraps. Members may not hold office, which they call principle and their critics call a way of avoiding consequences. The awkward part is that the argument is partly right. The Mithril Reserve, the Shadow Court and the Amphictyony all work as the Caste says they should.

Houses: none it admits. Advisers at Deiperduem, Corinth and Persemenid; a hand in the Foundlings' House at Deiperduem.

Now: the lot for the next Arbiter of Deiperduem is in four months, and the Caste has influenced the last two draws.

Joining: one does not apply. A member is someone who stops being mentioned.

The Scholars Philosophical circle · rift-classifiers

They divided the rifts into Bound, Shifting and Anchored, and their own files have holes in them.

no patron · The Impartial · Deiperduem, the Rift Register · Magistra Rerum Fractarum Theodora Aletheia

The authority that sorted the rifts into Bound Rifts, Shifting Rifts and Anchored Rifts, and the reason anyone talks about the Phenomenon in an orderly way. Their records are redacted in places. A body that catalogues holes in reality collects findings it would rather not publish, and the gaps in its own documents say as much as the entries.

Houses: the Rift Register at Deiperduem, open to all three empires by treaty; classifiers at Vael'Tharan Mountain, who think the Thin Places are a permanent Bound Rift and want to anchor one; teams at Eronis, copying the murals at dawn, noon and dusk and getting three texts.

Now: a fourth category, which nobody will name in public.

Joining: survive a season at a rift and write it up. Fellows are paid by the three empires jointly, which means late.

Children of the Sacred Forge Artisans · Titanic

Hyperion's smiths shape flame as worship, and each anvil-stroke is meant to echo the first light.

Hyperion · The Virtuous · a hidden forge in the Cloudspine · Forge-Mother Aurelia Thea

A Titan-sworn artisan order that predates the empires' pantheons. Their craft is steeped in tradition: every piece begins with fire lit from sunlight through a crystal, and is quenched in water drawn before dawn. They make little and sell less. A blade of theirs is said to hold the light of the morning it was made.

Houses: a forge in a cave on the Cloudspine above the Duneforged Citadel, tolerated by House Caerthain; a stall, once a year, at the Midsummer fair of Helionyx.

Now: the high metals of the Thin Places have begun to be mined. The Children want it stopped and cannot say why without saying what they are.

Joining: carry the sun-crystal from Helionyx to the forge without letting it see shade. Children own their tools and nothing else.

Guild of the Emerald Sigil Artisans · Titanic

Adamus's carvers cut symbols that order whatever they are carved on: a door that stays shut, a beam that does not rot.

Adamus · The Virtuous · Romulo, the Guild Square · Sigillarius Primus Ottone Verdecchi

Artisans who build divine intention into design. Their sigils are functional and beautiful, channelling the orderly vision of their Titan into lintels, seals, weights and boundary-stones. Every guild in Romulo's Guild Square uses an Emerald Sigil mark somewhere on its door, and very few know where it came from.

Houses: a workshop off the Guild Square at Romulo, which cut the seals for the Hall of Weights; a sigil-carver on retainer at the Treaty Hall of Deiperduem; carvers at the Mithril Reserve's branches, whose vault doors carry their marks.

Now: the master weights at Romulo need re-sealing for the Weighing of the Standards, and three cities want the Guild to swear their copies match.

Joining: carve a sigil that holds a door against a strong man for a night. Members are paid per mark and sworn never to carve the same mark twice.

Hammer of Lumina Forging order · Titanic

A sacred forge where sunlight becomes steel, worked unseen beneath Helios's own city.

Helios · The Virtuous · Helionyx, under the solar precinct · the Lightsmith, Phaethousa Kerkopis

The Hammer's artisans revere Helios and labour out of sight, tempering blades in focused noon light. Their weapons are made for those who fight darkness, and they are particular about who that is. Honour, they say, is tempered in the same fire.

Houses: the secret forge under the solar precinct at Helionyx, tempering blades in the arc's focused noon light; a contact among the Phaethontidai, House Phaethontidai, who guard the precinct.

Now: the Hammer has begun forging again in numbers, which it has not done since the war. Someone has ordered a great many blades for fighting things that are not men.

Joining: a vigil at noon on the solstice, eyes open. Members take no coin; patrons give metal.

Covenant of the Equinox Druidic circle · Titanic

Eos's druids walk the line between light and dark, and mark the two days a year when they are equal.

Eos · The Impartial · the Elysian Plains, the Ring of Heroes · Dawnwarden Aurora Kalyke

A druidic circle that honours the balance between light and dark, observing the turning of the year and the celestial balance on which they believe the world rests. At each equinox they hold the line, literally: a chain of druids across the land at dawn, from the plains to the sea.

Houses: the Ring of Heroes stone circle on the Elysian Plains; a dawn-station on the coast near Parvaz Cay; members in all three empires who walk to the line twice a year.

Now: last equinox the chain broke at three places. The Covenant wants enough walkers to close it this spring.

Joining: stand the dawn line at an equinox. No dues; members owe the walk.

Verdant Spearhold Fighters and mercenaries · Titanic

Selene's spear-dancers fight by moonlight and defend sacred lands for those who cannot.

Selene · The Virtuous · the Maeotis Helos · Spear-Mother Menippe of the Reeds

Warriors who fight with a grace born of moonlight and the rhythm of nature, mixing precision with instinct. They hire out to defend sacred land: a grove, a spring, a burial mound. They fight only at night and only on ground they have been asked to keep.

Houses: a stilt-camp in the Maeotis Helos near Marshroot Grove, the borderland that pays tribute to whoever asks; spear-holds hired by the Circle of the Whispering Leaves; a few contracted to the Verdant Sentinel Order at Nemibano, who are uncomfortable about it.

Now: the veteran colonies are claiming sacred ground. The Spearhold has more contracts than spears.

Joining: dance the spear-form under a full moon without a misstep. Pay is in kind, by the guarded place.

Forge of the Creators Secret enclave · Titanic

Every creation is a prayer to Ophion: a hidden workshop of mages and smiths hammering gods' dreams into form.

Ophion · The Virtuous · unknown; suspected in the Duneforged deep mines · the Demiurge (title)

A secretive enclave in which divine sparks start inventions. The Forge melds magic and metal to remake the world one artifact at a time. Its members are sculptors of destiny, and its pieces turn up unsigned: the bronze guardian Talos that walks Duneforged's wall is rumoured to be one, and so is a door in Mycarion that no thief has opened.

Houses: none admitted. Seen at the Lower Mines of the Duneforged Citadel, where Overseer Tarnak needs the hum explained, and in the workshops of House Virellarion.

Now: to finish something. The hum in the Lower Mines has grown louder for five years.

Joining: make a thing that surprises its maker. Members take a new name and give up their old works.

Expansion

Gazetteer of Sites

Aeterna City

Sites within and just beyond the sacred line of Aeterna, the capital. Districts referred to are on the city page: the Arx, the Forum, the Campus Hastarum.

The Aeterna Garrison Legionary camp

Codex now: The legion's camp at Aeterna, kept outside the sacred line as Invictian law requires.

A rectangular fortress on the standard plan at the north end of the Campus Hastarum: four gates, two crossing streets, the headquarters where they meet. It sits outside the sacred line because nothing armed may sit inside it. Beside it the Obsidian Phalanx keeps its ancient quarters, sworn to Bellona rather than the state, and between the two sprawl the Legates' retinue camps and the Tent Rows, where some twelve thousand discharged men sleep under old legion leather.

Now: the capital legion, the Praetorian Custodians, holds the camp under Legatus Varus Decianus, loyal to the Dominus Militum and to nobody else. The man who actually keeps it fed is the Praefectus Castrorum, Marcus Ulpius, a mountain dwarf who counts bricks the way priests count prayers. He has shored two of the Aqua's failing spans from camp stores.

Found here: a sutlers' row at the south gate selling army surplus nobody admits was surplus: hobnailed boots (4 sp), mail shirts with someone else's name scratched inside (40 gp), and good legion vinegar wine.

Hook: Ulpius needs a civilian party to audit the timber yard, because every soldier he sends comes back with the same figures and he no longer believes them.

The Amber Stalls Market lane

Codex now: A narrow lane of jewellers' booths in the capital where northern amber is polished, set and sold with a story attached.

A lane barely wide enough for two buyers to pass, running along the gates of the Circus Aeternus under the commons' hill. Every booth works northern amber and every piece comes with a story: a fly caught in sap, a tear wept by a grieving sister, a lump a legionary carried home from the cold. The stories are lies. The eyes behind them are the best in the capital.

Now: the lane is a collegium of nineteen booths under Gavia Rufilla, Mistress of the Lane, who has sold amber for forty years and can price a piece by touching it to her teeth. The collegium pays the aediles a flat fee and polices its own scales.

Found here: worked amber (a plain bead 5 sp, a carved pendant 15 gp, a piece with a whole insect 50 gp and up), black jet set beside it for contrast, pumice for polishing, and loupes for rent at a copper an hour. Bring a loupe and a friend.

Hook: a new booth sells amber with no flaws and no inclusions. It is glass. A dozen senators' wives are wearing it, and Rufilla wants the seller gone before the collegium's name goes with him.

The Basilica of Aeterna Law courts

Codex now: Aeterna's hall of law: courts, contracts and the property registers under one roof.

A long hall of grey columns on the Forum's flank, roofed in timber that has been replaced eleven times, with the magistrate's apse at the far end. Four courts sit at once, divided by curtains, so a pleader in one case can hear his rival's lawyer losing in the next. Cases come from across the Imperium. Contracts are witnessed in the side aisles. The property registers fill the galleries above, and that is where the city's bankers first saw the coin going light, a year before the Temple of Juno said so.

Now: the urban praetor, Numerius Tadius Crassipes, presides: a careful man who has never ruled against a Legate and has never had to. The registers are kept by freedmen clerks, among them Hermia, who files the aqueduct invoices.

Found here: a notary at every pillar (a witnessed contract, 2 sp); certified copies of any registered deed (1 gp, three days); and the best gossip in the capital about who is selling land, and why.

Hook: a patrician hires the party to sit in the gallery for a week and note every estate registered to a veteran of one particular legion.

The Baths of Aeterna Public baths

Codex now: Aeterna's public baths, where the city does its bathing, its gossip and most of its business.

Not one bath but forty-odd, from the vaulted Thermae of the Chair below the palace hill to neighbourhood bath-houses the size of a tavern. All follow the same sequence of cold, warm and hot rooms over furnace-heated floors, and all are free or nearly so. They are where Aeterna actually lives. The tenements have no room for business, gossip or politics, so the baths have all three.

Now: the great thermae are run for the Praefectus Urbi by a freedman contractor, Ampliatus the balneator, who knows which senator bathes at which hour and has never once been asked to testify. The furnaces burn forty cartloads of wood a day. The water comes from the Aqua Aeterna, which is why the hot pool has started running brown after rain.

Found here: entry for a quarter-copper; oil, strigil and towel for a copper; a masseur for 2 sp; a hired reader of the day's notices for 1 sp; and in the exercise yard, anyone who wants to be found.

Hook: a client of the party's patron is stabbed in the hot room in front of forty naked witnesses, none of whom saw anything.

The Forum of Aeterna Civic square

Codex now: Aeterna's civic square, where law, market and religion share one pavement.

The original that every Invictian forum copies, and too small for the city it serves. Seven centuries of temples and basilicas hem in the pavement; the Curia of the Senate closes the north end behind bronze doors; the speakers' platform stands between law and temple, studded with bronze rams from ships taken in the war. Proclamations are read here, the price of bread is argued about here in public, and the Annona's shortfalls are first felt here in the form of a crowd.

Now: the two aediles of the year keep order and the market weights. The senior, Lucius Cornificius Gallo, is twenty-nine, ambitious and frightened, because the dole queue now reaches the Forum when the portico on the commons' hill overflows. The Vigiles post a squad at each corner on dole days.

Found here: public notices on whitened boards; letter-writers (2 cp a page); bankers' tables at the foot of the Bankers' Stair, changing foreign coin at a posted rate; and a wine-shop on the south side where clients wait for their patrons.

Hook: someone paints a number on the speakers' platform each night. It drops by one every day. The aediles think it counts the days of grain left in the granaries. It does.

The Geese Court Temple court

Codex now: A white-paved court on the capital's hill where the sacred geese are kept, the swans glide on a royal pond and the dormice are fattened for feasts.

A court of white paving in Juno's precinct on the Arx. Along one wall is the long pen of the sacred geese, fed each morning at public expense and credited with having once woken the guards and saved the city. A pond at the far end holds silent swans. A row of clay jars along the kitchen wall holds dormice, fattened on walnuts for the feast days. A visitor who is rude to a goose is rude to the goddess, and is fined accordingly.

Now: the court belongs to the Temple of Juno. Its head priestess, Junia Tertulla, Keeper of the Standard, checks the geese herself before dawn. Their daily keeper is Philemon, an old Hellenorian-born freedman who talks to them in his own tongue and is believed by the geese, if by nobody else.

Found here: open on feast days. Goose-down charms for children (1 sp), blessed by the priestesses; a honeyed dormouse at the Feast of Juno, for those with an invitation.

Hook: the geese have fallen silent. Tertulla says it means nothing, has doubled the night watch, and is quietly hiring outsiders to sit up with the birds.

The Imperial Mint Mint

Codex now: A fortified workshop beside the temple of warning where the empire's coin is struck and every ounce of precious metal is weighed twice.

A fortified, windowless workshop inside Juno's precinct, the goddess of warning lending her name to the coin. Bullion comes up the Bankers' Stair under escort; assayers test every bar; dies are struck by hand in rooms lit by lamps behind glass. Every worker is searched at the door and again at the exit, and wears a numbered lead search-tag that is handed back at night.

Now: the Quaestor of the Mint, Gnaeus Laberius Asellus, strikes the coin that the quarterly Assay then weighs on Juno's steps. He is plump, smooth and well liked, has struck the coin lighter every quarter for ten years, and has an answer for every question about it.

Found here: nothing for sale. The temple's front hall shows a specimen of every issue in gold, silver and the pale electrum kept for ceremonial strikes, and the guards watch the visitors, not the coins. Down the hill, Odvar Ironhand of the Mithril Reserve posts the true silver content on a slate by his door: eighty-six parts in a hundred this quarter.

Hook: a worker's search-tag has gone missing, and someone has been using it to walk in at night.

The Sacred Line of Aeterna Sacred boundary

Codex now: The ancient boundary inside which no soldier may bear arms, which is why Aeterna's legions camp outside it.

A line of knee-high white stones, older than the walls, running through gardens and alleys and once through a tenement's ground floor, where a stone stands in a cobbler's shop. Inside it no soldier may bear arms and no army may camp; the only lawfully armed body is the Vigiles. A Legate lays down his command at the stones before he walks to the Senate. That one rule has shaped eight hundred years of the capital's politics.

Now: the line is the augurs' business. Augur Cnaeus Volteius Pulcher walks it each spring with a crooked staff, re-marks any stone that has shifted, and fines anyone who has built over one. Ten Vigiles stand at the Via Sacra crossing where Legates disarm. Five years after the Concord, everyone is watching to see whether someone steps over under arms.

Found here: at the main crossings, licensed sword-keepers hold a retinue's blades for a copper each, and take a further fee for not noticing a kept dagger.

Hook: one stone on the commons' hill has been moved a hundred paces inward overnight, putting a veterans' tavern outside the line. The owner wants it put back before someone arms his customers lawfully.

Romulo City

Sites of Romulo, the founding city and merchant capital, most of them on or beside the Founder's Forum.

The Basilica of Romulo Law courts and charter vaults

Codex now: Romulo's hall of law: courts, contracts and the property registers under one roof.

Low, like everything inside the old wall, and longer than it looks, because most of it is underground. The hall itself is plain: a single court, an apse, benches polished by nine centuries of litigants. Beneath it run the charter vaults, where a dozen guilds keep their founding documents and the Imperium keeps its own. Once a year the charters are read aloud in full, over three days, to a thin audience of old men and the occasional law student doing penance.

Now: the court has become the Imperium's contract registry. Every great contract involving a foreign cargo must be sealed against the master standards at the Hall of Weights and then entered here. The registrar, Marcia Vettia Prisca, a cousin of the Praefectus Ponderum, keeps the entry-books and charges by the line. Knights of the Order of the Silver Flame guard the vault stairs.

Found here: registered contracts (a fortieth part of the declared value, the same as the seal-fee); certified extracts of any guild charter (5 gp); and a reading room where scholars may consult the founding documents under a knight's eye.

Hook: a Farshore factor's contract has been entered with the wrong date, which voids it. He swears it was right when he left the hall.

The Baths of Romulo Public baths

Codex now: Romulo's public baths, where the city does its bathing, its gossip and most of its business.

Modest by the capital's standards and built low, because nothing inside the old wall may rise above two storeys. Romulans regard the scale as a virtue and the capital's thermae as vulgar. The rooms are the standard sequence, cold to hot, with a small exercise yard shaded by a fig older than most of the city's families. The mosaics in the warm room show the founding, in a version that leaves out the parts Romulans prefer not to discuss.

Now: the baths were built for a few thousand residents and now take the factors, caravan-masters and clerks of the swollen suburb as well. The bath-keeper, Gaius Ennius Felix, has started charging foreigners double and Romulans nothing, and nobody has stopped him. The best deals in the merchant capital are struck on the warm-room benches before they are sealed at the Hall of Weights.

Found here: entry for a copper (two for foreigners); a Tyrsan masseur who also sells charts; Khemareti linen towels for hire; and, from the attendants, the day's sealing list before it is posted.

Hook: two rival Farshore factors have both been told they will be sealed first tomorrow. They are sharing the hot room tonight.

The Forum of Romulo Civic square

Codex now: Romulo's civic square, where law, market and religion share one pavement.

The oldest forum in the Imperium and the smallest: a market square that became sacred by being first. The pavement is worn into hollows where the stalls stood for nine centuries. The Founder's Hut stands at one end, the basilica on the long side, and a speakers' stone that is only a stone, from which every magistrate of the Imperium is expected to speak once. Behind it, through a single arch, lies the colonnaded Guild Square, where the money is.

Now: the Forum is busier than at any time since the founding, because every cargo registered behind it brings its factor through the arch. The Dux, Marcus Horatius Barbatus, seventy-nine, sits on a bench by the speakers' stone each morning and is greeted by everyone; his granddaughter Horatia Minor stands behind him and answers the letters. The market weights are checked daily against the masters.

Found here: the most honest scales in the Imperium; olives, bread and wine at prices fixed by custom; and copies of the standard weights in bronze (a set, 30 gp) sold with a certificate.

Hook: a stallholder's bronze weight, certified last spring, now weighs light against the masters. Every weight sold that season may be wrong.

The Founder's Hut Shrine

Codex now: A humble hut, reverently rebuilt for nine centuries, said to stand where the Imperium was founded.

Wattle, daub and thatch, one room, a hearth-stone and a door too low for a tall man. It is certainly not the original. It is rebuilt in the same form whenever it decays, and its thatch is renewed each spring by the Vestals, who weave the first sheaf themselves. It is said to mark where the founder of the Imperium lived when the Imperium was a market town with ambitions. The Founding ends here each year after a full day of processions, and every Invictian magistrate is expected to attend at least once.

Now: the hut's guardian is the Rex Sacrorum, Aulus Pinarius Natta, the king-priest who keeps the rites no one else remembers. A Vestal sits by the door from dawn to dusk. Veterans walking the pilgrim road begin here; the hut is the first punch on their lead tokens.

Found here: a pilgrim's token (2 cp), punched at the door; a pinch of thatch from last year's roof, sold by the Vestals' servants for a silver piece and widely considered good for a marriage.

Hook: the spring thatching found a sealed clay jar buried under the hearth-stone. The Rex Sacrorum has forbidden anyone to open it, and three Legates have asked to be present when someone does.

The Old Wall of Romulo City wall

Codex now: Romulo's ancient wall of mortarless stone, walked each year in procession to re-mark the sacred line.

Grey stone laid without mortar, shoulder-high in places and three men high in others, its blocks fitted so close a knife blade will not go between them. It has not been fortified beyond that since the Imperium grew strong enough that fortifying the founding city would be an insult. Inside it, nothing may stand above two storeys. Outside it, in five years, the caravan suburb has gone up four.

Now: once a year the wall is walked in procession and the sacred line re-marked, with the Verdant Sentinel Order as wardens. The Order's local warden, Sentinel Caeso Ramnius, is responsible for the wall's upkeep, which means arguing with suburb landlords who keep leaning new buildings against it. Romulo has a town guard and no garrison, which is a statement rather than an oversight.

Found here: the Boundary Walk each spring, when anyone may follow the procession; wall-stone chips sold illegally in the suburb as luck-charms (1 sp each, a fine of 10 gp if caught).

Hook: a suburb landlord has cut a doorway through the wall into his new inn. Ramnius wants it bricked up; the landlord has a Legate's letter permitting it.

Aepistra City

Sites of Aepistra, the provincial capital on the Via Septentrionalis, a grid city laid out on the old camp. See the Principia, the Terminus Yards and the Castra Nova.

The Aepistra Garrison Legionary fortress

Codex now: The legion's camp at Aepistra, kept outside the sacred line as Invictian law requires.

The Castra Nova stands two miles down the road from the city: a legionary fortress on the standard plan, stone-walled, with a gate on each side and the headquarters at the crossing of the two streets. Around it lies the "Legate's Mile", new allotments ditched and measured for his veterans and recorded in his own name rather than the Imperium's. The city's walls are ceremonial. This is where the power is.

Now: Legatus Augusti Quintus Herennius Strabo, "the Squint", commands the province's legions from here and is generous to his men. The camp's day-to-day belongs to his Praefectus Castrorum, Titus Vibennius Crus, a one-eyed veteran who signs the land grants and remembers every man's name. The Order of the Silver Flame has opened a chapter house within sight of the gate.

Found here: recruiting tables (signing bounty 5 gp and a promise of land); a camp market where the canabae traders sell to the soldiers; and the best farriers in the province, borrowed from House Ollovica.

Hook: a surveyor measuring the Legate's Mile has disappeared with his chains and his book. The Dux wants the book; so does the Legate.

The Basilica of Aepistra Law courts and tax office

Codex now: Aepistra's hall of law: courts, contracts and the property registers under one roof.

A long brick hall on the forum's north side, more lavishly marbled than the capital's, because the local elite built it to prove they are more Invictian than Aeterna. The magistrate's apse is at the east end. As a provincial capital, Aepistra's basilica handles tax assessment for the whole province, and the Chyrsus Syndicate's tax-farmers sit at tables in its aisles, the single most resented fact in the city.

Now: the Iuridicus Septimia Vera runs the Assize and hears the appeals from the Invictian half of Ephelanum, with a Hellenorian-speaking clerk at her elbow. The Syndicate's factor, Atinius Lucrio, holds the tax farm and is polite, punctual, and loathed. The Golden Harvest Covenant pickets the steps on assessment days.

Found here: tax receipts (keep them); notaries; appeal petitions (2 gp to lodge); and the Ephelanum files, which a scholar of the Condominium can read for a fee and a reference.

Hook: a farmer's tax receipt has been declared forged by the Syndicate. If it is, he loses his farm; if it is not, the Syndicate's ledger is wrong.

The Baths of Aepistra Public baths

Codex now: Aepistra's public baths, where the city does its bathing, its gossip and most of its business.

Built to the standard plan and more lavishly than the capital's, by a local elite anxious to be thought more Invictian than Aeterna. The new hot room has a ceiling painted with the gods of the Imperium in the act of approving of Aepistra. There is an old bath as well, behind the canabae, where the regional tongue is spoken in the steam and nobody pretends.

Now: the new baths were paid for by Duumvir Tiberius Flavius Brannocus, whose name is cut over the door in letters a foot high. He flinches when anyone calls him Brannoc. The old bath is kept by Senna Ollovica's cousin Dagda the stoker, who heats it with horse-dung cakes and charges nothing to anyone who speaks the old tongue.

Found here: at the new baths, entry for a copper, oil and a slave to scrape you for another; at the old bath, a steam that smells of stables and the best local news in the province.

Hook: Brannocus's inscription has been chiselled overnight to read "Brannoc". He wants the vandal found before the Founding Day procession passes the door.

The Forum of Aepistra Civic square

Codex now: Aepistra's civic square, where law, market and religion share one pavement.

Exactly where the surveyors put it, at the crossing of the two main streets, on the footings of the old camp headquarters. Basilica to the north, the Capitolium to the west, speakers' platform between, colonnades all round. A citizen of Aeterna can find the law courts here without asking directions, and that is the point. The old shrine of the standards is now the Dux's chancery, and the Ephelanum files fill its back rooms.

Now: Dux Marcus Insteius Fronto governs the city from the chancery, holds audience on the platform each market day, and has filled none of the posts that matter, because the Legate filled them first. The Founding Day boundary-plough ends here, with the Duumvir at the plough handles.

Found here: the provincial market every ninth day (horses, grain, wool, Treaty Road silk); official notices, including the Legate's land-grant lists; and public scribes who write in both Invictian and the regional tongue.

Hook: the Legate's Games of the Province are to be held in the forum this year, and someone is selling forged seat-tokens with the Dux's seal.

The Relay Station of Aepistra Road station

Codex now: The Cursus Legionis station at Aepistra, where official riders change horses on the Imperium's roads.

Stables for sixty horses, a posting house, a strongroom for dispatch bags and a tower with a signal-beacon, at the east gate in the Terminus Yards. Official riders change horses here on the Via Septentrionalis, tax documents and orders go through day and night, and beside it the new caravanserai receives the Treaty Road caravans from Atarabad. Whoever controls the station reads the province's correspondence first.

Now: the station master is Aulus Pescennius Scaurus, an old courier who rode the war roads for thirty years and takes his seals seriously. He has not been able to keep the Legate's men out of the posting house. The remounts come from Senna Ollovica's herds, which makes her the one person in the province both sides must keep happy.

Found here: official post only, in theory; in practice a private letter travels in a courier's bag for 5 sp a stage, and a fast horse can be hired for a gold piece and a promise.

Hook: a courier bag from Ephelanum has reached the station opened and resealed. Scaurus wants to know whether the Legate's men, the Syndicate or the Hellenorians did it.

Mavelon City

Sites of Mavelon (Mavaholm to the Mavari), the cliff-ringed caldera port where a Reiks and a Dux rule as equals. See the High Crescent, the Ravines and the Outer Flank.

The Basilica of Mavelon Law courts

Codex now: Mavelon's hall of law: courts, contracts and the property registers under one roof.

A white hall on the south rim beside the Praetorium, its long side open to the caldera so that litigants can see the ships they are suing over. Most cases are guild disputes: patents of method, apprentices poached, a bridge-guild's mark cut by the wrong hand. Anything that crosses the halves of the city goes instead to the Gate Court in the gatehouse, and the basilica's magistrates resent every case they lose to it.

Now: the presiding magistrate is Quintus Fadius Rufinus, the Imperial iudex, who also sits in the Gate Court beside the Mavari doomsman. He spends mornings here and afternoons there, and is the only man in the city who knows both law books by heart. The ship registers are kept here too: every hull launched, who built it, who paid the keel-silver.

Found here: registration of a ship (3 gp) or a Farshore cargo's landing (a small fee, before it goes to Romulo for sealing); guild patents; and a lawyer for any trade dispute for 1 gp a day.

Hook: House Sentia has brought a suit against the Skeldings for "unlawful threats". Rufinus says it belongs in the Gate Court. Sentia says it does not, because the threat was made on the south side.

The Baths of Mavelon Public baths

Codex now: Mavelon's public baths, where the city does its bathing, its gossip and most of its business.

Fed not by furnaces but by the volcano: hot springs rise under the south rim and are led through lead pipes into rooms cut half into the cliff. The hot pool smells of sulphur and is hotter than any bath in the Imperium; the cold pool is the sea, through an arch at the bottom of the steps. The baths open before dawn for the forge shifts, and the arsenal's men come up black and go down grey.

Now: the baths are kept by the arsenal under the Praefectus Fabrum, Titus Gellius Naso, because the hot springs also feed the arsenal's steaming-sheds for bending hull planks. The bath-keeper, Hrodgard the Steamer, is Mavari, which is the one Imperial post on the south side always held by a north-sider, by an old clause of the Oath at the Gate.

Found here: free to arsenal workers, a copper to anyone else; sulphur mud for the skin (1 sp a pot); and the forge shifts' gossip about which slips will be idle next month.

Hook: the hot spring has turned scalding twice this month, and a man was boiled in the night pool. Hrodgard says the mountain is angry. Naso says someone has been tampering with the valves.

The Dyers' Fields Dye-plant fields

Codex now: Red and yellow strips on the river flats where the city's cloth-makers grow their own colours and stain their hands for a living.

Long alternate strips of red and yellow on the island's outer slope, where the ash soil runs gently down to the open sea. The red is madder, dug and dried in its third year; the yellow is weld, pulled whole and bundled for the vats. The families who harvest them have hands stained for life, and the dyers' guild wears the colour like a badge. Between them they turn out the red of every legion's cloak and the yellow of every Mavari feast-shirt.

Now: the guild is run by Mistress Rubria Tinctor, whose family has dyed the navy's sails for a century, and whose forearms are red to the elbow. The guild hates Tyrsan purple with a passion, because the Farshore dye-merchants now land their murex cloth at the Quays and sell it cheaper than the guild can sell red.

Found here: the fields are open and a visitor can watch the digging. Dried madder root (2 sp a pound), weld bundles, and cloth dyed red or yellow (from 5 sp a yard). The vats are behind a wall and a guild contract.

Hook: a guild member has been selling dyed cloth that fades after a month, and the navy has bought a season's sails from him.

The Eleven Bridges of Mavelon Bridges

Codex now: Mavelon's pride: eleven bridges over a fast river, each kept by a guild that cuts its mark on the parapet.

Eleven gorges cut the cliff-city from rim to water, and over each is a bridge older than it looks: arches of pumice concrete, timber spans, one a chain bridge that sways in the wind. Each is maintained by a guild that carves its mark into the parapet. Three cross wholly on the north side and are kept by Mavari guilds; the other eight are south-side or cross the halves. The bridges are the one thing the city is vain about.

Now: at the Bridge Walk every bridge is crossed in procession by its guild and the marks are recut. A bridge whose guild fails to appear is walked in silence, and that is a scandal; in the past it has been a revolution. The Master of the Bridges, an elected post, is held this year by Hrolf Rope-Hand of the north-side ropemakers, the first Mavari master in forty years.

Found here: tolls of a quarter-copper on the guild bridges; a chain of ferries below for those who will not pay; and from the guilds, a carved mark-stone cast in bronze (5 gp) for anyone who wants a guild's protection.

Hook: the Ropewalkers' guild, which keeps the chain bridge, has lost its charter in a debt suit. If no guild walks the bridge this year, both halves will read it as an omen.

The Forum of Mavelon Civic square

Codex now: Mavelon's civic square, where law, market and religion share one pavement.

Small, loud and functional, on the only flat ground at the summit of the south rim beside the Dux's Praetorium. It is ringed with guild halls rather than temples, because in Mavelon the guilds are the government in everything but name. Vulcan's temple faces Neptune's across the pavement, and the two priesthoods do not get on: one blesses the forge, the other the hull, and both claim the keel-silver.

Now: Dux Publius Arruntius Celer holds audience on the Praetorium steps on market days. The forum's market is run by the guild of chandlers, whose master Lucius Opsius Funarius also chairs the guild council that the Dux consults on everything from wages to launches. Mavari traders come through the Gate with fish and wool on market days, and the Gate Fights end here on festival nights.

Found here: ship's stores of every kind; a guild hall for every trade, where a visiting craftsman can find work for a day; Farshore goods resold from the Quays at a markup; and the city's official notices in Invictian and Mavari.

Hook: Vulcan's priests and Neptune's priests have each declared the other's festival unlucky for launching, and the next hull is due on the slips in a week.

The Glass-Stone Cellars Workshops

Codex now: Cool cellars under the river city where sheets of clear mineral are split for windows by men who work in silence.

A warren of cool cellars cut into the ravine walls, where blocks of clear volcanic glass and layered mica are split into thin sheets with wooden wedges. The cellars are silent by custom, because a shout can crack a sheet end to end, and the splitters speak a sign-language of their own that north-siders and south-siders both use. A sheet the size of a door is a rich man's boast, and every villa on the High Crescent has at least one.

Now: the splitters' guild is mixed, half Mavari and half Invictian, and is the one guild in the city where no one knows or cares which half a member comes from, since nobody speaks. Its master is Old Thane Wordless, who has not said a word aloud in thirty years and signs faster than most men talk.

Found here: a window-pane of mica (2 gp a hand's breadth), a clear sheet of volcanic glass (25 gp a square foot), obsidian blades and mirrors. A buyer is admitted to the front cellar and told to whisper. The back cellars are closed.

Hook: the silence rule hid a murder: a splitter's body lay in the third cellar for two days before anyone signed it. Every member saw something and none will speak.

The Mavelon Garrison Legionary camp

Codex now: The legion's camp at Mavelon, kept outside the sacred line as Invictian law requires.

A fortress on the standard plan on the Outer Flank below the Dyers' Fields, outside the city's sacred line, looking out to the open sea rather than into the caldera. It is small, and that is its danger: the city does not have a large force, it has the capacity to equip one, and every Legate knows it. The garrison holds a single cohort and the marines of the laid-up fleet.

Now: the camp is commanded by Tribune Gaius Vettulenus Rex, who reports to the Dux in theory and to the Praefectus Classis in practice, which neither man likes. The Ironclad Legion recruits at its gate; so, more quietly, do the Crimson Warlords. Mavari never serve in it, by the Oath; they serve the fleet as paid freemen.

Found here: a canteen that sells the cheapest wine on the island; marines selling off-duty protection for Farshore merchants; and the parade ground where the Gate Fights' losers are sometimes made to drill as punishment.

Hook: a Legate's agent has arrived with orders to "inspect" the garrison's armoury. The Dux was not told he was coming.

Duneforged Citadel

Sites of the Duneforged Citadel, the mountain city of House Caerthain at the southern end of the Via Ferraria. See the Helm, the Furnace Ring and House Caerthain.

Citadel Cathedral Cathedral

Codex now: The cathedral of the Duneforged Citadel, housing its temples.

A cathedral in the mountain's own stone on the Helm, carved downward rather than built up: a great domed crossing open to the sky through a shaft, and off it five temples held separately rather than as altars in a single nave. The Forge of Vulcan, the Temple of Juno, the Vault of Mercury, the Shrine of Anchiale and the Sanctum of Hoplodamus share the crossing, a bell and nothing else. Between them they cover craft, oath, trade, fire and the guardianship owed to those who fight in the Ju Colliseum. That a house ruled by the Caesars honours a god of creation and a god of binding oaths under one roof is not an accident of architecture.

Now: the Duke has spent more on the cathedral in five years of peace than in twenty of war: new bronze doors, a gilded dome-ring, a second bell cast in the Iron Furnaces. The Crossing is kept by Archpriest Edmund Corvane, Warden of the Five Doors, whose house is married into the Zayida and whose budget the Duchess approves each quarter, and each temple keeps its own priesthood and treasury.

Found here: the pilgrim road's last punch for Invictian pilgrims who have walked the Via Ferraria; candles (1 cp); and a seat at the Feast of the Five, when every priesthood serves bread at one table in the crossing.

Hook: the new bell cracked on its first ringing, and the Archpriest wants it recast before the Great Martial Festival. The founders say the mountain cracked it.

Healer's Sanctuary House of healing

Codex now: The house of healing within the Duneforged Citadel.

A long, whitewashed building on the Middle City's sunny side, between the arena and the market, standing among the citadel's named places rather than among the temples of the Cathedral. A citadel that keeps the Adamantine Line and runs the Ju Colliseum generates a steady supply of the wounded, and the Sanctuary is where they are brought: arena fighters on one side, mine crews on the other, and soldiers wherever there is a bed.

Now: the Sanctuary is kept by Physician-Mother Maren Holt, sixty, a former army surgeon who has set more bones than any priest has blessed, and who treats the Duke's heir and a debt-bonded fighter in the same tone. She sends hopeless and wealthy cases to the spa at Loutrokleion and keeps the rest. Funding comes from House Zayida, the arena's purse and whatever the Duchess can spare.

Found here: healing for anyone, paid by a sliding scale nobody understands; potions of healing (50 gp, when in stock); splints, salves and the Sanctuary's own bitter pain-draught (5 sp).

Hook: three miners from the lower shafts have been brought in humming the same note in their sleep, and Holt wants someone to go down and find out why before she has thirty.

The Dune Mines Mine

Codex now: Workings beneath the eastern slopes, where the lower shafts have fallen silent.

Mine workings beneath the eastern slopes, outside the walls, reached by a cut road and a ladder of hoist-towers. The upper levels run as they always have: iron and copper ore, a little silver, gangs from the Quarrymen District working by family. The lower shafts do not. Deep tremors and a low, continuous hum have stopped work there entirely. A hum is not a collapse. Collapses stop.

Now: Overseer Tarnak, Foreman of the Lower Mines, cannot get anyone to go back down, and a shut mine pays no wages. The upper mine's ore still goes north to Mavelon's arsenal on a long-haul contract with the Caravan of the Gilded Horizon, and the assay reports have trended one way for a decade. Idris Zayida of the Codex of Rule has noticed that the payroll counts more miners than the Codex does.

Found here: work, at a miner's wage of 2 sp a day; ore by the cartload; guides at Drakkur's Expeditionary for anyone going down; and, for the brave, a bonus of 50 gp a head from Tarnak for any party that maps the lower shafts.

Hook: Tarnak hires the party to go down the lower shafts and find the source of the hum. He would prefer they came back.

The Iron Furnaces Foundry

Codex now: A ring of blast-houses inside the fortress-city's outer wall, where the families who armed the legions still forge their steel.

A ring of squat blast-houses in the Furnace Ring inside the outer wall, working day and night in shifts, their chimneys streaking the wall above black. The armourer families who control them were armourers before the empires and wish to be nothing else. Their steel is sold to anyone who can pay and refused to anyone who can pay too little. They temper it by methods they do not discuss, and forge a few small ingots a year of cold iron, used against things that will not be struck with anything else.

Now: there are seven furnace families, bound to House Vulkrim by marriage and contract. The eldest master, Hedda Brandt, chairs their council, and speaks for the Ring to Lady Ottilde Vulkrim. Orders have fallen since the peace; two furnaces are banked, and one family has sold its blast-house to a Mavelon ironmaster.

Found here: a buyer is received in the front hall by armourers wearing their best work. Longsword (20 gp, better than the book), chain shirt (60 gp), plate on commission (1,800 gp and a season's wait), and cold iron by special arrangement (a dagger, 250 gp). Admire a blade and you are offered a price.

Hook: one family has begun making blades that do not ring. A rival smith has bought one and shown it to a priest of the Forge of Vulcan.

The Molten Crucible Alchemist and artificer

Codex now: Manage by a Vulkrim and Virellarion Family

An upscale alchemist's and artificer's in the Noble Districts on the Helm, where Vulkrim metal and Virellarion alchemy meet for the upper streets. Each house runs its own shop lower down: the Virellarions' Gilded Crucible for alchemy, the Vulkrims' Ember and Anvil for smithing. The Molten Crucible is where the two trades, and the two families, share a counter: enchanted metalwork, alchemical craft, and commissions neither house could fill alone. The front room is black marble and brass; the back room is a foundry with a laboratory on top of it.

Now: the shop is managed for both houses by Master-Factor Elowen Brask, a commoner chosen precisely because she belongs to neither family, and who keeps two ledgers in two colours of ink. Lady Ottilde Vulkrim and Lord Ambrose Virellarion each visit weekly, never on the same day.

Found here: potions and alchemical goods at the upper end (alchemist's fire 60 gp, antitoxin 60 gp); masterwork arms and armour; uncommon magic items on commission, a season's wait; and small marvels for the noble houses: self-warming cups, clockwork birds, lamps that light at a word.

Hook: a commission has gone out under both houses' seals that neither house admits ordering: a suit of forge armour from a design the Vulkrims keep in their forbidden archive.

The Temples Temple quarter

Codex now: Untitled

The temple quarter of the Helm, the lanes around the Citadel Cathedral where the five priesthoods keep their houses, schools, almonries and stores. The Cathedral keeps a temple for each of the powers the citadel honours, Titans and Invictian gods alike: the Forge of Vulcan for Vulcan, Artisan of Creation; the Temple of Juno, Protector of Bonds, where the coin is assayed; the Vault of Mercury, Trickster of Trade; the Shrine of Anchiale, Titan of fire and craft; the Sanctum of Hoplodamus, Titan of Guardianship and patron of the trials at the Ju Colliseum. That Titans are worshipped beside the Imperium's gods is a Duneforged peculiarity; elsewhere the Titans' worship is older and stranger than any state cult.

Now: the quarter is crowded with pilgrims for the Great Martial Festival, and the priesthoods' houses rent beds at festival prices. The quarter's peacekeeper is Tobin Ashgrove, an arena surgeon of the Hoplodamus house, who settles disputes between the five priesthoods by making them eat together.

Found here: beds (1 gp a night at festival time); candles, votive figurines and blessed iron nails; a scriptorium copying the citadel's prayers; and the almonry where the lower city's poor are fed on feast days.

Hook: Invictian priests arriving for the festival have objected to the Titans' shrines and want them screened during the Imperium's rites. The Duke has not answered.

Citadel Cathedral

The five temples held under one roof in the Duneforged Citadel's Cathedral (see Citadel Cathedral above).

Forge of Vulcan Temple

Codex now: A temple of the Citadel Cathedral, kept for the Artisan of Creation.

A temple that is also a working smithy: an altar-anvil under a smoke-hood, a forge that is never let go out, and racks of votive tools hung by apprentices who made them. A house given to a god of creation, in a citadel whose nobility made its name on levitation crystals and airships, is not a quiet corner of the Cathedral. It is where the work is blessed. Every Duneforged smith's first piece is laid on the altar-anvil, and every airship's first keel-bolt is struck here.

Now: the Duke has lavished money on the Forge since the peace, and its new bronze doors are the finest casting in the south. The High Smith-Priest, Hadrian Voss, is a smith first and a priest second, and the Order of Ember, Ferratus Vulkrim's warrior-smiths, treat the temple as their chapter house.

Found here: the blessing of a weapon or tool (5 sp, more for a masterwork piece); a smith may rent the altar-forge for a night's work for a donation, and such work is said to hold an edge longer.

Hook: High Smith-Priest Voss has been asked by a rival priest to examine a blade that does not ring, from the Iron Furnaces. He refuses to touch it and wants someone else to take it to the Shrine of Anchiale.

Sanctum of Hoplodamus Titan's sanctum

Codex now: A temple of the Citadel Cathedral, kept for the Titan of Guardianship.

A plain stone chamber with no statue, only a great bronze shield set into the wall, uncorroded, too large for any human arm. The trials fought at the Ju Colliseum are held sacred before Hoplodamus, Titan of Guardianship, and those who fight well there may be granted divine mercy, which the record defines as a fast, clean death. The guardianship offered in this sanctum is of that kind. Fighters come here before a match and leave a drop of blood on the shield's rim.

Now: the sanctum's keeper is Warden-Priest Garrick Ashgrove, of a family of pardoned arena fighters, who grants the mercy himself with a single blade kept on the altar. With the Great Martial Festival coming, the sanctum is full every evening; Marcia Ferox, the Unbought, prays here and leaves no blood, which Ashgrove permits for her alone.

Found here: a fighter's blessing (free, a drop of blood); the Mercy-Roll, the list of every fighter granted the clean death, which anyone may read.

Hook: a name has appeared on the Mercy-Roll of a fighter who is still alive and booked for the Festival. Ashgrove did not write it.

Shrine of Anchiale Titan's shrine

Codex now: A temple of the Citadel Cathedral, kept for the Flame Artisan.

A narrow shrine cut deep into the rock behind the Forge of Vulcan, reached by a passage that turns three times, so that no draught reaches the flame at its end. The Ju Colliseum names Anchiale, the Flame Artisan, for adaptability and cunning. A Titan of fire and craft honoured in a mountain citadel of smiths is an obvious patron. The cunning is the part worth watching: her priests are alchemists, her offerings are unsolved problems written on clay, and her favour is shown by an answer arriving in a dream.

Now: the shrine is House Virellarion's chapel in all but name, and Countess Aurelie Virellarion sits at the bench here as often as at the Crucible Spire. Its keeper is Ember-Keeper Isaura Quell, a quiet alchemist-priestess who has never been seen to eat and is not a Virellarion, which she reminds them of.

Found here: an offering tablet (1 sp) on which to write a problem; the priestess will consult on alchemical or artificing puzzles for a donation; and Anchiale's oil, which burns without smoke (2 gp a flask).

Hook: the clay tablets left at the shrine have begun to be answered in writing, in a hand nobody recognises, overnight.

Temple of Juno Temple

Codex now: A temple of the Citadel Cathedral, kept for the Protector of Bonds.

A square hall with a basin of still water at its centre and a set of assayer's scales on the altar. Oaths sworn here bind. In a citadel ruled by a house whose alliances rest on the Pact, a treaty signed in enchanted water, that is not a ceremonial function: marriages, debts and fealties are sworn with the hand in the basin. It is also where Duneforged's coin and the Mithril Reserve's bullion are assayed, sister to the Temple of Juno in Aeterna, and the figures read here are honest.

Now: the head priest is Prioress Elspeth Marrow, who reads the assay aloud each quarter in the same flat voice whatever the figures say, and whose readings are trusted from Deiperduem to Romulo. Lady Isolde Merca attends every assay. Tobin Ashgrove of the Hoplodamus house keeps the temple quarter's peace.

Found here: sworn oaths and contracts (from 5 gp, by the size of the stake); assay of coin or bullion (1 gp a sample), with a certificate the Reserve accepts; and a written copy of the quarterly assay figures, which bankers buy.

Hook: the Temple has received a shipment of Invictian silver to assay from the capital, with a letter asking that the figures be "read privately".

Vault of Mercury Temple and strongroom

Codex now: A temple of the Citadel Cathedral, kept for the Trickster of Trade.

A temple with a door like a bank's: iron-banded, double-locked, and opened by two keyholders at once. Inside, behind a statue of Mercury with his purse and wand, are rows of sealed niches where merchants deposit coin, contracts and sealed letters under the god's protection. It is called a vault rather than a shrine, which for a god of both trade and trickery is either an act of devotion or a precaution. Caravan masters stop here before taking the Via Ferraria north.

Now: the Vault is a quiet competitor to the Mithril Reserve for small deposits, which the Reserve tolerates because it is a temple. Its keeper is Vault-Priest Corwin Hale, a cheerful, sharp-eyed priest who makes small loans at the god's rate and keeps an exact ledger. The Caravan of the Gilded Horizon makes an offering here before each run.

Found here: a sealed niche (2 gp a year); small loans against goods; a blessing for a journey (5 sp); and Mercury's tokens, lead coins stamped with a winged sandal, accepted as tips by every carter on the road.

Hook: a niche sealed nine centuries ago, belonging to a man who died at the pass with Kaelen Caerthain, has been opened by someone with the right key.

Deiperduem City

Sites of Deiperduem, the neutral treaty city, both on Treaty Square.

The Assayers' Tower Neutral assay tower

Codex now: A neutral laboratory-tower in the treaty city where rare and magical materials are tested, certified and priced for the courts of three empires.

A six-storey tower of grey brick across the square from the Treaty Hall, built by a pact of the three powers to settle what is worth what. Each floor is a laboratory for a different class of material, the higher the rarer, and the top floor has no windows at all. Its assayers test every rare and magical material that crosses a border, and its stamp, a balance between three stars, is accepted at every court. It has no allegiance, which is why it is still standing.

Now: the tower is run by Master Assayer Ilse Kerovan, a gnome who was born in Deiperduem, has never left it, and refuses gifts so firmly that the embassies have stopped trying. The Temple of Juno at Aeterna sends trial pieces of every coin issue here, and the Mithril Reserve's branch master Hildra Ironhand uses its figures to set the Reserve's discount on Invictian silver. The door-wardens are impartial and politely armed.

Found here: assay of any material for a fee (common metal 5 gp; mithril or adamantine 50 gp; magical materials 100 gp and up); a certificate valid in three empires; and a sample cabinet of mithril, arcanaite, nullstone, tethtrium, embersteel, shattergleam crystal and anchoring gems that scholars may consult by appointment.

Hook: a sample certified last week has proved fake, and the assayer who stamped it is missing. The tower wants it closed quietly; three embassies want it opened loudly.

The Treaty Hall of Deiperduem Assembly hall

Codex now: The plain hall where the Treaty of Deiperdeum was signed, preserved exactly as it was on the day.

On the square of the old town: unglamorous, deliberately plain, and preserved exactly as it was on the day the three empires signed, down to the scuffed table and the chair whose leg the Acheaorian delegation insisted on shortening. Its plainness is the point. No empire could be seen to have built it. The Invictians call what was signed here the Great Concord, the Hellenorians the Treaty of Myrianth after the hall's old name, and the Acheaorians the Peace of the Signing.

Now: the Hall's wards are kept by Aulus Severinus Custos, Warden of the Treaty Wards, who has rooms above the archive and is rarely seen leaving them. Its door is kept by Hall-Warden Damis Orrel, a Deiperdene who was a boy sweeping the floor on the day of signing. The urn of the lot, from which a foundling draws the Arbiter's token every three years, stands in the antechamber.

Found here: the Hall is open to anyone on the Signing and to accredited envoys at other times. Copies of the treaty text in three languages (1 gp) are sold at the door; every copy differs slightly, and the Hall-Warden can tell you how.

Hook: at the next Signing each empire sends a delegation, every speech is checked in advance by everyone, and someone has asked the party to make sure one particular speech is not delivered as checked.

Eronis

The one site of Eronis, the dead capital of Nethrana on Velothis. See the Cypress Walk on the city page.

The Mourning Cypress Walk Avenue and necropolis

Codex now: A black-green avenue through the dead capital where the dream-walkers once buried their kings under the trees that never shed.

A long avenue of tall, dark cypresses running north through the ruined capital to the royal necropolis, planted by a dynasty that planned for its own funeral. The trees have outlived the dynasty and the city, and the avenue is still green while every house beside it is rubble. The burial-gardens at its end are planted with Vital Mauveroot, which the dream-walkers claimed could keep the dead from decay. The trees all lean the same way, as though listening. Visitors agree that the shadows fall the wrong way.

Now: nobody rules Eronis and nobody patrols the road. Herbalists from Willowheart come for Mauveroot cuttings and pay well; salvagers from the Quays of Irelas avoid the Walk. The Sanctuary of the Silver Veil keeps a watcher at the avenue's south end, a grey-robed woman named Sister Oriel, who asks every visitor to turn back and records the names of those who do not.

Found here: Mauveroot cuttings (worth 10 gp each to an embalmer or herbalist, if they survive the journey); cypress cones that, burned, give a smoke said to bring the dead into dreams; and silence.

Hook: Vesperine Ilaro, the Last Dreamwalker, was seen on the Walk in daylight. At the avenue's end, a door in the necropolis has been opened from below, and tracks lead up the avenue toward the sea.

Latium Plains

Sites of the Latium Plains, the capital province around Aeterna and Romulo.

The Aqua Aeterna Aqueduct

Codex now: The aqueduct that carries the capital's water sixty miles from the Klynin springs — and the reason a siege of Aeterna has never once succeeded.

Sixty miles of channel, most of it underground, carrying spring water from the Klynin foothills to Aeterna's fountains. Where the ground falls away the channel rides arcades of brick-faced concrete, and for the last four miles it runs on a double tier of arches visible from the Latium road. The gradient is the achievement: a little under one part in four thousand, held across three river valleys by surveyors whose names are recorded nowhere. Cutting it has never taken the city, which sits on cisterns, wells and a river; it supplies baths and fountains rather than survival. Twice in the war an Acheaorian force broke a span, and both times the channel was carrying again within the month.

Now: the maintenance office was funded from the war budget, which no longer exists. The state contract belongs to House Ovinia, and the Curator Aquarum, Sextus Plotius Libo, signs whatever they send him. Three upper spans are shored with timber meant to last a season that has lasted four years, and the water arrives brown after rain. Marcus Ulpius of the Aeterna Garrison has shored two more from camp stores, unasked.

Found here: inspection passages every mile, locked; the water-office's walkers, who will guide a traveller along the channel road for a few coppers.

Hook: a span on the upper course has begun to sag, and the Curator wants it repaired quietly, at night, by people who are not on any payroll.

Lime-Burners' Hollow Kilns

Codex now: A smoky hollow in the plains where kilns burn day and night, and builders come for lime and the grey volcanic sand that sets under water.

A hollow ringed by squat stone kilns, burning limestone to quicklime day and night. The smoke hangs in it like fog, the burners are grey from hair to boot, and the sound of the place is the clatter of carts and the rasp of coughing. A pit on the north rim yields pozzolana, the grey volcanic sand that makes mortar set hard even under water. Every concrete harbour wall in the Imperium began here: Fucostia's moles, Mavelon's slips.

Now: since the peace the order books have halved, and the kilnmen have started burning cheaper stone. Somebody's harbour will notice in ten years. The kiln-masters' headman is Lurco the Grey, a burner's son who can tell good lime by the hiss when it is slaked. Builders' agents from every city lodge at a long, dusty inn called the Whitewash.

Found here: quicklime (1 sp a bushel), pozzolana (2 sp a bushel, delivered by cart), a bed at the Whitewash (5 cp, and you will cough all night).

Hook: the burners have a custom of leaving the oldest kiln unlit. They say it was last fired for a body, and someone has lit it again.

The Chalk Downs Flint quarry

Codex now: Rolling white hills where black flint lies in the chalk like plums in a pudding, and the flint-knappers have worked since before the empires.

Smooth white hills so thin in soil that the chalk shows through the turf like bone. Dark nodules of flint lie in the chalk in bands, and the knappers who work them are the oldest trade on the plains: their fathers made spear-points here when the empires were villages. They still sell strike-a-lights and threshing-sledge teeth by the thousand, and regard metal as a fashion. Barrows crown the highest downs.

Now: the knappers' families hold their pits by custom, not deed, and the district magistrate has started asking for deeds. The eldest knapper, Old Mother Crabba, says little and charges less; she is the best tool-maker on the downs and the only one who will sell to a stranger at a fair price.

Found here: a fire-kit or flint blade for a copper; threshing teeth by the hundred; flint building-stone for walls; and the old pits, still open to any who ask.

Hook: a barrow on the highest down was opened last year, and what was found has been quietly reburied by order of the district magistrate. A Lexicon scholar wants it dug up again.

The Rye-Ghost Fields Grain district

Codex now: A grain district on the plains where the barley feeds the legions and the black-eared rye feeds the dreams of the villages.

A broad district of grain farms laid out in strips and worked in the old way with oxen and wooden ploughs. The barley is for the legions, the emmer for the farmers, and the rye is for whoever gets the black-eared kind, which in a wet year sends whole hamlets dancing and seeing the dead. The ditches grow soldier's nettle and hedge-mallow, which the farm wives use for everything.

Now: the Golden Harvest Covenant buys the clean grain for the Annona and leaves the black, which the poor bake anyway because it is free. The district's Magister Vici, Spurius Arrius Glabrio, is a tenant farmer with a loud voice who has written to the Prefect of the Annona four times about the price; the fourth letter was answered by a tax assessment.

Found here: bread offered to every traveller (after a wet spring, with a warning); legion barley by the sack; and from the physicians' agents, a good price for black rye-ghost, which hastens births and serves poisoners for other ends.

Hook: in a bad rye year the village of the third furrow dances for three days and nobody remembers. A tax-collector is due, and the rye was wet this spring.

The Umbrella Pines Coastal wood

Codex now: A shaded coastal wood of flat-topped pines where pilgrims rest, lovers meet and the pine-nut gatherers climb with hooks.

A coastal wood of wide, flat-topped pines that make a green roof forty feet up, with open ground beneath. Pilgrims on the road to the capital rest here, lovers meet here, and the pine-nut gatherers climb the trunks with long hooks and drop the cones into baskets. The Via Litoranea runs through its edge toward Napplesia, and a hedge of lovers' myrtle lines the road, said to have been planted by a goddess's gardener. It is the one place on the plains where nobody asks whose land it is.

Now: the wood is common land in custom and a patrician estate in law, and the estate's steward has not yet tried to enforce it. The innkeeper at its edge, Faustina Pinaria, sells roast pine-nuts by the paper cone and keeps a book of the couples who have carved their names on the third pine.
