Place up to twenty coins in one pan and speak Juno's name: the other pan settles to show the true metal of the coins as a fraction of their face value, and any coin that is counterfeit, illusory or conjured turns black until it leaves the pan. Weighing takes 1 minute. A creature who swears a statement about money with a hand on the beam and lies feels it tip; you know the lie, not the truth.

Lore. The Temple of Juno at Aeterna holds the Quarterly Assay with the great set; every Mithril Reserve branch keeps a small one, and has been discounting Invictian silver by what it says.

Hook. A temple acolyte brings the party the great set's private record: three quarters of figures that differ from the ones read aloud. Somebody would like the scales broken before the next Assay, and the acolyte with them.

Fasces of the Praetor Rod of office

Rare · rod · requires attunement by a magistrate or a creature acting under one's warrant · 3,500 gp

A bundle of elm rods bound with red leather around a small bronze axe. The rod has 5 charges and regains 1d4 + 1 at dawn. While holding it, you can expend charges to cast zone of truth (2 charges), command (1 charge; the command must be "halt", "kneel" or "speak") or hold person (3 charges), save DC 15. A creature that has been lawfully sentenced in your presence has disadvantage on its saving throw. Inside a sacred boundary (the pomerium of Aeterna or Romulo) the rods must be carried without the axe, and the rod cannot cast hold person.

Lore. Every praetor's lictors carried fasces; only the old patrician praetorships had magical ones, and the patricians kept them when the offices passed to the Council's men.

Hook. House Calpurnia lends its fasces to a praetor the Council of Legates is trying to remove. The Legates want them stolen before the trial.

The Grass Crown Corona of a saved army

Very rare · wondrous item · requires attunement · cannot be bought; only given by an army

A wreath of field grass, woven by soldiers of a legion its wearer saved, from the ground on which they were saved. It does not wither while one of those soldiers lives. While wearing it you and allies within 10 feet gain a +1 bonus to saving throws. Once per dawn, as an action, you can cast heroism on up to five creatures you can see, with no concentration needed; it lasts 1 minute. An Invictian soldier must succeed on a DC 15 Wisdom saving throw to attack you knowingly.

Lore. Three living men hold one. General Valerius Maximus, the Dominus Militum, received his after the Siege of the Two Rivers and wears it on campaign days. The grass on his crown has started to go brown at the edges.

Hook. When the last soldier of a saved legion dies, the crown dies with him. Someone has begun killing the old survivors of the Two Rivers, one a month, and a great many people would like to know whether the Dominus Militum's crown can be made to fail in public.

Key of the Twin Doors Temple of Janus

Very rare · wondrous item · requires attunement · not for sale (the Pontiffs hold it)

A bronze key as long as a forearm, with a bit at each end. While attuned, you can cast knock and arcane lock at will, and passwall once per dawn. A door you lock with the key cannot be opened by magic of 7th level or lower. The key opens and shuts the twin doors of the Temple of Janus at Aeterna: open, the Imperium is formally at war; shut, at peace.

Lore. The doors stood open for fifteen centuries and were shut at the Great Concord, with some difficulty and a team of oxen. The key is supposed to lie on the altar between them. Since the spring it has been a very good copy.

Hook. Whoever took the key can open the doors on any morning they choose, and every legion will read it as a declaration. The Pontiffs cannot report the theft without admitting it; they hire the party instead.

The Cloak on the Empty Chair Paludamentum of Iovianus Sandarion

Legendary · wondrous item · requires attunement · priceless

A general's purple cloak, sun-faded on one shoulder where it has lain over the arm of the Imperator's chair for five years. While wearing it you gain a +2 bonus to AC and saving throws, and advantage on Charisma checks with Invictian soldiers. Once per dawn you can cast mass suggestion (save DC 19); creatures who served in the legions have disadvantage on the saving throw. If you are not of Sandarion's blood, each time you use this property make a DC 15 Charisma saving throw; on a failure every Invictian who saw you do it knows you are not him.

Lore. The Imperator's chair stands empty "awaiting his recovery", with the founder-hero's cloak laid over it so that the Senate can address the cloak. The Praetorian at the chair changes every hour.

Hook. The cloak's dye has started to run, as if wet. The Senate's oldest member says it did the same the night Iovianus came home from the duel with Astraphael.

Arms of Hellenoria

Hellenoria fights at sea, argues on land, and keeps its best weapon in a shed with no number. Its magic belongs to cities and crews rather than to legions: wind sold by the knot, shields made in pairs, lamps that catch liars. Every League city has a law against owning Hellenic fire, and Hellarchon's is the only one that is enforced.

Hellenic Fire State secret, as hazard and weapon

Very rare · hazard and consumable (a sealed jar, about 4 pints) · no attunement · not for sale; 1,500 gp a jar on the black market; possession outside the fleet is death under League law

A dark, sticky liquid that ignites on contact with air when pumped under pressure, or when its seal is broken and it is struck. It burns on water, clings to whatever it touches, and does not care about rain.

As a hazard. A creature in an area of Hellenic fire, or hit by a stream or a jar of it, makes a DC 15 Dexterity saving throw, taking 4d6 fire damage on a failure or half as much on a success. On a failure it is also clinging: it takes 2d6 fire damage at the start of each of its turns until the fire is smothered. Water does not smother it; dousing a clinging creature with water spreads the fire to every creature within 5 feet (they make the save). Only sand, vinegar or old urine put it out: a creature (or an ally adjacent to it) can use an action and a gallon of any of them to end the effect. A jar broken on water sets a 20-foot square of sea burning for 1 minute; a ship's hull in it takes 4d10 fire damage per round and ignores the hull's damage threshold.

As a weapon. A jar thrown by hand (range 20/60 ft.) bursts in a 10-foot radius and uses the save above. Shipboard siphons are covered under the Shipshed Siphon.

Lore. The League's deterrent, compounded in the shipsheds of Hellarchon. Tyrants pay fortunes for a sample; the Treaty inspectors pretend not to look for it. Nerissa Thalassine's corsairs are known to have a little.

Hook. A sample of the plateau naphtha from the Pitch Seep is on its way to a Hellenorian tyrant's alchemist, who believes it is the missing ingredient. It is not, and his experiment will burn down a harbour.

Shipshed Siphon Fleet weapon

Very rare · wondrous item (ship weapon) · no attunement; requires a crew of three · not for sale (6,000 gp would not buy one)

A bronze-mouthed tube in the shape of a lion's head, a pump, a brazier and a lead reservoir holding enough Hellenic fire for ten discharges. Mounted at a warship's bow, it fires as an action by its siphoneer, provided two other crew spent their actions pumping that round. The stream is a line 60 feet long and 5 feet wide, using the Hellenic fire hazard rules. On a roll of 1 on a d20 rolled each time it fires, the fittings fail and the siphon fills the 10-foot area around its own mouth.

Lore. Only Voidfolk crews are trained on them, and only Voidfolk crews are allowed near the reservoirs. The fittings (valves, a particular bronze, a particular solder) are a secret in themselves, and are counted back into the shipsheds after every cruise.

Hook. A chest of siphon-fittings has gone missing on the Southern Run. Three different people will come looking for it, and one of them is Iason Erebides, who is not allowed to leave the city.

The Kiln Ring Academy bronze

Rare · ring · requires attunement · 4,500 gp (not sold; the Academy gives them)

A heavy ring of dark bronze, faintly sooty however often it is polished. While wearing it you have resistance to fire damage. The ring grows warm when a creature within 30 feet tells you a deliberate lie about money, a debt, a payment or a price; you know the statement was a lie, but not what the truth is.

Lore. Cast from the bronze of the Arcane Academy's first brazier. Kallisto Pyrphoros wears the original; the Academy has cast three more and given them to its treasurers, who are said to be the least popular people in the Academy Grove.

Hook. One of the treasurers' rings has been stolen, and the Academy's grant from the Assembly is due for renewal. Someone wants to sit across a table from the Hegemon's men and know when they lie.

Wind-Knots Sold at the Wreckers' Beacon

First knot: Common · wondrous item · 30 drachmas. Second knot: Uncommon · 300 drachmas. Third knot: Very rare, cursed · not for sale · no attunement

A cord of tarred hemp with three knots, each tied with a word. Untying a knot is an action.

First knot. A steady wind blows from the direction of your choice around your vessel for 24 hours; a sailing ship moves at full speed regardless of the weather. Second knot. A gale for 1 hour, as control weather centred on the ship (you choose the wind and precipitation); every creature on deck unsecured must succeed on a DC 12 Strength saving throw each 10 minutes or be thrown 10 feet. Third knot. As storm of vengeance centred on the ship, lasting until it sinks.

Lore. Sold by Ixion Keraunios from the Wreckers' Beacon and his stall by the Lechaion harbour at Corinth. Nobody who untied the third knot kept the ship.

Hook. A trierarch bought a cord with three knots, used two, and has been offered 10,000 drachmas for the third by a buyer who says it is for "a ship that deserves it".

Aspis of the Pair Sacred Band shields

Rare · armour (shield) · requires attunement · 3,000 gp a pair (sold only in pairs)

A round bronze-faced hoplite shield, made as one of a matched pair; the inside of each bears the other's owner's name. You gain a +1 bonus to AC while wielding it. While you and the creature attuned to its pair are within 5 feet of each other, each of you can use a reaction when the other is hit by an attack to halve the damage and take the other half yourself. If your partner dies while you are attuned, you have advantage on attack rolls for 1 minute and cannot be frightened for 24 hours; then the shield's bonus ends until it is attuned again to a new pair.

Lore. The Sacred Band of Thebesieas is three hundred warriors in sworn pairs. Epameinon Kleitarchos still carries his; Melanthios's name is inside it, and the other shield went on the pyre.

Hook. A Band widow sells her husband's shield in Corinth to pay a debt. The surviving partner wants it back, and wants to know who bought it, because whoever attunes to it will feel him in every fight.

Lamp of the Truth-Flame Tribunal instrument

Rare · wondrous item · no attunement · 2,000 gp; owning one without a Tribunal seal is impiety

A clay oil lamp glazed white, with a wick of braided flax. Lit (an action), it sheds bright light for 20 feet and dim light for a further 20 for up to 8 hours on a pint of oil. A creature in its bright light that knowingly speaks a lie makes the flame burn blue-white; the creature makes a DC 15 Charisma saving throw, taking 1d6 radiant damage on a failure. A creature that fails three such saves in an hour cannot speak again until the lamp is put out.

Lore. Lamps of the Tribunal of the Truth-Flame in Hellarchon, used at hearings by Inquisitor Vireon, Third Seat, and his clerks. The Assembly's courts do not use them; the Tribunal does not need the Assembly's leave.

Hook. A lamp was lit in a closed hearing last month and the witness, a shipowner's clerk, spoke for an hour without making it flicker. Then he died. Vireon wants to know how a man can lie to the flame, and so does every shipowner.

The Reach Chart Delphara's wind-book

Very rare · wondrous item · no attunement · 15,000 gp to any fleet; the oracle will not sell

A book of hour-by-hour wind tables for the Aeolus Reach, written on oiled linen in three hands. A navigator using it automatically succeeds on checks to navigate the Reach and Nereid's Veil, and knows the weather in Hellenorian waters for the next seven days as if by a perfect forecast. Once per day the reader can ask it one question about wind or current at a named place and time within the next season; the answer is correct unless someone with magic over the weather (a storm sorcerer, a wind-knot) interferes.

Lore. Kept at Delphara, corrected each season by Lysandra Anthemis with corrections supplied, for a fee and a look at the next season's page, by Ixion Keraunios.

Hook. A copy is being made, page by page, by a novice in the Exegete's office. The buyer is a Corinthian shipowner; the payment is a berth for the novice's brother; and Ixion has noticed that his winds are being predicted.

Star-Shard of Astraphael The Destructive Star's leavings

Legendary · wondrous item · requires attunement by a sorcerer, warlock or wizard · priceless; the Academy and the Imperium both claim it

A splinter of black-violet glass the length of a finger, never quite cool. While holding it you gain a +2 bonus to spell attack rolls and spell save DCs. Once per dawn, when you cast a spell that deals damage, you can change its damage type to force. Once per dawn you can cast fireball at 7th level as violet starfire (force damage).

Curse. While attuned, your shadow is violet at dusk, and the Arcane Academy's scryers can find you as if they knew you well. Each time you use the starfire, make a DC 15 Constitution saving throw; on a failure you take 4d10 force damage and the sky above you darkens to violet for an hour.

Lore. Astraphael, the Destructive Star, vanished after a duel with Iovianus Sandarion. Shepherds above the field found shards for a year afterwards; the Imperium bought most and the Academy stole the rest. The violet dusk over Hellarchon is an arcane scar, and the shards are made of the same thing.

Hook. A shepherd's grandson brings a shard to the party because it has started to hum at dusk. So has the sky.

Embolon of the Nikandridai Trireme ram

Rare · wondrous item (ship fitting) · no attunement · 5,000 gp

A three-finned bronze ram cast with an owl and a shipowner's mark. Fitted to a galley's bow (a week's work in a shipshed), it doubles the damage the ship deals when it rams, and the ship takes no damage from ramming. Once per day, when the ship rams a vessel of its own size or smaller, the target's crew must succeed on a DC 13 Wisdom saving throw or be frightened for 1 minute.

Lore. House Nikandridai cast twenty for the war fleet and kept the moulds. The Hegemon's ships still carry them; so, after five years of peace and two auctions, do some of Nerissa Thalassine's.

Hook. One of the Hegemon's rams has been identified on a corsair at Corinth. The Hegemon wants to know who sold it, and the auction records say it was his own steward.

Arms of Acheaoria

Acheaoria's magic is royal, sacred and bureaucratic at once: a fire carried from a temple, a cord that holds a soldier's name, a ring that turns a post-station's stable door. The King of Kings owns everything in principle; in practice the satraps own their arsenals and the Magi own the fire, and the creed owns the knives.

Oath-Cord of the Immortals Royal guard

Very rare · wondrous item · requires attunement by the soldier named on it · not for sale (traffic in cords is sacrilege and treason)

A braided cord of red and white wool, knotted with the soldier's name and his oath-day, worn under the scale shirt next to the skin. While wearing it you have advantage on saving throws against being frightened. Once per dawn, when you are reduced to 0 hit points but not killed outright, you can make a DC 10 Constitution saving throw; on a success you drop to 1 hit point instead.

After death the cord becomes the anchor of the Rite of Return: with the man's name on the roll and his cord in the brazier, a Magus of the Rite can raise him over seven nights. A cord taken from a corpse, or burned, denies the rite.

Lore. Every Immortal of the King's guard swears on his cord. The army says the Immortals are called so because their number never falls below ten thousand. Magus Rashnu-Vahram keeps the roll.

Hook. Cords are being cut from the dead on the northern frontier and sold to a buyer in Xerastri. Whoever holds a man's cord can deny the King his soldier, or bring the soldier back for someone else.

Pomegranate Spear The Ten Thousand

Rare · weapon (spear) · requires attunement · 2,500 gp (gold-pommelled: 6,000)

A cypress-shafted spear whose butt-spike is cast as a pomegranate, of silver for the rank and file of the Ten Thousand and gold for the thousand who stand nearest the King. You gain a +1 bonus to attack and damage rolls made with this magic weapon. When a creature enters your reach and you hit it with a readied attack or opportunity attack, it takes an extra 2d6 piercing damage and its speed becomes 0 until the end of the turn. Once per dawn, as a bonus action, you learn whether any creature within 30 feet intends to harm a creature you have sworn to guard.

Lore. The royal guard of Persemenid carries them on the Royal Stair. The gold pommels are counted every New Year's Day, and two have been short for three years running.

Hook. A gold-pommelled spear is offered for sale in the Atarabad bazaar. The seller says a guardsman of the thousand sold it to pay for his mother's funeral; the guardsman is still on duty, and still carries a spear.

The Cupbearer's Dagger Court of Vipers

Rare · weapon (dagger) · requires attunement · 4,000 gp (the creed does not sell; it retrieves)

A narrow dagger with a hollow hilt and a cup-shaped guard. You gain a +1 bonus to attack and damage rolls made with this magic weapon. Once per dawn, as a bonus action, you can make the blade sweat poison for 1 minute: the next creature you hit with it takes an extra 4d10 poison damage and must make a DC 15 Constitution saving throw, taking half the poison damage on a success; on a failure it is also poisoned for 1 hour. Dipped into a cup (an action), the blade tells you whether the drink is poisoned: poisoned wine tastes of ash on the steel.

Lore. The Keeper of the Royal Cellar tastes the King of Kings' wine. The office is held by Bagoas the Nameless, who carries a dagger of this pattern and has killed eleven people with it, by the creed's count.

Hook. A cupbearer's dagger is found beside a dead satrap's steward in Mithratal. The creed says it is not theirs. The creed has never said that before.

The Lion's Mane Lance House Mihran

Rare · weapon (lance) · requires attunement · 5,000 gp; to the Mihran, a blood-price

A long cavalry lance with a gilded lion's-head socket and a horsetail mane dyed saffron. You gain a +1 bonus to attack and damage rolls made with this magic weapon, and you do not have disadvantage on attacks with it against a target within 5 feet while mounted. If you move at least 20 feet in a straight line on your mount and then hit a creature with it, the target takes an extra 2d8 piercing damage and must succeed on a DC 15 Strength saving throw or be knocked prone.

Lore. The lance of the Mihran heir who died at the pass in Kaelen Caerthain's stand. It did not come home. It hangs in the ducal palace at the Duneforged Citadel among the trophies of the Cloudspine, and Spahbed Artabazos Mihran has sworn to take it down himself.

Hook. House Mihran offers a fortune, and an end to the feud for one generation, to whoever returns the lance. House Caerthain will treat its theft as an act of war.

Bow of the Backward Shot House Surena

Rare · weapon (longbow; a horn-and-sinew composite) · requires attunement · 3,500 gp

A short, sharply recurved bow of horn, wood and sinew, lacquered black. You gain a +1 bonus to attack and damage rolls made with this magic weapon, and it can be fired from horseback with no penalty. After you make a ranged attack with it while mounted, your mount's movement for the rest of the turn does not provoke opportunity attacks. Once per dawn, when a creature you can see moves to within 30 feet of you, you can use your reaction to make one attack with the bow against it.

Lore. The Surena of Xerastri have held the Parthian Ravine with bows like this for longer than the Mihran have held their squadron. Roxana Surena carries one strung with her late husband's hair.

Hook. A Malaunian band crossing the frontier is carrying Surena bows. The Surena say they were stolen from a dead patrol. The band says they were a gift.

Censer of the Undying Fire The Magi

Rare · wondrous item · requires attunement by a cleric, paladin or Magus · 3,000 gp (given, not sold)

A pierced brass censer on a chain, holding a single coal carried from the Fire-Temple at Atarabad. While the coal burns it sheds bright light for 20 feet and dim light for 20 more. Within its bright light you cannot be deceived by illusions (you see through them as if with truesight), and undead have disadvantage on attack rolls. Once per dawn you can cast daylight from it.

If the coal goes out it can be relit only at a fire-temple's flame, by a Magus, after a day's fast. The Magi hold that the dead defile fire; a censer that has burned within 30 feet of a raised Immortal is unclean until purified.

Lore. Carried by Magi on the Royal Road and by fire-priests to the frontier forts. Mobad Atar-Farnbag blessed the last hundred himself.

Hook. A frontier Magus writes that his censer goes dim whenever the royal relief column passes his fort. He wants an explanation and does not want it to be the one he suspects.

The Golden Tripod The King's dedication at Delphara

Legendary · wondrous item · requires attunement by the oracle or a priest of Delphara · beyond price; dedicated to the god

A tripod of solid gold, taller than a man, its bowl engraved with lions and the name of a past King of Kings. A question asked over the bowl while the sacred vapour rises is answered as commune, once every seven days. Once per year the attuned priest can cast foresight on a creature who has made an offering at its foot.

The bought answer. Unknown to most priests, when a question touches the interests of the House of Zindar, the answers lean. The DM shades any such answer towards the King of Kings' advantage; it is never false, only chosen.

Lore. It stands in the Acheaorian treasury on the Sacred Way at Delphara, the richest of all the treasuries, kept by the treasurers of House Vashtiri. Thread of the Golden Tripod: the oracle's neutrality is quietly bought.

Hook. A Hellenorian city about to go to war asks Delphara a question about Acheaoria. The party have proof that the tripod leans, and an hour before the answer is read.

Signet of the King's Eye The Eyes and Ears of the King

Rare · ring · requires attunement · 4,000 gp; forging one is death by the Law That Does Not Change

A lapis signet cut with an open eye. While wearing it you can cast clairvoyance once per dawn, and sending once per dawn to another bearer of the signet. At any post-station on the Royal Road a bearer shown the signet must be given a fresh horse, a meal and a bed, and must not be asked a name.

Lore. The King's Eyes and Ears report to the throne past the satraps, which is why the satraps fear them and why a few of them have been found at the bottom of wells. The rings are numbered inside the band; the number is the only name an Eye has at court.

Hook. The party take a ring from a dead man on the Royal Road. Its number belongs to an Eye who reported in person at Persemenid yesterday.

Barbat of the Licence The Melodic Circle

Rare · wondrous item (lute) · requires attunement by a bard · 4,500 gp

A short-necked lute of mulberry wood with a pomegranate rose carved in the soundboard. You can use it as a spellcasting focus. While you play it, you have advantage on Charisma (Performance) checks, and creatures cannot be charmed by anyone but you within 30 feet of you. Once per dawn you can play the Night Garden Song, casting hypnotic pattern (save DC 15) as an auditory effect; creatures affected forget, until the next dawn, which walls and gates belong to whom.

Lore. Made for the First Voices of the Melodic Circle in Persevalis. Shirin Navaz plays the oldest of them, and holds a Licence: while she plays she may say anything about any official without legal consequence. The protection ends when the music stops, which is why she rarely stops.

Hook. Someone has borrowed a Circle barbat and played the Night Garden Song outside a satrap's treasury. The gates were found open at dawn and the guards could not say whose they were.

House treasures of Duneforged

The Duneforged Citadel is a mountain worked from the inside out, and its great families have spent five generations making things nobody else can. The Vulkrim forge, the Merca count, the Virellarion transmute and the Zayida keep the books; the Caesars hold the sky. Their treasures are listed in the codex by name and little else. This is the rest. Officially every piece below is "held in trust under the Pact", which means nobody may write down where it is. People write it down anyway.

Gladius Aeternum House Vulkrim · Ferratus

Legendary · weapon (shortsword) · requires attunement · priceless

A short, broad blade of dark grey steel with a seam of red light down the fuller, as if it had been broken and welded with fire. You gain a +2 bonus to attack and damage rolls made with this magic weapon. It never dulls and cannot be broken by anything short of a wish. While holding it you have resistance to fire damage.

Drinks the heat. The blade gains 1 ember each time you reduce a hostile creature to 0 hit points with it and each time you take fire damage while holding it (maximum 5). When you hit with it you can expend any number of embers to deal an extra 1d6 fire damage per ember. Embers fade if you go 1 minute without fighting.

Lore. Forged, by the codex's account, by Ferratus Vulkrim, Forge-Lord of the Southern Ridges, the man who gave up politics for the forge and has an iron gauntlet fused to his left hand. A Caesar once came to his forge-fortress seeking a weapon worthy of an empire, and never spoke of what he found. The Duke's sword hangs on the wall of his hall at the Helm; the Duke does not carry it.

Hook. The Vulkrim archive holds a note in Ferratus's hand: "The Duke's original sword was not forged. It was repaired." A scholar from the Porticoes wants to see the blade and will pay for a night with it.

The Black Anvil House Vulkrim · Ferratus

Artefact · wondrous item (anvil, some 2 tons) · no attunement; requires a smith proficient with smith's tools · priceless

An anvil of black iron that is warm to the touch in the coldest gallery. A smith working at it crafts magic weapons and armour in half the usual time and at half the cost in materials, and anything forged on it can be made of embersteel or adamantium without the material's crafting penalties (see Materials). Once per year a smith may forge on it a weapon or armour that gains a +1 bonus or one property of the DM's choice, at no extra cost.

War-sense. The anvil pulses when war approaches. The DM keeps a war clock of six segments; each segment filled makes the anvil pulse once more often each day, and everyone in the Geomanthic Foundries feels it in their teeth. At six, a war has begun somewhere on the continent.

Lore. Buried deep within the mountain, in the lowest gallery under the Geomanthic Foundries. It has begun to pulse. The Order of Ember, Ferratus's brotherhood of warrior-smiths, keeps a watch beside it in shifts and records each beat.

Hook. The Order's beat-book shows three pulses a day this month, up from one a week at the Treaty. Ferratus wants to know which war, and has decided that adventurers are the cheapest instrument for finding out.

The Ferric Crown House Vulkrim · Ferratus

Very rare · wondrous item (helm) · requires attunement · 30,000 gp

An open helm forged with molten silver poured over a skull-cap of volcanic glass, so that the glass shows through like veins. While wearing it you have advantage on initiative rolls and cannot be surprised. Once per dawn you can ask the Crown about a battle that will happen within the next seven days: as an action you see a vision of it, as divination, with the DM describing one decisive moment truthfully.

Curse. Each vision forces a DC 14 Wisdom saving throw. On a failure, the next time you sleep you dream of your own last battle and gain no benefit from that long rest.

Lore. The third of Ferratus Vulkrim's attributed artefacts. Ferratus has worn it twice in public, once before the Siege of Twin Gates and once on the day the Treaty was signed; he took it off after an hour the second time and has not explained why. It is kept in the Order of Ember's shrine at the Geomantic Forge.

Hook. Count Faris Zayida wants the Crown worn before the next muster. Ferratus refuses. Lady Ottilde Vulkrim, his heir, has offered the party a key to the shrine.

Shield of Tenfold Defiance House Vulkrim · Velda

Legendary · armour (shield) · requires attunement · priceless

A tall oval shield of black steel rimmed with embersteel, dented nine times across the face. You gain a +2 bonus to AC while wielding it. While wielding it you cannot be moved against your will, and you have advantage on Strength and Constitution saving throws.

Defiance. Once per dawn, as an action, you plant the shield: for 1 minute (concentration), you and up to nine allies within 30 feet of you gain a +2 bonus to AC and resistance to bludgeoning, piercing and slashing damage, and creatures hostile to you treat the ground within 30 feet of you as difficult terrain.

Lore. Forged by Velda Vulkrim, whose shield turned a battle single-handedly. Each dent is a defiance, and the citadel's children can name all nine. It hangs in the Sanctum of Hoplodamus in the Citadel Cathedral, where Gavin Caesar swore his oath of command.

Hook. The temple has found a tenth dent, fresh, one morning. The shield had not left its wall. The priests want to know who it defied, and what.

Rune of Trust House Merca · Existing

Rare · wondrous item (contract) · no attunement · 500 gp per contract, plus a tenth of the sum secured, payable to the Reserve

A contract written in runes by a Merca notary in the presence of every party, with one counterpart per party. It cannot be forged: any attempt to copy, alter or imitate it fails, and detect magic shows the forgery as plain ink. It does not compel anybody to keep its terms. The moment a party breaches them, every counterpart bursts into a cold blue flame and burns to ash in a round, wherever it is; every holder knows at once that the contract is broken.

Lore. House Merca made its name on this craft. A Rune of Trust does not enforce a debt; it removes any argument about whether the debt was agreed. The destruction is the notification. Every branch of the Mithril Reserve sells them, and the Ironhands of Deiperduem write more of them than any other branch, mostly for embassies.

Hook. A counterpart in the party's keeping burns in the night. They were not a party to the contract; they were only asked to hold it. Now they must find out which of the signatories broke it, before the others decide it was them.

Ledgerlock House Merca · Existing

Very rare · wondrous item (ledger) · requires attunement by a blood-bound member or verified heir · not for sale

A ledger bound in grey leather with a mithril clasp. To anyone but a blood-bound member of its house or a verified heir it is a blank book; no magic short of wish reveals the writing, and the pages cannot be damaged by fire or water. An attuned reader can find any entry by thinking of it. Verification is a ritual of 1 hour in a Reserve vault, with a drop of blood and a Dominus Argentar as witness.

Lore. The Merca can be robbed of their records without being robbed of their secrets, which means an heir is worth considerably more to a thief than a vault. The family is rumoured to hold a Ledgerlock of every secret debt on the continent, the Duke's included, in the Vaulted Court.

Hook. A Ledgerlock has been stolen from the Deiperduem branch. The thieves cannot read it. Somebody has therefore started looking for a Merca, and Lord Selvane Merca is often at Deiperduem.

Coinborn Mark House Merca · the Coinborn Market

Very rare · wondrous item (coin) · no attunement · cannot be bought for money

A heavy coin of pale gold, stamped on one face with a stag on a pile of coins and on the other with a door. Spin it on a mirror or still water at midnight and a door opens in the nearest wall for 1 hour: it leads to the Coinborn Market, a vaulted trading chamber on another plane. Up to eight creatures may pass through with the bearer. Inside, no violence is possible (as sanctuary on every creature, DC 20), no lie can be spoken in a contract, and anything at all can be bought, priced in coin, favours and secrets. The coin is spent when the door closes behind its bearer for the last time; the Market returns it to the Merca.

Lore. The Merca are said to mint their own high-value currency, accepted only in elite circles; these are those coins. Holders include three satraps, two League oligarchs and, by rumour, the Dominus Militum's treasurer.

Hook. A Coinborn Mark turns up in a dead smuggler's purse on Zandar Isle. The Market will honour it once. The party have a week to decide what is worth buying, and the Merca will know they did.

Aetherblood Elixir House Virellarion

Rare · potion · no attunement · 1,200 gp a vial at the Gilded Crucible

A thin, quicksilver-blue draught that tastes of iron and snow. For 1 minute after drinking it, time seems to slow for you: you have advantage on Intelligence and Wisdom checks and on Dexterity saving throws, you gain a +5 bonus to initiative, and at the start of each of your turns you gain one extra reaction that you can use before the start of your next turn. When the effect ends, make a DC 13 Constitution saving throw; on a failure you gain one level of exhaustion. Drinking a second dose within 24 hours imposes disadvantage on the save.

Lore. Used by nobles at negotiations and by assassins at work. Lord Ambrose Virellarion sells it at the Gilded Crucible in the Middle District and keeps a list of buyers, which the Court of Vipers would like to read.

Hook. Three Aetherblood vials were bought last month by the same courier, for three different names. One of the names is Marcia Ferox's next opponent in the Ju Colliseum, and Marcia refuses elixirs on principle.

Soulcoil Core House Virellarion

Very rare · wondrous item (construct heart) · requires attunement by a creature proficient with tinker's tools or an artificer · 20,000 gp

A cage of bronze coils around a cut gem the size of an apple, which glows a colour that depends on the emotion inside it: red for fury, white for fear, gold for devotion. Set into a construct body (30 days' work, 5,000 gp of materials, and a DC 18 Intelligence check with tinker's tools), it animates the body as a shield guardian bonded to the attuned creature. The emotion sets its temper: a fury-core has advantage on attack rolls but must succeed on a DC 12 Wisdom save each round to break off a fight; a fear-core can cast shield on its master at will but will not leave its master's side; a devotion-core obeys anyone the master loves.

Filling a gem takes a living donor who feels the emotion strongly for an hour while holding it. The donor cannot feel that emotion for a week afterwards.

Lore. The engines of the war automata and the Crucible Spire's guardians. Countess Aurelie Virellarion's crystals hold up the Skyward Bastions as well.

Hook. Virellarion agents are buying grief. A widow in the Lower City sold hers for 50 gp and now cannot cry at her husband's grave.

Memorysteel Breastplate House Virellarion

Very rare · armour (breastplate) · requires attunement · 12,000 gp; the Countess makes one plate a year

A breastplate of matte grey metal that feels slightly soft, like cold wax. You have a +1 bonus to AC while wearing it. Any critical hit against you becomes a normal hit. The armour cannot be permanently destroyed: broken, cut or melted, it reforms overnight into the shape it remembers, provided at least half of it is in one place. Once per dawn, when you take damage, you can use your reaction to have the plate "remember" you unhurt: reduce the damage by 2d10 + your proficiency bonus.

Lore. Memorysteel is a Virellarion metal that remembers its last shape and reforms when broken. Aurelie Virellarion wears one, and makes one plate a year for whoever she thinks the citadel cannot afford to lose.

Hook. This year's plate was promised to Gavin Caesar. Roland Caesar, the heir, has asked for it instead, and Aurelie has asked the party to find out why he thinks he needs it.

The Nocturne Draught House Virellarion · Lyssira

Legendary · potion · no attunement · never sold; the recipe alone would fetch 50,000 gp from the Academy

A dark draught that smells of wet stone and night jasmine. When you drink it you fall asleep for 8 hours and walk, in body as well as mind, in the Dreaming. While under its effect you can enter the dream of any sleeping creature you know or can see, as dream but in person: you can speak, act, take objects out of the dream (they turn to glass on waking) and be harmed. Damage taken in a dream is real psychic damage. You can end the effect early as an action. When it ends, make a DC 18 Wisdom saving throw; on a failure you wake somewhere you dreamed, not where you fell asleep.

Lore. Brewed by Lyssira Virellarion, who wrote that she learned it from a "glass woman" in a dream. Aurelie has the recipe and has never dared drink it. The Dreamers' Hunt would pay anything for a dose.

Hook. A dose has been brewed, by someone with access to the Crucible Spire's still-room, and drunk. The Countess's nephew has not woken for six days, and his bed is full of glass.

The Heart-Smith's Gauntlet House Virellarion · Jevan

Artefact · wondrous item (gauntlet) · requires attunement · priceless; damnable

A gauntlet of black bronze with a crystal socket in the palm. While wearing it you can, as an action, touch a creature that died within the last minute, or a creature at 0 hit points, which makes a DC 19 Charisma saving throw. On a failure its soul is drawn into a gem held in the socket. A soul in a gem can be placed in a construct (as a Soulcoil Core, but the construct keeps the person's memories and personality) or released. While you hold a soul, you can speak with it and it cannot lie to you. Each use is an evil act: your alignment drifts one step towards evil after the third.

Destroying it. The gauntlet must be worn by its maker's soul. Jevan is still somewhere.

Lore. Forged by Jevan Virellarion, who could extract and reshape a soul into a vessel. Magus Rashnu-Vahram writes to Aurelie about it by every Reserve courier. The family says it was lost. It is in the Stillflame Vault, next to the unfinished creation that is said to be alive and waiting.

Hook. The thing in the Stillflame Vault has begun knocking. Aurelie thinks it wants the gauntlet. She is afraid it wants to give it to someone.

The Codex of Rule House Zayida

Legendary · wondrous item (ledger) · requires attunement by the keeper the Zayida appoint · priceless

A living ledger of a thousand pages whose ink moves. It tracks every registered citizen, soldier and sack of supply within the citadel's walls in real time. As an action the keeper can ask it the location, status (alive, dead, sick, imprisoned) and debts of any registered person, or the count of any category of goods in any store, and the entry rises to the page. It cannot track a person who has left the citadel's boundary stones, and it knows nothing of anybody it was never told about.

Lore. Designed by Archivist Meryn Zayida with the bureaucratic system the citadel still uses. Its keeper, Idris Zayida, has noticed that the Codex now counts fewer miners than the payroll does.

Hook. Idris gives the party a list of forty names that the payroll pays and the Codex does not count, and asks them to go and find the men.

The Chain of Command House Zayida

Very rare · wondrous item (sash) · requires attunement · 25,000 gp (the Zayida have five)

A ceremonial blue sash with a golden falcon clasp. At dawn you can name up to five creatures as your lieutenants. While you wear the sash and a lieutenant is within 120 feet of you: it uses the higher of its initiative roll and yours; it cannot be surprised unless you are; you can take the Help action as a bonus action to help a lieutenant you can see; and once per round, when a lieutenant fails a saving throw against being frightened or charmed, you can use your reaction to let it reroll.

Lore. Worn by Zayida commanders. The codex says it channels battle instincts to all lieutenants nearby; the lieutenants say it is like having a second pair of eyes in the back of the head, and a stern voice. Lady Nadira Zayida wears one to drill the Silent Warden Order.

Hook. A sash is stolen from the Aegistower. It still works; the Zayida lieutenants who wore it last can feel the new wearer's instincts, and he is planning something in the Middle City.

Warborn Oath House Zayida

Rare · wondrous item (oath-tablet and brand) · requires attunement by the sworn soldier · not for sale

A thin bronze tablet inscribed with an oath and the soldier's name, sealed with a drop of his blood, and a matching brand on the inside of the left wrist. While attuned you have advantage on saving throws against being charmed or frightened, and once per long rest, when you make an attack roll, ability check or saving throw, you can add 1d8 to it. If you act knowingly against the Duke's bloodline, the brand burns: you take 4d10 psychic damage, the tablet cracks, and the oath-breaker's mark appears on your face for a year and a day.

Lore. Given to elite soldiers of the citadel, chiefly the Silent Warden Order and the Adamantine Line under Commander Daud. The tablets are kept in the Aegistower; a cracked one is displayed in the gate for the length of the mark.

Hook. Three Warden tablets crack on the same night. None of the three soldiers has done anything. Something has happened to the Duke's bloodline instead.

The Sovereign Star House Caerthain · prototype airship

Unique · vehicle (airship, 90 ft.) · requires attunement by a creature of Caerthain blood to helm · not discussed

Vehicle. Gargantuan vehicle, AC 15, 400 hit points (damage threshold 15), speed fly 12 miles per hour (60 ft.); crew 12, passengers 20, cargo 4 tons. Its hull is lifted by levitation crystals grown in Lake Serathal and a single anchoring gem set in the keel. A Caerthain helm can, once per day, make the ship starlit for 1 minute: it becomes invisible, ignores weather, and can pass through solid rock and the grey fog that bars the rifts.

Lore. The house built the Serathian Fleet in the open and was celebrated for it. The Sovereign Star is filed with the lake, the worship and the question of whether the bloodline is still human, which suggests it is not simply a faster vessel. It is moored, people say, in a cave above Lake Serathal.

Hook. A Serathian Fleet rigger is found dead on a ledge no airship could reach, holding a fragment of glass that glows like starlight. The Zayida want the party to find out how he got there without anyone learning what he worked on.

Materials

The primordial meteor that struck during the Continental War brought ores and jewels pulsing with power, and the rifts have been coughing up more ever since. The codex lists nine of them as Ores, all assayed at the Assayers' Tower. Below are rules for working each one. The Duneforged Citadel works most of them; Mavelon's arsenal works the rest and pretends otherwise.

How crafting works. To make an item of a special material you need proficiency with the right tools (smith's tools for metal, jeweller's tools for crystal, mason's tools for stone), a forge or workshop of the right kind, the base item's cost, and the material, priced by weight (a dagger 1 lb, a shortsword 2 lb, a longsword 3 lb, a shield 6 lb, a breastplate 20 lb, plate 65 lb). Time is one workweek per 250 gp of total cost, minimum one week. At the end, make the check listed under each material with your tool proficiency. On a failure you lose a week and try again; on a failure by 5 or more, half the material is lost. An item of a special material is not a magic item unless the card says so, but it can be enchanted later like any other.

Mithril Ore · Existing

Pure: 2,500 gp per lb · Reserve-drawn: +800 gp per suit · Crafting DC 17 (smith's tools); pure work needs a moonlit forge

Reserve-drawn mithril is steel drawn with a thread of the metal. Armour made of it is uncommon: it has no Strength requirement and does not impose disadvantage on Dexterity (Stealth) checks (the DMG's mithral armour). Pure mithril weighs half as much as steel. Pure armour has the properties above and its wearer has advantage on Constitution saving throws to maintain concentration; a pure weapon never dulls, counts as magical for overcoming resistance, and repairs itself fully after a night in moonlight. A pure item is very rare.

Lore. The Mithril Reserve is named for the original Mithril Lode under the Vaulted Court, on a shard of which the Ironhand dwarves swear. The lode is thin now, which is one of the things Haldor Ironhand knows and the Duke does not.

Hook. A shipment of "pure" mithril is being sold in Mavelon at half the Reserve's price. It passes every test but one: it does not mend in moonlight.

Adamantium Ore · Existing

Pure: 5,000 gp per lb · Faced: +500 gp (armour) or +500 gp (weapon) · Crafting DC 20; needs a volcanic forge (the Geomanthic Foundries)

Faced work (steel with an adamantium edge or face) follows the DMG: faced armour turns critical hits into normal hits; faced weapons and ammunition score a critical hit against objects on any hit. Pure work has those properties and more: it is always cold; a fey or fiend hit by a pure weapon takes an extra 1d6 cold damage, and a pure item touched by a spell of 3rd level or lower suppresses the spell's effect on itself (as dispel magic, automatic). Pure adamantium cannot then be enchanted except at a forge like the Black Anvil.

Lore. Said to be fragments of the world's foundation. It forms only where elemental fire and earth balance in a volcano's heart, and the only reliable source the codex names is the Treasury of Hours.

Hook. The Geomanthic Foundries have been asked to make adamantium manacles sized for something the size of a horse. The order came under the Duke's seal; the Duke says he never sent it.

Cold Iron Ore · Existing

4 sp per lb (if you can find it) · Crafting DC 15; must be forged without heat after the first smelt · enchanting it costs double

Cold-iron weapons overcome the resistance and immunity of fey and fiends to nonmagical attacks. A fey or fiend restrained with cold-iron chains or manacles cannot teleport or become ethereal, and a creature made of pure magic (an elemental, a conjured creature) that touches cold iron takes 1d4 cold damage each round of contact. Because it disrupts magic, adding a magical property to a cold-iron item costs twice the usual time and gold.

Lore. Mined where the boundary with otherworldly realms grows thin. The Iron Furnaces of Duneforged forge a few ingots a year, and smiths who work it wear thick gloves, since prolonged contact is said to numb the soul.

Hook. Witch-hunters of the Sanctuary of the Silver Veil have bought the whole of this year's ingots. The fey of Nemibano's grove have noticed.

Arcanaite Ore · Existing

250 gp per thumb-sized crystal · Crafting DC 16 (jeweller's tools) · unstable in quantity

A crystal set into a spellcasting focus (a day's work) gives a +1 bonus to spell attack rolls made through it; the focus is an uncommon magic item. A crystal takes on the school of the first spell of 3rd level or higher cast through it; thereafter, once per long rest, you can add +1 to the save DC of a spell of that school. Ground to powder, one crystal can replace any material component worth up to 250 gp that is not consumed.

Instability. Whenever a spell of 1st level or higher is cast within 10 feet of six or more crystals, roll a d20; on a 1, roll on the Wild Magic Surge table. Large deposits grow aware and become what scholars call living dungeons.

Lore. Grows where great spellcasters fought. Mages use it as currency; artificers embed it in items to make them work better; the Arcane Academy keeps its stock in a cellar nobody visits.

Hook. A wartime battlefield in the Latium Plains has begun to sparkle. Three crews of diggers have gone in, and the field has started to rearrange itself around them.

Nullstone Ore · Existing

1,000 gp per lb · Crafting DC 18 (mason's tools); cannot be worked with magical tools; cannot be enchanted

Nullstone is immune to all magical effects. A pound of worked nullstone suppresses spells of 2nd level or lower in a 5-foot radius around it, as antimagic field; each further pound adds 5 feet to the radius and one spell level, to a maximum of 30 feet and 5th level. Nullstone manacles (2 lb, 2,100 gp) prevent their wearer from casting spells or using magical abilities.

Drain. A spellcaster who spends 24 hours in contact with nullstone makes a DC 15 Constitution saving throw. On a failure they lose their highest-level spell slot until they receive greater restoration. After seven days of contact the loss is permanent.

Lore. Forms at the centre of dead-magic clearings like a scab over reality. Some rulers line their throne rooms with it; the Truth-Flame's cells at Hellarchon are floored with it.

Hook. The Treaty Hall at Deiperduem is quietly buying nullstone, by the cartload, through three different factors. Aulus Custos does not know, and his wards will not survive it.

Tethtrium Ore · Existing

1,500 gp per lb · Crafting DC 17 (smith's tools) · lockpicks (0.1 lb): 300 gp

Tethtrium lockpicks give advantage on checks to pick locks and can pick a lock from the other side of a door up to 6 inches thick. A tethtrium-edged weapon (half its weight in tethtrium) can strike creatures on the Ethereal Plane from the Material Plane and ignores resistance granted by being incorporeal. On a natural 1 with such a weapon it phases out and drops through the floor; it reappears 1d4 rounds later somewhere within 30 feet.

Hazard. A smith who fails the crafting check by 5 or more partly leaves the world: for 1d4 days they are under a blink effect they cannot control.

Lore. Matter from the space between worlds, named after the first scholar to study it. It forms near old portals and rift-sites, and thieves pay anything for it.

Hook. A Mithril Reserve vault in Aepistra has been emptied without a single lock being broken, and the Dominus Argentar wants to know who sold tethtrium to whom.

Embersteel Ore · Existing · the Embersteel Line

1,000 gp per lb · Crafting DC 20 (smith's tools); the ingot burns away on a failure unless the smith is of House Vulkrim or trained at the Geomanthic Foundries · weapons uncommon, armour rare

Embersteel glows like a forge's heart and warms without burning its wielder. An embersteel weapon sheds dim light for 10 feet and deals an extra 1d4 fire damage on a hit. As an action you can touch its flat to a creature at 0 hit points to stabilise it. Embersteel armour gives resistance to cold damage. Either repairs itself overnight, and in fire it hardens: an embersteel item exposed to fire damage gains a +1 bonus (to attack and damage, or AC) for 1 minute. The DM may award a permanent +1 to an embersteel item after a genuinely heroic deed done with it, once.

Lore. House Vulkrim forges the Embersteel Line exclusively, from ore that forms where legendary fires burned. Their hidden forgefire is said to be a shard of elemental flame.

Hook. Embersteel blades are being sold in Corinth without the Vulkrim mark. Quartermaster Thestun Vulkrim thinks the Jackal of the Broken Gate stole ingots, and wants the forger found before Ottilde hears.

Shattergleam Crystal Ore · Existing · "Earth's Cruel Joke"

Worthless to smiths · 50 gp to a showman · cannot be crafted

Every attempt to work shattergleam in magic, smithing or alchemy has failed, and the rules reflect it: no crafting check succeeds, and the dust evaporates within hours. Collecting a geode intact takes a DC 18 Dexterity check with jeweller's tools; on a failure it bursts, and each creature within 5 feet takes 2d6 piercing damage from splinters. In darkness a geode throws ghostly halos and shapes; they are not magical and do not register to detect magic, but a creature seeing them for the first time must succeed on a DC 10 Wisdom saving throw or believe them a sign.

Dwarven miners call it Mhalaz-dur and leave it alone. A character who carries one into a dwarf-worked mine has disadvantage on Charisma checks with the miners for a week.

Hook. A R'eyshar kiln-master says his shattergleam shows the same picture every night: a gate with a socket over it, and a light in the socket.

Anchoring Gem Ore · Existing · artificial

Very rare · 25,000 gp and up (none are openly sold) · cannot be made: the method is lost

A gem like arcanaite, its surface rippling over a grey core. An anchoring gem can tether a Bound Rift to the world. The ritual takes 8 hours at the rift and a DC 20 Intelligence (Arcana) check by a creature able to cast 5th-level spells. On a success the rift becomes an Anchored Rift and stays open as long as the gem stays in its setting. On a failure by less than 5 the rift closes; by 5 or more it becomes a Shifting Rift for 1d4 hours, and something comes out. Removing the gem from an Anchored Rift collapses it in 1d10 rounds, with anyone inside.

Lore. Made by scholars of the ancient times before magic rampaged; the Bound Rift used to produce them closed unexpectedly, and the art went with it. Each empire guards the few it holds. Some gems turn up by accident on old sites, and the Assayers' Tower buys them without asking where.

Hook. A child in Alderpool has been playing with a grey, rippling pebble. Three different buyers arrive in the same week, and the forest behind the village has started to look like somewhere else.

Common magic of the three empires

What a party of fourth level can actually buy: the small magic of soldiers, sailors and diggers, sold in every market that has a temple and a garrison. Prices are city prices.

Sarcina of the March Invictian legion kit

Common · wondrous item (marching pole and pack) · no attunement · 75 gp (surplus at Anticata: 40)

A forked pole with a leather satchel, cooking pot, mess-tin, entrenching tool and stake, all stamped with a legion's mark. While carrying it you count as one size larger for determining your carrying capacity, and you make no Constitution saving throws for a forced march during the first 2 hours of travel beyond the usual eight. As an action you can drive the stake: a 10-foot square around it is cleared and levelled for a camp in 10 minutes.

Lore. "Mules", the legions called themselves. Demobilised men sell their sarcinae at the Veterans' Field, and the quartermasters buy them back at half price when they remember to.

Hook. A bought sarcina still has its last owner's discharge diploma sewn into the lining, with a land-grant nobody honoured. His widow would like the land.

Posca Canteen Invictian legion kit

Common · wondrous item · no attunement · 60 gp

A tin canteen in a felt cover. Water poured into it becomes posca, the sour wine-and-water of the legions, and any disease or poison in the water is neutralised. Once per dawn, a creature that drinks a full ration from it ends the poisoned condition on itself and needs only half the usual water that day. It holds 2 pints.

Lore. Issued to every legion on campaign; quartermasters treat them as better than any surgeon. They are sold at every Annona station that still has stock, which is fewer every quarter.

Hook. A batch of canteens from the Aeterna depots turn water to vinegar and do nothing else. Someone sold the depot's blessing and kept the blessing money.

Eye of the Prow Hellenorian sea charm

Common · wondrous item (painted board) · no attunement · 60 drachmas

A pair of eyes painted on cedar boards, nailed to either side of a vessel's bow and blessed at a harbour shrine. While fitted, the vessel's pilot has advantage on checks to navigate in fog and darkness, cannot become lost in Nereid's Veil, and knows when the vessel is within a mile of rocks or shoals. A ship whose eyes are painted over (an old insult) loses the benefit until reblessed.

Lore. Every Hellenorian hull has eyes; only a blessed pair works. The pilots' shrine at the Lechaion blesses about four hundred a year, and refuses any ship carrying a charmed keel.

Hook. Someone is painting over the eyes of Corinthian ships at night. Three have since gone on the rocks inside the Veil.

Diver's Stone Hellenorian sponge-divers

Uncommon · wondrous item · no attunement · 150 gp

A flat, drilled slab of marble on a rope, the weight a sponge-diver rides to the bottom. While holding it underwater you sink up to 60 feet per round if you wish, you can hold your breath for 10 minutes, and you take no damage from pressure. Once per dawn, as an action while holding it, you can cast water breathing on yourself only, lasting 1 hour.

Lore. The divers of the Sponge Banks hand their stones down mother to daughter. A stone with four generations of knots on its rope is worth twice the price and is never sold.

Hook. The divers have found a wreck in sixty fathoms with bronze fittings and a sealed lead reservoir. They want a buyer for the fittings and someone else to open the reservoir.

Drachmae Divine coin · Existing

Common · wondrous item (coin) · no attunement · 100 gp without divinity; 500 gp with divinity; 1,000 gp to the temple of the deity on the coin (negotiable)

A gold coin struck from gold transmuted by a quasi- or demi-deity and charged with its divinity. Thrown into a rainbow (natural, or one made with a prism, spray or prestidigitation in sunlight), it carries a message of up to twenty-five words to any creature you name, as sending; the reply returns on the next rainbow you see. The coin is consumed. A coin "without divinity" is good gold and nothing more, and only a priest can tell the difference by eye (or detect magic).

Lore. Temples buy them back at double the market, which tells you who mints most of them. The Mithril Reserve will not hold them on deposit, on the grounds that a coin which talks to gods is not neutral.

Hook. A purse of drachmae paid to the party turns out to be charged, and each coin carries the face of a god nobody at the temple recognises.

Muqanni's Lamp Acheaorian qanat lamp

Common · wondrous item · no attunement · 90 gp

A clay lamp on a rope with a wick that never needs oil. It sheds bright light for 15 feet and dim light for 15 more until covered. The flame turns blue and gutters when there is bad air (poisonous gas, smoke or too little air to breathe) within 30 feet, and leans towards the nearest running water within 300 feet. Lowered down a shaft on its rope, it shows what lies at the bottom as a faint image in the smoke.

Lore. The muqanni who dig and clear the qanats carry them down; the Mark of a lamp on a rope is the badge of the Gav family at Qa'zshahrv'in. A muqanni whose lamp goes blue climbs at once, and nobody calls him a coward for it.

Hook. Every lamp in a qanat town went blue on the same night, and stayed blue. Nobody will go down, and the channel has started to slow.

Plateau Fire-Oil Acheaorian naphtha flask

Common (not magical) · adventuring gear · no attunement · 25 gp per sealed flask (1 lb); temple licence required in Acheaoria

A clear, light oil from the seeps of the plateau, sealed in a clay flask with wax. As an action you can throw it at a creature or object within 20 feet; make a ranged attack, treating the flask as an improvised weapon. On a hit the target takes 2d6 fire damage and burns, taking 1d6 fire damage at the start of each of its turns until a creature uses an action to smother it with a successful DC 13 Dexterity check. It burns on water. Its vapour catches from a spark: a flask opened within 5 feet of an open flame ignites in the opener's hands.

Lore. The priests tend the eternal fires above the seeps in the Parthian Ravine and near Mithratal, and ask pilgrims not to hold the oil up to the light. It is not Hellenic fire, however many tyrants' alchemists hope it is.

Hook. A Chyrsus Syndicate factor wants twenty flasks carried west on the Treaty Road, unlicensed. The Magi want to know who is selling the earth's breath.

Expansion

The Farshore Realms in Detail

Asetheria's three empires spent fifteen centuries fighting each other and almost no time looking outward. The peace changed that within a year. Ships from beyond the outer sea now tie up at the Farshore Quays on the eastern mole of Mavelon's south harbour, pass the Aurum Pact's isolation sheds, and send their cargo inland to be weighed and sealed in the Hall of Weights at Romulo, where some sixty foreign offices line the Guild Square, each with a mosaic before its door. Hellenoria lets the same ships into Corinth, Ephelanum and Hellarchon's Spice Wharf for the harbour Fiftieth; Acheaoria meets the far east at the end of its caravan roads in Atarabad. What follows is what the Farshore peoples are like at home, as far as Asetherians can tell, and what they want here.

What the Farshore ships bring

GoodFromPrice at Romulo (sealed)Price on the quay at Mavelon (unsealed)Notes
Tin, per ingot (10 lb)Pretanna, via Qart-Hadeth12 gp8 gpBronze is impossible without it; Duneforged bell-founders buy by the shipload
Purple cloth, per boltTyrsa, Qart-Hadeth150 gp110 gpSumptuary law in Aeterna limits who may wear it; nobody obeys
Grain, per 100 modiiKhemaret9 gp6 gpHalf the Annona's price; the Golden Harvest Covenant lobbies for a tariff
Papyrus, per rollKhemaret2 sp1 spEvery chancery on the continent now writes on it
Saffron, per ounceKeftara15 gp11 gpCompetes with Atarabad's Saffron Terraces
Aksumari gold pieceAksumar1.15 gp1.1 gpTrades above face value because it is true gold
Frankincense / myrrh, per poundSabaia, Aksumar25 gp18 gpEvery temple burns it; the fire-temples buy it and deny it
Pepper, per poundMaurash4 gp3 gpThe fashionable spice of Romulo's merchant tables
Wootz steel, per ingotMaurash120 gp90 gpA blade forged from it counts as a silvered weapon against lycanthropes (DM option)
Silk, per boltSeres (overland via Atarabad)200 gpnot legally soldAcheaoria controls the road and the price
Cacao, per poundIxtal40 gpnone in yearsThe last stocks are hoarded by three Romulo houses
Obsidian mirrorIxtal500 gpnoneNethranan scholars pay anything; see the DM note
Qart-Hadeth, the New City Merchant republic across the southern sea

Rulers: the shofetim Hanno-Baal and Abdmelqart (this year) and the Council of the Hundred and Four · Emblem: the elephant · Faith: the Lord of the Harbour and the Lady of the Face

At home. A city on a headland with two harbours: an oblong merchant harbour and a round, roofed war-harbour whose central island holds the admiralty, so no spy can count the hulls. Two shofetim, judges elected each year, preside; the real power is the Hundred and Four, a court that audits generals and has crucified two who lost. Its merchant clans, the house of Magon chief among them, own plantations inland worked by debt-labour, and hire their wars out to mercenaries.

In Asetheria. The largest office on Romulo's Guild Square belongs to Himilkat of the house of Magon, who keeps the best table in the caravan suburb and lends to Invictian patricians at rates the Mithril Reserve undercuts and he does not care. At Mavelon, the harbour agent Bomilqar handles their tin, ivory and purple, and is very polite about the fact that his republic is the Imperium's oldest sea rival abroad. The Imperium still forbids Mavelon's yards to sell Qart-Hadeth a keel.

What they want. Silver, iron and above all Mavelon-built hulls and the secret of Hellenic fire. Hellenoria sells them everything except the fire. Acheaoria courts them as a counterweight to both.

Tyrsa, the Rock Purple-dye island city, mother of Qart-Hadeth

Ruler: King Ithobaal III and the Elders of the Rock · Emblem: the murex shell · Faith: the City-Lord who dies and rises each spring

At home. An island city a few hundred yards off its own coast, walled to the waterline, stinking gloriously of the murex vats that make its purple. Its pilots are taught from the age of seven and its charts are guarded as royal property. Tyrsa founded Qart-Hadeth and is now the poorer and older of the two, proud, prickly and indispensable.

In Asetheria. Adonibaal of Tyrsa, the best pilot in the Mouth of Mavelon, sells charts of seas no Invictian has sailed and buys rumours at the same rate. The Imperial navy quietly hires Tyrsan pilots for every Farshore voyage and pretends the charts are its own. Ephelanum's Tyrian Vats were named for the Rock, which Tyrsans find hilarious, and Helionyx's dyers hate their purple.

What they want. Cedar, which Asetheria's mountains have and their coast no longer does, and the right to dye in Asetheria without paying the dyers' guilds.

Khemaret, the Two Lands of the Great House River kingdom

Ruler: the Great House, Neferkare-Ahmes, god-king · Emblem: the ibis · Faith: a hundred animal-headed gods and the king who is one of them

At home. A green ribbon of fields on either side of one enormous river, desert beyond it in both directions, a flood every year that the priests predict to the day. Its god-king is called only "the Great House" because his name is too holy to use. Its scribes are the oldest bureaucracy anyone knows of, and its embalmers keep the dead looking alive for a thousand years.

In Asetheria. Khemareti grain hulls are the largest ships at the Farshore Quays. Their arrival is a political event: a year of Khemareti grain would end the Golden Harvest Covenant's grip on the Annona, and every Legate knows it. The Khemareti office on the Guild Square, under the ibis mosaic, is run by a scribe-priest, Pa-di-Aset, who has asked twice to witness the Acheaorian Rite of Return.

What they want. Timber, silver and knowledge of how the Immortals are raised. Their priests think the Acheaorians have stolen a secret that belongs to the embalmers' god.

Keftara Fading island of the labyrinth-palaces

Ruler: the Priest-Queen of Kenossa · Emblem: the double axe · Faith: the Mother of the Mountain and the bull from the sea

At home. An island of palace-towns with no walls, because for a thousand years its fleet was the wall. Its palaces are mazes of light-wells and painted corridors; its young people leap over charging bulls in sacred games. The fleet is a fraction of what it was, the palaces are half-empty, and an earthquake twenty years ago took the north coast.

In Asetheria. Keftara's office on the Guild Square has been shuttered for a decade, its double-axe mosaic swept daily by a Romulo slave paid from a fund nobody can trace. Keftaran bull-leapers still perform at Romulo's festivals for whoever pays their passage, and its saffron undercuts Atarabad's.

What they want. Help, which they will not ask for directly: grain, ships and a protector against Qart-Hadeth.

Aksumar Highland kingdom beyond the narrow sea

Ruler: Negasi Ezana-Gebre, King of Kings of the highlands · Emblem: the coin · Faith: the Moon and the Morning Star, and lately a stranger god

At home. A kingdom of terraced highlands, granite stelae taller than any Invictian column, and a harbour on the narrow sea where ivory, gold and frankincense meet the monsoon ships. It is the only Farshore realm that strikes its own gold coin, and strikes it true.

In Asetheria. The coin mosaic on the Guild Square marks the busiest money-changing table in Romulo. In an Imperium whose silver loses weight every quarter, the Aksumari gold piece is the most trusted coin on the continent: the Mithril Reserve takes it at a premium and the Imperial Mint would give a great deal for its assay.

What they want. Iron tools, glass, wine and alliances against Sabaia, their incense rival across the strait.

Sabaia The incense kingdom

Ruler: Queen-Mukarrib Bilqa'at · Emblem: the censer · Faith: the Moon-God of the great dam

At home. A desert kingdom made rich by a single great dam and the trees that weep frankincense and myrrh. Its queen rules by priestly title as much as crown, and her caravans and sewn-plank ships carry the smoke of every temple in the known world.

In Asetheria. Every temple in all three empires burns Sabaian incense, which gives a small kingdom a remarkable hold. Its envoys travel with the Queen's letter and a list of which temples have paid. The Magi hold incense impure and buy it anyway, through Wheelwalker middlemen, so the purchase is never recorded.

What they want. Ships, now that their own sewn-plank hulls cannot match Mavelon's, and the guarantee that no empire will try to grow the incense tree.

Maurash, the Ninefold Kingdom Reached on the monsoon

Ruler: the Emperor Chandragupta-Vasu over nine kings · Emblem: the pepper vine · Faith: many gods and a wheel of law carved on pillars

At home. An empire so large Asetherians do not believe its census, watered by monsoon rains that arrive as if summoned. Its emperor carves edicts on stone pillars along every road; its philosophers walk naked and argue in the market; its smiths make steel watered like silk.

In Asetheria. Maurashi pepper boats come in on the monsoon to Acheaoria's southern harbours and to Mavelon; its caravans reach Atarabad. Its watered-steel ingots are the only metal House Vulkrim admits to envying. One of its naked philosophers has been debating Krates the Dog on the Porticoes of Thessalonika for a month and neither will concede.

What they want. Horses, wine and gold; and the philosophers want to know what Asetherians think the gods are for.

Seres, the Seric Throne The far-east continent

Ruler: the Son of the Sky · Emblem: none shown; an empty office · Faith: Heaven's mandate and the ancestors

At home. Almost nothing is known for certain. The silk at the end of the Silk Terminus comes from there, by roads Acheaoria controls and charges for. Seric envoys are so rare they are treated as omens. Seric crossbows, which a child can span, are a weapon every Legate wants and none has seen working.

In Asetheria. On Romulo's Guild Square one swept, empty office is kept for the Seric Throne. Last year, for the first time, a Seric ship reached Mavelon by sea, bypassing the caravan road; the Acheaorian embassy in Deiperduem has asked three times what was in its hold. A Seric envoy's ship has now entered the Mouth again, and every ceremony on the island is postponed while the priesthoods argue what it portends.

What they want. Horses that can carry an armoured man, glass, and, the envoys say, "to see the other edge of the world before the Throne decides what to do about it".

Pretanna, the Tin Isles Misty northern islands

Rulers: many kings and queens, and the druids above them · Emblem: the hound · Faith: groves, springs and drowned kings

At home. Islands of rain, hill-forts and tin streams, ruled by quarrelsome kings who all defer to the druids, who never write anything down. Its warriors paint themselves blue and fight from chariots; its hunting dogs are the best afloat.

In Asetheria. Without Pretannic tin there is no bronze, and without bronze no Hellenorian statue, Invictian standard or Duneforged bell. Pretannic skippers trade at the hound mosaic in Romulo, but they prefer Mavelon's north harbour, out of the Dux's sight, where the Mavari swap songs with them about drowned kings and both peoples pretend the songs are only songs. Its druids correspond with the Circle of the Eternal Grove in Foloicauria.

What they want. Wine, bronze vessels, and to be left out of Asetheria's politics, which they consider a southern disease.

The Feathered Courts of Ixtal Across the western ocean

Rulers: the city-kings of the stepped pyramids · Emblem: the jade mask · Faith: the feathered serpent, the maize god, blood offered for the sun

At home. City-kingdoms of white stepped pyramids in a green country, where kings read the stars from temple-tops and record their victories on carved stelae in a script of faces. Their ships have reached Asetheria twice in living memory.

In Asetheria. The last Ixtali ship, thirty-one years ago, left a carved stela on Mavelon's south quay that nobody can read and a jade mask that now hangs over the weighers' door in Romulo's Hall of Weights. Cacao has become the ruinous vice of Romulo's merchant houses. Their polished obsidian mirrors fascinate the scholars of Nethrana, for obvious reasons.

What they want. Unknown. The first ship came to trade; the second came, by the stela's pictures, to warn.

Expansion

Inns, Shops and Services

Inns, Shops and Services

Where to sleep, what to buy and who sells magic, city by city. Prices follow the 5e Player's Handbook and Dungeon Master's Guide; the local coin is given first and the gp value where it matters.

Fifteen centuries of war left three coinages, three sets of weights and a continent of money-changers who are never short of work. The peace has made it worse, because now everybody's coin reaches everybody else's market. Every price in this part is what a willing seller asks a stranger who looks as if he can pay. Haggling (Persuasion DC 12) takes a tenth off; a known local pays a fifth less without trying.

The practical rule: an obol, an as and a pashiz are all small change; a drachma, a denarius and a siglos are each worth about a gold piece at full weight; a daric is a fortune in one hand. The Invictian denarius is the exception that matters. It is debased every quarter at the Assay in the Temple of Juno, and nobody outside the Imperium takes it at face.

Magic for sale: common items are found in most cities; uncommon in any city with a Mithril Reserve branch; rare only to order or by luck. Items carry their Asetherian names first and the game name in brackets. Double these prices in a town; halve them when the seller is in a hurry.

Aeterna Imperium Invicta · prices in denarii and asses

A million mouths, short grain, light coin. Everything is for sale and most of it is cheaper than last year, because the demobilised legions are selling their kit to eat.

The Three Geese Inn · under the Arx

Keeper: Opimia Galla, a centurion's widow · Where: the foot of the Arx, by the stair to Juno Moneta (the Arx)

A tall brick inn with real glass in the front windows, named for the sacred geese on the hill above and kept by a woman who served nine years beside her husband's century and can still clear a room with one word. Mint clerks, Assay officials and provincial petitioners waiting for an audience drink in the front room; the back room is for anyone with a seal.

Rooms: a shared garret, 3 asses (poor); a room with a door and a lock, 8 sestertii (comfortable, 2 gp at face); the "Senator's room" with a brazier and a bath brought up, 4 denarii (aristocratic). Food: lentils and sausage, goose on Juno's day, a sharp Falecosa white at 2 asses a cup.

Rumour: the Assay scales were weighed against Romulo's master standard last month, privately, and the clerks came back looking ill.

The Wet Hen Tavern and lodging · the Insulae

Keeper: Sextus Pupius, called Hen · Where: ground floor of a six-storey block in the Insulae

A counter open to the street with jars of hot stew sunk into it, a back room of benches, and four floors of rooms above that would burn in ten minutes. Veterans from the camps at the boundary stones drink here and argue about the land they were promised; the Vigiles drink here to listen.

Rooms: a mat on the floor, 1 as (squalid); a shared room, 2 asses (poor). Food: chickpea stew, 1 as; bread that is half Annona bran. Who drinks: veterans, porters, a Vigiles informer called Lupa.

Rumour: a Legate's recruiter pays a denarius a head for men who still have their own armour, and does not ask which legion they left.

Fulvius and Sons, Armourers Smith · the Campus

Master: Gaius Fulvius Faber · Where: the Campus Hastarum

The old legion contractors, now living off surplus. The yard is stacked with returned kit bought from veterans at a tenth of its price: helmets, shields and the plated cuirass the legions call segmented armour. Fulvius refurbishes and sells it with the legion stamp filed off, which is legal, and the unit number left on the inside, which is not.

Stock: legion short sword 8 denarii; spear 1; scutum (shield) 8; refurbished splint-cut cuirass (splint) 160; chain shirt 40; a new mail hauberk (chain mail) 70. Repairs while you wait. Prices a fifth under the PHB for anything secondhand.

The Amber Stalls Market lane · existing

Mistress of the Lane: Gavia Rufilla · Where: by the Circus gates under the commons' hill

Nineteen jewellers' booths that sell northern amber with a story attached; the stories are lies and the eyes are the best in the capital. For everything else, the Emporium wharves sell rope, oil, lamps, sacks and Farshore papyrus straight off the Fucostia barges at PHB prices, and a sack of Annona wheat at the back door for three denarii.

Stock: a plain amber bead 5 sp; carved pendant 15 gp; amber with a whole insect 50 gp and up; loupes for hire at an as an hour.

The Artisan's Forge of Wonders Magic seller · licensed collegium

Master of the collegium: Appius Lentulus Vatia, a dry man in a scorched toga · Where: a fortified shop off the Forum

The capital's only licensed sellers of enchanted goods, and the reason the Gilded Crucible cannot open a counter in Aeterna. Everything carries a collegium seal. Prices are high, quality is honest, and the collegium reports every buyer of a weapon to the Prefect of the Vigiles.
