The Ravens of the Campus Odd service · augury for hire

Augur: Titus Aufidius Corax · Where: a marked square of turf at the edge of the Campus

A licensed augur with a lituus staff and a cage of trained ravens. He will take the auspices for any enterprise: 2 denarii for a private matter, 10 for a contract, 50 for a voyage or a marriage, the price of a farm for a Legate. A favourable sign is worth advantage on one Persuasion check with any pious Invictian who hears of it.

Rumour: two Legates have each paid him for the same answer to the same question, and he has given it to both.

Romulo Imperium Invicta · prices in denarii, foreign coin weighed

Every great cargo is sealed at the Hall of Weights, so every Farshore factor on the continent eventually sleeps here. The old town is two storeys high; the money sleeps outside the wall.

The Four Storeys Inn · the Caravan Suburb

Keeper: Marcus Vettius Calvus, a former customs clerk · Where: the Caravan Suburb

The first building outside the wall to go up four storeys, and named so that nobody would forget it. Caravan yards behind, factors' rooms above, a dining hall where a Qart-Hadethi shofet's agent and a Tyrsan pilot may share a table and a translator. Calvus keeps a slate of the day's seal queue at the Hall of Weights and charges nothing to read it.

Rooms: a bunk in the drovers' loft, 1 sestertius; a factor's room with a strongbox, 2 denarii (wealthy); stabling 2 sestertii a beast. Food: pepper on everything, because the factors pay for it; Khemaret beer; fish sauce from Fucostia.

Rumour: the swept empty office in the Guild Square, kept for the Seric Throne, had its lamp lit last week. Nobody admits to lighting it.

The Hearth-Step Inn · inside the wall

Keeper: Postumia, of a family that has kept it since the city was a market town · Where: near the Hearth

Two storeys, as the law demands, and six rooms only. Pilgrims to Vesta's first hearth stay here, and so do patricians who would rather not be seen in the suburb. Quiet, clean and expensive, with a courtyard well that the family claims is older than the walls.

Rooms: 3 denarii a night (aristocratic), meals included. Food: spelt porridge, honey, old-fashioned and correct. Who drinks: nobody, loudly.

The Sealwright's Smith · seals, weights and locks

Master: Gnaea Arria, sealwright to the Hall · Where: the Vault Streets

Romulo's smiths make few swords. They make bronze weights checked against the master standard, seal-rings, padlocks and strongboxes, and the iron-bound cargo chests that the Hall of Weights will seal. A sword can be had to order from a back forge, at PHB price plus a fifth.

Stock: a certified weight-set 20 denarii; seal-ring cut to your device 5; good lock 10; strongbox with two keys 25; manacles 2.

The Coin Mosaic Table Money-changer and Farshore importer · the Guild Square

Changer: Hanno son of Bodashtart, Qart-Hadethi · Where: the Guild Square

The busiest money-changing table in Romulo, on the mosaic of Aksumar's coin. Hanno changes any coin on the continent and several from off it, sells Farshore goods by sample and takes orders for the next ship into Mavelon. He takes Aksumari gold at 1.15 gp and pays it out at 1.1.

Stock: pepper 4 gp a pound; papyrus 2 sp a roll; a bolt of Tyrsan purple 150 gp; wootz steel ingot 120 gp; cacao "next season"; a war-elephant on a year's notice and a deposit that would buy a villa.

The Temple Shop of Mercury of the Square Magic seller · temple concession

Keeper: the priest Lucius Mercatorius Felix · Where: the end of the Guild Square

Mercury's priests sell travellers' charms and the god's own goods to merchants about to risk everything, and accept payment in any coin, which is a blessing in itself.

ItemPriceAvailability

The Hall of Weights Sworn Copyist Odd service · certified copies

Copyist: Decimus Tullius Scriba, blind in one eye · Where: a stool outside the Hall's door

A contract sealed at Romulo binds everywhere in the Imperium. A sworn copy of the seal register costs 5 denarii a line and proves a cargo was weighed. Tullius also offers, quietly, to "find" a seal register entry that was never made, at 200 denarii.

Rumour: the master standard was taken out of its case at night and returned a little lighter.

Aepistra Imperium Invicta · prices in denarii

A camp turned city at the end of the Via Septentrionalis, where the Treaty Road brings Acheaorian silk and the Legate's recruiters buy drinks.

The Mansio at the Terminus Inn · state posting-house

Keeper: Manius Accius Rufus, mansionarius · Where: the Terminus Yards

The state post's inn, built to the regulation plan: stables round a court, baths in one wing, rooms in the other. Couriers with a warrant sleep free. Everyone else pays, and Acheaorian caravaneers pay double because the clerk can.

Rooms: a cot, 4 asses (modest); a private room, 1 denarius (comfortable); a fresh post-horse only with a warrant. Food: barley bread, camp sausage, and Acheaorian tea, which the clerks have taken to. Who drinks: couriers, customs men, the Suren-Pahlav factor.

Rumour: the Legate's couriers carry two bags, and only one goes to Aeterna.

The Speaking Horse Tavern · the Canabae

Keeper: Brannoc's widow Senna, a native of the old tongue · Where: the Canabae

A low tavern by the horse-fair with the white mare painted over the door. The old regional tongue is spoken openly and the Legate's recruiters drink here every night, paying a denarius a mark.

Rooms: loft beds, 2 asses. Food: mutton, beer, a harsh corn spirit. Rumour: the recruiters' list includes men who were never asked.

The Fabrica Smith · old legion workshop

Master: Quintus Ennius Malleolus · Where: the Old Lines

The legion's arms workshop stayed when the legion moved; the smiths now work on contract, and the contract is mostly the Legate's. Civilian orders wait behind his. Saddlery and horse-harness for the caravans are quicker.

Stock: longsword 15 denarii; lance 10; scale cuirass 50; saddle 10; horseshoes and shoeing 1. Military orders first; a bribe of 5 jumps the queue.

The Silk Shed of House Suren-Pahlav General trader · Treaty Road goods

Factor: Mehrdad Suren, nephew of the house · Where: beside the Terminus Yards

The western end of the Silk Terminus. Silk, saffron and carpets in; Invictian silver out, weighed. Also road gear for the Treaty Road: water-skins, tents, camel tack, and introductions to the Caravan of the Gilded Horizon.

Stock: silk bolt 200 gp; saffron 15 gp an ounce; a Tabrishi'ir carpet 50–500 gp; camel 50 gp; a seat on the Gilded Horizon to Deiperduem 20 denarii.

The White Mare's Garden Magic and herb seller · temple of Ceres

Seller: Mother Cinnia, herb-woman to the temple · Where: behind the Ceres shrine

Kettil's Back Counter Odd service · caravan finance

Banker: Kettil Ironhand, Dominus Argentar, Mithril Reserve

Kettil finances caravans on a share of the profit, a tenth up front and a third at the far end. He will also hold a party's valuables in the vault at 1 gp a month a box, and does not ask what is in the box.

Rumour: the Legate's account grows faster than a Legate's pay allows.

Mavelon Imperium Invicta · two harbours, two prices, and the gate between

North of the gate the Mavari price in silver by weight and in favours. South of it everything is in denarii, sealed, and dear. The Farshore Quays on the south harbour's eastern mole are where the world comes ashore.

The Upturned Keel Inn and mead-hall · north side

Keeper: Hrodlaug Ingvarsdottir, a cousin of the Reiks · Where: the North Harbour

A long hall roofed with an old longship turned keel-up, a hearth down the middle, and benches where idle Mavari crews watch the empty slips across the water. Strangers drink at the door end until someone vouches for them. A guest who breaks the peace of the hall answers to the Thing.

Rooms: a bench by the fire, 2 asses or a story; a box-bed in the cave behind, 1 sestertius (modest). Food: smoked fish, barley, mead sweetened with cliff-thyme honey. Who drinks: shipwrights, fishermen, Mavari spear-bearers, and the odd navy rating who has married north.

Rumour: the Dux's men measured the north gate's hinges at night.

The Farshore House Inn · south harbour

Keeper: Batbaal of Tyrsa, a pilot who stopped sailing · Where: by the Farshore Quays, the South Harbour

A whitewashed courtyard inn with cedar beams from Tyrsa and a dozen languages on the menu board. Factors from Qart-Hadeth, Khemaret, Sabaia and Maurash wait here for their cargo to clear customs and for a Romulo seal. Batbaal sells charts in the back room.

Rooms: 2 denarii (wealthy), a suite over the water 4 (aristocratic). Food: spiced fish in the Tyrsan way, Khemaret bread, wine cut with snow brought down from the rim. Who drinks: Farshore factors, navy officers on half-pay, Hallveig Ironhand's clerks.

Rumour: a Qart-Hadethi ship unloaded no cargo and left lighter than it came.

The Great Forge-Hall of House Demetria Smith · the Mill Banks

Master: Demetrius Glaukos · Where: the Mill Banks

The ironmasters of the Imperium's arsenal sell to private buyers whatever the navy has not ordered this year, which since the peace is a great deal. Ship-fittings, boarding axes, marine armour, grapnels and chain. "Opus loquitur": the work speaks, and is priced as if it sang.

Stock: boarding axe (handaxe) 6 denarii; trident 6; half-plate 800; breastplate 420; grappling hook 3; fifty feet of arsenal chain 6. Ship repairs by quote.

The Tide Market General market · north harbour

Warden: Old Sigrun of the Fish-Stones

Opens at the turn of the tide on the shingle: fish untaxed by treaty, clinker boats built to order, rope from the ropewalks, pumice, lamp-oil and seal-fat. Payment in silver by weight; debased denarii go on the scale like anything else.

Stock: rowing boat 50 gp; a fast clinker dispatch hull 3,000 gp; 50 ft hemp rope 1 gp; a barrel of smoked fish 2 gp; pumice by the sack, a copper.

The Glass-Stone Cellars Magic and alchemy · volcanic-glass workings

Seller: Lucretia Vatinia Obsidiana, glass-adept · Where: under the Ravines

Black volcanic glass is cut and polished in the old cellars, and some of it takes enchantment better than any crystal. The workshop also sells Farshore remedies it should not have.

The Baths of Mavelon Odd service · volcanic hot springs

Keeper: Tertia Sulpicia, for the Dux's office

Fed by the volcano and open before dawn for the forge shifts; the only building on the south side where Mavari and Invictians strip to the same skin. A quadrans to enter, an as for oil and a strigil, a denarius for a private room. A long soak counts as a short rest that also ends one level of exhaustion from heat or labour.

Rumour: the Reiks and the Dux met here alone last month, and both deny it.

Duneforged Citadel Invictian-aligned · prices in denarii at full weight; the Reserve reckons in gp

A citadel of smiths, debt and airships. Old full-weight denarii pass at face here, debased ones go to the Mithril Reserve counter at the market end, and every good shop belongs to a noble house.

The Parched Ox Drinking hall and hiring hall · existing

Keeper: Branwen Stonecutter, quarryman's daughter · Where: the Lower City

The long vaulted room with the stone counter and the slate by the door where work and grievances are chalked. Gang masters hire here; disputes are settled at the back table by whoever the room agrees is impartial. Gavin Caesar drinks here and the lower city adores him for it.

Rooms: none officially; a pallet in the cellar, 2 asses (poor). Food: black bread, onion soup, beer at an as a mug. Who drinks: quarrymen, mine crews, gang masters, Gavin Caesar.

Work: a miner's wage is 2 sp a day; a guard for a cart up the hoists 5 sp. Rumour: the deep galleries hum at night, and the Duke has stopped sending surveyors.

The Molten Crucible House Inn · the Helm

Keeper: Ser Edric Zayida, a younger son of House Zayida · Where: the Helm, beside the Molten Crucible

The Upper City's guest-house, run by the steward-house as a courtesy and a listening post: carpeted, warm from the forge-flues in the walls, and booked by foreign officers come to buy Vulkrim steel. The Gilded Imperator Casino is a short walk down the stair.

Rooms: 2 denarii (wealthy); the Envoy's Suite, 4 (aristocratic). Food: mountain mutton, ibex in season, wine from the Imperium and the Acheaorian kind nobody admits importing. Who drinks: foreign officers, airship captains, Zayida clerks.

Rumour: a Mihran guest booked a room under a merchant's name and asked which window looks at the Caerthain palace.

Ember & Anvil Smith · House Vulkrim's foundry · existing

Master-Smith of House Vulkrim · Where: the Middle District by the Marketplace

"Steel forged in dragonfire, enchanted by the stars." The showroom of the Vulkrim foundry: the heavy work is done in the Geomanthic Foundries below; the town forge is for show and fitting. Peace has cut the army orders, so the shop courts adventurers. Commissions need a deposit of half and a Citadel guarantor; prices move a quarter either way with the market.

Stock: runed longsword (+1 longsword) 300 gp; any martial weapon at PHB price plus a fifth; plate 1,500 gp; mithral-lined shield (+1 shield) 450 gp; a mithral chain shirt 800 gp to order; a cold-iron dagger 40 gp, one a month.

Drakkur's Expeditionary Outfitter · existing

Keeper: Drakkur · Where: the Middle City

Rope, lamps, water-skins, dust masks and rock hammers, and by the door a ledger larger than the stock. Every party signs out and signs back in. Guides for the Dune Mines by the day. He will not outfit anyone for the sealed ground, and says so loudly enough that people ask why.

Stock: explorer's pack 10 gp; climber's kit 25 gp; miner's lamp (hooded lantern) 5 gp; dust mask 2 sp; pick 2 gp; a guide 5 sp a day, 2 gp below the third gallery.

The Gilded Crucible Alchemy · House Virellarion's atelier · existing

Keeper: Lord Ambrose Virellarion, brother of Countess Aurelie · Where: the Middle District

"Where essence meets excellence." Rare preparations need a drop of the buyer's blood "for calibration", which most customers do not question. Prices swing a quarter either way with demand.

The Gilded Imperator Casino Odd service · gambling hall

House manager: Cassius Fenn, for House Zayida · Where: where the Helm drops to the Middle City

Brass and marble on wall-stone, dice where the battle-roar used to be. Commoners play bones and the wheel for denarii; the high table plays Mindflayer's Gambit for land, marriage pacts and favours. The house holds stakes in escrow and never loses one. Minimum at the high table: 100 gp.

Rumour: the house has a buyer for any secret staked and lost, and the buyer sits on the Duke's council.

Hellarchon Hellenoria · prices in drachmas and obols

The owl drachma is struck here at full weight and the city knows it. A foreigner pays the metic price, which is the citizen price plus whatever the seller thinks of his accent.

The Trireme's Eye Inn · the Emporion

Keeper: Pamphile, a trierarch's widow · Where: the Emporion, behind the Spice Wharf

A courtyard inn with a painted marble ship's eye over the gate, taken from a hull that did not come back. Captains waiting on cargo, Sabaian traders and Academy students who cannot afford the upper city fill it. Pamphile lets rooms by the night or by the sailing.

Rooms: a mat on the roof in summer, 2 obols (poor); a room, 4 obols (modest); a room over the war basins, 1 drachma (comfortable). Food: grilled sprats, barley cakes, oil and figs, and a wine so resinated the Invictians think it is varnish. Who drinks: captains, oarsmen on 3 obols a day, a pickpocket who pays guild dues.

Rumour: the shed with no number in the Shipsheds has started taking deliveries of naphtha by night.

The House of the Two Hills Guest-house · upper city

Keeper: Aristomache Lykou, of a minor oligarch house · Where: the Two Hills

A rich man's house let room by room since its owner's trireme sank with the family fortune aboard. Envoys, League delegates and Imperial couriers sleep here; House Nikandridai pays for two rooms that are always empty and always ready.

Rooms: 3 drachmas (wealthy), meals and a slave to carry your lamp included. Food: tuna from the Reach, honey cakes, a sweet island wine. Rumour: the Emperor's latest letter was copied here before it was read in the Assembly.

The Bronze-Beaters of the Clay Gate Smith and armourer

Master: Kallias Chalkeus, of the Hephaestus guild · Where: the Clay Gate

Hoplite bronze: the round aspis, the crested helmet, greaves beaten to the buyer's own calves. The rich buy a full panoply as a mark of class; marines buy the linen cuirass, which is cheaper and floats longer.

Stock: aspis (shield) 10 drachmas; spear 1; xiphos (shortsword) 10; linen cuirass (padded) 5; bronze cuirass (breastplate) 400; full hoplite panoply (half-plate and shield) 760.

The Spice Wharf and the Long Stoa Market · existing

Harbour-master: Glaukos Timonos · Where: the Emporion

Warehouses sealed at night with three locks; every pinch weighed in front of the buyer and the tax-clerk. Sample bags, money tables and the windowless Mithril Reserve block in the Long Stoa, where Dorgrim Ironhand chalks the day's discount on Invictian silver by the door.

Stock: pepper a drachma an ounce on the quay; Sabaian incense 25 drachmas a pound; oil 1 sp a flask; papyrus 2 sp a roll; deck passage to Corinth 3 drachmas.

The Owl Window of the Arcane Academy Magic seller · the Academy shop

Keeper: Theron Glaukopis, junior lecturer in charge of "revenue" · Where: the Academy Grove

The Academy sells what its students make and its faculty will not miss. Copying a spell into a spellbook from the Academy's own texts, 50 drachmas a spell level; identification for a fee and a signature. The Truth-Flame inspects the stock monthly.

A Philosopher for the Afternoon Odd service · the Agora stoas

Broker: Menippos the Lame · Where: the Agora

Menippos rents out philosophers, rhetors and speech-writers by the hour. Two drachmas, or a meal, buys a man to argue anything; twenty buys a defence speech for a jury of 501, guaranteed to be good and not guaranteed to win. Advantage on one Persuasion check before a League court, if the writer is paid in full.

Rumour: the best speech-writer in the city wrote both sides of the last ostracism.

Corinth Hellenoria · prices in drachmas; staters for anything that floats

Everything that crosses the isthmus pays. Two harbours, a stone road between them and the League's second money market, where the Mithril Reserve and the Vaults of Equilibrium watch each other across the street.

The Wise Owl Inn Inn · existing

Landlord: Tolmides · Where: against the old city wall above the Lebes

Three storeys dark with smoke and a little owl in the rafters that the regulars treat as the house's conscience. Tolmides keeps twelve beds and three rules, recites them on arrival, and credits the owl with knowing things he should not. Ixion Keraunios drinks here between sales of wind on the quay.

Rooms: a bed at four obols (modest); the room under the eaves, 1 drachma. Food: excellent local red, octopus, lentil soup. Who drinks: pilots, sponsors of athletes, men who fix games.

Rumour: your conversation of last night will be repeated to you on the quay, word for word, by a stranger.

The Haulers' Rest Tavern and bunkhouse · the Haulway

Keeper: Big Phrynon, a retired hauler · Where: the Haulway, by the eastern toll-house

A long shed of bunks and a counter where haulers are hired by the day. Every crew belongs to a toll-farmer, and every crew knows whose ship is carrying more than it declared.

Rooms: a bunk, 1 obol (squalid). Food: barley porridge, beans, vinegar wine. Work: hauling at 3 obols a day. Rumour: Bacchiad ships cross with iron in the ballast, and the haulers are paid double to feel nothing.

Corinthian Bronze of the Forge Temple Smith · temple workshops

Master: Euphranor Chalkidas · Where: beside the Forge temple, the Isthmian Quarter

The famous closed-faced helmet with the eye-slots, and a bronze alloy whose recipe the city guards like a harbour chain. And, through a back door that is not on the guild roll, good Mavelon iron.

Stock: Corinthian helmet (a status piece; part of half-plate) 60 drachmas; spear 1; bronze breastplate 400; iron longsword 15 "from stock", meaning from Mavelon; bronze mirror 5.

The Agora of the Counting-Houses Market and sea-loans

Where: the Street of Counting-Houses and the Agora

The busiest and least decorous market in the League. Atarabad silk from the Suren-Pahlav factor, Qart-Hadeth tin, Corinthian bronze, Araavyna jars, sea-loans on any captain, and "Delpharan copies" of the Aeolus wind-chart at five drachmas, a tenth of the price of a true one.

Stock: bottomry at a quarter to a third for the season; a keelboat 3,000 drachmas; Haulway passage about 40 drachmas for a light galley; bills honoured by Hjalma Ironhand at the Reserve.

Ixion's Wind-Knots Magic seller · a stool on the Lechaion quay

Seller: Ixion Keraunios, or his boy when the Reach is calling · Where: the Lechaion

Winds sold in knotted cords, and a few other things a storm-sorcerer can make between sailings. He sells to any captain who pays and to no Hellarchon navy officer at all.

The Sherd-Mender Odd service · forger

Craftsman: Kleon the Glue · Where: a workshop off the Agora

Officially he mends pots. In fact he glues fragments of famous painted jars from Araavyna's breaking-ground into "whole antiques" for Hellarchon collectors, and he will forge a seal, a letter of credit or a manumission tablet for 50 drachmas a document. He rolls with a forgery kit at +6; a Bacchiad clerk spots his work on Investigation DC 16.

Rumour: Nerissa Thalassine has used his toll-passes, and the Prytanis pretends not to know.

Delphara Hellenoria · prices in drachmas; doubled in a Games year

Hospitality is the town's only industry. A third of the beds belong to House Labyadai, every guide is licensed, and every goat for sacrifice is certified.

The Hostel of the Seven Turns Inn · House Labyadai

Keeper: Euthymos Labyadas, master of the lodging brokers · Where: the Sacred Way, at the seventh turn

A terraced hostel built into the switchbacks, with a door for every turn and a lamp at every door. The oath of silence is enforced: a guest who repeats what another pilgrim asked the god is exiled. Delegates from twelve cities sleep here in strict order of precedence.

Rooms: a dormitory bed, 1 drachma (modest, pilgrim rate); a terrace room, 3 drachmas (wealthy); the Delegates' rooms, not for hire but for sale. Food: roast goat from the morning's sacrifices, barley bread, the Oracle's Vineyards' thin red. Who drinks: pilgrims, envoys, tyrants' delegates who will not sit together.

Rumour: a question asked under the guides' seal has been repeated word for word in a Hellarchon wine-shop.

The Goat-Sellers' Pens Market · the Lower Town

Where: the Lower Town Agora

Goats and cockerels certified fit for sacrifice (a goat must shiver when sprinkled with water, or it is refused), lodging brokers, money-changers and laurel-sellers. A licensed guide costs three obols a turn of the Way.

Stock: a certified goat 2 gp (6 in a Games year); a cockerel 1 sp; a laurel wreath 2 obols; a votive bronze 5 drachmas; pilgrims' letters of credit at the Mithril Reserve vault, where Durgan Ironhand is offended by gold that is never lent.

The Votive Founders Smith · bronze-casters

Master: Damarete, a bronze-founder of an old Delpharan family · Where: below the treasuries

They cast victory statues, tripods and armour dedications for cities that have won a war, and mend pilgrims' weapons on the side. A city's victory statue costs a talent; a hoplite's dedication shield, 20 drachmas.

Stock: spears and daggers at PHB prices; shield 10 drachmas; a bronze tripod 100; repairs to bronze armour overnight.

The Exegetes' Table Magic seller · temple concession

Seller: Philonoe, a junior Exegete trained under Lysandra Anthemis · Where: the Phoibad Terrace

The Oracle and the Dream Dormitory Odd service · consultation

Where: the Temenos and the Dream Dormitory

A private consultation of the oracle: the pelanos cake (10 drachmas), the certified goat, a gift to the treasury (100 drachmas is respectable), and a wait of days or months. Cities with promanteia go first; so, quietly, does Persemenid. A lot-oracle answer, yes or no from a bowl of beans, costs 2 drachmas and is quicker. A night's incubation in the Dream Dormitory costs a drachma by custom; treat it as a divination spell, once per character per year.

Rumour: the Acheaorian treasury's answers are always favourable.

Ephelanum Condominium · drachmas in the city, denarii at the harbour; both taken everywhere

Two governments, one goddess, two currencies. The Dux's customs men price everything at the quay in denarii; the city prices it again in drachmas; a pilgrim pays both.

The Doe and Bow Inn · harbour end

Keeper: Gaius Antistius Hellenicus, half one thing and half the other · Where: by the Silting Harbour

The only inn with two price boards, one in each tongue, and two sets of weights hung by the door. Pilgrims arriving by sea sleep here before they climb to the goddess; garrison officers drink here because the wine is better than in the camp.

Rooms: 4 obols or an old-issue denarius (modest to comfortable); triple in Fair season. Food: red-earth bread, olives, harbour mullet, a garrison posca the officers swear by. Rumour: the harbour silts faster since the Dux stopped paying for the Dredging.

The Silversmiths' Row Smith · the guild of the Smiths' Offering

Guild-master: Hermias Argyrides · Where: the Forum Line, below the sanctuary

Silver models of the temple and the Lady in every size, from a pilgrim's 5-drachma charm to a 500-drachma household shrine. The guild also silvers weapons, which the Lady's hunters bless. Mention the Weighing and the whole row will tell you the story at once.

Stock: silvering a weapon 100 drachmas; silvered arrows 1 drachma each; a silver shrine model 5–500; ordinary weapons to order from the garrison's armourer.

The Red-Earth Sheds Trader · existing

Where: the Red Plain

Sinopic red, a painter's best vermilion earth, at 2 gp a jar; a pilgrim's jar for the forehead at a drachma; pigment by the sack for workshops with a letter. Harvest-loans, land deeds in two languages and notaries at a drachma a seal in the lower market, where the sheds' stamp is being forged.

The Lady's Herb-Garden Magic and herb seller · temple concession

Seller: Korinna, a novice of the Hierarchis · Where: the gate of the Sanctuary

The Lady's Milk (potion of healing)50 drachmasalways

The Baths of Ephelanum Odd service · the condominium's bath-house

Attendant: Synphoros, a freedman under the bath-master Gnaeus Sulpicius Lavator

The first stop for pilgrims by sea and the one building the treaty assigns to both governments; the joint board meets monthly in the warm room. Entry a quadrans or a chalkous; a private room 1 drachma. For 10 drachmas Synphoros will seat a guest in the warm room's alcove on board day, where every word of the meeting can be heard.

Rumour: the Dux's wife Vettia Prisca bathes here daily and has learnt Hellenorian, and the board has stopped speaking freely in front of her.

Helionyx Hellenoria · prices in drachmas; nothing sold between noon and mid-afternoon

A lime-white harbour under a sun that does not relent. The market shuts at noon and the city sleeps under awnings; the College decides which days trade may happen at all.

The Fallen Hand Inn · the Fallen Quarter

Keeper: Androkles, a stonemason who stopped carving · Where: the Fallen Quarter

Built against one bronze finger of the fallen colossus, which is taller than the inn. Sailors, salt factors and pilgrims to the Sun Temple drink in its shade. Androkles charges a chalkous to touch the finger and makes more from that than from the beds.

Rooms: a roof-mat, 2 obols; a room, 4 obols (modest). Food: salt fish, early almonds, a white wine cooled in the cistern. Rumour: the oracle forbade raising the colossus, but someone is buying its bronze by the knuckle.

The Purple Works Trader · dye and salt

Master: Sosibios Halikos, a cousin of the senior prytanis · Where: the Dye Works and the Salt Flats

Murex vats that stink for a mile, and salt by the cart. Tyrsan purple is undercutting the city's own, so the works now sell cheaper and louder. Salt is the town's real money.

Stock: a bolt of purple 110 drachmas; purple thread 5 a skein; salt by the cart 2 drachmas; smoked glass for watching the sun, a drachma.

The Anchor-Smiths of the Mole Smith

Master: Hagnon Ankyreus · Where: the harbour mole

Anchors, chain, boat-nails and the long marine spear. They forge to order, sharpen for an obol and never work at noon. Their iron comes from Corinth and is cheaper than it should be.

Stock: anchor 20 drachmas; pike 5; trident 5; 10 ft of chain 5; scale cuirass 50.

The Astromancers' Porch Magic seller · the College of the gnomon

Seller: Kleoboule, a reckoner of the College · Where: Temple Hill

The Court of the Jettison Odd service · maritime arbitration

Where: the Awning Agora, at dawn

Jettison judges for hire as arbitrators in any sea dispute: 10 drachmas a hearing, 50 for a written ruling that every maritime court in the League will cite. Bottomry contracts drawn at a quarter to a third for the season.

Rumour: the Fucostia harbour court has copied the last three rulings without acknowledgement, and the judges are composing a reply.

Thebesieas Hellenoria · prices in drachmas

A farm-city with seven gates and the League's only real army. Everything here is cheap except iron, which is cheaper still, and nobody will say why.

The Seventh Gate Inn · gate ward

Keeper: Ismenia, a farmer's widow · Where: the Seven Gates

A farmhouse inn inside the gate, as plain as the city. Carters, horse-buyers from Argotiko and off-duty men of the phalanx drink here; the pairs of the Sacred Band drink elsewhere, and together.

Rooms: 3 obols (modest); a stall for a horse, an obol. Food: eel from the wet plain, barley, a heavy dark wine. Rumour: the gate-ward smiths have more iron than the plain has ever bought.

The Iron of the Gate Wards Smiths

Master: Pagondas Sidereus · Where: the smiths' street of the Seven Gates

The phalanx's armourers. Iron spear-heads and swords by the hundred, all of it, the smiths say, "old stock", though the wagons come up the Inland Road from Corinth every month. They sell to visitors at prices that make Hellarchon envious.

Stock: spear 5 obols; longsword 12 drachmas; iron-faced shield 8; chain shirt 40; breastplate 350. Ask where the iron comes from and the price doubles.

The Muster Ground Market Market

Where: the Muster Ground

A parade ground first and a market when the army is not using it: barley, horses, carts and hides. Bergthor Ironhand of the Reserve holds mortgages on a third of the plain and lends against harvests nobody can yet see.

Stock: riding horse 75 drachmas; mule 8; cart 15; barley a copper a pound; a mortgage at a fifth a year.

The Club of Hercules Magic seller · temple shop

Seller: the temple warden Kallikrates · Where: the Temple Ward

The Pairs Ground Trainers Odd service · arms masters

Where: the Pairs Ground

Veterans of the phalanx teach shield-wall, spear and wrestling at 3 drachmas a lesson. Ten workweeks at 25 drachmas a week teach proficiency in shields or one martial weapon under the downtime training rules. The Sacred Band's lochagos, Epameinon Kleitarchos, watches the best pupils and now and then makes an offer.

Thessalonika Hellenoria · prices in drachmas, posted and audited

The tidiest market in the League. Debts are recorded at the Agora and called on the day; the Epistates publishes the city's accounts on whitened boards every quarter, and the prices are posted beside them.

The Glazed Stoa Inn Inn · the Lower Grid

Keeper: Euboule Kerkine, who keeps a ledger of everything · Where: the Lower Grid

A gridded block of rooms round a courtyard, glazed against the north wind, with a posted tariff on the door and a receipt for every meal. Grain factors, academy students and travelling lecturers stay here.

Rooms: 4 obols (modest); a room with a brazier, 1 drachma (comfortable). Food: bean soup, northern mutton, steppe beer and southern wine. Rumour: this quarter's audit boards carry a line nobody can explain: "for the Horse Gate, as agreed".

The Horse Gate Yards Camp-inn and steppe market · outside the walls

Keeper: Tamar the Felt-Seller · Where: the Horse Gate

A fenced field of felt tents and horse-lines round a cookfire under a tarred roof. A foreigner sleeps in a tent for an obol and is safe as long as he does not count the horses aloud.

Food: mare's milk, mutton, flatbread. Stock: steppe pony (riding horse) 60 drachmas; warhorse 400; felt tent 2; amber 5 sp a bead; furs 5–50.

The Citadel Bowyers Smith and bowyer

Master: Lysimachos Toxotes · Where: below the Citadel

Bows, mostly: the city learned from the steppe. Composite bows of horn and sinew, and the armour its horse-archers wear.

Stock: shortbow 25 drachmas; longbow 50; 20 arrows 1; scimitar 25; hide armour 10; scale 50.

The Porticoes' Book-Stall Magic seller · academy stall

Krates in the Portico Odd service · free philosophy

Philosopher: Krates the Dog

The one service in Thessalonika with no posted price. Krates insults the rich for nothing and teaches the poor for less. A day of his questions counts as a short rest in which nothing pleasant happens; at the DM's discretion it ends one charm or fear effect by sheer rudeness.

Persemenid Acheaoria · prices in sigloi and darics; nothing posted, everything bargained

Not a market city: the great trading is done at Atarabad, and what arrives here arrives as obligation. But a court spends, and a court's servants spend more.

The Royal Caravanserai of the Quarter of Tongues Caravanserai · delegations

Keeper: Hamid Kaarvan, under contract to House Nahid'zar, which feeds and beds every delegation · Where: the Quarter of Tongues

Every delegation that climbs the stair sleeps here first, in an order of precedence the Karin keep and revise daily. A merchant who is not a delegation gets the far court, the cheaper rooms and the same excellent tea.

Rooms: a cell in the far court, 5 sp (modest); a delegation's suite with a fountain, 3 sigloi (wealthy); stabling a pashiz-handful a night. Food: rice with saffron and barberries, lamb kebab, flatbread from the clay oven, rose sherbet. Who drinks tea: envoys, interpreters, the Reserve's dwarves, a King's Eye pretending to be a carpet-seller.

Rumour: a delegation from Shir'abad D'ar arrived with gifts and no tribute, and was given the near court anyway.

The Wine-Shop That Is Not One Tavern · Hellenorian traders

Keeper: Lykophron of Corinth, a metic who is "selling grape syrup" · Where: the Quarter of Tongues

Hellenorian traders argue here over wine that is served in tea-bowls and called syrup, because the Magi frown on public drinking and the Lykophron family has been here for three generations. Spies from all three empires drink here because nobody else does.

Rooms: two, above, 1 siglos. Food: olives, cheese, syrup. Rumour: the hazarapat's steward buys a jar every week for a guest who is never seen.

The Coppersmiths' Lane Smiths · the Bazaar

Warden: Ustad Bahman Mesgar · Where: the Bazaar of Persemenid

Hammering from dawn; trays, ewers and braziers for the court, and in the back courts the armourers who equip the Ten Thousand's private orders. A scale coat to fit a court officer takes a month and fits like a robe.

Stock: scimitar 25 sigloi; composite bow (shortbow) 25; scale armour 50; a gilded parade shield 60; copper ewer 2. Court orders first.

The Sage's Archive Stall Magic seller · copyists of the Archive

Seller: Dabir Kartir Nevisandeh, copyist · Where: by the Archive gate on the Terrace

The Archive's copyists sell protective texts, Magi-blessed water and a few things the Archive has duplicates of. Magus Rashnu-Vahram's people buy here and sell nothing.

The Petition-Writers of the Royal Stair Odd service

Where: the foot of the Royal Stair

Thirty scribes on cushions write petitions to the King of Kings in the correct court style, with the eleven forms of address and the right colour of ink: 2 sigloi a petition, 10 for one that will be read, 1 daric for one that will be answered. Hulda Ironhand of the Reserve notes that the answered ones are the ones that come with a daric attached.

Rumour: the King of Kings has not read a petition in a year, and his answers are in four different hands.

Atarabad Acheaoria · prices in sigloi; Invictian silver weighed, never counted

The largest bazaar on the continent: forty-one lanes, a carpet hall domed like a temple, a ring of caravanserais and a weigh-house where Arashshara Shahdokht Abrisham keeps the city weights.

The Western Caravanserai Caravanserai · the Treaty Road gate

Keeper: Mihrdad Sarband, steward for House Suren-Pahlav, which leases it · Where: the Caravanserai Ring

Once the smallest of the ring and a yard for spies and smugglers; now it sends out three convoys west for every one that leaves by the eastern gates. Invictian and Hellenorian factors lodge above; the Mithril Reserve's stone branch stands beside the gate.

Rooms: a bay in the arcade, 2 sp (poor); a room above the storerooms, 5 sp (modest); a factor's suite, 2 sigloi (wealthy); stabling and fodder for a camel 5 cp. Food: lamb and apricot stew, yoghurt, tea without end. Who drinks tea: drovers, Suren-Pahlav clerks, Wheelwalkers, a Hellenorian buying saffron by the hundredweight.

Rumour: the saffron in the third lane is cut with the cheap kind, and the lane's warden knows.

The Caravan Stone Rest-house · a day east of the city

Keeper: Mother Golpari, eighty and loud · Where: a desert crossroads on the eastern routes

A walled rest-house round a stone on which every caravan master has carved a name for a thousand years. Golpari's stew of caravan cumin and red-hand leaf is why many travellers choose this road. Her grandsons hold the gate.

Rooms: a bed, 4 sp. Food: a bowl of the stew, 5 cp, worth a silver. Rumour: one name on the stone has been scratched out, and it was a satrap's.

The Lane of Hot Copper Smiths · the Bazaar

Warden: Ustad Firuzeh Ahangar, a woman smith · Where: the Bazaar of Atarabad

Bladesmiths, armourers and farriers for every caravan that leaves. The lane sells good caravan-guard kit at honest prices, and wootz blades from Maurash, brought overland, for those who can pay.

Stock: scimitar 25 sigloi; lance 10; chain shirt 50; scale 50; a wootz scimitar 160 (counts as silvered, DM option); shoeing a camel, which cannot be done, 1 siglos for trying.

The Weigh-House Market and money-changing

Keeper of the city weights: Arashshara Shahdokht Abrisham

Every coin is weighed here before a large sale. Invictian denarii are weighed rather than counted and paid out at weight, usually three-quarters of face. The forty-one lanes sell everything else: silk, saffron, carpets, cassia, tents, camels, water-skins.

Stock: silk bolt 200 sigloi (only here and on the road west); saffron 12 an ounce; a camel 50; a caravan tent 5; Brokk Ironhand's Custodes as escort, 1 siglos a day each, to the Western Caravanserai and not one step further.

The Cobra Heaps Odd service · snake-charmers and antidotes

Master charmer: Old Shapur Marbaz

A walled yard of snake-pits where charmers perform, milk venom and sell antidotes. Antitoxin 50 sigloi; a vial of milked venom (basic poison) 100; a charmer to clear a house of snakes, 5. A charm against snakebite, a knotted cord, works one time in six.

Rumour: the charmers have found a snake nobody can name and have locked their gate.

Mithratal Acheaoria · prices in sigloi

The oath-city, where a covenant sworn before the fire binds anywhere on the plateau. Its trade is ink, wax, seals and waiting.

The Lodge of the Two Cypresses Waiting lodge · inn

Keeper: Arashshara Parisa Dastgir · Where: the Waiting Lodges

One of the walled lodges where parties to a covenant wait out the intervals the law requires. Each party has its own gate; rival parties are kept on opposite sides of the garden. Poets hired to fill the waiting recite in the evenings.

Rooms: 1 siglos a night (comfortable), 25 for the full forty-day interval. Food: cardamom rice, pomegranate stew, sweet tea. Who waits: satraps' agents, merchant houses, a family that has been waiting two years. Rumour: two satraps' agents are waiting for each other, and their masters are not telling the throne.

The Seal-Cutters' Lane Smiths and trade · the scribes' bazaar

Warden: Ustad Kambiz Mohrkan · Where: the Bazaar of Mithratal

Seal-cutters, paper-sellers and notaries. A personal cylinder seal in agate takes three days; a stamp seal, one. The lane sells paper, ink, wax and lockable document cases, and a smith at its end makes good knives and better locks.

Stock: agate cylinder seal 10 sigloi; ink 10 gp a bottle; paper 2 sp a sheet; document case 1; lock 10; dagger 2.

The Covenant-Clerks of the Precinct Odd service · oaths before the fire

Where: the Precinct

A covenant sworn before the fire, witnessed and recorded: 10 sigloi for a private bargain, 1 daric for a contract between houses, a fixed tenth of the sum for a loan. Breaking a sworn covenant is a crime anywhere on the plateau. Odila Stonebrow of the Reserve decides which covenants the bank will honour, and has quietly stopped honouring covenants of neighbourhood.

Persevalis Acheaoria · prices in sigloi

The garden satrapy: a hillside of walled gardens and the court's best tables. Everything here smells of something, and the something is for sale.

The Caravanserai at the Foot of the Slope Caravanserai

Keeper: Arashshara Nargess Bastani, on contract to House Golab · Where: the Foot of the Slope

Where the green ends and the plateau's ordinary dust begins: carters, fruit-pickers, drovers and buyers for the court's kitchens. Green-nut orchards behind; mules in front.

Rooms: 3 sp (modest); a garden room 1 siglos (comfortable). Food: fresh fruit in every season, a pistachio pilaf, cold sherbet with snow. Rumour: the water in the high channels is running the wrong way at night.

The Still-Houses Trader · attar and rose-water

Still-mistress: Azar Golab · Where: the Still-Houses

Copper stills distilling rose, orange-blossom and willow. Azar Golab can tell a field's year by the smell of its attar and a forger's by the colour. Perfume sells to three empires; the orchard bazaar sells the fruit.

Stock: rose-water 1 siglos a flask; attar of roses 25 an ounce; a perfume (PHB) 5; dried fruit 1 sp a pound; a forger's attar, offered to Golab, recognised at once.

The Gardeners' Smithy Smith

Master: Ustad Hormoz Beylchi · Where: the orchard bazaar

Pruning knives, sickles, channel-gates and the iron sluices that steer the water. Weapons on request; the satrap's guard buy their spears here.

Stock: sickle 1 siglos; spear 1; scimitar 25; sluice-gate 20; a lockable water-gate key, not for sale, often for sale.

The Moon Pavilion Herbary Magic seller

The Hall of Strings Odd service · musicians and licensed critics

Where: the Hall of Strings, seat of the Melodic Circle

Musicians, poets and singers for hire from the Melodic Circle: 5 sigloi for an evening, 1 daric for a poet to write you into a song, 5 darics to have a rival written out of one. Licensed critics will ruin a performer for less. Shirin Navaz hears the best of them and keeps a list.

Xerastri Acheaoria · prices in sigloi; the garrison pays in tallies

The shield against the steppe. Two walls, the empire's largest garrison outside the capital, a subsidy cut twice since the peace, and a Horse Fair that has become a hiring fair.

The Caravanserai of the Truce Yards Caravanserai · the Horse-Fair Ground

Keeper: Sohrab Asbdar, yard-master for House Asbdar · Where: the Horse-Fair Ground

Inside the outer gate, round great yards where steppe clans, remount buyers and recruiters meet under truce. No blade drawn inside the yard gate; the penalty is the horse you came on.

Rooms: a felt in the yard, 1 sp; a room, 4 sp (modest). Food: roast mutton, mare's milk, flatbread, the garrison's barley beer. Who drinks: Malaunian riders, Invictian recruiters from the Legates' private legions, Hellenorian horse-buyers. Rumour: the Legates' recruiters are paying in Aksumari gold.

The Saddlers' and Bowyers' Lanes Smiths · the Bazaar

Warden: Ustad Arash Kamandar · Where: the Bazaar of Xerastri

A city that rides and shoots like its enemy makes the best horse-archer kit on the continent. Composite bows, quivers that hold sixty, lamellar coats and saddles with the high steppe cantle.

Stock: composite bow (longbow) 50 sigloi; shortbow 25; 20 arrows 1; lance 10; scale armour 50; military saddle 20; a garrison-surplus chain shirt 30 when the subsidy is late.

The Remount Fair Market

Where: the Horse-Fair Ground

Horses by the thousand at the summer fair, by the dozen the rest of the year. Steppe ponies, desert mares, Acheaorian chargers.

Stock: riding horse 70 sigloi; warhorse 400; draft horse 50; a mare of the satrap's line, 20 darics and a reference.

The Hunting Altar Stall Magic seller

Seller: the huntress Shirin Kigavand, of the Predator's Guild · Where: by the Hunting Altar of Kiga

The Hiring Fair Odd service · mercenaries

Where: outside the outer wall, in summer; the yards the rest of the year

Malaunian riders hire out to all three empires in the same season. A horse-archer costs 2 gp a day with his own mounts; a band of ten, 15 gp; Tomyra of the Lion Grass, whatever she says and half in advance. Gunnvor Ironhand of the Reserve holds hiring contracts in escrow for a tenth.

Deiperduem Neutral · every coin taken; the Reserve's rate posted hourly

The city where the war was signed away. Rents would buy a farm in any province, the notaries are the best on the continent, and every price is quoted in three coinages at once.

The Green Lamp Inn · existing

Keeper: Mother Ottla of the Green Lamp · Where: the Old Town

The most famous neutral inn on the continent, where the three delegations drank, separately and at the same time, through the last month of negotiations. Motto over the door: "No opinions on the premises". Mother Ottla seats rivals back to back, never face to face.

Rooms: 1 gp in any coin (comfortable); the Delegates' rooms, 4 gp (aristocratic). Food: a dish from each empire every night, a rule kept for ninety years; the snug's ale. Who drinks: embassy secretaries, Treaty Hall notaries, guests of the compounds. Rumour: Jory the cellarman sells what is said in the snug, and believes nobody knows.

The Wheelwalkers' Fire Camp-inn · the Caravan Fields

Keeper: Auntie Zarrin of the Painted Wagons · Where: the Caravan Fields

The Wheelwalkers' permanent camp lets wagon-berths and a seat at the fire to anyone who can sing or pay. Cheaper than the Old Town by a factor of ten, and better informed.

Rooms: a berth in a wagon, 2 sp (poor). Food: a stew from three cuisines at once. Rumour: the Gilded Horizon's Thursday caravan carries a passenger nobody sees board.

The Iron Cup Forge Smith · neutral weapons

Master: Hob of the Iron Cup, a cousin of the innkeeping family · Where: Lantern Row

No troops by treaty means no army contracts, so the city's best smith makes locks, blades for the watch and the Ironclad Legion's repairs. Every weapon sold is registered with the watch.

Stock: any simple or martial weapon at PHB price plus a tenth; chain mail 80 gp; a watch-pattern shield 12 gp; masterwork lock 25 gp.

The Market of Nations Market · high summer

Where: every lane of the Old Town, each empire in its own quarter

Nominally a trade fair, in practice the year's most productive week of diplomacy. The rest of the year the Counting Ward does the trade. Hildra Ironhand's Reserve branch, the largest outside Duneforged, posts the hourly rate.

Stock: anything in the PHB at list price; Acheaorian silk 200 gp; Invictian wine 2 sp a pitcher; Hellenorian oil 1 sp a flask; a sworn translation in all three tongues 25 gp a page; a certified copy with two embassies' seals 100 gp.

The Seven Quills Magic seller · copyists and scroll-scribes

Keeper: Ysolde of the Seven Quills · Where: the Old Town

An old house-sign family of copyists who added scrolls when the Treaty wards needed copying. They sell to all three embassies and to nobody's spies, or say so.

The House of Three Doors Odd service · rooms for gods

Keeper: Mother Wenna of the Iron Cup · Where: Lantern Row

Temples are illegal by treaty, so the gods of three empires rent wings of an inn on a ninety-nine-year lease. A rite in any wing costs a donation to its priest and a fee of 1 sp to the house for the lamp. A traveller may light a lamp in all three wings at once for 3 sp, which the Iron Cup calls insurance.

Rumour: something has been leaving offerings at the Fourth Shrine, and the house has only three wings.

Eronis Ruin · no coin of its own; salvagers take anything that weighs

Nobody lives in the dead capital of the dream-walkers. A few dozen salvagers camp at the Quays of Irelas a day's walk away, and that camp is the only place on Velothis with a fire at night.

The Salvagers' Fire Camp and lodging · the Quays of Irelas

Camp-mother: Hesper Drown-Not, a diver with one ear · Where: the Quays of Irelas

A roofless warehouse with a sail stretched over half of it, a fire in the middle and a rule that nobody sleeps alone, because sleepers alone on Velothis wake somewhere else. Divers, relic-hunters and the occasional Academy party.

Rooms: a place in the ring round the fire, 5 sp a night and a watch to stand (poor). Food: fish, ship's biscuit, whatever the last boat brought. Rumour: a door in the Palace has been opened from below.

Hesper's Boat Trader · supplies and passage

Where: moored at the quays

Everything here came on Hesper's boat and costs triple: rope, lamp oil, rations, diving weights. She buys salvage at a tenth of Romulo prices and takes passengers back to the mainland at 20 gp a head, more if they are carrying something that hums.

Stock: rations 1.5 gp a day; 50 ft rope 3 gp; lamp oil 3 sp a flask; passage 20 gp.

The Bronze Camp Arms, free to anyone · the eastern shore

Where: the Bronze Camp

The racks of the old siege army still hold bronze spears, swords and shields. They are free, heavy and old (treat as normal weapons that break on a natural 1). Nobody takes them home. The salvagers say they are cursed; the truth is that they are heavy and the curse is a useful rumour.

Frozen Illusions Magic, as found

Dealer: whoever brought it up last

Glass cargoes from the ships that sank at their moorings, some still holding a Nethranan illusion. An unbroken "frozen illusion" sells in Romulo for the price of a house.

The Dream-Guide Odd service

Guide: a silent woman the camp calls Lamp

For 10 gp a day Lamp leads parties through the Mural Streets by routes that do not change while you walk them. She refuses to enter the Palace. She has never told anyone her name, and the Enchanted Muse, Delphara and the Academy would each pay a great deal to know it.

Towns one inn and one trader each

Town prices run higher for anything brought in and lower for anything made there. Magic items are rarely for sale in a town; when one is, double the city price.

Anticata Imperium Invicta · road town

Inn: the Milestone. The Pollii, masters of the Collegium of Innkeepers for four generations, keep the largest inn on the mile of painted frontage. A bed in the loft costs two asses, a room with a door a denarius, and the upstairs suite is kept for officers and let to merchants who look like them. Fried fish, horse-bread, and the Legate's men always in the posting house. Rumour: the two repainted milestones were moved a hundred paces nearer each other, and the Cursus pays by the mile.

Trader: the Stabularia smithy. The state remount yards' smith shoes horses at a sestertius a hoof and sells remounts to civilians when the register is "short" (riding horse 75 denarii, no questions about the brand).

Falecosa Imperium Invicta · wine town

Inn: the Tread-Floor. A grower's house above the Press Yard, kept by Helvia Secunda, with four rooms at 6 asses (modest) and the town's own wine at 2 asses a cup, a quarter of what the capital pays for it. Tenants drink here; landlords' agents do not. Rumour: Lucius Helvius has said in this tavern that he will break an absentee landlord's terrace wall, and meant it.

Trader: the Press Yard. An amphora of a good year costs 4 denarii here and fetches forty in Aeterna; the grower who trod it is paid four. Barrels, wineskins and vine-knives at PHB prices.

Fucostia Imperium Invicta · grain port

Inn: the Lighterman's Lamp. A towpath tavern open at all hours, kept by Mamurra the One-Handed. Bunks 2 asses; fish sauce on barley; porters who can count to three weeks. Rumour: a sack of Annona wheat fetches three denarii at the back door, no questions, more than the dole is worth to the man who carried it.

Trader: the Horrea brokers. Barge charters to Aeterna (5 denarii a passenger, 50 a barge), rope, sacks and Farshore papyrus by the bale. The harbour court copies Helionyx's sea-law and charges 10 denarii a hearing.

Napplesia Imperium Invicta · bay town of springs

Inn: the Retired Eagle. A villa turned guest-house on the Ripa, kept by a cohort commander's widow who charges 2 denarii a night (wealthy) and seats every guest by former rank. A villa for the season rents for two hundred denarii. Rumour: the veterans meet in the Great Bath on Discharge night to discuss their pensions, and a cohort commander drowned last year.

Trader: the Farshore Quay at Napplesia. Tyrsan purple, Sabaian myrrh for the baths and Keftaran bull-leapers hired for dinners, at Romulo prices plus a fifth. Admission to the Great Bath is a quadrans, the same for senator and fishwife.

Nemibano Imperium Invicta · grove town

Inn: the Antler on the Rim. Pilgrims' lodging on the crater rim, kept by the Ocreae family, 4 asses a bed. No meat from the slope, no fire after dark below the rim, lake fish and chestnut bread. Rumour: the Rex Nemorensis, Gnaeus Ferrus, has held the grove nineteen years, and a stranger at the inn has been asking how one challenges him.

Trader: the Votive Steps. A pilgrim's lamp costs an as; a votive clay stag, two; a guide to the treeline at dusk, a denarius, paid to the Ocreae and no one else. Healing herbs from the grove under the Verdant Sentinels' licence (healer's kit 5 denarii).

Araavyna Hellenoria · kiln town

Inn: the Cracked Pithos. A potter's house with rooms over the drying yards, 3 obols (modest), kept by a woman suing four of her neighbours. Lentils, goat's cheese and the town's lawsuits as entertainment. Rumour: the huge order of heavy jars came through Corinth, and the jars are the size to hold naphtha.

Trader: the Kiln Terraces. Storage jars 2 cp a gallon of capacity, painted cups 1 drachma, a family glaze recipe not for sale. Collectors pay boys to search the breaking-ground for sherds of famous hands.

Argotiko Hellenoria · horse town

Inn: the Bloodline. On Buyers' Street, backing onto the sale paddocks; factors from three empires drink Acheaorian tea and eat roast lamb. Rooms 1 drachma (comfortable). Rumour: the sacred bloodline registry has entries in a newer ink.

Trader: the Registry paddocks. A registered riding horse 100 drachmas, a cavalry warhorse 450, an unregistered horse of the same blood 60. Cavalry for hire by the season, under contract with the Registry.

Atticenea Hellenoria · olive and philosophy town

Inn: the School Steps. Lodgings above the press quarter, 2 obols a mat (poor), where students and visiting teachers sleep in rows. Bread, oil and argument. Rumour: the tyrant pays the teachers so well that they have stopped criticising him, and one has started again.

Trader: the Press Quarter. Oil of the ancient terraces, 2 sp a flask (twice Hellarchon's price and worth it); lamp oil 1 sp; a philosopher's tutoring at a drachma a day.

Carianea Hellenoria · sponge-divers' town

Inn: the Widow's Net. Kept by a diver's widow who owns the building, like most widows here: 3 obols (modest), octopus and retsina. Divers retire at forty and drink here until fifty. Rumour: the tyrant Mnasilochos is taking twelve companions to Loutrokleion for a six-week cure, and not all of them are ill.

Trader: the Sponge Racks. Sponges 1 sp to 5 gp; diving weights and knives; a diver for hire 5 sp a day; a fishing boat 40 drachmas secondhand.

Kirimitsana Hellenoria · mountain hamlets

Inn: the Hive-Hearth. A shepherd's stone house at the highest well, beds by the fire 1 obol, dark honey on everything. Rumour: the Luminastra alchemists have offered for the herb-lore, and a beekeeper sold one remedy and went blind.

Trader: the Beekeepers' Hall. Dark honey 2 drachmas a jar, herb remedies (healer's kit 5 drachmas), and, for those who know to ask, a mad-honey (basic poison) at 100 drachmas.

Loutrokleion Hellenoria · spa town

Inn: the Guest-House by the First Spring. House Hydriadai's best lodging ("Hot, and quiet"): 4 drachmas a night (aristocratic), diet-kitchen meals and a bath slot included. Lower down the Lodging Terraces, a dormitory bed costs 2 obols. Rumour: the tyrant's party has booked the whole of the best lodging, and League envoys are moving to the middle pools to talk.

Trader: the Physicians' Assembly dispensary. Potion of healing 75 drachmas, antitoxin 60, a six-week cure (removes one disease and one level of exhaustion) 300 drachmas.

De'rakhtak Bon Acheaoria · cold-store town

Inn: the Lamp Galleries lodging. Rock-cut rooms off the lamp galleries, cool in summer, 4 sp (modest). Stored fruit in any season and bread baked by the root's warmth. Rumour: a prince's grain is filling the deep chambers, and the Frataraka was not asked.

Trader: the Cold-Store brokers. Storage by the chamber-month (1 siglos for a cart's worth), ice in summer at 1 sp a block, preserved fruit for caravans.

Qa'zshahrv'in Acheaoria · well town

Inn: the Caravanserai. A third of the town; run by Arashshara Soheila Ab'kesh, who sets the water price at dawn. A room 5 sp; a camel's water 2 sp, a man's 5 cp, both more in a dry year. Rumour: she is selling forward water contracts to caravans not yet arrived, and the pool's marks are lower again.

Trader: the Muqanni Row. Qanat diggers' lamps, ropes and plumbs; a muqanni to inspect a well 2 sigloi; a Muqanni's Lamp, when one can be pried loose, priced as the Items part gives it.

R'eyshar Acheaoria · old walled town

Inn: the Inner Quarter guest-house. Six rooms in a mansion built for twenty, 3 sp (modest), orchard fruit and the names of streets that are gone read aloud at supper. Rumour: the court wants the archive and will not say why, and an archive clerk has started sleeping at the inn.

Trader: the Kiln Yards. Glazed tiles salvaged from the empty quarters, 1 sp each, and carpet fragments for Tabrishi'ir's restorers; old maps of the town at a siglos, every one slightly different.

Shir'abad D'ar Acheaoria · satrapal seat

Inn: the Waiting Bench. Inside the Lion Gate, the only part of town with ordinary people in it; petitioners queue for the satrap here for days. Bench space 2 sp, a room 6 sp. Rumour: the squadrons drilling in the Barracks are larger every month, and the tribute caravan is smaller.

Trader: the Lion Gate masons and armourers. Squadron kit sold out of the back of the barracks: lance 10 sigloi, scale 45, a warhorse 350 "surplus".

Tabrishi'ir Acheaoria · carpet town

Inn: the Loom Court. A weaving family's guest rooms, 4 sp (modest), with a loom in every corridor and dyed wool drying on the roof. Rumour: Invictian buyers are paying in silver that weighs less every quarter, and the arashshara have started pricing carpets in Aksumari gold.

Trader: the Strongroom Square. Pattern-books under lock; carpets from 50 sigloi for a village rug to 500 for a court piece (and a Warding Carpet, never, officially); dyes by the jar.

Zi'rzamin Dar'a Acheaoria · underground refuge

Inn: the Guest Levels. Rock rooms two levels down, free to anyone fleeing and 3 sp to anyone who is not; no names asked, no names written, ever. Barley bread, stored dates, cold water. Rumour: a satrap has demanded a list of everyone sheltered here, and the Frataraka has replied that no list exists.

Trader: the Upper Levels store. Lamps, oil, rations and rope at PHB prices plus half; a guide through the air galleries 1 siglos.

Expansion

Player Options

Player Options

Everything a player needs to make a character who was born somewhere, owes someone, and has an opinion about the Treaty.

Asetheria is five years out of a war that lasted fifteen centuries. Every adult alive was raised by people who knew nothing but the war, and every institution was built to fight it. Peace has left millions of soldiers without a war, three empires without an enemy, and a great many debts unpaid. A character who fits this world is one of those loose ends.

This part holds: a primer for each people a character can come from (what a native knows and gets wrong); the codex's existing citizenship options, unchanged, with additions for the peoples that sit between the empires; sixteen backgrounds; ten feats; how each class is seen and licensed in each empire, with six spells in Asetherian style; and a one-page checklist that ties a finished character to the cities and orders of the codex.

Everything here is player-safe. What the primers say is what a native believes. Some of it is wrong. The DM knows which parts.

SectionWhat it gives you
Where you come fromSix primers: Imperium Invicta, Hellenoria, Acheaoria, the Mavari of Mavelon, the Duneforged, the Deiperdenes
CitizenshipThe codex's benefit and drawback options (kept as written), three new lists, and the house rules every character lives with
BackgroundsSixteen, from the Demobilised Legionary to the Farshore Factor's Child
FeatsTen, each tied to an empire or an order
Classes and spellsHow every class is seen and licensed, subclass fits, six new spells
Your character and the worldA one-page checklist, and how the current party fits

Where You Come From

What a native knows, believes, fears and gets wrong. Read your own; skim the others, because your character has already formed opinions about them.
