Imperium Invicta Primer · the west

Capital: Aeterna · First city: Romulo · Motto: "Vincit qui se vincit" · Status: the Orders of the Imperium

What you know

Iovianus Sandarion built the Imperium out of frightened tribes in the worst years of the war, and the Legion held it together for fifteen hundred years. He is recovering from his wounds in Aeterna; the Imperator's chair stands empty until he is well. In the meantime General Valerius Maximus, the Dominus Militum, keeps order with the Council of Legates. The Senate meets. You know your rank in the census as you know your own name, and you know that a grain tessera in Aeterna is worth more than a speech.

What you believe

That discipline is a virtue and not a habit. That roads, aqueducts and law are the gifts the Imperium gave the continent. That the other empires were allies in the war, and junior ones. That a citizen may appeal and a non-citizen may be flogged, and that this is fair.

What you fear

The legions without pay: your brother, your cousin, the man next door, all promised land that has not come. The quarterly Assay at the Temple of Juno, because the silver in your purse buys less every season. The Speculatores Interni, who hear things. Monsters in the provinces that the war kept busy.

What you get wrong

You think the Imperium won the war. It signed a treaty. You think the Senate governs, or used to; it has not for a thousand years. You think Mavelon is an Invictian city with some islanders in it. Ask a Mavari.

At the table

Take the Imperium's citizenship options. Good fits: Demobilised Legionary, Vigiles Freedman, Patrician Remnant, Romulo Weigher.

Hellenoria Primer · the north and the sea

Capital: Hellarchon (Aetherion) · Motto: "Wisdom and will, we are one" · Status: Citizen, Metic, Slave

What you know

You are from a city first and an empire second. The cities govern themselves and answer the Emperor's summons; Hellarchon leads the League of the Hellenes because it owns the fleet. Emperor Thalorion IV has not been seen in public for ten years, which everyone knows and nobody says in the agora; his proclamations are read aloud, and every region swears the voice sounds like theirs. Astraphael, the Destructive Star, saved the empire and vanished after his duel with Iovianus Sandarion. The dusk over Hellarchon is violet.

What you believe

That argument is how free people find the truth. That your city's festival is the best one. That the Arcane Academy is the greatest school in the world, and that an Academy seal is worth more than a sword. That the sea is yours.

What you fear

Tyrants: several cities have one, and yours may be next. The Truth-Flame, whose inquisitors take an interest in unsanctioned books and wrong dialects. Hellarchon's shipowners, who are buying your city's harbour one debt at a time. The day the Theoric Fund is spent on war, because it means the Assembly has been overruled.

What you get wrong

You think the cities are equal members of a league. Hellarchon thinks otherwise, and so does its fleet. You think the violet sky is old and lovely magic; there are dissidents who say it is a wound, and they are not invited to dinner. You think the tieflings were welcomed. They were filed.

At the table

Take the Hellenorian options. Good fits: Metic Shipwright, Theoric Citizen, Voidfolk Accord Tiefling, Oracle's Dream-Sleeper.

Acheaoria Primer · the east and the desert

Capital: Persemenid · Motto: "Together We Rise, Together We Conquer" · Status: the Ranks of the Realm

What you know

Zindar Rashan al-Khavari united the desert tribes and built the Royal Road, and the King of Kings, Shahanshah Vishtaspa III, sits on his throne in Persemenid. Satraps govern the provinces; the zarates, the great houses, hold land for soldiers; the arashshara run the workshops and markets, and you bow to an arashshara's seal before you bow to most men. The Magi keep a fire in every city that must never go out. The qanats bring water under the sand, and where the shafts stop, the empire stops.

What you believe

That the empire once held seven-tenths of the continent and will be great again. That the Immortals never fall alone and always return, by rites older than the empire. That purity matters: fire, earth and water are not to be defiled, and the dead belong on the towers. That a debt of hospitality is real money.

What you fear

A dry shaft. A satrap who stops forwarding tribute and starts calling himself something grander. The creed, whose members kill only for the empire, they say, which is not as comforting as it sounds. The Court of Vipers, where a word in the wrong ear ends a family. Being a subject people's child in a Persemenid street.

What you get wrong

You believe the official history, and you have never seen it disagree with itself. Kor's readers at the Sage's Archive have. You think the King of Kings rules; the satraps think they do. You think foreigners scoffed at the qanats out of ignorance. They scoffed out of envy, which is worse.

At the table

Take the Acheaorian options. Good fits: Arashshara's Factor, Qanat Muqanni, Wheelwalker, Fire-Temple Acolyte.

The Mavari of Mavelon Primer · the north side of the Gate

Home: Mavelon, which you call Mavaholm · Ruler: Reiks Ansvald of the Hrodnings, chosen by the Thing · See the Gate, the north harbour, the Hollows

What you know

The Imperium took your island some two hundred and forty years ago, burned the longship sheds and put your great-grandfathers on the galley benches by levy. Ninety-one years ago, on the Burning of the Slips, the Mavari crews mutinied together and held the caldera until the Imperium signed the Oath at the Gate. Since then the Reiks and the Dux are equals: each holds one key to the Gate, and the bronze leaves open only when both turn. Mavari serve the fleet as paid freemen. The north harbour's fish are untaxed. Every hull launched pays the Thing its keel-silver.

What you believe

That a free spear-bearer speaks at the Thing and nobody can stop him except the Lawspeaker. That a man-price is owed for a man, and a fine paid to a treasury is an insult. That the Gate Fights on festival nights are sport, and anyone who draws steel in them is not Mavari. That your steersmen are the best on any sea, which may be true.

What you fear

Peace. Fewer launches mean less keel-silver and idle crews. The Council of Legates has started asking whether a wartime oath binds in peace. The Skelding feud, live since the spring, because a caulker died under a Sentia hull and his kin got nothing.

What you get wrong

You think the Oath is sacred to both sides. It is sacred to you; to the south it was an expedient that became a habit. You think all southerners are alike. Some married your cousins.

At the table

Take the Imperium's options or the new Mavari options. Good fits: Mavari Oarsman of the Thing, Farshore Factor's Child; feat: Keel-Born.

The Duneforged Primer · the mountain citadel

Home: the Duneforged Citadel · Ruler: Duke Roderick Caesar, House Caerthain · See House Caerthain, the Adamantine Line, the Quarrymen District

What you know

The Citadel speaks the common tongue and keeps its own titles: Duke, Marquis, Count. It sides with the Imperium and is ruled by nobody in Aeterna. House Caerthain held the Cloudspine Ridge against a coalition and broke an Acheaorian advance at the pass; the dead of that stand are carved into the walls. House Merca founded the Mithril Reserve, whose stone branches stand in every great city. The Adamantine Line under Commander Daud guards the Duke, and the Serathian Fleet's airships make a mountain house master of the sky.

What you believe

That stone keeps its word. That a gang's name for a clean face is a living. That the Caesars are the only nobles on the continent who earned it. That a Mithril Reserve note is better than any empire's coin, and lately you have been right.

What you fear

House Mihran, who lost their heir at the pass and have not forgotten. Collapse in the deep galleries. Debased Invictian silver arriving by the cartload. What the old miners say about how deep the mountain goes.

What you get wrong

You think the Citadel is safe because it has never fallen. You think the Imperium needs you more than you need it; both halves of that are argued in the Duke's council.

At the table

Take the Imperium's options or the new Duneforged options. Good fits: Duneforged Quarryman, Demobilised Legionary (of the Line); feat: Argentar's Eye.

The Deiperdenes Primer · the treaty city

Home: Deiperduem · Ruler: Arbiter Hesper of the Brass Scales, chosen by lot · See Treaty Square, the Compounds, the Counting Ward

What you know

Your city is where the three road systems meet and where the Treaty was signed. No army may garrison it; the watch and the Ironclad Legion, on contract, keep the peace. Each empire keeps an embassy compound and a high-born guest in a rival's. The Arbiter is chosen every three years by lot from three nominees, one per empire. Everything is written in three copies.

What you believe

That a contract is the only thing all three empires respect. That you are the only people on the continent who can count in three coinages and insult in three languages. That neutrality is a profession, and it pays.

What you fear

An incident in the compounds. The day a guest dies. The day one empire decides the Treaty is cheaper to break than to keep, and your city is the first place it is broken.

What you get wrong

You think neutrality protects you. It protects the Treaty; you are standing next to it.

At the table

Take the Nomad options or the new Deiperdene options. Good fits: Deiperdene Notary, Wheelwalker.

Citizenship

The house rule stands: pick an empire's citizenship or none. You take one benefit and one drawback from your list.

The codex options below are kept exactly as the house rules give them. The three new lists are for characters whose people sit between the empires: the Mavari and the Duneforged may take either the Imperium's list or their own; Deiperdenes may take the Nomad list or their own. Choose one benefit and one drawback. A drawback that names a benefit (Arcanic Overthinker, Programmed Conquerors) can only be taken with that benefit.

Imperium Invicta Codex house rule · kept
Benefits
  • Martial Training. You gain proficiency with one martial weapon (e.g., longsword, battleaxe) and medium armor.
  • Tactical Mind. You gain a +2 bonus to initiative rolls.
  • Battle Formation. If wielding a shield, you can take the Dash action as a bonus action at the start of combat.
Drawbacks
  • Rigid Views. When encountering unforeseen circumstances, you must succeed on a DC 10 Intelligence saving throw. On a failure, you are unable to act for one turn due to indecision.
  • Programmed Conquerors. If you select Battle Formation, your movement speed is halved while retreating from combat.
  • Enforced Brutality. You cannot deal non-lethal damage. Any attack that reduces a creature to 0 hit points results in its death.

In the world: a citizen may appeal to the capital and claim the grain dole in Aeterna; see the Orders.

Hellenoria Codex house rule · kept
Benefits
  • Arcane Insight. Once per long rest, you can cast Detect Magic without expending a spell slot or requiring components.
  • Cultural Empathy. You gain proficiency in one additional language and advantage on Intelligence checks related to cultural knowledge. You also have advantage on Charisma checks when interacting with fellow Hellenorians.
  • Philosopher's Insight. Once per short or long rest, you can grant yourself advantage on an Intelligence check or saving throw.
Drawbacks
  • Arcanic Overthinker. If you choose Arcane Insight, you cannot cast spells or concentrate on spells during the first round of combat.
  • Skeptical Nature. You cannot gain Inspiration from allies unless you have spent at least 6 months in-game with them or had a meaningful bonding moment (DM's call).
  • Overanalyzing. During the first turn of combat, your movement speed is reduced to 0.

In the world: citizenship is of a city, not the empire; elsewhere in Hellenoria you are a well-treated foreigner. See Citizen, Metic, Slave.

Acheaoria Codex house rule · kept
Benefits
  • Endurance of the Sands. You can forgo sleep for up to 12 hours without suffering exhaustion, once between long rests.
  • Survivor's Resilience. You gain advantage on Constitution saving throws.
  • Veil of Sand. While in familiar terrain, you can use your bonus action to hide in lightly obscured areas.
Drawbacks
  • Harsh Life. Healing from spells or potions is reduced by 2 points.
  • Cautious Demeanor. Once per encounter, you can only take the Dash, Disengage, Hide, or Dodge action on your turn.
  • Tempered Feet. In cold or wet terrain, your speed is reduced by 10 feet.

In the world: your rank decides how low you bow and to whom; see the Ranks of the Realm.

Nomad Codex house rule · kept · no citizenship
Benefits
  • Urban Adaptability. You gain advantage on Intelligence checks to find information (locations, rumors, etc.) in urban environments.
  • Nomadic Insight. You have advantage on Dexterity (Stealth) checks while moving through urban areas.
  • Traveler's Charm. You gain advantage on checks involving haggling or negotiation in markets.
Drawbacks
  • Rootless Existence. You cannot gain the benefits of friendship or allies until you've spent at least one in-game month with a group.
  • Isolation. You cannot benefit from the Help action during social encounters unless you and the assisting character agree (in character and with the DM) that a bond of trust has formed.
  • Wandering Heart. If you remain in the same settlement for more than a month, you suffer a -1 penalty to Wisdom (Perception) checks until you leave.

In the world: no empire protects you and none taxes you as a citizen. Farshore-born characters and the road-folk usually start here.

Mavari New · north side of the Gate
Benefits
  • Steersman's Eye. You have proficiency with water vehicles, and advantage on checks to navigate, read weather or keep your feet on a moving deck.
  • Spear-Ring. You may invoke the Thing's law: any Mavari who hears you name your clan and swear on your ring gives you shelter for a night and will not lie to you about a debt.
  • Gate-Fighter. When you shove a creature or grapple it, you can do so as a bonus action once per short rest.
Drawbacks
  • Man-Price. When a companion or kinsman is harmed, you must seek redress from the one responsible before you take a long rest, or you have disadvantage on Wisdom saving throws until you do.
  • North-Sider. Invictian officials, nobles and guards treat you as a non-citizen: disadvantage on Charisma checks with them outside Mavelon.
  • Landsick. After more than ten days away from the sea, you have disadvantage on Wisdom (Perception) checks until you next spend a night within sight of salt water.
Duneforged New · the Citadel
Benefits
  • Stonewise. You know the approximate depth underground, can tell if stonework is unsound with a minute's inspection, and have advantage on checks to notice traps or collapse in worked stone.
  • Line-Trained. You gain proficiency with heavy crossbows and with shields.
  • Reserve Account. You hold a Mithril Reserve account: you can draw up to 50 gp at any branch once per month against your name, repaid at the DM's discretion with interest.
Drawbacks
  • Blood at the Pass. House Mihran and its clients know your people's crest. Acheaorian nobles start one step less friendly toward you.
  • Mountain-Proud. You cannot accept payment or a gift from a non-citizen without returning its equal within a month, or you take disadvantage on Charisma checks until you do.
  • Deep-Born. In bright sunlight on open ground with no shade, you have disadvantage on Wisdom (Perception) checks that rely on sight for the first hour of each day.
Deiperdene New · the treaty city
Benefits
  • Three Tongues. You gain proficiency in two languages, and you can always tell which empire a coin, seal or uniform comes from.
  • Treaty Manners. Once per long rest, when a social encounter with officials of two or more empires turns hostile, you can make a Charisma (Persuasion) check at advantage to delay violence for one minute of talk.
  • Contract-Minded. You have advantage on checks to find loopholes, forged clauses or hidden terms in a written agreement.
Drawbacks
  • Everyone's Suspect. Each empire's agents assume you report to another. Disadvantage on Charisma checks to gain the trust of any empire's soldiers or officials on first meeting.
  • Neutral to a Fault. You cannot take the Help action for one side in a dispute between two empires' subjects unless the DM agrees a personal bond outweighs your habit.
  • Counted Out. No empire will ransom you, appeal on your behalf or extradite your attacker.
House rules your character lives with Codex · kept
  • Martial Check. Once on each of your turns, a free check against a DC set by the DM to read an enemy's skills, AC, hit points or speed, or its intentions next round. Proficiency in Investigation adds your Investigation modifier. Several options below build on it.
  • Precision Strike. Roll 4d10 on the hit-location table when an attack exceeds the target's AC by 5 or more, or on a critical hit.
  • Foraging and Herbalism. DC 15 to find a useful plant (herbalism kit, or Wisdom (Survival) or Intelligence (Nature)); DC 20 to identify an unfamiliar plant's properties; using one is a Use an Object action.
  • Worship. You may follow a god or none; the connection is personal and binds you to no service. The empires' licensing laws still apply to what you do with it (Faith and licensed magic).

Backgrounds

Sixteen ways to have been somebody before the adventure started. Each gives two skills, two tools or languages, starting equipment, a feature and a short table of characteristics.

Roll or pick on each table's columns separately. The tables are trimmed to four rows; the PHB backgrounds' tables still work if you want more. Starting coin is in the coin of the background's home: Invictian denarii pass at four-fifths of face value outside the Imperium this year, and the Mithril Reserve will tell you why.

Demobilised Legionary Background · Imperium Invicta

Skills: Athletics, Survival · Tools: one gaming set (knucklebones or dice), vehicles (land)

You served twenty years, or five, or until the Concord sent your legion home. You carry a bronze diploma promising land in a province you have never seen, and a pension the treasury has not paid. Millions of you walk the Imperium's roads. The Council of Legates would like your loyalty; so would the bandits.

Equipment. A folded bronze discharge diploma naming your legion and the allotment you were promised, a dolabra (counts as a handaxe that also digs), a mess tin and marching pole, a vine-wood stick if you made optio, a set of common clothes, and a belt pouch with 10 gp in denarii.

Feature: Honourable Discharge

Any legion camp, veterans' colony or roadside station on an Invictian road gives you a meal and a bunk for a night, and a serving centurion will hear you out. You have read a thousand shield-walls: when you make a Martial Check against soldiers in formation or wearing issued gear, you add your proficiency bonus if you would not otherwise add it.

d4TraitIdealBondFlaw
1I still wake at the fourth watch and polish something.Order. A camp laid out square is a camp that survives the night.My contubernium: seven men who shared a tent with me. Three are still alive.I treat every stranger on the road as a scout for the enemy.
2I measure distance in marching days and food in rations.The Pact. The state promised land; I will collect it.My legion's eagle, lost or laid up in a temple.I will follow a man with a crest on his helmet further than I should.
3I tell war stories badly and at length.Brotherhood. Any veteran is owed my last coin.The centurion who saved my life and now begs at the Porta.I drink to forget the war and then talk about nothing else.
4I salute officers out of habit, even foreign ones.Peace. I have seen enough war to want it never again.The allotment on my diploma. I have walked to see it. Someone else farms it.I despise civilians who did not serve, and I let it show.
Vigiles Freedman Background · Aeterna

Skills: Insight, Perception · Tools: carpenter's tools, one gaming set

You were a slave, then a freedman with your old master's name, then a man of the Vigiles, Aeterna's night watch and fire brigade: seven cohorts with axes and buckets, the only lawfully armed men inside the sacred line. You are a citizen, barred from office. Your sons would not be. You know which insulae will burn first and whose they are.

Equipment. A fire-axe (handaxe), a leather bucket, 50 feet of knotted rope, a freedman's felt cap, a wax tablet recording your manumission, a set of common clothes, and a belt pouch with 10 gp.

Feature: Seventh Cohort

Any Vigiles station in an Invictian city gives you shelter and gossip. You know the night streets: given an hour, you can learn who owns, rents and insures any building in an Invictian city, and which doors the watch does not knock on. Your former master is your patron, by law; he can ask favours of you and you of him.

d4TraitIdealBondFlaw
1I smell smoke before anyone, and I say so, every time.Duty. A fire does not care whose house it is.Titus Oppius Ursus, Prefect of the Vigiles, who signed my enrolment.I still flinch when a patrician raises his voice.
2I break doors first and apologise later.Freedom. Nobody will own me again.My patron, who freed me, and whom I do not entirely forgive.I take bribes from landlords, small ones, so they fix nothing.
3I know a joke for every cohort station.Respect. A freedman's son should be able to stand for office.The family I pulled out of a burning insula. They named a child after me.I resent anyone born free and tell them so.
4I count exits in every room.Community. The Subura looks after its own.The slave I was freed alongside, who was not.I trust the watch over the law, and the law notices.
Patrician Remnant Background · Aeterna

Skills: History, Persuasion · Tools: one musical instrument · Languages: one of your choice

Your family's name is older than the Imperium's and your family's money is not. The Cursus Honorum still runs, and your relatives still climb it, and none of it commands a single legion. The soldiers rule. You were raised to rule them, and to marry well, which may be the same thing: ask House Calpurnia.

Equipment. A signet ring with your gens's seal, a toga with the broad stripe (darned), an ancestor's wax mask in a cedar box, a letter of introduction to a senator, a set of fine clothes, and a purse with 25 gp (and debts of 200).

Feature: The Ancestors' Atrium

Patrician households receive you as one of their own, and you can obtain an audience with a senator, a Comes or a priest of a state cult within a day or two. The legates and their officers are another matter: to them you are a name that needs a job, and they will offer you one, on terms.

d4TraitIdealBondFlaw
1I quote my great-grandfather's speeches from memory.Tradition. The Senate was right once and can be again.The ancestor's mask I carry. I talk to it.I assume servants are furniture.
2I am impeccably polite to people I despise.Restoration. My house will be great again, whatever it costs.A cousin married into a rival empire for the family's sake.I will not admit we are poor, even to people paying for my dinner.
3I have perfect manners at table and none on the road.Responsibility. The well-born owe the city.Our clients, who still come to the door each morning for a coin we cannot spare.A soldier who insults my name gets an answer, however large he is.
4I read everything, including other people's letters.Power. A name is a weapon; I intend to use mine.A debt my father owed to a legate, which I have inherited.I gamble, because it is the only thing patricians are still allowed to win.
Mavari Oarsman of the Thing Background · Mavelon

Skills: Athletics, Perception · Tools: vehicles (water), carpenter's tools

You are a free spear-bearer of the Mavari, sworn at the Thingstead, and you pulled an oar (or held the steering board) on an Imperial warship as a paid freeman under the Oath at the Gate. The fleet is laying up hulls. Your bench is empty and your keel-silver short. You have walked the Bridge Walk, fought in the Gate Fights and been pulled out of them at the third hour by people who were also drunk.

Equipment. A bronze spear-ring sworn on at the Thing, an oar-blade carved with your bench number (a club), a whale-oil lamp, a sealskin bag, a set of traveller's clothes, and a pouch with 10 gp in hack-silver.

Feature: Free Spear

You can claim passage on any ship with a Mavari steersman in exchange for work. You may speak at the Thing and swear before the Gate Court, and your oath is recorded by the doomsman. Mavari crews in any harbour will hide you, feed you, or start a fight on your behalf, though not all three on the same night.

d4TraitIdealBondFlaw
1I sing at the oar and anywhere else that has a rhythm.The Oath. Ninety years of keeping it is what makes us free.My clan, Hrodning or Skelding, and the man-price it is owed.I settle insults with my fists before anyone has finished the insult.
2I judge everyone by how they handle a boat.Equality. A Reiks is a man the Thing chose; he can be unchosen.A south-side shipmate I would die for and will not admit to liking.I do not trust anyone who cannot swim.
3I am silent on land and loud at sea.Kin. Blood is paid with silver or with blood.The Lawspeaker, who once stopped a Reiks mid-sentence for my sake.I take every slight to the Mavari personally and keep count.
4I name every ship I meet, and judge it.Freedom. No levy, no bench, no master.The bench I rowed on and the hull it belonged to, now laid up.I spend keel-silver faster than it comes.
Romulo Weigher Background · Romulo

Skills: Insight, Investigation · Tools: calligrapher's supplies, one language of your choice

Romulo keeps the copy that counts of every institution, including the master weights and measures under Juno's seal in the Hall of Weights. Every foreign cargo and great contract is registered and sealed there. You sat under the colonnade testing other people's scales and refusing their bribes, or accepting them, for the Praefectus Ponderum, the most bribed-at man in the Imperium.

Equipment. A folding bronze balance with a set of sealed weights, a lead seal-press with a cancelled die, a stylus and wax tablets, a set of plain fine clothes, and a purse with 15 gp.

Feature: The Copy That Counts

With a minute and your balance you can tell a false weight, a short measure or a clipped coin. Clerks of the Hall of Weights will look up a registered contract or cargo for you, and any merchant who trades through Romulo recognises your seal and will at least read what you have sealed.

d4TraitIdealBondFlaw
1I weigh things in my hand without thinking, including food.Honesty. A just weight is a prayer to Juno.The master standards in the strongroom. I have seen them; I would know a copy.I cannot let a short measure pass, even when silence would save us.
2I speak six languages' worth of haggling and one of small talk.Commerce. Trade between strangers is the only real peace.A Farshore factor who taught me their numerals.I took one bribe, years ago. Someone has the receipt.
3I keep receipts for everything, including favours.Precision. Approximately is a lie with manners.The Praefectus Ponderum, who protected me once.I treat people as accounts to be balanced.
4I am suspicious of round numbers.Fairness. The small merchant and the great house use the same scales.My family's office under the colonnade, with its mosaic and its debts.I assume everyone is cheating me, and say so.
Hellenorian Metic Shipwright Background · Hellarchon, Corinth

Skills: Athletics, Investigation · Tools: carpenter's tools, vehicles (water)

Hellenoria has the finest shipbuilders on the continent, and most of them are not citizens. You are a metic: a resident foreigner who pays the yearly tax, needs a citizen sponsor, owns no land and votes on nothing, and who builds the triremes that make Hellarchon a hegemon. In the shipsheds metics outnumber citizens and run the yards.

Equipment. An adze and a caulking iron, a bronze sponsor's token stamped with your patron's deme, this year's metic-tax receipt, a set of work clothes stained with pitch, and a pouch with 10 gp.

Feature: The Yards Remember

Any shipyard in Hellenoria will hire you for a day wage and lodging. You can tell which yard built a ship, roughly when, and whether it has been repaired by someone cheaper. Metics in any Hellenorian port talk to you as one of their own.

d4TraitIdealBondFlaw
1I tap hulls, walls and tables to hear if they are sound.Craft. A ship that floats is the only argument that matters.The citizen sponsor I owe, who can end my residence with a word.I despise citizens who have never worked, which is most of them.
2I sketch keels on anything flat.Belonging. Twenty years here should make me something.The first hull I helped launch, still at sea.I pad every estimate by a third.
3I swear in four ports' dialects.Independence. I owe the city work, not love.The yard-master who taught me, a metic like me, who died in debt.I talk about ships until people leave.
4I am at ease on a deck and nervous on a road.Fairness. Those who build the fleet should have a say in it.A secret about how a certain ship was built, and why.I will cut a corner if no one will see it.
Theoric Citizen Background · any Hellenorian city

Skills: History, Performance · Tools: one musical instrument · Languages: one of your choice

You are a full citizen of a Hellenorian city, born of two citizen parents and enrolled in your deme. The Theoric Fund pays your festival seat, and the law says it cannot be spent on war; you know that law better than you know your trade. You have voted, shouted in the Assembly, sung in a chorus and watched a comedy mock your Archon to his face.

Equipment. A bronze theatre token stamped with your deme and tribe, a chorus mask, a himation, a scroll of a banned comedy, and a pouch with 10 gp.

Feature: The Citizen's Seat

In your own city you have a vote and the right to speak once in any Assembly. You know which demagogue wants what and which tyrant's men drink where. Your deme will vouch for you, lend you a bed and a little money, and expect you at the next festival. In other cities you are a well-born foreigner, which gets you a hearing and a suspicious look.

d4TraitIdealBondFlaw
1I argue both sides of anything, for fun.Liberty. A city with a tyrant is a city in chains.My deme, and the old men on its bench who taught me to vote.I cannot keep quiet when an argument is being lost.
2I quote poets at people who did not ask.Law. The Fund is for the festivals, and that is what makes us free.A playwright whose work I memorised before it was burned.I look down on metics and slaves, though I would deny it.
3I know every festival's date and grudge.Glory. My city first, then the League.My city's harbour, which Hellarchon is buying.I sell my vote, but only to the right side.
4I applaud loudly and heckle louder.Reason. Truth comes from argument, not from the Truth-Flame.A friend exiled by ostracism, whom I voted against.I treat every disagreement as an Assembly debate.
Voidfolk Accord Tiefling Background · Hellenoria

Skills: Insight, Stealth · Tools: one gaming set · Languages: Infernal or Abyssal

Hellenoria absorbed your people under the Voidfolk Accord. Its terms are classified; you have never read them, and neither has anyone you know. What you know is what it does: you hold a status of your own, neither metic nor citizen, recorded by number in a register an Accord officer keeps. You are protected in ways you do not fully understand and watched in ways you understand very well.

Equipment. A black bronze Accord token with a number and no name, a hooded travelling cloak, a sealed letter from your district's Accord officer, a set of common clothes, and a pouch with 10 gp.

Feature: Numbered, Not Named

In a Hellenorian city you may not lawfully be enslaved, expelled or tried by a city court without an Accord officer present; showing your token stops most trouble with the watch. You can always find the Voidfolk quarter of a Hellenorian city and a bed in it. The cost: an Accord officer expects to be told when you leave a city, and asking questions about the Accord itself is the surest way to meet the Truth-Flame.

d4TraitIdealBondFlaw
1I hide my tail, horns or eyes, out of habit, even among friends.Truth. I want to read the Accord, whatever it says.My number. I was given it; I intend to make it a name.I assume every kindness is surveillance.
2I am charming to officials and cold to everyone else.Survival. The Accord protects us; do not test it.The Voidfolk quarter that raised me.I lie about my origins even when the truth would help.
3I keep a list of everyone who has been kind to me.Belonging. I am Hellenorian; let them argue otherwise.An Accord officer who bent a rule for me once.I provoke people to see whether they will flinch.
4I laugh at my own reflection.Freedom. A status is still a cage with better food.A grandparent who remembered life before the Accord and would not speak of it.I break small laws to prove I can.
Oracle's Dream-Sleeper Background · Delphara

Skills: Insight, Religion · Tools: herbalism kit · Languages: one of your choice

At Delphara, below the oracle, the Dream Dormitory takes pilgrims who sleep in the sanctuary and bring their dreams to the priests for reading. You were one of the sleepers kept on, because your dreams were clear, or strange, or paid for. You know the Sacred Way, the treasuries, and the price of an early consultation. Lately, people from far away have been asking the dream-sleepers too many questions.

Equipment. A ram's fleece to sleep on, a clay tablet and stylus for writing dreams on waking, a vial of laurel oil, a set of plain robes, and a pouch with 5 gp and two offering cakes.

Feature: Incubant

Any Hellenorian sanctuary gives you a mat and a meal. You know the protocol for consulting any oracle or dream-shrine, and the priests of Delphara will read your dreams for free. Once per adventure, if you sleep at a sanctuary, the DM may give you a dream: an image, never an answer.

d4TraitIdealBondFlaw
1I tell people what I dreamed about them.Revelation. The gods speak; most people sleep through it.The priest who first read my dreams.I cannot tell a dream from a memory after a week.
2I nap anywhere and wake suddenly.Neutrality. The oracle belongs to every city.A pilgrim whose dream I read wrong.I take omens far too seriously.
3I am serene until someone touches my fleece.Service. Pilgrims come in fear; they should leave with hope.A dream I have had since childhood, of a city of mirrors.I suspect the oracle's neutrality is for sale and say so.
4I whisper the names of the gods when I am nervous.Mystery. Some questions should stay asked.The Dream Dormitory, and its keepers, who did not want me to leave.I sleepwalk.
Arashshara's Factor Background · Acheaoria

Skills: Insight, Persuasion · Tools: weaver's tools · Languages: one of your choice

The arashshara, women overseers of production and trade, run Acheaoria's workshops and markets, and an arashshara's seal outranks most men's. You were her factor: you carried her samples, counted her bales, negotiated with caravan masters and satraps' stewards, and reported everything you saw. She has sent you out into the world with her trust, her money and a list of questions.

Equipment. A clay sealing with your mistress's sign, a measuring cord knotted in cubits, a ledger of commissions, a sample case of dyed silk, a set of fine clothes, and a purse with 15 gp.

Feature: The Overseer's Seal

Workshops and markets under arashshara in Acheaoria are open to you, and you buy trade goods there at producer's price (a tenth less). Merchants who insult you insult her, and they know it. Your mistress expects a report by every caravan, and occasionally sends an errand back.

d4TraitIdealBondFlaw
1I note the price of everything, aloud.Craft. Good work deserves a good market.My arashshara, who raised me from the loom-floor.I cannot resist a bargain, even one I do not need.
2I am gracious to everyone until the contract is signed.Loyalty. Her name is on my seal; I keep it clean.The weavers of Tabrishiir, whose work I sell.I gossip; it is how I was trained.
3I touch cloth to judge it, and people to judge them.Ambition. I will have a seal of my own.A rival factor who cheated my mistress.I treat men who will not deal with women as already beaten, and let them know it.
4I keep two ledgers: hers and mine.Prosperity. Trade waters the desert better than any qanat.The caravan master who carried me on my first road.I keep secrets from my mistress, and she suspects.
Qanat Muqanni Background · the Qanat Line

Skills: Athletics, Survival · Tools: mason's tools, one gaming set

The qanats bring water under the desert through tunnels dug and cleared by the muqanni, who go down the shafts in white shrouds because a man in a qanat is already halfway to the dead. Where the shafts stop, the empire stops. In towns like Qa'zshahrv'in your families are the most protected residents, which is another way of saying hostages. You came up one last time and kept walking.

Equipment. A clay lamp, 50 feet of windlass rope, a short mattock (light hammer), a white shroud, a set of common clothes, and a pouch with 10 gp.

Feature: Down the Shaft

You can always find water in desert or broken country if any is within a day's walk, and you have advantage on the foraging check to locate it. Underground you can judge bad air, rising water and failing roof before others notice. Every town on the Qanat Line feeds a muqanni, by custom and self-interest.

d4TraitIdealBondFlaw
1I listen to the ground with my palm flat.Water. Everything else is decoration.My family, left behind in the Pool Ward.I hate open sky and say so.
2I am calm in the dark and jumpy in crowds.Duty. The channel must be kept, whoever rules.The shaft my father did not come up from.I hold grudges as long as a tunnel.
3I ration water even when there is plenty.Community. A town that shares water does not die.A master muqanni who taught me the old marks on the tunnel walls.I do not believe anything a satrap's man tells me.
4I sing the counting songs of the shafts.Freedom. I went down a dead man; I came up my own.A tunnel mark I found that no one could read.I take reckless risks underground, because I have already died once.
Wheelwalker Background · the roads

Skills: Animal Handling, Insight · Tools: vehicles (land), carpenter's tools

The Wheelwalkers are Jauhar's caravan families: they own no land, keep no house, and have a cousin in every city. Your family's carts work the Royal Road and the Treaty Road, mending wheels and carrying what the great caravans will not. The senior uncle, Javid of the Wheels, keeps the courtyard of carts at Atarabad and the family's memory of every debt.

Equipment. A spoke carved with your family's knots, an ox-goad, a list of cousins in your own cipher, a set of traveller's clothes, and a pouch with 10 gp.

Feature: A Cousin in Every City

In any city on the Royal Road, the Treaty Road or the Via Ferraria you can find Wheelwalker kin who will lodge you and your companions for a night, mend a wheel, and tell you what the road is saying: bandits, tolls, which watch takes bribes. In return they may ask you to carry a parcel, a message or a cousin.

d4TraitIdealBondFlaw
1I call everyone cousin, including enemies.Family. The road is our house.Javid of the Wheels, who keeps the family's memory.I cannot stay anywhere more than a few nights without itching.
2I can sleep in a moving cart.Freedom. No land, no lord, no tax.The ox that pulled our cart when I was a child.I trust kin over friends, even bad kin.
3I bargain with gestures as well as words.Hospitality. A guest is sacred; a host is sacred back.A cousin who went missing on the Treaty Road.I borrow things and forget whose they were.
4I read a road's dust like a letter.Fairness. Tolls should be paid once.A family debt owed to the Chyrsus Syndicate.I despise settled folk a little and they can tell.
Fire-Temple Acolyte Background · Atarabad or any Acheaorian city

Skills: Religion, Medicine · Tools: herbalism kit · Languages: one of your choice

You tended a fire that must never go out. The Magi keep one in every city; the oldest, at Atarabad's Fire Hill, under Mobad Atar-Farnbag, the First Flame. You fed it sandalwood with a veil over your mouth so your breath would not defile it, learned the purity laws, and carried the dead to the towers so they would touch neither fire, earth nor water.

Equipment. A white mouth-veil, a bundle of sandalwood, a sacred cord of three knots worn at the waist, a small brass fire-bowl, a set of white robes, and a pouch with 5 gp.

Feature: Keeper of the Flame

Fire-temples in Acheaoria shelter and feed you. You can perform the purification rites the law requires (a purification normally costs 25 gp and a day) for yourself and your companions, and you never commit a purity crime by accident. You can tell at a glance whether a sacred fire has been defiled, and how.

d4TraitIdealBondFlaw
1I wash my hands before and after everything.Purity. Good thoughts, good words, good deeds.The fire I tended. I know its colour like a face.I recoil from corpses, blood and anyone who handles them.
2I speak softly near any flame.Truth. The lie is the first defilement.The Mobad who gave me my cord.I lecture foreigners on how they bury their dead.
3I stare into fires and see things, or say I do.Charity. The Fire warms the beggar and the king.A tower of silence where my parents lie.I keep asking questions about the Rite of Return that I was told not to ask.
4I keep a coal from my temple alive in a brass bowl.Order. The world is a battle between the clean and the corrupt.A fellow acolyte expelled for a reason no one gave.I judge people as clean or unclean within a minute.
Deiperdene Notary Background · Deiperduem

Skills: Investigation, Persuasion · Tools: calligrapher's supplies · Languages: one of your choice

In Deiperduem everything is written in three copies, and on Notaries' Row you were the one who wrote them. You witnessed marriages between houses that had killed each other's sons, sales of cargo that did not yet exist, and at least one confession you were paid to forget. Your seal is registered at the Arbiter's house.

Equipment. A brass notarial seal, a case of inks and reeds, three blank treaty-form sheets, a set of fine clothes, and a purse with 15 gp.

Feature: Three Copies

A document you witness and seal is accepted as genuine in Deiperduem's courts and in all three embassy compounds. You can consult the notarial registry on Notaries' Row, and embassy clerks of all three empires know your face and will tell you whom to bribe, and how much.

d4TraitIdealBondFlaw
1I read the small clauses first.Neutrality. I serve the document, not the party.Arbiter Hesper, who once took my side.I cannot stop correcting people's grammar, in three languages.
2I write everything down, especially promises.Law. A world held together by contracts is held together.A treaty clause my grandmother drafted.I will witness anything for enough money.
3I am precise about dates and vague about myself.Peace. Ink is cheaper than blood.The guest in one of the compounds, who was kind to me as a child.I know one secret too many and it shows.
4I insist on three copies of everything, including dinner bills.Profit. Neutrality is a trade.The confession I was paid to forget.I trust paper over people.
Duneforged Quarryman Background · the Citadel

Skills: Athletics, Nature · Tools: mason's tools, one gaming set

You cut stone on the face of the Quarrymen District, in a family gang whose name for a clean face is its living. Pay was good and lives were short. Every year's last block is carved and set into the district wall, and one of them has your name on it. The deep galleries supply the Citadel's walls, its Reserve vaults and its stories.

Equipment. A gang token on a cord, a mason's maul (light hammer), a set of chisels, a fist-sized chip of a year-block, a set of work clothes grey with dust, and a pouch with 10 gp.

Feature: A Name for a Clean Face

Quarry gangs and miners anywhere will share a meal and a rumour with you. You can judge the age and soundness of stonework, find the weak point in a wall, and follow a mine gallery back toward the surface. In the Citadel, the gangs will vouch for you to the Line.

d4TraitIdealBondFlaw
1I knock on walls before I lean on them.Craft. A clean face outlasts a king.My gang and the name we cut.I have no patience for people who talk instead of working.
2I am quiet, then very loud.Loyalty. The Caesars held the pass; we hold the stone.A friend lost in a collapse in the deep galleries.I drink like the dust is still in my throat.
3I collect interesting stones.Fairness. The Reserve's vaults were cut by our hands.Overseer Tarnak, who gave me my first face.I do not trust anything Acheaorian.
4I measure people by their grip.Curiosity. I want to know what is below the deepest gallery.The year-block with my name on it.I take on any weight to prove I can.
Farshore Factor's Child Background · Romulo or Mavelon

Skills: Insight, Persuasion · Languages: two of your choice (one is your parent's Farshore tongue)

Your mother or father kept a house's office for a realm beyond Asetheria: Qart-Hadeth's elephant or Tyrsa's murex shell on the pavement of Romulo's Guild Square, a warehouse on Mavelon's Farshore Quays, or something rarer: a jade token from Ixtal, a Seric envoy's seal. You grew up between two worlds, fluent in both and native to neither, and you have been sent, or have run, inland.

Equipment. A token bearing your house's emblem, a small merchant's scale, a letter in a script no one in Asetheria can read, a set of traveller's clothes, and a purse with 15 gp in a foreign coinage.

Feature: Under the Colonnade

Your house's office in Romulo or Mavelon will shelter you, pass messages home on the next ship and change foreign coin at a fair rate. Farshore merchants of other realms treat you as a colleague's child: civil, curious, and ready to trade. Asetherians treat you as an omen, a curiosity or a spy, depending on the day.

d4TraitIdealBondFlaw
1I compare everything to home, unfavourably.Exchange. Strangers who trade do not fight.My parent's office and its mosaic on the pavement.I forget local customs and blame them for it.
2I collect words in every language I hear.Discovery. This continent has more to show me.Someone who travelled with me to Asetheria and was lost on the way.I mock Asetherian gods, quietly.
3I am homesick for a place I barely remember.Belonging. I will make this land my own.The ship that brought me, and its pilot.I tell people what they want to hear about where I come from.
4I eat anything once.Profit. My house will prosper here or I will know why.A letter I cannot open until a certain day.I treat every Asetherian as a customer.

Feats

Ten feats learned in a particular drill-yard, temple or harbour. Each is balanced against the PHB's: a half-feat gives +1 to an ability score and a modest feature; the others give a little more.

A feat tied to an order assumes your character trained with it or alongside it. That does not make you a member; it makes you someone the order recognises, which can be better or worse. Prerequisites are suggestions where marked "story"; the DM may waive them for a good reason.

FeatEmpire or orderPrerequisiteIn short
Legion DrillImperium Invicta, the legionsshield proficiency+1 Str or Con; shield-wall AC, read formations
Seventh Cohortthe Vigilesnone+1 Con or Wis; smoke, fire and broken doors
Academy Sealthe Arcane Academy, Ecliptica Arcanumthe ability to cast a spell+1 Int, Wis or Cha; a planned working
Agora RebuttalHellenoria, the AssemblyCha 13+1 Int or Cha; interrupt a lie or a threat
Sacred BandThebesieasStr or Con 13+1 Str or Con; fight beside a bonded comrade
Purity of Firethe Maginone+1 Wis; sacred flame, disease, and denying the dead
Ravine RiderXerastri, horse-archersDex 13+1 Dex; shoot and ride away
Wheelwalker Cousinthe Wheelwalkersnone+1 Wis or Cha; roads, carts and kin
Argentar's Eyethe Argentar, the Mithril ReserveInt 13+1 Int; read coin, contract and liar
Keel-Bornthe Mavarinone (story: raised at sea)+1 Str or Con; swim, steer, and hold a deck
Legion Drill Feat · Imperium Invicta

Prerequisite: proficiency with shields

Twenty years of drill on the Campus have taught you that a legionary is a brick and the line is the wall.

  • Increase your Strength or Constitution by 1, to a maximum of 20.
  • While you hold a shield and an ally holding a shield is within 5 feet of you, you and that ally gain a +1 bonus to AC. The bonus does not stack with itself from several allies or several feats.
  • When you make a Martial Check against a group of creatures fighting in formation, a success reveals the information for every creature in that formation, not just one.
Seventh Cohort Feat · the Vigiles

Prerequisite: none

You have run into burning insulae with an axe and a wet cloak, and come out with somebody's grandmother.

  • Increase your Constitution or Wisdom by 1, to a maximum of 20.
  • You have advantage on saving throws against inhaled poisons and smoke, and you do not suffer the effects of heavily obscured areas made of smoke on your Wisdom (Perception) checks that rely on hearing or touch.
  • Rubble, burning debris and collapsed floors are not difficult terrain for you.
  • As a bonus action, you can extinguish flames on a creature or object within 5 feet of you, or force open a door or shutter that is stuck (not locked). Against a locked door, you have advantage on the Strength check to break it.
Academy Seal Feat · the Arcane Academy

Prerequisite: the ability to cast at least one spell

The Ecliptica Arcanum teaches that a working planned three weeks in advance rarely needs to be impressive. You passed the examination and carry the seal that opens every Hellenorian city's doors to a mage.

  • Increase your Intelligence, Wisdom or Charisma by 1, to a maximum of 20.
  • Planned working. When you finish a long rest, choose one 1st-level spell you have prepared or know. Until your next long rest, you can cast it once at 1st level without expending a spell slot, provided you spend 1 minute before the casting marking its ground, drawing its figure or reciting its notation. If the spell's casting time is longer than 1 minute, use its own time.
  • You hold an Academy seal (worth 100 gp in Hellenoria; see the Academy, the Lexicon and the Tribunal). In Hellenorian cities, officials treat you as a certified mage, not a suspect.
Agora Rebuttal Feat · Hellenoria

Prerequisite: Charisma 13 or higher

You learned rhetoric where a bad argument gets you pelted with figs and a good one gets you exiled.

  • Increase your Intelligence or Charisma by 1, to a maximum of 20.
  • When a creature you can see within 60 feet of you makes a Charisma (Deception, Intimidation or Persuasion) check against someone other than you, and you can be heard, you can use your reaction to interject and impose disadvantage on that check. You can use this feature a number of times equal to your proficiency bonus, regaining all uses on a long rest.
  • When you address a crowd of ten or more for at least a minute, you have advantage on Charisma checks to sway it, or to stop it from becoming a mob.
Sacred Band Feat · Thebesieas

Prerequisite: Strength or Constitution 13 or higher

Thebesieas's Sacred Band fights in sworn pairs, on the principle that nobody runs in front of the person they love. Epameinon Kleitarchos commands it; you trained beside it, or in it.

  • Increase your Strength or Constitution by 1, to a maximum of 20.
  • When you finish a long rest, you can name one willing ally as your comrade until your next long rest. While your comrade is within 5 feet of you, you both have advantage on saving throws against being frightened.
  • When your comrade is reduced to 0 hit points or hit by a critical hit while within 30 feet of you, you can use your reaction to move up to half your speed toward the attacker and make one melee weapon attack against it if it is in reach.
Purity of Fire Feat · the Magi

Prerequisite: none

You have been taught by the Magi that the clean and the corrupt are at war, and that fire takes a side.

  • Increase your Wisdom by 1, to a maximum of 20.
  • You learn the sacred flame cantrip. Wisdom is your spellcasting ability for it.
  • You have advantage on saving throws against disease.
  • You can spend 10 minutes performing a purification rite over a corpse. For 10 days it cannot be raised as undead, and any creature trying to animate it must first succeed on a spellcasting ability check against a DC of 8 + your proficiency bonus + your Wisdom modifier.
Ravine Rider Feat · Xerastri

Prerequisite: Dexterity 13 or higher

On the northern frontier the horse-archers of the Parthian Ravine, under Roxana Surena, teach that a horseman who stops is a target.

  • Increase your Dexterity by 1, to a maximum of 20.
  • While mounted, being within 5 feet of a hostile creature does not impose disadvantage on your ranged weapon attack rolls.
  • While mounted, after you make a ranged weapon attack on your turn, your mount's movement for the rest of the turn does not provoke opportunity attacks from the creature you attacked.
  • When a ranged weapon attack you make while mounted scores a Precision Strike, you may roll the 4d10 twice and choose either result.
Wheelwalker Cousin Feat · the Wheelwalkers

Prerequisite: none

The caravan families adopted you, or you were born on a cart. Either way, you are family, which means you owe everyone something.

  • Increase your Wisdom or Charisma by 1, to a maximum of 20.
  • You gain proficiency with land vehicles and with carpenter's tools; if already proficient in either, you gain proficiency with one artisan's tool of your choice instead.
  • When you lead a group travelling on a road, the group can move at a fast pace without the usual penalty to passive Wisdom (Perception), and at a normal pace it can forage or navigate as if moving slowly.
  • Once per settlement per month, you can find a Wheelwalker who gives you lodging for the night and one true rumour about the road ahead.
Argentar's Eye Feat · the Argentar, the Mithril Reserve

Prerequisite: Intelligence 13 or higher

You learned at a Reserve counter, from a Dominus Argentar who had seen every lie a borrower can tell, and that the Reserve is now discounting Invictian silver.

  • Increase your Intelligence by 1, to a maximum of 20.
  • You gain proficiency in Insight or Investigation. If you are already proficient in both, double your proficiency bonus for one of them when the check concerns money, contracts or debts.
  • By handling a coin, ingot or gem for an action, you learn its metal content or quality, whether it is debased, clipped or false, and its fair value in the nearest Reserve branch's reckoning.
  • When a creature tries to deceive you about a sum, a price or a debt, you have advantage on the Wisdom (Insight) check to tell.
Keel-Born Feat · the Mavari

Prerequisite: none (story: raised at sea or on the north harbour)

You learned to walk on a deck and swim before that. Mavari steersmen take southern masters' warships through the caldera's Mouth in fog, and do not mention it.

  • Increase your Strength or Constitution by 1, to a maximum of 20.
  • You gain a swimming speed equal to your walking speed, and you can hold your breath for twice as long as normal.
  • You have advantage on ability checks and saving throws to avoid being knocked prone or pushed while standing on a ship, a pier or other unsteady footing.
  • You gain proficiency with water vehicles. When you steer a vessel, its crew has advantage on checks to keep it from foundering, running aground or being boarded.

Classes and Spells

Every class exists in every empire. What changes is who licenses it, who fears it, and what the neighbours call it behind its back.

The empires do not ban magic; they license it (Faith and licensed magic). In the Imperium an arcane caster must belong to a licensed collegium (50 gp a year and an Arcana DC 14 examination); in Hellenoria a mage wants an Academy seal (100 gp and Arcana DC 15) and a priest of an unrecognised god is unprotected; in Acheaoria the Magi care less about who casts than about what is defiled, and the dead must never touch fire, earth or water. Mavelon's north side, the Duneforged Citadel and Deiperduem have their own customs.

ClassImperium InvictaHellenoriaAcheaoriaMavari, Duneforged, Deiperduem
BarbarianA "provincial" or an auxiliary. Tolerated in the legions' allied cohorts, never promoted.Hired from the frontier, admired in the arena, kept out of the Assembly.Steppe-folk like Tomyra: hired by all, ruled by none.Mavari: honoured, if they keep the Gate Fights unarmed. Duneforged: dwarven clans' battle-rage is respected.

Deiperduem pays translators who can also sing.

The Citadel distrusts anyone who talks to stone.

Subclass fits Flavour notes · not rules
  • Barbarian. Path of the Totem Warrior (stag) for the grove at Nemibano, as Gnaeus Ferrus; Berserker for steppe hires; Zealot for a Mavari sworn to the sea.
  • Bard. Glamour for the Melodic Circle (Shirin Navaz); Lore for a Hellenorian sophist; Eloquence for a Senate orator; Swords for an arena showman.
  • Cleric. Light for the Magi (Atar-Farnbag); War for Mars and Bellona; Knowledge for Athena; Order for Juno and the Assay; Grave for the towers of silence.
  • Druid. Shepherd for Nemibano (Sylvia Nemorina); Land (desert) for the Qanat Line; Sea or Moon for the Mavari.
  • Fighter. Battle Master for the legions (Decimus Corvus); Champion for the arena (Marcia Ferox); Cavalier for the zarates (Artabazos Mihran); Eldritch Knight for Academy-trained marines.
  • Monk. Open Hand for a Cynic; Shadow for the creed's novices; Four Elements, carefully, near the Magi.
  • Paladin. Devotion for the Sacred Band (Epameinon); Crown for a legion's eagle; Ancients for the Mavari Oath; Vengeance for the Cloudspine Feud, on either side.
  • Ranger. Hunter for the Ravine (Roxana Surena); Gloom Stalker for the qanats; Horizon Walker for Treaty Road wardens.
  • Rogue. Assassin for the creed (Bagoas); Swashbuckler for Corinth (Nerissa); Inquisitive for the Speculatores; Mastermind for the Court of Vipers.
  • Sorcerer. Storm for the Aeolus Reach (Ixion); Divine Soul for a Magi foundling; Draconic for a Duneforged deep-blood.
  • Warlock. Archfey and Great Old One patrons are as unwelcome as Fiends; the Dreaming Gods have taken pacts before (Vesperine Ilaro, hunted). Hexblade for a soldier who kept something from the war.
  • Wizard. Evocation at the Academy (Kallisto); Divination at Delphara (Lysandra); Abjuration at Deiperduem; Necromancy only under the throne's licence at Persemenid.
  • Artificer. Alchemist for the Crucible Spire; Armorer for Mavelon's arsenal; Battle Smith for the Adamantine Line.
Licences at a glance What to carry
  • Imperium. Collegium licence for arcane casters (50 gp a year). Unlicensed casting in a city: 200 gp fine or a month in chains. Priests of state gods need nothing; foreign priests need the pontiffs' leave.
  • Hellenoria. Academy seal (100 gp). Books in unsanctioned dialects invite the Truth-Flame. Unrecognised gods: worship freely, expect no protection.
  • Acheaoria. No licence to cast; a capital crime to defile a fire. A corpse in a city without rites means arrest; a purification costs 25 gp and a day.
  • Mavelon. The south follows Imperial law; the north follows the Thing, which cares what you did, not how.
  • Duneforged. Casters register with House Virellarion's Crucible Spire; nobody casts near the Reserve vaults.
  • Deiperduem. No licences, but the Treaty Wards record every spell above a certain strength cast inside the walls.
Peoples in the empires How you will be seen
  • Humans dominate all three empires and assume they always will.
  • Dwarves are at home in the Duneforged Citadel and the Mithril Reserve (Clan Ironhand runs many branches); old clans like Hugrakkur were Imperial vassals, not citizens.
  • Elves and half-elves are rare enough to be stared at in cities and old enough to remember things the archives edit.
  • Tieflings are Hellenoria's Voidfolk, with their own status; elsewhere they are assumed to be Hellenorian whether they are or not.
  • Halflings, gnomes, dragonborn and half-orcs live in every empire, mostly as craftsmen, sailors and soldiers; half-orcs met discrimination in the war and still do.
  • Fey and stranger folk are uncommon and treated as Farshore visitors, omens or problems.

New spells

Six spells with an Asetherian accent. Each names the classes that may learn it. A spell taught by one empire's institutions is not illegal elsewhere, but casting it in public announces where you trained.

Muqanni's Ear Divination cantrip · Acheaoria

Casting time: 1 action · Range: self (30 feet) · Components: S · Duration: Concentration, up to 1 minute · Classes: druid, ranger (as a cantrip known if your DM allows), sorcerer, wizard, artificer

You press your palm to earth or stone and listen the way the qanat-diggers do. For the duration you sense, within 30 feet and through up to 10 feet of earth or stone, the direction and rough distance of running or standing water, hollow spaces at least the size of a door, and creatures of Small size or larger moving through earth. You learn nothing of what is inside a hollow except that air moves there.

Muqanni families teach it as a working song; the Magi call it harmless, which is high praise from them.

Juno's Assay 1st-level divination (ritual) · Imperium Invicta

Casting time: 1 minute · Range: touch · Components: V, S, M (a touchstone and a drop of water from a temple of Juno, or any clean water) · Duration: Instantaneous · Classes: artificer, bard, cleric, wizard

You draw the coin, ingot or object across the touchstone and speak Juno's formula of honest weight. You learn the precise metal content and purity of up to 100 coins or one object of up to 10 pounds; whether it has been clipped, plated, debased or recast; and the mint mark or maker's mark it bears, even if defaced. If an illusion or transmutation disguises the material, you learn that a disguise is present and its school.

The priests of Juno cast it at the quarterly Assay before the crowd. The result is announced; the numbers are not.

Testudo 1st-level abjuration · Imperium Invicta

Casting time: 1 bonus action · Range: self (10-foot radius) · Components: V, S, M (a shield you are holding) · Duration: Concentration, up to 1 minute · Classes: cleric, paladin, wizard, artificer

You raise your shield and bark the drill-word, and a faint bronze sheen locks over every shield within reach. Until the spell ends, you and each friendly creature within 10 feet of you that is holding a shield gain a +2 bonus to AC against ranged attacks and advantage on Dexterity saving throws against effects that fall from above (rocks, collapsing ceilings, rains of arrows). A creature loses the benefit while it is more than 10 feet from you. Your speed is halved while you concentrate on the spell.

At higher levels. When cast with a slot of 3rd level or higher, the radius becomes 20 feet.

Wind-Seller's Knot 1st-level transmutation (ritual) · Hellenoria

Casting time: 10 minutes · Range: touch · Components: V, S, M (a cord at least a foot long, tied in the open air) · Duration: 24 hours or until untied · Classes: druid, sorcerer, wizard, bard

You tie a breath of the living wind into a knot. Any creature holding the cord can untie it as an action to release the wind in one of two ways: a gust as the gust of wind spell, a line 60 feet long and 10 feet wide, lasting until the end of that creature's next turn; or a steady following wind that gives one sailing vessel within 30 feet an extra 2 miles per hour for 1 hour. If the knot is not untied within 24 hours, it slips loose with a sigh and nothing else.

On the Aeolus Reach the knots are sold by the dozen, and Ixion Keraunios charges for each. Sailors buy them in threes: one for leaving, one for coming home, one in case.

Incubation 1st-level divination (ritual) · Hellenoria

Casting time: 8 hours (cast while sleeping) · Range: self · Components: V, M (a fleece, a bed of laurel or a sanctuary floor) · Duration: Instantaneous · Classes: bard, cleric, druid, warlock, wizard

You speak a question before you sleep and lie down on the material component. If you sleep the full 8 hours, you dream an answer: a single image or short scene related to the question, chosen by the DM, true but rarely plain. If you cast it in a sanctuary of a god, the dream is clearer, and the DM may add a single word. You can cast this spell only once between long rests, and you gain the benefits of the rest as normal.

The Dream Dormitory at Delphara has used it for centuries. Asking the same question twice gets the same image, which is the closest the gods come to impatience.

Ward of the Undefiled 2nd-level abjuration · Acheaoria

Casting time: 1 action · Range: touch · Components: V, S, M (a flame you touch, and sandalwood worth 5 gp, which the spell consumes) · Duration: Concentration, up to 10 minutes · Classes: cleric, paladin, druid

You feed sandalwood to a fire and name it clean. A 15-foot-radius sphere centred on the flame becomes warded. An undead or fiend that enters the area for the first time on a turn or starts its turn there must make a Wisdom saving throw. On a failure it takes 3d6 radiant damage and cannot willingly move closer to the flame until the start of its next turn. On a success it takes half damage and is unaffected otherwise. The spell ends early if the flame goes out.

At higher levels. When cast with a slot of 3rd level or higher, the damage increases by 1d6 for each slot level above 2nd.

The Magi teach it to every acolyte. They do not say why the fires are kept burning in the halls of honour where the returned dead are kept.

Your Character and the World

One page. Answer each line in a sentence. If you cannot, ask the DM; the answer is probably already in the codex.

1. Where were you born? Origin
  • Pick a city or town. Imperium: Aeterna, Romulo, Aepistra, Mavelon, Anticata, Fucostia, Napplesia, Nemibano, the forest villages of Alderpool, Nemorus and Silva Caminia.
  • Hellenoria: Hellarchon, Corinth, Delphara, Ephelanum (a condominium: which half?), Helionyx, Thebesieas, Thessalonika, Argotiko.
  • Acheaoria: Persemenid, Atarabad, Mithratal, Persevalis, Xerastri, Qa'zshahrv'in, Tabrishiir, R'eyshar.
  • Between: the Duneforged Citadel, Deiperduem, Zandar Isle, Marshroot Grove; or beyond the sea, through Mavelon's Farshore Quays.
  • Which citizenship did you take, and which benefit and drawback? (Citizenship)
2. What did the war do to you? The last fifteen centuries
  • The Treaty is five years old. Where were you when it was signed, and what do you call it?
  • Who in your family served, and were they paid? (Military)
  • What did you lose, and do you blame an empire, a god or a person?
  • Do you believe Iovianus Sandarion is recovering, the Emperor is well, and the Immortals are honoured dead? Your character may be right or wrong; decide what they think.
3. Who counts you? Status and law
  • Your rank: patrician, freedman, metic, Voidfolk, azata, kurtash, free spear, nobody? (Citizenship and status)
  • What document proves who you are, and what happens if you lose it? (a tessera, a sponsor's token, an Accord number, an arashshara's sealing, a spear-ring)
  • Can you be flogged, or must you be tried? Who would appeal for you? (Law)
4. What do you worship, and what do you cast? Faith and licence
  • Which god, if any? The connection is personal; the empire's rules are not. (Faith and licensed magic)
  • If you cast spells: do you hold a collegium licence, an Academy seal, or neither? Where did you learn?
  • What would a Magus, a pontiff or the Truth-Flame think of your magic?
5. Who do you owe? Orders, houses and debts
  • Name one order you trained with, served or crossed: the Vigiles, the Adamantine Line, the Ironclad Legion, the Amphictyony, the Ecliptica Arcanum, the Enchanted Muse, the Melodic Circle, the Wheelwalkers, the Caravan of the Gilded Horizon, the Chyrsus Syndicate, the Argentar.
  • Name one person who would lend you money and one who wants it back. Is either at a Mithril Reserve branch? (Banking)
  • Name one great house you have a feeling about: Caerthain, the Hrodnings, Bacchiadai, Nikandridai, the House of Zindar.
6. Why are you on the road? The hook
  • What are you looking for that cannot be found at home? (a person, a cure, a debt, land, a name)
  • Which road are you on? The Via Ferraria, the Long Lane, the Royal Road, or the Treaty Road through Deiperduem.
  • What would make you go home, and what would stop you?
  • Give the DM one rumour your character believes. It does not have to be true.

The party in the world

Suggestions only: each player decides. These show how the current company could use the options above without changing a word of their backstories.

  • Francis Almer Tauranis high-elf cleric · Noble — a noble raised alone in a castle while his father served and his family's money went on cures for a cursed mother. The Imperium's patrician remnant or a Hellenorian eupatrid house both fit an old name with thin funds. His search for a cure runs naturally through Delphara's dream-readers, the Magi's purification lore and the apothecaries and black markets of the herbalism rules. Citizenship to consider: Hellenoria (Philosopher's Insight) or the Imperium. Feats to consider: Academy Seal, Purity of Fire.
  • Thorfinn Hugrakkur mountain-dwarf barbarian — of Clan Hugrakkur of the lost mountain Kharveth, Imperial vassals but never citizens, now bound for the Duneforged Citadel. The Nomad options or the new Duneforged list both fit; the Quarryman background is the life waiting for him in the Citadel if he wants it, and the Citadel's gangs and the Argentar's dwarven bankers are the people most likely to have heard the name Kharveth.
  • Silvyre half-elf ranger · Outlander — a forest-village girl driven out by what bound itself to her at an old shrine. The Araucarian forest villages (Alderpool, Nemorus, Silva Caminia) suit her childhood. The Nomad list (Rootless Existence is already her story) fits, and the Wheelwalker Cousin feat gives a rootless ranger a road-family. Shrines and artefacts are licensed, catalogued and argued over in every empire; someone will know Pon's shrine.
  • Yinzhang fairy wizard · Haunted One — came to Asetheria from somewhere else and lost his cousin Zhangyin on the way. The Farshore Realms are the natural reading: Seric envoys are rare and treated as omens, and newcomers land at Mavelon and trade at Romulo, so the Farshore Factor's Child offices are where anyone tracing a lost traveller would ask. As a wizard he needs a collegium licence in the Imperium or an Academy seal in Hellenoria; a mind like Yangzhang's is exactly what the Academy wants to study.
  • Haver de Fraudre reborn paladin — heir to a jackal-crowned bloodline, betrayed at a false parley, risen after five years. Her bloodline's god and the "Jackal Crown" sit naturally in the Farshore river kingdom of Khemaret, whose embalmers' arts and god-king the codex already names. In Acheaoria a Reborn will make the Magi uneasy; in the Imperium she will need to explain herself to a pontiff. The Sacred Band feat suits a protector who held a gate.

Expansion

Travel and Journeys

Five years of peace have put more people on the roads than fifteen centuries of war did. Soldiers walk home, factors walk out, pilgrims who could not reach Delphara for three generations queue on the Sacred Way, and every one of them is taxed, fed, robbed and lied to at the same handful of inns. This part is for running the journey rather than skipping it: how long, what it costs, who stops you, and what happens in the middle.

The DM's map is not drawn, so everything here is in days, and the days agree with what the city sections already say: Romulo half a day from Aeterna, Aepistra six days up the Via Septentrionalis, Mavelon about six by the Via Ferraria or three by sea from Fucostia, the Duneforged Citadel three weeks south, Corinth two days from Hellarchon by the Long Lane and a day's sail from Delphara, Argotiko a day's ride from Thebesieas, Persevalis two days from Persemenid for a laden convoy, Persemenid to Xerastri in seven days by relay, and Deiperduem nine or ten days east of Aepistra.

Pace, in the empires' own terms

On foot or with a wagon caravan: about 24 miles a day on a made road (normal pace), 18 off it. Ox-carts, mule trains and the long camel strings of the east move at the same pace, because they stop when the animals do. Mounted: about 36 miles a day for riders who change horses at posting-houses or caravanserais, and for the Caravan of the Gilded Horizon's coaches, which change teams at their own yards. A rider on one horse without remounts goes no faster than a walker over a week; the horse simply arrives tired. Couriers are another order of creature. An Invictian rider with a post warrant takes fresh horses at every station and covers 80 miles a day; the Acheaorian relay does the same with a fresh rider waiting, which is how a letter goes from Persemenid to Xerastri in seven days, a journey of sixteen stages for anyone else. Ships under sail make about 48 miles in a day's run; galleys are faster in a calm and slower in everything else; coasting ships put in each night and lose a third of the time to it.

The empires measure differently and nobody converts. Invictians count milestones, a thousand paces each, with a posting-house (mansio) every day's march. Hellenorians count stades and the days between harbours; their roads are narrow and every city taxes its own stretch. Acheaorians count stages, one post-station to the next, a parasang-marked day's ride apart; a stage is a day mounted and a little more on foot.

Travel times between the nineteen cities

Each cell gives days on foot or with a wagon caravan / days mounted / days by ship, by the quickest usual route. Ship times are sea-only, harbour to harbour: Aeterna counts as a port by the Tiberius barge to Fucostia (one day down, two back up; the table uses the downstream figure), and Eronis counts as a port by Irelas, the dead city's quay a day's walk from the Palace. Overland times to and from the Duneforged Citadel and Acheaoria use Kaelen's Pass, open to trade by treaty and to nobody's comfort. Times between Hellenoria and Xerastri cross the Malaunian Steppe with no road at all. Eronis has no land route; Velothis is an island.

Days between the nineteen cities: on foot or with a wagon caravan / mounted / by ship. A dash means no such way.
